learning. As a university, we too need to increase the systems that support students, starting
with scholarships."

Using these results as a reference, the university has decided to increase the number of advice
desks on student life from next year.

</details>

## Say it

```speak
{何|なに}について{発表|はっぴょう:0}するんですか。
= What are you going to present on?
この{件|けん}に{関|かん}して、ご{質問|しつもん}はありますか。
= Do you have any questions concerning this matter?
{会話|かいわ}を{中心|ちゅうしん:0}に{勉強|べんきょう}しています。
= I'm studying with a focus on conversation.
この{論文|ろんぶん:0}は、とても{参考|さんこう:0}になりました。
= This paper was very useful (as a reference).
{例|たと}えば、どんな{例外|れいがい:0}がありますか。
= For example, what exceptions are there?
```

## Common mistakes

- ×{映画|えいが}に{関|かん}して{話|はな}そうよ in a chat with a friend. In casual speech, について:
  {映画|えいが}について{話|はな}そう.
- ×{留学|りゅうがく}について{資料|しりょう}. Before a noun, add の: {留学|りゅうがく}についての{資料|しりょう}
  (or, more formally, {留学|りゅうがく}に{関|かん}する{資料|しりょう}).
- ×{田中|たなか}さんをはじめ、{来|き}ました. をはじめ needs a group after it: {田中|たなか}さんをはじめ、
  {多|おお}くの{人|ひと}が{来|き}ました.
- ×{家|いえ}において{昼|ひる}ご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べた. において is formal: events, fields and
  periods. For everyday places, で.
- Spelling: について, において and をはじめ in kana; に{関|かん}して and を{中心|ちゅうしん}に in kanji.

## Key points

- 〜について: about; についての + noun; については (as for); についても (about … too).
- 〜に{関|かん}して: concerning (formal); に{関|かん}する + noun, common in headings.
- 〜を{中心|ちゅうしん}に(して): centred on, mainly; を{中心|ちゅうしん}とした / とする + noun.
- 〜をはじめ(として): starting with, including (a famous example, then a group);
  をはじめとする + noun.
- 〜において: formal "in, at" for events, fields and periods; における + noun. In speech, で.
- {解答|かいとう} (to a test) and {回答|かいとう} (to a survey) sound the same.
- New kanji: 論 調 解 例 科 術 表 示 第 関 参 内 容.

The reference sheet "Formal phrases" has these with lesson 11's and the rest of the module's. The
words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete the
lesson.

lessons.title: Depending on and instead of: によって, による, 代わりに, に反して
topics: によって and による
に反して and と違って
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Lessons 11 and 12 gave roles, viewpoints and topics. This lesson is about difference and
replacement: things that vary from place to place, what's done by means of what, who made
something, what takes the place of what, and results that go against expectations. The theme
is differences between countries, regions and cultures: customs abroad, living in another
country, international exchange and local products.

{国|くに}によって{習慣|しゅうかん}が{違|ちが}います。 — Customs differ from country to country.
この{町|まち}では、{米|こめ}の{代|か}わりにパンを{食|た}べる{人|ひと}が{増|ふ}えています。 — In this town more and more people eat bread instead of rice.
{予想|よそう}に{反|はん}して、{日本|にほん}の{夏|なつ}はとても{暑|あつ}かったです。 — Contrary to what I expected, the Japanese summer was very hot.

Spelling: によって, による and によると in kana; {代|か}わりに, {代|か}わって and
に{反|はん}して with their kanji ({代|か}わる and {反|はん}する keep their meanings).

## 〜によって: four jobs

N4 used によると for sources and recognized によって as the "by" of a passive. N3 uses
によって in four ways. The first is by far the most common in conversation.

### 1. Depending on

Noun + によって + a word of difference: {違|ちが}う, {変|か}わる, いろいろだ, さまざまだ (all sorts),
{決|き}まる. "It depends on…", "from … to …", "it varies with…".

{国|くに}によって、あいさつの{仕方|しかた}が{違|ちが}います。 — The way people greet each other differs from country to country.
{地方|ちほう}によって、{同|おな}じ{料理|りょうり}でも{味|あじ}が{変|か}わります。 — Even the same dish tastes different depending on the region.
{人|ひと}によって{考|かんが}え{方|かた}はさまざまです。 — Ways of thinking vary from person to person.
{行|い}くかどうかは、{天気|てんき}によって{決|き}めましょう。 — Let's decide whether to go depending on the weather.

によっては means "in some (cases)": the variation is real, and some of the cases are
different.

{国|くに}によっては、レストランでチップを{払|はら}う{必要|ひつよう}があります。 — In some countries you need to tip in restaurants.
{店|みせ}によっては、カードが{使|つか}えないこともあります。 — Some shops don't take cards.

As a short reply it's simple: それは{場合|ばあい}によります (that depends on the case) and
{人|ひと}によりますね (it depends on the person) are everyday replies, using the verb よる itself.

### 2. By means of

Noun + によって says by what means something is done. It's formal; in speech, で is usual.

インターネットによって、{世界中|せかいじゅう}の{人|ひと}と{交流|こうりゅう}できるようになった。 — Through the internet, we've become able to interact with people all over the world.
{話|はな}し{合|あ}いによって、{問題|もんだい}が{解決|かいけつ}しました。 — The problem was solved by talking it over.

({話|はな}し{合|あ}い = a discussion, from {話|はな}し{合|あ}う, lesson 27.) In a chat: メールで{送|おく}って
(send it by email), not ×メールによって{送|おく}って.

### 3. By (the maker in a passive)

When a passive sentence says who created, discovered, wrote, built or founded something,
the person takes によって, not に.

『げんじものがたり』は、むらさきしきぶによって{書|か}かれました。 — The Tale of Genji was written by Murasaki Shikibu.
{電話|でんわ}はベルによって{発明|はつめい}されたと{言|い}われています。 — The telephone is said to have been invented by Bell.
この{寺|てら}は、{今|いま}から{八百年前|はっぴゃくねんまえ}に{地元|じもと}の{人々|ひとびと}によって{建|た}てられました。 — This temple was built by local people eight hundred years ago.

(The titles and names are in kana here because their kanji are outside N3.) For everyday
passives (being praised, scolded, called, stepped on), keep N4's に: {先生|せんせい}にほめられた.

### 4. Because of

Lesson 6 met によって as a cause, mostly in news and reports: {台風|たいふう}によって{電車|でんしゃ}が
{止|と}まった (the trains stopped because of the typhoon).

### による + noun, and によると

Before a noun, によって becomes による: {国|くに}による{違|ちが}い (differences between countries),
{台風|たいふう}による{遅|おく}れ (delays caused by the typhoon).

によると / によれば (according to) is N4 review: {天気予報|てんきよほう}によると、{明日|あした}は{雨|あめ}だ
そうです. The sentence ends with a hearsay word (〜そうだ, 〜らしい, 〜ということだ). Don't mix it
up with the "depending on" によって: {天気|てんき}によって (depending on the weather) and
{天気予報|てんきよほう}によると (according to the forecast).

## 〜代わりに: instead of; in exchange for

{代|か}わり is a noun meaning "a substitute", so it keeps its kanji. Noun + の{代|か}わりに, or a
verb in the plain form + {代|か}わりに.

### Instead of

{米|こめ}の{代|か}わりに、パンを{食|た}べる{人|ひと}が{増|ふ}えた。 — More people eat bread instead of rice.
{電話|でんわ}する{代|か}わりに、メールを{送|おく}りました。 — Instead of calling, I sent an email.
{今日|きょう}は{雨|あめ}なので、{代|か}わりに{明日|あした}{行|い}きましょう。 — It's raining today, so let's go tomorrow instead.

On its own at the start of a clause, {代|か}わりに means "instead" (the last example).

### In exchange for; but on the other hand

{代|か}わりに can also balance one thing against another: you get A, and in return there's B.

{日本語|にほんご}を{教|おし}えてもらう{代|か}わりに、{英語|えいご}を{教|おし}えています。 — In exchange for being taught Japanese, I teach English.
この{仕事|しごと}は{給料|きゅうりょう}が{高|たか}い{代|か}わりに、{休|やす}みが{少|すく}ない。 — This job pays well, but on the other hand there are few days off.

### 〜に代わって: on behalf of, in place of

Noun + に{代|か}わって (formal: に{代|か}わり) says someone or something takes another's place. It's
common in speeches, announcements and writing about change.

{社長|しゃちょう}に{代|か}わって、{部長|ぶちょう}があいさつをしました。 — The department head gave the speech on the president's behalf.
{人|ひと}に{代|か}わって、ロボットが{働|はたら}く{工場|こうじょう}が{増|ふ}えている。 — Factories where robots work in place of people are increasing.

For standing in for a person, の{代|か}わりに works too and sounds more everyday:
{田中|たなか}さんの{代|か}わりに{私|わたし}が{来|き}ました (I've come instead of Mr Tanaka).

## 〜に反して: contrary to

Noun + に{反|はん}して says the result went against something: usually an expectation, a
prediction, a wish or a rule. It's formal and mostly written. Before a noun: に{反|はん}する.

{予想|よそう}に{反|はん}して、{外国人|がいこくじん}の{観光客|かんこうきゃく}は{減|へ}らなかった。 — Contrary to predictions, foreign tourists didn't decrease.
みんなの{期待|きたい}に{反|はん}して、{新|あたら}しい{店|みせ}はすぐになくなってしまった。 — Against everyone's hopes, the new shop soon closed down.
ルールに{反|はん}することはしないでください。 — Please don't do anything against the rules.
{予想|よそう}に{反|はん}する{結果|けっか}が{出|で}た。 — The results went against the predictions.

({予想|よそう} = prediction, lesson 26; {期待|きたい} = expectation, lesson 1;
{観光客|かんこうきゃく} = tourist, lesson 14.)

## 〜と違って: unlike

Noun + と{違|ちが}って (or とは{違|ちが}って, stressing the contrast) says how one thing differs from
another. It's everyday and written.

{東京|とうきょう}と{違|ちが}って、{私|わたし}の{町|まち}は{夜|よる}とても{静|しず}かです。 — Unlike Tokyo, my town is very quiet at night.
{日本|にほん}とは{違|ちが}って、この{国|くに}ではチップを{払|はら}うのがふつうです。 — Unlike in Japan, in this country tipping is normal.
{去年|きょねん}と{違|ちが}って、{今年|ことし}は{雪|ゆき}が{少|すく}ない。 — Unlike last year, there's little snow this year.

Before a noun: と{違|ちが}う + noun: {日本|にほん}と{違|ちが}う{習慣|しゅうかん} (customs different from
Japan's). Lesson 11's のに{対|たい}して also compares, but it lays two facts side by side, like a
report; と{違|ちが}って starts from one thing and says the other is different from it.

## Kanji

Thirteen kanji for kinds, differences and the world beyond your own country. Only the readings
you meet at N3 are listed.

### Japanese ways

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 和 | Japan; peace | ワ | | 8 | {和食|わしょく}, {和服|わふく} (Japanese clothes), {和風|わふう} (Japanese-style), {和式|わしき}, {平和|へいわ} (peace, lesson 4) |
| 式 | style; ceremony | シキ | | 6 | {方式|ほうしき} (method, system), {正式|せいしき} (formal), {和式|わしき}, {結婚式|けっこんしき}, {入学式|にゅうがくしき} |
| 慣 | get used to | カン | な(れる) | 14 | {慣|な}れる, {習慣|しゅうかん} |

### Kinds and differences

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 種 | seed; kind | シュ | たね | 14 | {種|たね} (seed), {種類|しゅるい} |
| 類 | kind, sort | ルイ | | 18 | {種類|しゅるい}, {人類|じんるい} (humankind), {書類|しょるい} |
| 差 | difference | サ | | 10 | {差|さ} (a gap, a difference), {時差|じさ} (time difference), {差別|さべつ} (discrimination), {交差点|こうさてん} |
| 他 | other | タ | ほか | 5 | {他|ほか}, {他人|たにん} (other people, strangers), その{他|た} (and others), {他国|たこく} |

### Sides and pairs

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 側 | side | | がわ | 11 | {側|がわ}, {右側|みぎがわ}, {両側|りょうがわ}, {内側|うちがわ} |
| 両 | both | リョウ | | 6 | {両方|りょうほう} (both), {両親|りょうしん}, {両手|りょうて}, {両国|りょうこく} |
| 互 | mutual | | たが(い) | 4 | {互|たが}い, お{互|たが}いに (each other) |

### Making and places

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 産 | produce; be born | サン | | 11 | {生産|せいさん} (production), {産地|さんち} (where something comes from), {名産|めいさん} (famous local product), {産業|さんぎょう}, {国産|こくさん}, お{土産|みやげ} |
| 島 | island | トウ | しま (じま) | 10 | {島|しま}, {島国|しまぐに} (island nation), {半島|はんとう} (peninsula), {島々|しまじま} |
| 交 | cross, mix | コウ | | 6 | {交流|こうりゅう} (exchange), {交通|こうつう}, {交差点|こうさてん}, {交番|こうばん}, {交代|こうたい} (lesson 11) |

Carried words you can now write with kanji: {種類|しゅるい}, {書類|しょるい}, {習慣|しゅうかん},
{両親|りょうしん}, {両手|りょうて}, {他|ほか}, {島|しま}, {交通|こうつう}, {交差点|こうさてん}, {交番|こうばん},
{結婚式|けっこんしき} (with lesson 17's kanji), and お{土産|みやげ}, a special reading: 土 and 産 are
read ド and サン elsewhere, but お{土産|みやげ} is みやげ as a whole word.

Notes:

- 他 has two readings you'll use: ほか on its own ({他|ほか}の{人|ひと}, other people; {他|ほか}に, besides)
  and タ in compounds ({他人|たにん}, {他国|たこく}, その{他|た}). その{他|た} (and others, miscellaneous) is
  the usual last line of a list or a form.
- 側 is がわ after a word (sometimes かわ): {右側|みぎがわ}, {向|む}こう{側|がわ} (the other side).
- 島 becomes じま after another word in many names: {小島|こじま}, and in {島々|しまじま} (the islands).
  々 repeats the kanji before it.
- お{互|たが}いに and {互|たが}いに (to each other, mutually) are lesson 17's words; this lesson teaches
  {互|たが}い, usually with お: お{互|たが}いの{国|くに} (each other's countries).
- {和|わ} on its own means "Japan, Japanese" in compounds: {和食|わしょく} / {洋食|ようしょく} (Western
  food), {和式|わしき} / {洋式|ようしき} (a Japanese-style / Western-style toilet), {和室|わしつ} (a
  Japanese-style room).

Memory notes (hooks, not etymology):

- 和: a stalk of grain and a mouth (口): rice for every mouth, and so peace.
- 種 also has the grain stalk on the left, with 重 (heavy): a heavy grain, a seed. 類 has rice (米)
  at the top left: things sorted into kinds, like grains.
- 差: a sheep's horns on top and a worker (工) below: two workers with different jobs, a
  difference.
- 他 and 側 both start with the person radical (the thin 人): the other person, the person at
  your side.
- 両 looks like a pair of scales with a pan on each side: both.
- 互 is two hooks catching each other: mutual.
- 産 has 生 (life) at the bottom: things that are born or produced. 島 is a bird (鳥) sitting on a
  mountain (山) in the sea: an island.
- 交 is a person with crossed legs: crossing. 式 has 工 (work) and a stake: the set way of doing
  the work. 慣 has 心 (heart) on the left: what the heart gets used to.

```trace
和式慣種類差他側両互産島交
```

## Dialogue: three years in Japan

Rina came from Brazil to study three years ago. She's talking with Kohei, a Japanese friend
from her university. (Casual: friends.)

```dialogue
# At a family restaurant
こうへい: リナ、{日本|にほん}に{来|き}てもう{三年|さんねん}だよね。{日本|にほん}の{生活|せいかつ}にはもう{慣|な}れた？
= Rina, it's been three years since you came to Japan, hasn't it? Are you used to life here now?
リナ: うん、だいたいね。でも、{最初|さいしょ}はびっくりすることばかりだったよ。
= Yeah, mostly. But at first everything surprised me.
こうへい: {例|たと}えば？
= For example?
リナ: {店|みせ}の{人|ひと}がすごくていねいなこと。それに、チップがいらないこと。ブラジルでは、レストランによっては、{会計|かいけい}にサービス{料|りょう}が{入|はい}ってるんだ。
= How polite shop staff are. And that you don't need to tip. In Brazil, in some restaurants, a service charge is included in the bill.
こうへい: へえ、{日本|にほん}と{違|ちが}うね。{他|ほか}には？
= Huh, that's different from Japan. Anything else?
リナ: {和式|わしき}のトイレ！ {初|はじ}めて{見|み}たとき、{使|つか}い{方|かた}が{分|わ}からなかった。
= Japanese-style toilets! The first time I saw one, I couldn't work out how to use it.
こうへい: ああ、{最近|さいきん}は{洋式|ようしき}が{多|おお}いけど、{駅|えき}や{公園|こうえん}によっては、まだあるね。
= Oh, these days most are Western-style, but some stations and parks still have them.
リナ: あと、{時差|じさ}が{十二時間|じゅうにじかん}もあるから、{家族|かぞく}と{話|はな}すのが{大変|たいへん}。{電話|でんわ}の{代|か}わりに、メッセージを{送|おく}ることが{多|おお}いかな。
= And there's a twelve-hour time difference, so talking to my family is hard. I usually send messages instead of calling.
こうへい: そうか。じゃあ、ホームシックになったりしない？
= I see. So don't you get homesick?
リナ: {一年目|いちねんめ}はね。でも、{留学生|りゅうがくせい}の{交流|こうりゅう}{会|かい}で{友|とも}だちができてから、{平気|へいき}になった。
= In the first year, yes. But after I made friends at the international students' exchange group, I was fine.
こうへい: よかった。それに、リナは{日本語|にほんご}もすごく{上手|じょうず}になったよね。
= Good. And your Japanese has got really good, too.
リナ: ありがとう。お{互|たが}いの{国|くに}の{料理|りょうり}を{作|つく}って{食|た}べる{会|かい}、また{今度|こんど}やろうよ。
= Thanks. Let's do another evening where we cook and eat each other's food sometime.
```

びっくりする = to be surprised (N4); {会計|かいけい} = the bill; サービス{料|りょう} = a service charge;
{平気|へいき} = fine, not bothered. The time difference Rina mentions is for São Paulo, which is
twelve hours behind Japan; it differs across Brazil.

## Reading: a blog from abroad

A blog post by a Japanese woman who moved to a small town in Europe for her husband's work. It's
in the plain だ style of diaries and blogs.

> {夫|おっと}の{転勤|てんきん}で、この{町|まち}に{来|き}て{半年|はんとし}になる。{来|く}る{前|まえ}は{不安|ふあん}でいっぱいだったが、{予想|よそう}に{反|はん}して、{毎日|まいにち}がとても{楽|たの}しい。
>
> {一番|いちばん}びっくりしたのは、{日曜日|にちようび}にほとんどの{店|みせ}が{閉|し}まっていることだ。{日本|にほん}と{違|ちが}って、この{国|くに}では{日曜日|にちようび}は{家族|かぞく}と{過|す}ごす{日|ひ}だと{考|かんが}える{人|ひと}が{多|おお}いらしい。{最初|さいしょ}は{不便|ふべん}だと{思|おも}ったが、{今|いま}は{私|わたし}も{日曜日|にちようび}は{買|か}い{物|もの}の{代|か}わりに、{近|ちか}くの{森|もり}を{歩|ある}くようにしている。
>
> {食|た}べ{物|もの}もずいぶん{違|ちが}う。{朝|あさ}はパンとチーズが{中心|ちゅうしん}で、{米|こめ}はスーパーにも{一|ひと}つか{二|ふた}つの{種類|しゅるい}しかない。その{代|か}わり、チーズは{何十|なんじゅう}{種類|しゅるい}もあって、{毎週|まいしゅう}{違|ちが}うものを{試|ため}している。でも、{地元|じもと}の{人|ひと}によると、{店|みせ}によっては{日本|にほん}の{米|こめ}も{買|か}えるそうだ。{今度|こんど}{探|さが}してみようと{思|おも}う。
>
> {先週|せんしゅう}、{近所|きんじょ}の{人|ひと}たちとの{交流|こうりゅう}{会|かい}があった。{私|わたし}がおにぎりを{作|つく}って{持|も}っていく{代|か}わりに、となりの{家|いえ}のおばあさんが{地元|じもと}の{名物|めいぶつ}のケーキを{焼|や}いてくれた。{国|くに}によって{習慣|しゅうかん}は{違|ちが}っても、おいしいものを{一緒|いっしょ}に{食|た}べれば、すぐになかよくなれる。{言葉|ことば}はまだ{下手|へた}だが、{少|すこ}しずつこの{町|まち}の{一員|いちいん}になれたらいいと{思|おも}っている。

{夫|おっと} = husband (lesson 17's kanji); {不安|ふあん} = anxiety, worry (N4); {過|す}ごす = to spend
(time), lesson 25; {不便|ふべん} = inconvenient (N5); 〜ようにしている = to make a point of doing
(N4); {探|さが}す = to look for (lesson 19's kanji); {近所|きんじょ} = neighbourhood (N4); その{代|か}わり = instead, to make up for it; {試|ため}す = to try out;
{一緒|いっしょ}に = together (lesson 17's kanji); なかよくなる = to become friends (one kanji is outside N3).

<details>
<summary>Questions (answers inside)</summary>

1. How does the writer feel about life in the town, compared with what she expected? — She was
   full of worries before coming, but, contrary to what she expected, every day is a lot of fun.
2. What does she do on Sundays now, and why? — She walks in the nearby woods instead of going
   shopping, because most shops are closed on Sundays.
3. What did she hear about Japanese rice? — A local person told her that some shops sell it.
4. What happened at the neighbourhood get-together? — She brought rice balls, and in exchange the
   old woman next door baked a cake that the town is known for.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Translation</summary>

It's been half a year since I came to this town with my husband's transfer. Before coming I was
full of worries, but contrary to what I expected, every day is great fun.

What surprised me most is that almost all the shops are closed on Sundays. Unlike in Japan,
many people in this country seem to think of Sunday as a day to spend with family. At first I
thought it was inconvenient, but now I too make a point of walking in the nearby woods on
Sundays instead of shopping.

The food is quite different too. Breakfast is mainly bread and cheese, and even the supermarket
has only one or two kinds of rice. On the other hand, there are dozens of kinds of cheese,
and I try a different one every week. But according to a local, some shops sell Japanese rice. I
think I'll look for it next time.

Last week there was a get-together with the neighbours. I made rice balls and brought them, and
in exchange the old woman next door baked a cake that's a local speciality. Customs may differ
from country to country, but if you eat something delicious together, you soon become friends.
My language is still poor, but I hope that little by little I can become a member of this town.

</details>

## Say it

```speak
{国|くに}によって{習慣|しゅうかん:0}が{違|ちが}います。
= Customs differ from country to country.
それは{人|ひと}によりますね。
= That depends on the person.
{電話|でんわ}の{代|か}わりに、メールを{送|おく}ります。
= I'll send an email instead of calling.
{日本|にほん}と{違|ちが}って、チップを{払|はら}います。
= Unlike in Japan, you tip.
{予想|よそう}に{反|はん}して、{試合|しあい}に{勝|か}ちました。
= Contrary to expectations, we won the match.
```

## Common mistakes

- ×{国|くに}によって、{日本|にほん}に{来|き}ました. "Depending on" needs a word of difference after it
  ({違|ちが}う, {変|か}わる, さまざまだ). "Because of my country" isn't によって.
- ×メールによって{送|おく}ってね in a chat. By-means-of によって is formal; in speech, で.
- ×『げんじものがたり』はむらさきしきぶに{書|か}かれた. For the maker of a work, によって:
  むらさきしきぶによって{書|か}かれた.
- ×{電話|でんわ}の{代|か}わり、メールを{送|おく}った. Keep the に: {代|か}わりに.
- ×{予想|よそう}に{反|はん}して、{試合|しあい}に{勝|か}ってください. に{反|はん}して reports what happened; it
  doesn't take requests.
- によると and によって: {天気予報|てんきよほう}によると (according to the forecast) vs {天気|てんき}によって
  (depending on the weather).

## Key points

- 〜によって: (1) depending on (+ {違|ちが}う, {変|か}わる…); によっては, in some cases; (2) by means
  of (formal); (3) by, for the maker in a passive; (4) because of (news).
- による + noun; によると / によれば: according to.
- 〜{代|か}わりに: instead of; in exchange for, on the other hand. 〜に{代|か}わって: on behalf of,
  in place of.
- 〜に{反|はん}して: contrary to (expectations, predictions, rules); に{反|はん}する + noun.
- 〜と{違|ちが}って: unlike; と{違|ちが}う + noun.
- Spelling: によって and による in kana; {代|か}わりに and に{反|はん}して in kanji.
- New kanji: 和 式 慣 種 類 差 他 側 両 互 産 島 交.

The reference sheet "Formal phrases" has these with the rest of the module's. The words from this
lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete the lesson.

lessons.title: Comparing places and times: に比べて, から〜にかけて, を通して, 最も
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

This lesson's phrases compare: one year with another, one place with another, and the best or
highest of a group. They also map out spans of place and time ("from the Kanto region up to
Tohoku", "from late March into April") and what happens throughout a period or through a
means. They're the language of travel guides and forecasts, so the theme is travel and
sightseeing: trips, places to visit, where to stay, landscapes, mountains, islands and the
seasons to go.

{去年|きょねん}に{比|くら}べて、{観光客|かんこうきゃく}が{増|ふ}えました。 — Compared with last year, there are more tourists.
{三月|さんがつ}の{終|お}わりから{四月|しがつ}にかけて、さくらがさきます。 — The cherry trees bloom from the end of March into April.
この{島|しま}は{一年|いちねん}を{通|とお}して{温|あたた}かいです。 — This island is warm all year round.
{日本|にほん}で{最|もっと}も{高|たか}い{山|やま}は、ふじさんです。 — The highest mountain in Japan is Mount Fuji.

Spelling: に{比|くら}べて, を{通|とお}して and {最|もっと}も are written with their kanji; にかけて is in
kana (かける is the "hang over, span" verb). (ふじさん is in kana because one of its kanji
is outside N3, and さく, to bloom, has a kanji outside N3 too.)

## 〜に比べて: compared with

Noun + に{比|くら}べて (or と{比|くら}べて) says what something is being compared with. What follows
is a comparison: {多|おお}い, {少|すく}ない, {安|やす}い, {増|ふ}えた, {減|へ}った, ずっと, {少|すこ}し, のほうが.

{電車|でんしゃ}に{比|くら}べて、バスは{安|やす}いですが、{時間|じかん}がかかります。 — Compared with the train, the bus is cheaper but takes longer.
{十年前|じゅうねんまえ}と{比|くら}べて、{一人旅|ひとりたび}をする{人|ひと}が{増|ふ}えた。 — Compared with ten years ago, more people travel alone.
{平日|へいじつ}に{比|くら}べると、{週末|しゅうまつ}は{宿|やど}の{料金|りょうきん}が{高|たか}くなります。 — Compared with weekdays, inns cost more at the weekend.

- に{比|くら}べて and と{比|くら}べて mean the same in most sentences.
- に{比|くら}べると / と{比|くら}べると sound a little more like "if you compare them".
- {比|くら}べると can also start a sentence: {比|くら}べると、こちらのほうが{静|しず}かですね (comparing
  the two, this one's quieter).
- In writing you'll see に{比|くら}べ, without て: {昨年|さくねん}に{比|くら}べ、{観光客|かんこうきゃく}が
  {二割|にわり}{増|ふ}えた (tourists rose 20% on the previous year; {昨年|さくねん} is lesson 25's word).

{比|くら}べる is N4's くらべる, now in kanji with lesson 4's 比.

## 〜から〜にかけて: from … through to …

から〜にかけて marks a span of place or time whose edges are loose: "from around A to around
B", "across", "through". It's the language of forecasts, guides and news.

{関東|かんとう}から{東北|とうほく}にかけて、{雪|ゆき}が{降|ふ}るでしょう。 — Snow is expected from the Kanto region up through Tohoku.
{十月|じゅうがつ}の{終|お}わりから{十一月|じゅういちがつ}にかけて、もみじが{見|み}ごろになります。 — From the end of October into November, the autumn leaves are at their best.
{日本|にほん}の{多|おお}くの{地方|ちほう}では、{六月|ろくがつ}から{七月|しちがつ}にかけて{雨|あめ}が{多|おお}い。 — In much of Japan it rains a lot from June into July.

({見|み}ごろ = the best time to see something.)

Compare から〜まで, which has exact ends: {店|みせ}は{九時|くじ}から{五時|ごじ}まで{開|あ}いています (the shop
is open from nine to five), not ×{九時|くじ}から{五時|ごじ}にかけて. A timetable or opening hours want
まで; a season, a region or a stretch of road wants にかけて.

にかけて can also follow the end point without a から: {明日|あした}の{朝|あさ}にかけて (into
tomorrow morning), {週末|しゅうまつ}にかけて (through to the weekend).

## 〜を通して / 〜を通じて: throughout; through

### 1. Throughout a period

Noun of time + を{通|とお}して: all through it, without a break.

この{島|しま}は{一年|いちねん}を{通|とお}して{観光客|かんこうきゃく}が{多|おお}い。 — This island has lots of tourists all year round.
{夏休|なつやす}みを{通|とお}して、{毎日|まいにち}{泳|およ}ぎに{行|い}った。 — I went swimming every day all through the summer holidays.

### 2. Through (a means, a person, an experience)

Noun + を{通|とお}して: by way of, through. It suggests passing through something in between.

{友人|ゆうじん}を{通|とお}して、{今|いま}の{会社|かいしゃ}を{知|し}りました。 — I found out about my current company through a friend.
{旅行|りょこう}を{通|とお}して、{多|おお}くのことを{学|まな}びました。 — I learned a lot through travelling.
ホームページを{通|つう}じて{宿|やど}を{予約|よやく}した。 — I booked the inn through its website.

を{通|つう}じて means the same and is a little more formal or written; {通|つう}じる is read つう.
Compare lesson 13's によって (by means of): によって names the means or the cause; を{通|とお}して
stresses something you go through, an intermediary or an experience.

## The most: superlatives

You know 〜の{中|なか}で〜が{一番|いちばん}〜 from N5. N3 adds the written forms.

- {最|もっと}も is the written, formal {一番|いちばん}: {日本|にほん}で{最|もっと}も{古|ふる}い{寺|てら} (the
  oldest temple in Japan). In conversation, {一番|いちばん} is more natural.
- 〜のうちで is "among" a set group, a little more formal than の{中|なか}で:
  {春|はる}、{夏|なつ}、{秋|あき}、{冬|ふゆ}のうちで、{秋|あき}が{一番|いちばん}{旅行|りょこう}に{向|む}いている
  (of the four seasons, autumn is best for travelling; {向|む}く = to suit, this lesson).
- 〜ほど〜はない: nothing is as … as A. It's another way of saying "the most":
  {京都|きょうと}ほど{古|ふる}い{寺|てら}が{多|おお}い{町|まち}はない (no city has as many old temples as Kyoto).
  With もの for things: {旅|たび}ほど{楽|たの}しいものはない (there's nothing as fun as travelling).
- 〜ほどではない: not as much as A: {北海道|ほっかいどう}ほどではないが、ここも{冬|ふゆ}は{寒|さむ}い (it's not
  as cold as Hokkaido, but winter is cold here too). Lesson 15 looks at ほど in detail.

In writing, the prefixes {最|さい}〜 do the same job inside a word: {最高|さいこう}の (the best, the
highest), {最大|さいだい}の (the biggest), {最初|さいしょ} and {最後|さいご} (lesson 15's kanji).

| Style | "The most popular sight in Kyoto" |
|---|---|
| Speech | {京都|きょうと}で{一番|いちばん}{人気|にんき}がある{所|ところ} |
| Writing | {京都|きょうと}で{最|もっと}も{人気|にんき}のある{観光地|かんこうち} |
| Another way | {京都|きょうと}でここほど{人気|にんき}がある{所|ところ}はない |

## Kanji

Thirteen kanji for getting out and seeing places. Only the readings you meet at N3 are listed.

### Views

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 景 | view, scene | ケイ | | 12 | {景色|けしき}, {風景|ふうけい} (scenery), {夜景|やけい} (night view), {絶景|ぜっけい} (a superb view), {景観|けいかん} |
| 観 | look at, view | カン | | 18 | {観光|かんこう}, {観光客|かんこうきゃく}, {観光地|かんこうち}, {観客|かんきゃく} (spectators, lesson 15) |

### Staying and visiting

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 宿 | lodging | シュク | やど | 11 | {宿|やど} (an inn), {民宿|みんしゅく} (a guesthouse), {宿題|しゅくだい} |
| 訪 | visit | ホウ | おとず(れる), たず(ねる) | 11 | {訪|おとず}れる, {訪問|ほうもん}, {訪|たず}ねる (to visit) |
| 寄 | come close; drop in | | よ(る), よ(せる) | 11 | {寄|よ}る (to drop in), {立|た}ち{寄|よ}る, {寄|よ}り{道|みち} (a detour) |

### Going over, going up, arriving

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 越 | go over | | こ(える), こ(す) | 12 | {越|こ}える (to cross over), {越|こ}す, {引|ひ}っ{越|こ}す |
| 登 | climb | ト, トウ | のぼ(る) | 12 | {登|のぼ}る, {登山|とざん} (mountain climbing), {山登|やまのぼ}り |
| 到 | arrive | トウ | | 8 | {到着|とうちゃく} (arrival) |
| 向 | face, towards | コウ | む(く), む(ける), む(かう), む(こう) | 6 | {向|む}かう, {向|む}く, {向|む}ける, {向|む}こう, {向|む}かい (opposite), {方向|ほうこう} (direction) |

### Places and crossings

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 園 | garden, park | エン | | 13 | {公園|こうえん}, {動物園|どうぶつえん}, {遊園地|ゆうえんち} (amusement park), {庭園|ていえん} (a formal garden) |
| 橋 | bridge | キョウ | はし (ばし) | 16 | {橋|はし}, {鉄橋|てっきょう} (railway bridge), {歩道橋|ほどうきょう} (footbridge) |
| 横 | side; across | オウ | よこ | 15 | {横|よこ}, {横断|おうだん} (crossing), {横切|よこぎ}る (to cut across) |
| 泳 | swim | エイ | およ(ぐ) | 8 | {泳|およ}ぐ, {水泳|すいえい} |

Carried words you can now write with kanji: {観光|かんこう}, {宿題|しゅくだい}, {引|ひ}っ{越|こ}す,
{登|のぼ}る, {山登|やまのぼ}り (N5 wrote 山のぼり), {到着|とうちゃく}, {向|む}こう, {公園|こうえん},
{動物園|どうぶつえん}, {横|よこ}, {泳|およ}ぐ, {水泳|すいえい}, {橋|はし}, {比|くら}べる (lesson 4's kanji), and
{景色|けしき}, a special reading: 景 is ケイ and 色 is しょく or いろ elsewhere, but {景色|けしき} is read
as a whole.

Notes:

- {訪|たず}ねる (to visit a person or place) sounds like N4's たずねる (to ask), but it's a different
  use with its own kanji. "To ask" is written with a kanji outside N3, so it stays in kana:
  {道|みち}をたずねる (ask the way), {友|とも}だちを{訪|たず}ねる (visit a friend). {訪|おとず}れる is the
  more written word, often for places and seasons: {春|はる}が{訪|おとず}れる (spring comes).
- {越|こ}える is crossing over something high or a line (a mountain, a border, a limit);
  {越|こ}す is similar and also means "to move house" in {引|ひ}っ{越|こ}す.
- 向 has four kun forms from one root: {向|む}く (to face; to suit), {向|む}ける (to turn something
  towards), {向|む}かう (to head for), {向|む}こう (over there, the other side).
- 橋 is ばし after another word: {日本橋|にほんばし} (a district of Tokyo).
- 登 is ト in {登山|とざん}, and トウ in {登場|とうじょう} (appearing on stage).

Memory notes (hooks, not etymology):

- 景: the sun (日) above a capital city (京): the city scene in sunlight.
- 観: a crested bird on the left, 見 (see) on the right: looking around like a bird.
- 宿: a roof over a person and 百 (hundred): a hundred guests under one roof.
- 訪: words (言) and 方 (direction): asking the way when you visit.
- 寄: a roof on top: come in under someone's roof, drop in.
- 越: 走 (run) on the left: run over the top.
- 登: two feet (the top part) climbing up onto a stand.
- 到 ends in a knife (the two strokes on the right, like 別): the journey cut short, you've
  arrived.
- 向: a window under a roof: facing out towards something.
- 園: a big enclosure round a garden. 橋 and 横 start with 木 (tree): bridges and the bars
  across a gate were wood.
- 泳: the water radical (three drops) on the left: swimming.

```trace
景観宿訪寄越登到向園橋横泳
```

## Dialogue: at a travel agency

Mr Ishida wants to take his parents on a trip in the autumn. He's at the counter of a travel
agency. (Polite: staff and customer. The staff member uses N4's keigo.)

```dialogue
# At the travel agency
スタッフ: いらっしゃいませ。どちらへのご{旅行|りょこう}をお{考|かんが}えですか。
= Welcome. Where are you thinking of travelling?
いしだ: {十一月|じゅういちがつ}の{初|はじ}めに、{両親|りょうしん}を{連|つ}れて、もみじを{見|み}に{行|い}きたいんです。
= At the beginning of November I'd like to take my parents to see the autumn leaves.
スタッフ: それでしたら、{東北|とうほく}はいかがでしょうか。{例年|れいねん}、{十月|じゅうがつ}の{中|なか}ごろから{十一月|じゅういちがつ}の{初|はじ}めにかけてが{見|み}ごろです。
= In that case, how about Tohoku? In a typical year the leaves are at their best from the middle of October to the beginning of November.
いしだ: {京都|きょうと}も{考|かんが}えたんですが…。
= I'd thought about Kyoto too...
スタッフ: {京都|きょうと}は{東北|とうほく}に{比|くら}べて{遅|おそ}く、{十一月|じゅういちがつ}の{中|なか}ごろから{終|お}わりごろが{見|み}ごろです。それに、もみじの{時期|じき}の{京都|きょうと}は、{一年|いちねん}で{最|もっと}も{観光客|かんこうきゃく}が{多|おお}い{時期|じき}の{一|ひと}つなんです。
= Kyoto is later than Tohoku: the leaves are at their best from mid to late November. And Kyoto in the autumn-leaves season is one of the busiest times of the year for tourists.
いしだ: そうですか。{両親|りょうしん}は{人|ひと}が{多|おお}いところが{苦手|にがて}なので、{東北|とうほく}にします。
= I see. My parents don't like crowded places, so I'll go for Tohoku.
スタッフ: こちらの{宿|やど}はいかがでしょう。{部屋|へや}から{山|やま}の{景色|けしき}がよく{見|み}えますし、{近|ちか}くに{古|ふる}いお{寺|てら}もございます。
= How about this inn? You get a good view of the mountains from the rooms, and there's an old temple nearby.
いしだ: いいですね。{駅|えき}からは{遠|とお}いですか。
= That sounds good. Is it far from the station?
スタッフ: {駅|えき}から{宿|やど}のバスで{二十分|にじゅっぷん}ほどです。{途中|とちゅう}で{大|おお}きな{橋|はし}を{渡|わた}りますが、そこからの{景色|けしき}も{有名|ゆうめい}なんですよ。
= It's about twenty minutes by the inn's bus from the station. On the way you cross a big bridge, and the view from there is famous too.
いしだ: じゃあ、{帰|かえ}りにその{橋|はし}に{寄|よ}れますか。
= Then can we stop at that bridge on the way back?
スタッフ: はい、バスの{運転手|うんてんしゅ}に{言|い}えば{止|と}まってくれます。ご{予約|よやく}は、こちらのホームページを{通|とお}してもお{取|と}りいただけます。
= Yes, if you tell the bus driver, he'll stop for you. You can also make the booking through our website.
```

{例年|れいねん} = in a typical year; {時期|じき} = time, season (lesson 1); {苦手|にがて} = not good with,
not fond of (N5); {渡|わた}る = to cross (lesson 2's kanji); {運転手|うんてんしゅ} = driver; ございます
= polite あります (N4). Autumn-leaf dates move with the weather each year and vary by place and
height, so the staff member hedges with {例年|れいねん}.

## Reading: a travel column

From the travel page of a regional newspaper, in the plain だ style of columns. The town is
made up for this course.

> {白山町|しらやままち}は、{県|けん}の{北部|ほくぶ}にある{小|ちい}さな{山|やま}の{町|まち}だ。{東京|とうきょう}から{電車|でんしゃ}で{三時間|さんじかん}かかるが、{一年|いちねん}を{通|とお}して{多|おお}くの{観光客|かんこうきゃく}が{訪|おとず}れる。
>
> {春|はる}から{夏|なつ}にかけては、{登山|とざん}を{楽|たの}しむ{人|ひと}が{多|おお}い。{町|まち}の{西|にし}にある{白山|しらやま}は{県内|けんない}で{最|もっと}も{高|たか}い{山|やま}だが、{初心者|しょしんしゃ}でも{登|のぼ}りやすい{道|みち}がある。{途中|とちゅう}には{小|ちい}さな{神社|じんじゃ}があり、{多|おお}くの{人|ひと}がそこで{一休|ひとやす}みしてから{上|うえ}を{目指|めざ}す。{山|やま}の{上|うえ}から{見|み}る{景色|けしき}は、まさに{絶景|ぜっけい}だ。
>
> {秋|あき}は、{十月|じゅうがつ}の{中|なか}ごろから{十一月|じゅういちがつ}にかけて、{山|やま}が{赤|あか}やきいろに{変|か}わる。{町|まち}の{人|ひと}によると、{有名|ゆうめい}な{観光地|かんこうち}に{比|くら}べて{人|ひと}が{少|すく}なく、ゆっくり{歩|ある}けるのがいいところだそうだ。
>
> {冬|ふゆ}は{雪|ゆき}が{多|おお}く、スキー{場|じょう}がにぎわう。{最近|さいきん}は、スキーを{通|とお}して{日本|にほん}の{山|やま}の{暮|く}らしを{知|し}りたいという{外国人|がいこくじん}も{増|ふ}えている。{駅|えき}の{前|まえ}には、{英語|えいご}で{相談|そうだん}できる{観光|かんこう}の{窓口|まどぐち}もできた。
>
> {町|まち}に{大|おお}きなホテルはないが、{民宿|みんしゅく}が{二十|にじゅっ}けんほどある。どの{宿|やど}も、{地元|じもと}の{野菜|やさい}や{川|かわ}の{魚|さかな}を{使|つか}った{料理|りょうり}がじまんだ。{日帰|ひがえ}りもできるが、この{町|まち}のよさは、{一晩|ひとばん}とまってみなければ{分|わ}からない。ここの{夜空|よぞら}ほど{美|うつく}しいものはないと{言|い}う{客|きゃく}も{多|おお}い。

{県|けん} = prefecture (N4); {初心者|しょしんしゃ} = beginner (lesson 1); まさに = truly, exactly; きいろ =
yellow (the noun of N4's きいろい; one kanji is outside N3); にぎわう = to be lively, busy with people; {暮|く}らし = way
of life (lesson 23); {一休|ひとやす}み = a short rest; {目指|めざ}す = to aim for (lesson 29's kanji);
{窓口|まどぐち} = a service desk; 〜けん counts houses and shops (its kanji is outside N3); じまん = pride, the
thing a place is proud of; とまる = to stay the night (its kanji is outside N3); {夜空|よぞら} = the
night sky.

<details>
<summary>Questions (answers inside)</summary>

1. When do people visit Shirayama-machi? — All year round ({一年|いちねん}を{通|とお}して).
2. What is special about Mount Shirayama? — It's the highest mountain in the prefecture, but there
   are paths that even beginners find easy to climb.
3. What do local people say is good about the town in autumn? — Compared with famous tourist
   spots, there are fewer people, so you can walk at a leisurely pace.
4. Why does the writer suggest staying the night? — You can't understand what's good about the
   town unless you stay a night; many guests say nothing is as beautiful as its night sky.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Translation</summary>

Shirayama-machi is a small mountain town in the north of the prefecture. It's three hours by
train from Tokyo, but many tourists visit all year round.

From spring into summer, many people come to enjoy mountain climbing. Mount Shirayama, to the
west of the town, is the highest mountain in the prefecture, but there are paths that are easy
to climb even for beginners. Halfway up there's a small shrine, and many people take a short
rest there before heading for the top. The view from the top is truly superb.

In autumn, from the middle of October into November, the mountains turn red and yellow.
According to people in the town, what's good is that compared with famous tourist spots there
are fewer people, and you can walk at your own pace.

In winter there's a lot of snow, and the ski slopes are busy. Recently more and more foreigners
want to learn about life in the Japanese mountains through skiing. In front of the station there's now a tourist information desk where you can
ask for help in English.

There are no big hotels in the town, but there are about twenty guesthouses. Every inn is proud
of its cooking with local vegetables and fish from the river. You can come for the day, but you
won't understand what's good about this town unless you stay a night. Many guests say nothing
is as beautiful as the night sky here.

</details>

## Say it

```speak
{去年|きょねん}に{比|くら}べて、{観光客|かんこうきゃく:3}が{増|ふ}えました。
= Compared with last year, there are more tourists.
{関東|かんとう}から{東北|とうほく}にかけて、{雪|ゆき}が{降|ふ}るでしょう。
= Snow is expected from Kanto through Tohoku.
この{島|しま}は{一年|いちねん}を{通|とお}して{温|あたた}かいです。
= This island is warm all year round.
{日本|にほん}で{最|もっと:3}も{古|ふる}いお{寺|てら}はどこですか。
= Where is the oldest temple in Japan?
{帰|かえ}りに{寄|よ}り{道|みち:0}しましょう。
= Let's make a detour on the way back.
```

## Common mistakes

- ×{店|みせ}は{九時|くじ}から{五時|ごじ}にかけて{開|あ}いています. Exact hours take から〜まで; にかけて is
  for loose spans of place and time.
- ×{東京|とうきょう}に{比|くら}べて、{大|おお}きい{町|まち}です. に{比|くら}べて needs a comparison after it:
  {東京|とうきょう}に{比|くら}べて{小|ちい}さい / {人|ひと}が{少|すく}ない.
- ×{一年|いちねん}に{通|とお}して. The particle is を: {一年|いちねん}を{通|とお}して.
- ×{最|もっと}もいい{友|とも}だちだよ in a chat. {最|もっと}も is written and formal; in speech, {一番|いちばん}.
- ×{北海道|ほっかいどう}ほど{寒|さむ}い. ほど compares only with a negative or in the "nothing is as…"
  pattern: {北海道|ほっかいどう}ほど{寒|さむ}くない, {北海道|ほっかいどう}ほど{寒|さむ}い{所|ところ}はない.
- {訪|たず}ねる is "visit"; "ask" stays in kana: たずねる.

## Key points

- 〜に{比|くら}べて / と{比|くら}べて (written: に{比|くら}べ): compared with; a comparison follows.
- 〜から〜にかけて: a loose span of place or time (forecasts, seasons, regions); exact hours take
  から〜まで.
- 〜を{通|とお}して / を{通|つう}じて: (1) throughout a period; (2) through a person, a means, an
  experience.
- Superlatives: {最|もっと}も (written {一番|いちばん}), 〜のうちで, 〜ほど〜はない (nothing is as…),
  〜ほどではない (not as … as).
- {訪|おとず}れる, {訪|たず}ねる, {越|こ}える, {向|む}かう, {寄|よ}る: verbs of travel with this lesson's kanji.
- New kanji: 景 観 宿 訪 寄 越 登 到 向 園 橋 横 泳.

The reference sheet "Formal phrases" has these with the rest of the module's. The words from this
lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete the lesson.

lessons.title: Degree and emphasis: ほど, くらい, さえ, こそ, あまり
topics: あまり and せめて
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

The last core lesson of the module turns from formal phrases to small words with a big effect.
ほど and くらい say how far something goes ("so tired I couldn't stand"); さえ picks out an
extreme case ("not even water"); こそ says "this one, and no other" ("this time for sure");
あまり says something went too far; and せめて asks for the least you'd settle for. The theme is
sport, games and competitions, where all of them come up: winning and losing, training,
rankings, fans, the Olympics and board games.

{試合|しあい}の{後|あと}、{立|た}てないほど{疲|つか}れていました。 — After the match I was so tired I couldn't stand.
{忙|いそが}しくて、{水|みず}を{飲|の}む{時間|じかん}さえありませんでした。 — I was so busy I didn't even have time to drink water.
{今度|こんど}こそ{勝|か}ちたいです。 — This time I really want to win.
あまりにも{相手|あいて}が{強|つよ}くて、{一点|いってん}も{取|と}れませんでした。 — The other team was just too strong; we didn't score a single point.
せめて{一回|いっかい}は{勝|か}ちたかった。 — I wanted to win at least once.

さえ and こそ are **[[emphatic particles]]**: particles whose job is to put weight on a word, not
to show its role in the sentence. (N4's しか and N5's も are close relatives.)

## Degree: 〜ほど and 〜くらい・ぐらい

A verb, an adjective or a noun + ほど or くらい (ぐらい) says the degree: "so … that", "to the
point of", "enough to". The part before ほど is often an exaggeration.

{泣|な}きたいほど{痛|いた}かった。 — It hurt so much I wanted to cry.
{死|し}ぬほど{疲|つか}れた。 — I'm dead tired. (casual: literally "tired enough to die")
{信|しん}じられないくらい{強|つよ}いチームだ。 — It's an unbelievably strong team.
{宿題|しゅくだい}が{山|やま}ほどある。 — I've got a mountain of homework.

As degree words, ほど and くらい mostly mean the same. ほど sounds a little more formal or
written; くらい (or ぐらい: both are fine) is the everyday choice. Both are grammar words, so they
stay in kana: the kanji 位 (this lesson) is for rank, not for くらい.

### くらい: at least, only that much

くらい has a job ほど doesn't: it can mark something as small, the minimum or "nothing much".

{自分|じぶん}の{部屋|へや}ぐらい、{自分|じぶん}でそうじしなさい。 — At least clean your own room yourself.
{一回|いっかい}くらい{勝|か}ちたい。 — I'd like to win at least once.
そのくらい、{気|き}にしなくていいよ。 — Don't worry about a little thing like that.

Here ほど is wrong: ×{一回|いっかい}ほど{勝|か}ちたい would mean "I want to win about once". (くらい
and ほど after a number both mean "about": {三十分|さんじゅっぷん}ほど / くらい, about thirty minutes.)

### ほど〜ない and くらいなら

N4's A は B ほど〜ない (A isn't as … as B) is the same ほど: {兄|あに}は{私|わたし}ほど{速|はや}く{走|はし}れない
(my brother can't run as fast as I can). Lesson 14 added 〜ほど〜はない (nothing is as …) and
lesson 4 〜ば〜ほど (the more…, the more…).

One more to recognize: 〜くらいなら means "rather than (something you'd hate)": {負|ま}けるくらいなら、
{最初|さいしょ}から{出|で}ない (if I'm going to lose, I'd rather not enter at all).

## 〜さえ: even

さえ marks an extreme example, so the rest goes without saying: "even X (so of course everything
else)". It's usually in negative or surprising sentences.

{忙|いそが}しくて、{水|みず}を{飲|の}む{時間|じかん}さえなかった。 — I was so busy I didn't even have time to drink water.
{家族|かぞく}にさえ{言|い}わなかった。 — I didn't even tell my family.
その{選手|せんしゅ}は、{名前|なまえ}さえ{知|し}られていなかった。 — Nobody even knew that player's name.

- さえ replaces が and を, and goes after the other particles: にさえ, とさえ, からさえ.
- For a subject, でさえ is common and a little stronger: この{問題|もんだい}は{先生|せんせい}でさえ
  {解|と}けなかった (even the teacher couldn't solve this problem); {子供|こども}でさえ{知|し}っている
  (even children know it).
- も can also mean "even" ({名前|なまえ}も{知|し}らない), but さえ makes the extreme clearer.

### 〜さえ〜ば: as long as, if only

さえ + a conditional says that only one condition is needed: "as long as A, (B is fine)".

{天気|てんき}さえよければ、{試合|しあい}はあります。 — As long as the weather's good, the match is on.
{毎日|まいにち}{練習|れんしゅう}さえすれば、{必|かなら}ず{上達|じょうたつ}しますよ。 — As long as you practise every day, you're sure to improve.
ボールを{投|な}げさえすれば、{犬|いぬ}は{喜|よろこ}ぶ。 — As long as you throw the ball, the dog's happy.
あなたさえいれば、{何|なに}もいらない。 — As long as I have you, I don't need anything.

| What comes before | Form | Example |
|---|---|---|
| noun | noun + さえ + ば form | {天気|てんき}さえよければ, あなたさえいれば |
| する verb | noun part + さえすれば | {練習|れんしゅう}さえすれば |
| other verbs | ます stem + さえすれば | {投|な}げさえすれば, {走|はし}りさえすれば |
| て form | て form + さえいれば | {笑|わら}ってさえいれば (as long as you keep smiling) |

## 〜こそ: this very one

こそ picks out one thing as the one that really counts: "this is the one", "it's X that…".
It usually stresses something positive or important.

{今度|こんど}こそ{勝|か}ちたい。 — This time I really want to win. (after losing before)
{今年|ことし}こそ、マラソンを{完走|かんそう}するつもりだ。 — This year, for sure, I'm going to finish the marathon.
「よろしくお{願|ねが}いします。」「こちらこそ。」 — "I look forward to working with you." "Likewise." (literally "it's me who should say so")

- 〜からこそ: precisely because: {好|す}きだからこそ、{毎日|まいにち}{練習|れんしゅう}を{続|つづ}けられる
  (it's precisely because I love it that I can keep training every day).
- 〜ときこそ: {苦|くる}しいときこそ、{笑顔|えがお}を{忘|わす}れないで (it's when things are hard that you
  should keep smiling; {笑顔|えがお} = a smile, lesson 10).
- こそ replaces は, が and を, and can follow other particles (にこそ, でこそ).

{完走|かんそう}する = to run the whole distance and finish; こちらこそ is from N5.

## 〜あまり and あまりにも: too much

N5's あまり〜ない (not very) is a different use. Here あまり is about excess.

あまりにも (or あまりに) + an adjective or verb: far too, so extremely that…

あまりにも{相手|あいて}が{強|つよ}くて、{一点|いってん}も{取|と}れなかった。 — The other side was so strong we couldn't score a point.
あまりに{寒|さむ}いので、{試合|しあい}は{中止|ちゅうし}になった。 — It was so cold that the match was called off.

Plain あまり works this way too before a reason (あまり{寒|さむ}いので…), but with a negative it's
N5's "not very" (あまり{寒|さむ}くない), so あまりにも is the clearer choice for "too".

noun + のあまり or verb + あまり: so much (of a feeling) that something happens, often
something you didn't mean to do.

うれしさのあまり、{泣|な}いてしまった。 — I was so happy I cried.
きんちょうのあまり、{何|なに}も{言|い}えなかった。 — I was so nervous I couldn't say a thing.
{勝|か}ちたいと{思|おも}うあまり、ルールを{忘|わす}れてしまった。 — He wanted to win so badly that he forgot the rules.

(きんちょう = nerves, tension; its kanji are outside N3.) To recognize: あまりの + noun + に:
あまりの{寒|さむ}さに、{声|こえ}も{出|で}なかった (it was so cold I couldn't even speak).

## せめて: at least

せめて gives the smallest thing you'd be happy with. It goes with wishes, hopes and requests
(〜たい, 〜てほしい, 〜てください, 〜ば), not with plain facts, and often with だけでも or くらい.

せめて{一回|いっかい}は{勝|か}ちたい。 — I want to win at least once.
{優勝|ゆうしょう}は{無理|むり}でも、せめて{予選|よせん}は{通|とお}りたい。 — Even if winning is impossible, I'd at least like to get through the qualifiers.
せめて{名前|なまえ}だけでも{教|おし}えてください。 — Please at least tell me your name.

For a fact, use {少|すく}なくとも (at least, no fewer than): {少|すく}なくとも{三百人|さんびゃくにん}の
ファンが{来|き}た (at least three hundred fans came), not ×せめて{三百人|さんびゃくにん}{来|き}た.

## Kanji

Thirteen kanji for competition. Only the readings you meet at N3 are listed.

### Winning and losing

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 勝 | win | ショウ | か(つ) | 12 | {勝|か}つ, {勝|か}ち, {優勝|ゆうしょう} (winning a championship), {勝利|しょうり} (victory), {決勝|けっしょう} (the final) |
| 負 | lose; bear | (ブ) | ま(ける) | 9 | {負|ま}ける, {負|ま}け, {勝負|しょうぶ} (a contest), {勝|か}ち{負|ま}け |
| 敗 | defeat | ハイ | やぶ(れる) | 11 | {敗|やぶ}れる (to be defeated), {敗退|はいたい} (being knocked out), {失敗|しっぱい}, {連敗|れんぱい} |

### Fighting

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 戦 | fight, battle | セン | たたか(う) | 13 | {戦|たたか}う, {戦|たたか}い, {戦争|せんそう} (war), {作戦|さくせん} (tactics), {対戦|たいせん} |
| 争 | compete, dispute | ソウ | あらそ(う) | 6 | {争|あらそ}う, {争|あらそ}い, {戦争|せんそう} |

### Ball games

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 球 | ball, sphere | キュウ | たま | 11 | {球|たま}, {野球|やきゅう}, {球場|きゅうじょう} (ballpark), {地球|ちきゅう} (the earth, lesson 26) |
| 投 | throw | トウ | な(げる) | 7 | {投|な}げる, {投手|とうしゅ} (pitcher) |
| 打 | hit, strike | ダ | う(つ) | 5 | {打|う}つ |

### Rankings and results

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 位 | rank, position | イ | | 7 | 〜{位|い} (… place: {一位|いちい}), {上位|じょうい} (the top places), {首位|しゅい} (first place), {地位|ちい} (lesson 11), {単位|たんい} (lesson 12) |
| 選 | choose | セン | えら(ぶ) | 15 | {選|えら}ぶ, {選手|せんしゅ}, {予選|よせん} (qualifying round) |
| 点 | point, dot | テン | | 9 | {点|てん}, {得点|とくてん} (points scored), {同点|どうてん} (a tie), {失点|しってん}, {点数|てんすう} |
| 最 | most | サイ | もっと(も) | 12 | {最高|さいこう}, {最大|さいだい}, {最低|さいてい}, {最初|さいしょ}, {最後|さいご}, {最近|さいきん}, {最|もっと}も |
| 達 | reach; skilled | タツ | | 12 | {上達|じょうたつ} (improvement), {達成|たっせい} (achievement), {配達|はいたつ} |

Carried words you can now write with kanji: {勝|か}つ, {負|ま}ける, {失敗|しっぱい} (with lesson 24's 失),
{野球|やきゅう}, {選|えら}ぶ, {選手|せんしゅ}, {点|てん}, {点数|てんすう}, {最低|さいてい}, {最初|さいしょ},
{最後|さいご}, {最近|さいきん}, {配達|はいたつ}, and {走|はし}る (N4's 走). One stays as it is: ともだち is
written {友達|ともだち} in full by many people, but this course keeps the established mixed spelling
{友|とも}だち, as N4 did.

Notes:

- 負 is ブ only in {勝負|しょうぶ} among N3 words; its usual on'yomi フ comes at N2.
- {敗|やぶ}れる (to be defeated) is a written word: {決勝|けっしょう}で{敗|やぶ}れた. In speech, {負|ま}ける.
  Don't confuse it with {破|やぶ}れる (to tear), lesson 29's kanji.
- 〜{位|い} counts places in a ranking: {一位|いちい}, {二位|にい}, {三位|さんい}. くらい (about) is a
  grammar word and stays in kana.
- {最|もっと}も is lesson 14's grammar word; {最|さい}〜 starts many compounds.
- 打 is ダ in {打者|だしゃ} (batter).

Memory notes (hooks, not etymology):

- 勝 and 敗: 勝 has the moon (月) and 力 (strength): you win with strength. 敗 has a shell (old
  money) on the left and a hand with a stick on the right: what you had is beaten out of you.
- 負: a person (the top part) on a shell (money): someone carrying a debt, losing.
- 戦 has a spear on the right, like 職 in lesson 11: fighting. 争 is two hands pulling a stick
  between them: a tug of war.
- 球: 王 (a jewel on the left) and 求 (to seek, lesson 8): a round jewel everyone wants, a ball.
- 投 and 打 both start with the hand radical (a hand drawn as three strokes): throwing and hitting are done by hand.
- 位: a person (the thin 人) standing (立) in their place: rank.
- 選 sits on the "moving" radical with two people on a stand: choosing who goes forward.
- 点 has four dots of fire at the bottom, like 熱 (lesson 3): points burned in to keep score.
- 最: the sun (日) over 取 (to take): taking the top place, the most.
- 達 has a sheep (with one extra stroke) sitting on the "moving" radical: the flock reaches where it's
  going.

```trace
勝負敗戦争球投打位選点最達
```

## Dialogue: after the tournament

Takumi and Nanami play table tennis in their company's club. They've just lost in the second
round of a city tournament. (Casual: club friends.)

```dialogue
# On the way home
たくみ: あーあ、{負|ま}けちゃったね。くやしいなあ。
= Oh well, we lost. That's so frustrating.
ななみ: {本当|ほんとう}に。{二回戦|にかいせん}の{相手|あいて}、{信|しん}じられないくらい{強|つよ}かったね。
= Really. The second-round team was unbelievably strong.
たくみ: うん。あまりにも{球|たま}が{速|はや}くて、{最初|さいしょ}は{見|み}えなかったよ。
= Yeah. The ball was so fast I couldn't even see it at first.
ななみ: {私|わたし}なんか、きんちょうのあまり、サーブを{三回|さんかい}も{失敗|しっぱい}しちゃった。
= As for me, I was so nervous I messed up my serve three times.
たくみ: でも{最後|さいご}の{試合|しあい}は{同点|どうてん}まで{行|い}ったじゃない。{去年|きょねん}は{一点|いってん}さえ{取|と}れなかったのに。
= But in the last game you got it to a tie. Last year you couldn't even get one point.
ななみ: そうだね。{少|すこ}しは{上達|じょうたつ}したのかな。
= That's true. Maybe I've improved a little.
たくみ: したよ。{毎週|まいしゅう}あれほど{練習|れんしゅう}してるんだから。
= You have. You've been practising that hard every week, after all.
ななみ: {来年|らいねん}こそ、せめて{三回戦|さんかいせん}までは{行|い}きたいな。
= Next year, for sure, I want to get to at least the third round.
たくみ: だいじょうぶ。ななみなら{行|い}けるよ。{練習|れんしゅう}さえ{続|つづ}ければね。
= You'll be fine. You can do it, as long as you keep practising.
ななみ: ありがとう。たくみくんこそ、{来年|らいねん}は{優勝|ゆうしょう}をねらってよ。
= Thanks. You're the one who should be aiming to win next year.
たくみ: {優勝|ゆうしょう}？ それは{夢|ゆめ}のまた{夢|ゆめ}だよ。
= Win? That's a dream beyond a dream.
ななみ: {夢|ゆめ}は{大|おお}きいほどいいでしょ。
= The bigger a dream is, the better, right?
```

くやしい = frustrated, gutted (its kanji is outside N3); {二回戦|にかいせん} / {三回戦|さんかいせん} = the
second / third round; サーブ = a serve; {私|わたし}なんか = as for me (modest, lesson 20); あれほど =
that much; だいじょうぶ = all right (one kanji is outside N3); ねらう = to aim for (its kanji is
outside N3); {夢|ゆめ}のまた{夢|ゆめ} = an impossible dream; {大|おお}きいほどいい = the bigger, the
better (lesson 4's ほど). Count the emphatic particles: さえ twice and こそ twice. Takumi's こそ in
たくみくんこそ is like こちらこそ: "you, rather than me".

## Reading: I started running at forty

An essay from a running club's newsletter, in the plain だ style of essays.

> {私|わたし}が{走|はし}り{始|はじ}めたのは、{四十歳|よんじゅっさい}のときだ。{健康|けんこう}のために{始|はじ}めたのだが、{最初|さいしょ}は{五分|ごふん}{走|はし}っただけで{息|いき}が{苦|くる}しくなるほどだった。{近所|きんじょ}の{公園|こうえん}を{一回|いっかい}{回|まわ}ることさえできなかった。
>
> それでも、{毎朝|まいあさ}{走|はし}る{時間|じかん}を{少|すこ}しずつ{長|なが}くしていった。{一年|いちねん}{後|ご}には、{一時間|いちじかん}{走|はし}っても{平気|へいき}なくらいになった。そこで、{初|はじ}めてマラソン{大会|たいかい}に{出|で}ることにした。
>
> {大会|たいかい}の{日|ひ}、{私|わたし}はきんちょうのあまり、{朝|あさ}ご{飯|はん}がほとんど{食|た}べられなかった。{三十|さんじゅっ}キロを{過|す}ぎると{足|あし}が{痛|いた}くて、{何度|なんど}もやめようと{思|おも}った。でも、{道|みち}の{両側|りょうがわ}から{知|し}らない{人|ひと}たちが「がんばれ！」とおうえんしてくれた。あの{声|こえ}があったからこそ、{最後|さいご}まで{走|はし}れたのだと{思|おも}う。
>
> {結果|けっか}は{五時間|ごじかん}{以上|いじょう}かかって、{一万人|いちまんにん}のうち{八千位|はっせんい}ぐらいだった。{速|はや}い{選手|せんしゅ}に{比|くら}べると、とても{遅|おそ}い。でも、{私|わたし}にとっては{最高|さいこう}の{一日|いちにち}だった。
>
> {今|いま}のもくひょうは、{五時間|ごじかん}を{切|き}ることだ。{若|わか}い{人|ひと}ほど{速|はや}くは{走|はし}れないが、せめて{去年|きょねん}の{自分|じぶん}には{勝|か}ちたい。{走|はし}るのが{好|す}きな{気持|きも}ちさえあれば、{年|とし}は{関係|かんけい}ないのだから。

{健康|けんこう} = health (lesson 5); {息|いき} = breath (lesson 5); {平気|へいき} = no trouble at all;
{過|す}ぎる = to pass (N4, lesson 25's kanji); がんばれ = the imperative of がんばる, "keep going!"
(N5); おうえんする = to cheer on (kanji outside N3); もくひょう = a goal (N4; one kanji is outside
N3); {五時間|ごじかん}を{切|き}る = to finish in under five hours; のだ = the written んだ (lesson 26).

<details>
<summary>Questions (answers inside)</summary>

1. How fit was the writer at the start? — Five minutes of running made breathing hard; the writer
   couldn't even run once round the local park.
2. Why couldn't the writer eat breakfast on race day? — Because of nerves (きんちょうのあまり).
3. What does the writer say made it possible to finish? — The cheering of strangers along both
   sides of the road; it was precisely because of their voices (あの{声|こえ}があったからこそ).
4. What is the writer's goal now, and what's the least the writer hopes for? — To finish in under
   five hours; at least to beat last year's self.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Translation</summary>

I started running when I was forty. I began for my health, but at first just five minutes of
running made my breathing so hard it hurt. I couldn't even get once round the park near my
home.

Even so, every morning I made my running time a little longer. A year later I'd got to the
point where running for an hour was no trouble. So I decided to enter a marathon for the first
time.

On the day, I was so nervous I could hardly eat breakfast. After thirty kilometres my legs hurt,
and many times I thought of giving up. But from both sides of the road, people I didn't know
shouted "Keep going!" to cheer me on. I think it was precisely because of those voices that I
could run to the end.

It took me over five hours, and I came about 8,000th out of 10,000 runners. Compared with fast
runners, that's very slow. But for me, it was the best day ever.

My goal now is to finish in under five hours. I can't run as fast as young people, but I want at
least to beat the me of last year. As long as you love running, age doesn't matter, after all.

</details>

## Say it

```speak
{今度|こんど}こそ{勝|か}ちたいです。
= This time I really want to win.
{練習|れんしゅう}さえすれば、{上達|じょうたつ:0}します。
= As long as you practise, you'll improve.
{水|みず}を{飲|の}む{時間|じかん}さえありませんでした。
= I didn't even have time to drink water.
{泣|な}きたいほど{痛|いた}かったです。
= It hurt so much I wanted to cry.
せめて{一回|いっかい}は{勝|か}ちたいです。
= I want to win at least once.
```

## Common mistakes

- ×{一回|いっかい}ほど{勝|か}ちたい for "at least once". The minimum is くらい: {一回|いっかい}くらい
  {勝|か}ちたい (or せめて{一回|いっかい}は).
- {水|みず}をさえ{飲|の}まなかった sounds old-fashioned. さえ usually replaces を and が: {水|みず}さえ{飲|の}まなかった.
- ×{練習|れんしゅう}をすればさえ. さえ goes before the conditional: {練習|れんしゅう}さえすれば.
- ×せめて{三百人|さんびゃくにん}{来|き}た. せめて is for wishes; for facts, {少|すく}なくとも.
- Spelling: ほど and くらい are grammar words in kana; 〜{位|い} is a rank.

## Key points

- 〜ほど / 〜くらい (ぐらい): degree, "so … that" ({泣|な}きたいほど, {信|しん}じられないくらい).
  Only くらい marks a minimum: {一回|いっかい}くらい, そのくらい.
- 〜さえ (でさえ for subjects): even, an extreme example; さえ replaces が and を.
- 〜さえ〜ば: as long as ({練習|れんしゅう}さえすれば, {天気|てんき}さえよければ, {笑|わら}ってさえいれば).
- 〜こそ: this very one ({今度|こんど}こそ, こちらこそ); 〜からこそ: precisely because.
- あまりにも + adjective: far too; noun + のあまり / verb + あまり: so (nervous, happy…) that.
- せめて: at least, the minimum you hope for; for facts, {少|すく}なくとも.
- さえ and こそ are emphatic particles.
- New kanji: 勝 負 敗 戦 争 球 投 打 位 選 点 最 達.

The reference sheet "Degree and emphasis" has these side by side. The words from this lesson are
listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete the lesson.
