lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Lesson 17 sorted what you're sure of. This lesson is for what you aren't: supposing something is
true, guessing that it might be, refusing to believe it could be, and putting forward a careful
suspicion. These are the words of detective stories and of the news, so the theme is crime: theft
and fraud, police and investigations, suspects, witnesses and the courts.

{彼|かれ}の{話|はなし}が{本当|ほんとう}だとしたら、{犯人|はんにん}はほかにいる。 — If what he says is true, the
culprit is someone else.
もしかしたら、{犯人|はんにん}はまだ{近|ちか}くにいるかもしれない。 — The culprit may still be nearby.
まさか{彼|かれ}がそんなことをするとは{思|おも}わなかった。 — I never imagined he'd do such a thing.
{犯人|はんにん}は{家|いえ}の{中|なか}の{人|ひと}なのではないか。 — Could the culprit be someone in the house?

## Supposing: 〜としたら, 〜とすれば, 〜とすると

These three put forward a **[[hypothetical]]**: a situation you suppose for the sake of argument,
without saying it's true. "Supposing that…, if it's true that…, if we say that…". They follow the
plain form; nouns and な-adjectives take だ.

| Before としたら | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| verb | {留学|りゅうがく}するとしたら | supposing I study abroad |
| verb (past) | {彼|かれ}が{見|み}たとしたら | if he did see it |
| い-adjective | そんなに{高|たか}いとしたら | if it's really that expensive |
| noun / な-adj + だ | {本当|ほんとう}だとしたら, {犯人|はんにん}が{彼|かれ}だとしたら | if it's true; if he's the culprit |

もし{百万円|ひゃくまんえん}あったとしたら、{何|なに}をしますか。 — Supposing you had a million yen, what
would you do?
その{話|はなし}が{本当|ほんとう}だとしたら、{大変|たいへん}なことだ。 — If that story's true, it's serious.
{犯行|はんこう}が{夜|よる}{十時|じゅうじ}だとすれば、{彼|かれ}にはアリバイがある。 — If the crime was at ten at
night, he has an alibi. (アリバイ: alibi.)

### Which one?

- としたら is the everyday one, common in speech.
- とすれば sounds more logical, a step in an argument: "if A, then it follows that B". It's
  common in writing and explanations.
- とすると is similar, and also stands at the start of a sentence as "in that case, then":
  {犯人|はんにん}は{窓|まど}から{入|はい}った。とすると、{窓|まど}は{開|あ}いていたはずだ (The culprit came in
  through the window. In that case, the window must have been open).

### としたら or たら?

N4's たら is for real conditions, including things that will surely happen: {駅|えき}に{着|つ}いたら
{電話|でんわ}してください. としたら is only for suppositions, so it doesn't fit plain arrangements:
×{駅|えき}に{着|つ}いたとしたら{電話|でんわ}してください sounds as if arriving were in doubt. In return,
としたら makes the unreal or unconfirmed clear: たからくじが{当|あ}たったとしたら (supposing I won
the lottery). The second half is usually a judgment, a feeling or a question (どうする？,
{怖|こわ}い, 〜だろう), less often a request.

## Maybe: もしかしたら, もしかすると, もしかして

A guess you make without full evidence is a **[[conjecture]]**. Japanese marks a weak one with
もしかしたら (perhaps, possibly) at the start and かもしれない at the end.

もしかしたら、{明日|あした}は{雪|ゆき}になるかもしれない。 — It might even snow tomorrow.
もしかすると、{彼|かれ}は{何|なに}か{知|し}っているのかもしれない。 — It's possible he knows something.

- もしかすると is a little more formal than もしかしたら; the meaning is the same.
- もしかして is used mostly in questions and in guesses you say to someone: "by any chance,
  could it be that…?"

もしかして、{山田|やまだ}さんですか。 — Are you Mr Yamada, by any chance?
もしかして、{怒|おこ}ってる？ — You're not angry, are you?

## Surely not: まさか

まさか expresses disbelief: the speaker didn't think, or doesn't want to think, that something
could be so. It has several patterns:

| Pattern | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| まさか〜とは{思|おも}わなかった | まさか{彼|かれ}が{犯人|はんにん}だとは{思|おも}わなかった | I never imagined he was the culprit |
| まさか〜ないだろう / 〜ないよね | まさか{忘|わす}れていないよね？ | You haven't forgotten, surely? |
| まさか〜？ (fearing it) | まさか、もう{全部|ぜんぶ}{食|た}べちゃった？ | Don't tell me you've eaten it all already? |
| まさか！ on its own | 「たからくじが{当|あ}たった」「まさか！」 | "I won the lottery." "No way!" |

まさか{自分|じぶん}がさぎにあうとは{思|おも}ってもいなかった。 — I never dreamed I'd be the one taken
in by a scam.

In news and sport you'll also see まさかの + noun: まさかの{結果|けっか} (an unbelievable result).

## Can't be, no way: はずがない, わけがない, まさか

Three ways to deny a possibility, from three different angles:

| | はずがない (N4) | わけがない (lesson 7) | まさか |
|---|---|---|---|
| What it is | a conclusion from facts | an emphatic "no way" | a reaction of disbelief |
| Feeling | calm, logical | emotional, often about yourself | surprise, shock |
| Example | かぎをかけたから、{開|あ}いているはずがない (I locked it, so it can't be open) | あんな{人|ひと}を{好|す}きになるわけがない (as if I'd fall for someone like that) | まさか、{開|あ}いてる？ (don't tell me it's open?) |

Only まさか can stand on its own as a reaction: 「{犯人|はんにん}は{田中|たなか}さんだって」「まさか！」 ("They say
Tanaka did it." "No way!"). はずがない and わけがない need a sentence in front of them. Between those
two, the difference is feeling more than meaning, and they often overlap. When you reject an idea
about yourself, わけがない is the usual, emotional choice: {私|わたし}がそんな{人|ひと}と{結婚|けっこん}するわけが
ないでしょう (As if I'd marry someone like that!). はずがない sounds like a reasoned conclusion:
{私|わたし}がそんなことを{言|い}うはずがない (I can't have said that: it's not something I'd say). The
three also combine: まさか{彼|かれ}が{犯人|はんにん}のはずがない (surely he can't be the culprit).

## A careful suspicion: 〜のではないか, 〜のではないだろうか

〜のではないか (casual 〜んじゃないか, 〜んじゃない？) puts forward a view softly: "isn't it the case
that…, I suspect that…". It's gentler than と{思|おも}う and leaves room for the listener. Plain form +
のではないか; な-adjectives and nouns take な.

| Before のではないか | Example |
|---|---|
| verb | {犯人|はんにん}はもう{逃|に}げたのではないか |
| い-adjective | {少|すこ}し{高|たか}いのではないか |
| な-adjective + な | この{方法|ほうほう}のほうが{安全|あんぜん}なのではないか |
| noun + な | {彼|かれ}が{犯人|はんにん}なのではないか |

〜のではないだろうか (and polite 〜のではないでしょうか) is softer still, and common in writing and
news commentary; lesson 26 comes back to it.

{警察|けいさつ}は、{犯人|はんにん}は{近所|きんじょ}の{人|ひと}なのではないかとみている。 — The police suspect that the
culprit is someone from the neighbourhood.
{何|なに}か{事情|じじょう}があったのではないでしょうか。 — Perhaps there was some reason behind it?
それ、ちょっと{高|たか}すぎるんじゃない？ — Isn't that a bit too expensive?

Keep the の: without it, 〜ではないか can be a different thing, a strong "isn't it!" or a
reproach (ちゃんと{言|い}ったではないか: I told you, didn't I!).

## What on earth: いったい

いったい goes with a question word and adds force: "what on earth, who in the world". The
sentence often ends in んだろう or のか. (With kanji it's {一体|いったい}; kana is common.)

いったいだれがこんなことをしたんだろう。 — Who on earth could have done this?
いったい{何|なに}があったんですか。 — What in the world happened?
いったいどうして{彼|かれ}はうそをついたのか。 — Why on earth did he lie?

Readings to watch:

- 逃 has a second kun reading, のが(す), in チャンスを{逃|のが}す (to miss a chance). に(がす) is to let
  something go.
- 捕 is also と(る) in some words, but at N3 it's つか(まえる) and つか(まる).
- 盗 and 逃 are both トウ; 察 and 殺 are both サツ. Context and the other kanji tell them apart.
- {行方|ゆくえ} is a special reading: ゆく (going) + え (direction).

Memory notes (hooks, not etymology):

- 犯: an animal (the radical 犭 on the left) next to a crouching person: acting like a beast.
- 罪: a net (the top part) over 非 (wrong, lesson 9): a wrong you get caught for.
- 殺: a tree with a cross (the left side) and a hand holding a weapon (the right side).
- 盗: a bowl at the bottom, with water dripping beside an open mouth above: someone drooling
  over a bowl that isn't theirs.
- 件: a person (亻) and 牛 (cow): one cow per person, a single item, one case.
- 警: a sign for respect over 言 (words): respectful words that warn you to take care.
- 察: under a roof (宀) and a ritual: looking carefully into things.
- 捕: a hand (扌) grabbing: catch.
- 追 and 逃 both have the road radical (辶): one runs after, one runs away.
- 探: a hand (扌) reaching into a hole: searching.
- 疑: 14 strokes of someone stopped at a crossroads, not sure which way to go.

## Dialogue: a burglary in the street

Two neighbours, Ms Kobayashi and Mr Yamamoto, talk outside their houses. Polite, as neighbours
usually are.

```dialogue
# Did you hear?
こばやし: {山本|やまもと}さん、{聞|き}きました？{駅|えき}の{近|ちか}くの{家|いえ}にどろぼうが{入|はい}ったそうですよ。
= Mr Yamamoto, have you heard? Apparently a house near the station was burgled.
やまもと: ええっ、まさか。あの{静|しず}かな{通|とお}りで？
= What? You're joking. On that quiet street?
こばやし: ええ。{昼間|ひるま}、{家|いえ}の{人|ひと}が{出|で}かけている{間|あいだ}に、{窓|まど}を{割|わ}られたらしいんです。
= Yes. During the day, while the family were out, someone broke a window, it seems.
やまもと: {昼間|ひるま}に？いったいだれがそんなことを…。
= In broad daylight? Who on earth would do that...
こばやし: {最近|さいきん}、{知|し}らない{車|くるま}がよく{止|と}まっていましたよね。もしかしたら、あの{車|くるま}の{人|ひと}かもしれません。
= There's often been a car we don't know parked round here lately. Maybe it's the person in that car.
やまもと: でも、しょうこもないのに{疑|うたが}うのはよくないですよ。{工事|こうじ}の{人|ひと}だったのではないでしょうか。
= But it's not right to suspect someone without any evidence. Couldn't it have been the builders?
こばやし: そうですね。{警察|けいさつ}も、まだ{何|なに}も{分|わ}かっていないようです。
= You're right. The police don't seem to know anything yet either.
やまもと: {犯人|はんにん}がこの{近|ちか}くに{住|す}んでいるとしたら、{怖|こわ}いですね。
= If the burglar lives near here, that's frightening.
こばやし: まさか。そんなはずはないと{思|おも}いますけど…。
= Oh, surely not. I don't think that can be so...
やまもと: うちも{今夜|こんや}から、ちゃんとかぎをかけることにします。
= From tonight we'll make sure we lock up properly too.
こばやし: それがいいですよ。あやしい{人|ひと}を{見|み}たら、すぐ{通報|つうほう}しましょう。
= Good idea. If we see anyone suspicious, let's report it straight away.
やまもと: ええ。それにしても、ぼうはんカメラがあればよかったのに。
= Yes. All the same, if only there'd been a security camera.
```

{昼間|ひるま} = daytime; {割|わ}る = to break
(glass); {止|と}まる = to be parked, stopped; {工事|こうじ} = building work; 〜ことにする = decide to (N4);
〜ばよかったのに: lesson 18.

## Reading: bicycle thefts at the station

A short article from a local newspaper's website, in the plain だ style of news writing.

> {今月|こんげつ}に{入|はい}ってから、{南駅|みなみえき}の{前|まえ}の{自転車|じてんしゃ}{置|お}き{場|ば}で、{自転車|じてんしゃ}の{盗難|とうなん}が{続|つづ}いている。{警察|けいさつ}によると、{十日間|とおかかん}で{十二件|じゅうにけん}。どれも{夜|よる}{九時|くじ}から{十一時|じゅういちじ}の{間|あいだ}に{起|お}きている。
>
> ひがいにあった{自転車|じてんしゃ}の{多|おお}くには、かぎがかかっていた。{警察|けいさつ}は、{同|おな}じ{人物|じんぶつ}かグループが{道具|どうぐ}でかぎをこわして{盗|ぬす}んだのではないかとみている。{置|お}き{場|ば}にはぼうはんカメラがあるが、{犯人|はんにん}は{顔|かお}をかくしていたという。{中|なか}には、{買|か}ったばかりの{新|あたら}しい{自転車|じてんしゃ}もあったそうだ。
>
> {近|ちか}くの{店|みせ}の{人|ひと}は「まさかこの{町|まち}でこんな{事件|じけん}が{起|お}きるとは{思|おも}わなかった。{犯人|はんにん}が{近所|きんじょ}の{人|ひと}だとしたら、{怖|こわ}い」と{話|はな}す。また、もくげきしゃの{一人|ひとり}は「{夜|よる}、{黒|くろ}っぽい{服|ふく}の{男|おとこ}が{自転車|じてんしゃ}を{運|はこ}んでいるのを{見|み}た。もしかしたら、あれが{犯人|はんにん}だったのかもしれない」と{言|い}う。
>
> {警察|けいさつ}は、{盗|ぬす}まれた{自転車|じてんしゃ}がインターネットで{売|う}られているのではないかと{考|かんが}えて、{調|しら}べている。そして、{自転車|じてんしゃ}にはかぎを{二|ふた}つかけること、{夜|よる}はなるべく{明|あか}るい{場所|ばしょ}に{止|と}めることを{呼|よ}びかけている。{今後|こんご}は、{夜|よる}の{見回|みまわ}りも{増|ふ}やすという。

{自転車|じてんしゃ}{置|お}き{場|ば} = bicycle parking (lesson 27); {人物|じんぶつ} = person, figure; こわす = to
break (N4); 〜という = it's said, reportedly; 〜とみている = (the police) believe, suspect; なるべく =
as far as possible (lesson 5); {呼|よ}びかける = to call on, urge.

<details>
<summary>Questions (answers inside)</summary>

1. When do the thefts happen? — Between nine and eleven at night.
2. What do the police suspect? — That one person or group broke the locks with a tool
   (〜のではないかとみている), and that the bikes are being sold online.
3. Why didn't the security camera help? — The culprit had hidden his face.
4. How sure is the witness that the man was the thief? — Not sure at all: もしかしたら…
   かもしれない is only a possibility.
5. What do the police advise? — Use two locks, and park in a well-lit place at night where
   possible.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Translation</summary>

Since the start of the month there has been a string of bicycle thefts at the bicycle parking in
front of Minami Station. According to the police, there have been twelve in ten days, all of them
between nine and eleven at night.

Most of the stolen bikes were locked. The police believe the same person or group broke the locks
with a tool and stole them. The parking has a security camera, but the culprit is said to have
hidden his face. Some of the bikes were brand new.

A shopkeeper nearby says, "I never imagined something like this would happen in this town. If
the thief is someone from the neighbourhood, that's frightening." One witness says, "At night I
saw a man in dark clothes carrying a bike. Maybe that was the thief."

The police are investigating whether the stolen bikes are being sold on the internet. They are
urging people to put two locks on their bikes and, at night, to park them in well-lit places
where possible. From now on they will also patrol more at night.

</details>

## Pronunciation

- [まさか:1] falls after the first mora: ま\さか. Said alone in surprise, it's often drawn out:
  まさかー！
- [もしかしたら:1] also falls right after も. In normal speech the し is whispered (said without
  voice), so it can sound like もsかしたら.
- {逃|に}がす / {逃|に}げる and {盗難|とうなん} / {逃走|とうそう}: とう is two morae, a long お sound.
- いったい has a small っ: い・っ・た・い, four morae, flat: [いったい:0].
- {警察官|けいさつかん:4} has six morae: け・い・さ・つ・か・ん. The けい is a long え in normal speech.

```speak
それが{本当|ほんとう}だとしたら、{大変|たいへん}ですね。
= If that's true, it's serious.
もしかしたら、{彼|かれ}は{何|なに}か{知|し}っているかもしれない。
= Maybe he knows something.
まさか{彼|かれ}が{犯人|はんにん}だとは{思|おも}わなかった。
= I never imagined he was the culprit.
{何|なに}か{事情|じじょう}があったのではないでしょうか。
= Perhaps there was some reason behind it?
いったい{何|なに}があったんですか。
= What on earth happened?
あやしい{人|ひと}を{見|み}たら、{警察|けいさつ}に{通報|つうほう}してください。
= If you see anyone suspicious, please report it to the police.
```

## Common mistakes

- Using としたら for plain arrangements: ×{家|いえ}に{帰|かえ}ったとしたら、メールして. It's
  {帰|かえ}ったら.
- Forgetting だ after a noun: ×{犯人|はんにん}としたら. It's {犯人|はんにん}だとしたら (noun + としたら without だ is a different use,
  "from the standpoint of": {私|わたし}としたら, as far as I'm concerned).
- Dropping の in のではないか: {彼|かれ}が{犯人|はんにん}なのではないか, with な after the noun.
- Using もしかしたら with a certain ending: ×もしかしたら{必|かなら}ず{来|く}る. It goes with
  かもしれない or another weak guess.
- Using まさか for "of course": it means the opposite, "no way, surely not".

## Key points

- A **[[hypothetical]]** is a supposed situation. 〜としたら / 〜とすれば / 〜とすると (noun, な-adj + だ):
  supposing, if it's true that. たら is for real conditions.
- A **[[conjecture]]** is a guess. もしかしたら / もしかすると…かもしれない: perhaps; もしかして: by any
  chance (questions).
- まさか: surely not, I never imagined (〜とは{思|おも}わなかった, 〜ないだろう, まさか！).
- はずがない (a reasoned "can't be"), わけがない (an emphatic "no way"), まさか (disbelief; can stand
  alone).
- 〜のではないか / 〜のではないだろうか / 〜んじゃない？: a soft suspicion (noun, な-adj + な).
- いったい + question word: what on earth.
- New kanji: 犯 罪 警 察 盗 逃 捕 殺 件 疑 官 追 探.

lessons.title: Not only…, and how!: だけでなく, ばかりか, はもちろん, 上に, ことか, なんて
topics: だけでなく and ばかりか
はもちろん and 上に
なんて and なんか
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

The last core lesson of the module is about emphasis: adding one point on top of another ("not
only…but also", "on top of that", "not to mention"), saying how strongly you feel ("how often I
cried!"), and showing surprise or scorn with a single word (なんて, なんか).

These are the words people use when they talk about something they love or can't stand, so the
theme is entertainment and the arts: films, music, books and manga, theatre, TV and radio,
painting and museums.

この{映画|えいが}は{子供|こども}だけでなく、{大人|おとな}も{楽|たの}しめる。 — Not only children but adults
can enjoy this film too.
{彼|かれ}は{歌|うた}がうまいばかりか、{作曲|さっきょく}もする。 — Not only is he a good singer, he even
writes songs.
{最終回|さいしゅうかい}を{見|み}て、どれだけ{泣|な}いたことか。 — How I cried at the final episode!
{彼|かれ}が{舞台|ぶたい}に{立|た}つなんて、{信|しん}じられない。 — I can't believe he's going on stage.

## Not only…but also: 〜だけでなく, 〜ばかりでなく

A + だけでなく + B + も: "not only A, but B too". In casual speech, だけじゃなく(て).
ばかりでなく means the same and is a little more formal.

| Before だけでなく | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| noun | {音楽|おんがく}だけでなく | not only music |
| verb | {歌|うた}うだけでなく | not only sings |
| い-adjective | {面白|おもしろ}いだけでなく | not only interesting |
| な-adjective + な | {有名|ゆうめい}なだけでなく | not only famous |

この{美術館|びじゅつかん}には、{絵画|かいが}だけでなく{写真|しゃしん}もある。 — This museum has photographs as
well as paintings.
あの{女優|じょゆう}は{演|えん}じるだけでなく、{映画|えいが}も{作|つく}っている。 — That actress doesn't just
act; she makes films too.
この{本|ほん}は{面白|おもしろ}いばかりでなく、{勉強|べんきょう}にもなる。 — This book isn't only fun, it's
educational too.

## Not only, but even: 〜ばかりか

〜ばかりか also means "not only…", but it builds up to something more surprising or more extreme
in the second half, often with まで, さえ or も: "not only A, but even B".

{彼|かれ}は{歌|うた}がうまいばかりか、{自分|じぶん}で{曲|きょく}まで{作|つく}る。 — Not only does he sing
well, he even writes his own songs.
その{映画|えいが}は{日本|にほん}ばかりか、{海外|かいがい}でも{話題|わだい}になった。 — The film became a
talking point not only in Japan but abroad too.
{彼|かれ}は{約束|やくそく}を{忘|わす}れたばかりか、もんくまで{言|い}った。 — Not only did he forget
the appointment, he even complained.

Because ばかりか states a fact and reacts to it, the second half isn't a request, an invitation
or your own plan: ×{歌|うた}うばかりか、おどってください. Use だけでなく there:
{歌|うた}だけでなく、ダンスも{見|み}せてください.

## Not to mention: 〜はもちろん

A + はもちろん、B + も: "B too, and A goes without saying". A is the obvious case; B is the
one worth pointing out.

このアニメは{子供|こども}はもちろん、{大人|おとな}にも{人気|にんき}がある。 — This anime is popular with
adults, not to mention children.
{彼女|かのじょ}は{日本|にほん}はもちろん、アジアの{国|くに}でも{知|し}られている。 — She's known in other Asian
countries too, not to mention Japan.

## On top of that: 〜{上|うえ}(に)

〜{上|うえ}(に) adds a second point in the same direction: good on top of good, bad on top of bad.

| Before {上|うえ}に | Example |
|---|---|
| verb | {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}っている{上|うえ}に |
| い-adjective | {安|やす}い{上|うえ}に |
| な-adjective + な | {便利|べんり}な{上|うえ}に |
| noun + の / である | {学生|がくせい}の{上|うえ}に, {学生|がくせい}である{上|うえ}に |

このホールは{駅|えき}から{近|ちか}い{上|うえ}に、{席|せき}も{広|ひろ}い。 — This hall is close to the
station, and on top of that the seats are roomy.
{昨日|きのう}は{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}っていた{上|うえ}に、{電車|でんしゃ}も{遅|おく}れた。 — Yesterday it was raining, and
the trains were late on top of it.

If the two points go in opposite directions, use のに or けど: {安|やす}いのに、まずい (cheap, but
bad), not ×{安|やす}い{上|うえ}に、まずい.

## Both… and: 〜も〜ば〜も, 〜も〜し〜も

To give two features side by side, Japanese can repeat も with a ば form (or なら) in the first
half:

{彼女|かのじょ}は{歌|うた}もうまければ、ダンスも{上手|じょうず}だ。 — She sings well, and she dances well too.
この{店|みせ}は{値段|ねだん}も{高|たか}ければ、{店員|てんいん}のたいども{悪|わる}い。 — This shop is expensive, and
the staff are rude too.
{好|す}きな{人|ひと}もいれば、{苦手|にがて}な{人|ひと}もいる。 — Some people like it, some don't.

The last one is a common pattern of its own: 〜もいれば〜もいる (some…, others…). The casual
version uses N4's し: {歌|うた}もうまいし、ダンスも{上手|じょうず}だ.

## How…!: 〜ことか

A question word (どんなに, どれほど, どれだけ, {何度|なんど}) + plain form + ことか turns a sentence
into an exclamation: "how (much)…!, how many times…!". It's emotional and a little literary:
common in writing, songs and heartfelt speech.

{合格|ごうかく}の{知|し}らせを{聞|き}いて、どんなにうれしかったことか。 — How happy I was when I heard I'd
passed!
この{曲|きょく}に{何度|なんど}{助|たす}けられたことか。 — How many times this song has helped me!
{彼|かれ}が{来|く}るのを、どれだけ{待|ま}ったことか。 — How long I waited for him to come!

A な-adjective takes な: どんなに{静|しず}かなことか (how quiet it is!). Don't confuse it with a real
question ending in ことか: here no answer is expected.

## Surprise and scorn: 〜なんて, 〜なんか

### なんて

なんて has several jobs, all with feeling:

| Use | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| after a noun: belittling | {宿題|しゅくだい}なんてやりたくない | homework? I don't want to do it |
| after a clause: surprise | {彼|かれ}が{歌手|かしゅ}になるなんて！ | I can't believe he's going to be a singer! |
| quoting (= などと) | 「やめる」なんて{言|い}わないで | don't say things like "I'll quit" |
| before an adjective: how… | なんてきれいな{絵|え}だろう | what a beautiful picture! |

{一日|いちにち}で{全部|ぜんぶ}{読|よ}んだなんて、すごいね。 — You read it all in one day? That's amazing.

### なんか

なんか is casual など. After a noun it can be modest, dismissive or a soft suggestion:

{私|わたし}なんか、まだまだです。 — Someone like me still has a long way to go.
ホラー{映画|えいが}なんか、{見|み}たくない。 — Horror films? I don't want to see them.
お{茶|ちゃ}なんかどう？ — How about some tea or something?

On its own at the start of a sentence, なんか is the filler you met in lesson 5h1 ("kind of,
somehow"): なんか、{変|へん}だね.

> **Review (N4).** 〜など lists examples ("such as, and so on"):
> {映画|えいが}や{音楽|おんがく}などが{好|す}きです. Polite and neutral; なんか is its casual form.

## Entertainment and the arts

### Stage, screen and radio

| Word | Meaning | Word | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| {舞台|ぶたい} | stage | {公演|こうえん} | performance, show |
| えんげき | theatre, plays | ミュージカル | musical |
| {演|えん}じる | to act, play (a role) | {出演|しゅつえん}する | to appear (in) |
| {主役|しゅやく} | lead role | {主人公|しゅじんこう} | main character |
| はいゆう, {女優|じょゆう}, {声優|せいゆう} | actor, actress, voice actor | {演出|えんしゅつ} | direction, staging |
| {観客|かんきゃく} | audience | はくしゅ | applause |
| {放送|ほうそう}, {生放送|なまほうそう}, {再放送|さいほうそう} | broadcast; live; rerun | {放送局|ほうそうきょく} | broadcaster |
| {最終回|さいしゅうかい} | final episode | {続|つづ}き | continuation, next part |
| ふきかえ | dubbing | {番|ばん} | (one's) turn |

### Music

{曲|きょく} (a piece, a song), {名曲|めいきょく} (a classic), {新曲|しんきょく} (a new song), {主題歌|しゅだいか}
(theme song), かし (lyrics), {作曲|さっきょく}する and {作曲家|さっきょくか} (compose; composer), えんそう
(performance), ライブ (gig), {演歌|えんか} (enka ballads), {鳴|な}る (to ring, sound) and {鳴|な}く (of
birds and animals: sing, call).

### Pictures, books and stories

{絵画|かいが} (painting), {名画|めいが} (a famous painting), {美術|びじゅつ} (fine art), {画家|がか} (painter),
{絵|え}の{具|ぐ} (paints), てんらんかい and てんじ (exhibition; display), げいじゅつ (art), {作家|さっか}
and {作者|さくしゃ} (writer; author of a work), {読者|どくしゃ} (reader), {物語|ものがたり} (story),
{絵本|えほん} (picture book), {名作|めいさく} (classic), {原作|げんさく} (the original work), {結末|けつまつ}
(ending), {王様|おうさま}, {王子|おうじ}, {女王|じょおう} (king, prince, queen), {感想|かんそう} (what you
thought of it), かんしょう (enjoying art, films, music), {面|めん} (aspect: {音楽|おんがく}の{面|めん}で),
{優|すぐ}れる (to excel), {浮|う}かぶ, {浮|う}く, {思|おも}い{浮|う}かべる (to float; to come to mind; to
picture), {舞|ま}う (to dance, flutter).

## Kanji

Thirteen kanji for the arts and the stage.

### The stage and the screen

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 演 | perform | エン | | 14 | {演|えん}じる, {公演|こうえん}, {出演|しゅつえん}, {演歌|えんか} |
| 舞 | dance | ブ | ま(う) | 15 | {舞|ま}う, {舞台|ぶたい} |
| 放 | release | ホウ | はな(す) | 8 | {放送|ほうそう}, {放|はな}す (let go) |
| 組 | group; put together | | くみ (ぐみ) | 11 | {番組|ばんぐみ}, {組|くみ} (class, group) |
| 番 | number; turn | バン | | 12 | {番|ばん}, {番号|ばんごう}, {番組|ばんぐみ}, {一番|いちばん}, {交番|こうばん} |
| 優 | gentle; excellent | ユウ | やさ(しい), すぐ(れる) | 17 | {優|やさ}しい, {優|すぐ}れる, {女優|じょゆう}, {声優|せいゆう} |

### Music and pictures

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 曲 | bend; tune | キョク | ま(がる), ま(げる) | 6 | {曲|きょく}, {名曲|めいきょく}, {曲|ま}がる |
| 絵 | picture | カイ, エ | | 12 | {絵|え}, {絵本|えほん}, {絵画|かいが} |
| 鳴 | cry, ring | メイ | な(く), な(る) | 14 | {鳴|な}く, {鳴|な}る |
| 想 | idea, think | ソウ | | 13 | {感想|かんそう}, {理想|りそう} |

### Stories

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 王 | king | オウ | | 4 | {王様|おうさま}, {王子|おうじ}, {女王|じょおう} |
| 面 | face, surface | メン | おも | 9 | {面|めん}, {画面|がめん}, {面白|おもしろ}い, {真面目|まじめ} |
| 浮 | float | フ | う(く), う(かぶ), う(かべる) | 10 | {浮|う}く, {浮|う}かぶ, {思|おも}い{浮|う}かべる |

Carried words you can now write with kanji: {絵|え}, {番組|ばんぐみ}, {番号|ばんごう}, {電話番号|でんわばんごう},
{一番|いちばん}, {交番|こうばん}, {留守番|るすばん}, {曲|ま}がる, {面白|おもしろ}い, {画面|がめん}, {面倒|めんどう},
{優|やさ}しい (kind) and {真面目|まじめ}.

Readings to watch:

- {真面目|まじめ} is a special reading: the three kanji (true, face, eye) are read as one word,
  まじめ. Learn it whole.
- 絵 is カイ in {絵画|かいが} and エ on its own: え is in fact an on'yomi, though it feels native.
- 優 has two kun readings: やさ(しい), kind (not {易|やさ}しい, easy: lesson 18), and すぐ(れる), to
  excel.
- 組 is くみ on its own and in school class names ({三年二組|さんねんにくみ}: year 3, class 2), but
  ぐみ in {番組|ばんぐみ}.
- 鳴 is な(く) for animals and な(る) for bells and phones. People cry with {泣|な}く (lesson 10).
- 王 becomes おう in {女王|じょおう} (not じょうおう).

Memory notes (hooks, not etymology):

- 演: water (氵) flowing on and on: a long performance.
- 舞: a dancer with sleeves spread out at the top and feet stepping at the bottom.
- 放: a hand with a stick (the right side) driving something away: let go.
- 組: the thread radical on the left and a pile (the right side): threads plaited together.
- 番: a field (田) at the bottom with seeds scattered above: fields tended in turns.
- 優: a person (亻) beside a figure bowed with worry: someone who feels others' worries is kind.
- 曲: a bent frame with two posts: something bent.
- 絵: the thread radical and 会 (meet): threads meeting in a picture, as in embroidery.
- 鳴: a mouth (口) and a bird (鳥): a bird's call.
- 想: 相 (mutual, lesson 22) over 心 (heart): thinking about each other.
- 王: three lines (heaven, people, earth) joined by one stroke: the king connects them.
- 面: a face seen from the front, with the nose in the middle.
- 浮: water (氵) and a hand holding a child: keeping it afloat.

## Dialogue: after the musical

Haruto and Nana come out of a theatre after seeing a musical. Casual, excited speech.

```dialogue
# Coming out of the theatre
なな: どうだった？
= So, what did you think?
はると: すごかった！{歌|うた}だけじゃなく、ダンスもレベルが{高|たか}かったね。
= It was amazing! Not just the singing, the dancing was really high level too.
なな: でしょう？{主役|しゅやく}の{人|ひと}、{歌|うた}がうまいばかりか、{作曲|さっきょく}もするんだって。
= Right? The lead apparently doesn't just sing well, he writes music too.
はると: ほんとう？{演|えん}じるのも{上手|じょうず}だし、{顔|かお}もかっこいいし。
= Really? He's a good actor, and he's good-looking too.
なな: しかも、{去年|きょねん}までふつうの{会社員|かいしゃいん}だったらしいよ。
= What's more, apparently he was an ordinary office worker until last year.
はると: えっ、{会社員|かいしゃいん}だった{人|ひと}があんな{舞台|ぶたい}に{立|た}つなんて！
= What? Someone who was an office worker, up on a stage like that!
なな: {最後|さいご}の{曲|きょく}、{聞|き}いてて{何度|なんど}{泣|な}きそうになったことか。
= The last song... I can't tell you how many times I nearly cried listening to it.
はると: ぼくなんか、もう{泣|な}いてたよ。
= Me, I was already crying.
なな: このホール、{駅|えき}から{近|ちか}い{上|うえ}に、{席|せき}も{見|み}やすいね。また{来|こ}よう。
= This hall's close to the station, and the seats give a good view too. Let's come again.
はると: うん。{次|つぎ}はぼくがチケットを{取|と}る{番|ばん}だね。
= Yeah. Next time it's my turn to get the tickets.
なな: じゃあ、{原作|げんさく}の{小説|しょうせつ}も{読|よ}んでおこうかな。
= Then maybe I'll read the original novel first.
はると: {小説|しょうせつ}なんて、{何年|なんねん}も{読|よ}んでないなあ。
= Novels... I haven't read one in years.
```

でしょう？ = right? (with rising intonation); 〜んだって = I hear (lesson 22); しかも = what's more
(lesson 28); ふつう = ordinary (N4); {会社員|かいしゃいん} = office worker (N5); {聞|き}いてて =
{聞|き}いていて; ぼく: "I" for men, in kana.

## Reading: a film review

A post on a film fan's blog, in the plain だ style of blogs.

> {昨日|きのう}、{話題|わだい}の{映画|えいが}「ほしの{王子|おうじ}」を{見|み}てきた。{原作|げんさく}は{子供|こども}{向|む}けの{絵本|えほん}だが、{映画|えいが}は{子供|こども}はもちろん、{大人|おとな}も{十分|じゅうぶん}{楽|たの}しめる。{始|はじ}まってから{一|いっ}か{月|げつ}で、もう{百万人|ひゃくまんにん}が{見|み}たそうだ。
>
> {主人公|しゅじんこう}は、{小|ちい}さなほしに{一人|ひとり}で{住|す}む{王子|おうじ}だ。ある{日|ひ}、{空|そら}に{浮|う}かぶ{不思議|ふしぎ}な{鳥|とり}に{出会|であ}い、{一緒|いっしょ}に{旅|たび}に{出|で}る。{王子|おうじ}の{声|こえ}を{演|えん}じたのは、まだ{十二歳|じゅうにさい}の{少年|しょうねん}だ。{彼|かれ}は{演|えん}じるのがうまいばかりか、{主題歌|しゅだいか}まで{自分|じぶん}で{歌|うた}っている。{声|こえ}がきれいな{上|うえ}に、{話|はな}し{方|かた}もとても{自然|しぜん}だ。
>
> {音楽|おんがく}の{面|めん}でも{優|すぐ}れている。{有名|ゆうめい}な{作曲家|さっきょくか}が{書|か}いた{曲|きょく}は、どれも{美|うつく}しく、{場面|ばめん}が{目|め}に{浮|う}かぶようだ。{絵|え}の{色|いろ}も{明|あか}るければ、{音|おと}も{気持|きも}ちがいい。{特|とく}に、{王子|おうじ}が{夜|よる}の{空|そら}を{飛|と}ぶ{場面|ばめん}の{曲|きょく}は、{今年|ことし}{一番|いちばん}の{名曲|めいきょく}ではないだろうか。
>
> {正直|しょうじき}に{言|い}うと、{結末|けつまつ}は{少|すこ}し{分|わ}かりにくかった。{観客|かんきゃく}の{中|なか}には、{首|くび}をかしげている{人|ひと}もいた。それでも、{最後|さいご}の{場面|ばめん}で{王子|おうじ}が{鳥|とり}を{空|そら}に{放|はな}すところでは、{目|め}が{熱|あつ}くなった。アニメなんて{子供|こども}が{見|み}るものだと{思|おも}っている{人|ひと}にこそ、{見|み}てほしい。{映画館|えいがかん}を{出|で}たあと、どれだけこの{曲|きょく}を{口|くち}ずさんだことか。

{話題|わだい} = topic, talking point; ほし = star (in kana: its kanji is outside N3); {不思議|ふしぎ} = mysterious (N4); {旅|たび} = journey
(N4); {場面|ばめん} = scene; {首|くび}をかしげる = to tilt one's head (puzzled); {目|め}が{熱|あつ}くなる =
to feel tears coming; こそ = the very ones (lesson 15); {口|くち}ずさむ = to hum, sing to oneself.

<details>
<summary>Questions (answers inside)</summary>

1. Who is the film for? — The original is a children's picture book, but the film is for adults
   as much as children (〜はもちろん、〜も).
2. What does the boy actor do besides acting? — He sings the theme song himself (〜ばかりか、
   〜まで).
3. What didn't the writer like? — The ending was a little hard to follow; some of the audience
   looked puzzled.
4. Who does the writer most want to see the film? — People who think animation is only for
   children.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Translation</summary>

Yesterday I went to see "The Star Prince", the film everyone's talking about. The original is a
picture book for children, but the film is something adults can enjoy fully, let alone children. In the month since it opened, a million people have already seen it, I hear.

The hero is a prince who lives alone on a little star. One day he meets a strange bird floating in
the sky, and the two of them set off on a journey together. The prince is voiced by a boy of only
twelve. Not only is he a good actor, he even sings the theme song himself. His voice is lovely,
and on top of that the way he speaks sounds completely natural.

The film is excellent on the musical side too. The songs, by a famous composer, are all
beautiful, and seem to bring each scene before your eyes. The colours of the pictures are bright,
and the sound is pleasing too. The music for the scene where the prince flies through the night sky
may well be the best song of the year.

To be honest, the ending was a little hard to follow. Some people in the audience were tilting
their heads, puzzled. Even so, in the last scene, when the prince lets the bird go into the sky, I
felt tears coming. I'd like the people who think animation is just for kids to see this, of all
people. After I left the cinema, how many times I hummed that song!

</details>

## Pronunciation

- だけでなく: in speech often だけじゃなく or だけじゃなくて.
- ばかりか: ば・か・り・か, four morae. Don't confuse it with ばかり (only, just), which it contains.
- なんて and なんか: both start with a full ん beat: な・ん・て, な・ん・か. When surprised, なんて is
  said with force: {彼|かれ}が{来|く}るなんて！
- ことか: the sentence before it carries the feeling, so the voice usually rises on どんなに or
  {何度|なんど} and falls away at ことか.
- {女王|じょおう:2} is three morae, じょ・お・う; not じょうおう.

```speak
この{映画|えいが}は{子供|こども}だけでなく、{大人|おとな}も{楽|たの}しめます。
= Not only children but adults can enjoy this film too.
{彼|かれ}は{歌|うた}がうまいばかりか、{曲|きょく}まで{作|つく}る。
= Not only does he sing well, he even writes songs.
このアニメは{子供|こども}はもちろん、{大人|おとな}にも{人気|にんき}がある。
= This anime is popular with adults, not to mention children.
{駅|えき}から{近|ちか}い{上|うえ}に、{席|せき}も{広|ひろ}い。
= It's close to the station, and the seats are roomy too.
どんなにうれしかったことか。
= How happy I was!
{彼|かれ}が{歌手|かしゅ}になるなんて！
= I can't believe he's going to be a singer!
```

## Common mistakes

- Ending a ばかりか sentence with a request: ×{読|よ}むばかりか、{書|か}いてください. Use だけでなく.
- Using {上|うえ}に for contrast: ×{高|たか}い{上|うえ}に、おいしくない. Two opposite points take のに / けど:
  {高|たか}いのに、おいしくない.
- Forgetting な with a な-adjective: ×{有名|ゆうめい}だけでなく, ×{便利|べんり}{上|うえ}に. It's {有名|ゆうめい}な
  だけでなく, {便利|べんり}な{上|うえ}に.
- ことか without a question word: ×うれしかったことか. Add どんなに / どれだけ: どんなにうれしかったことか.
- Using なんか about someone else's things to their face (あなたの{絵|え}なんか): it sounds rude.
  About yourself ({私|わたし}なんか) it's modest.
- Mixing up {鳴|な}く and {泣|な}く: birds {鳴|な}く, babies {泣|な}く.
- Reading {真面目|まじめ} as しんめんもく: it's まじめ, a special reading.

## Key points

- 〜だけでなく / 〜ばかりでなく…も: not only…but also. な-adj な, noun as is.
- 〜ばかりか…(まで / さえ / も): not only, but even (something more extreme); not with requests.
- A はもちろん、B も: B too, not to mention A.
- 〜{上|うえ}(に): on top of that, in the same direction.
- 〜も〜ば〜も / 〜も〜し〜も: both… and; 〜もいれば〜もいる: some…, others….
- どんなに / どれだけ / {何度|なんど} + 〜ことか: how…! (emotional, literary).
- なんて: belittling (noun), surprise (clause), quoting; なんか: casual など (modest, dismissive,
  soft suggestions).
- New kanji: 演 曲 絵 舞 放 組 番 優 鳴 想 王 面 浮, and the special reading {真面目|まじめ}.

lessons.title: A mystery story: the painting that disappeared
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Detective stories are built from the grammar of this module: people guess (かもしれない,
のではないか), suppose (としたら), are sure (に{違|ちが}いない, はずだ), refuse to believe
(まさか), and the reader tries to keep up. This lesson is one original story in four parts. Read
each part, answer the questions under it, and try to solve the case before the detective does.

The story is told by the detective's assistant in the plain だ style of novels; what people say is
in polite speech. The crime words are lesson 19's; the few new words are listed first.

## Story words

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| {手|て}がかり | a clue |
| アリバイ | an alibi |
| なぞ | a mystery, a puzzle |
| すいりする | to deduce, work out |
| あしあと | footprints |
| あいかぎ | a spare key |
| {物音|ものおと} | a noise (of something moving) |

Also in the story: アトリエ (a painter's studio), お{手伝|てつだ}いさん (a housekeeper), {引|ひ}き{出|だ}し
(a drawer), {画家|がか} (a painter, lesson 20), 〜{点|てん} (counter for paintings and works of art).

## Part 1: a call on a snowy morning

> その{朝|あさ}、{町|まち}は{一面|いちめん}{真|ま}っ{白|しろ}だった。{夜中|よなか}の{十二時|じゅうにじ}ごろまで{降|ふ}り{続|つづ}いた{雪|ゆき}が、{庭|にわ}も{道|みち}もすっかり{白|しろ}くしていた。{事務所|じむしょ}の{電話|でんわ}が{鳴|な}ったのは、{八時|はちじ}{過|す}ぎだった。
>
> 「{青木|あおき}です。{父|ちち}の{絵|え}が{消|き}えたんです」
>
> {電話|でんわ}の{声|こえ}は、{去年|きょねん}{亡|な}くなった{画家|がか}、{青木|あおき}{正|ただし}の{長男|ちょうなん}、{健一|けんいち}さんだった。たんていの{森川|もりかわ}さんは、コーヒーを{一口|ひとくち}{飲|の}んでから「すぐ{行|い}きます」と{答|こた}えた。
>
> {青木|あおき}さんの{家|いえ}は、{駅|えき}から{歩|ある}いて{二十分|にじゅっぷん}の{古|ふる}い{家|いえ}だ。{二階|にかい}にはお{父|とう}さんのアトリエがあり、{小|ちい}さな{絵|え}が{三点|さんてん}{掛|か}けてあった。そのうちの{一点|いってん}、{海|うみ}をかいた「{夏|なつ}の{海|うみ}」が、{今朝|けさ}なくなっていたという。お{父|とう}さんが{一番|いちばん}{大切|たいせつ}にしていた{絵|え}だ。
>
> アトリエのかぎを{持|も}っているのは{健一|けんいち}さんだけで、あいかぎは{台所|だいどころ}の{引|ひ}き{出|だ}しに{入|い}れてある。{家|いえ}には{健一|けんいち}さんのほかに、{大学生|だいがくせい}の{末|すえ}っ{子|こ}の{由美|ゆみ}さんと、お{手伝|てつだ}いの{田村|たむら}さんが{住|す}んでいる。
>
> 「かぎを{持|も}っているのが{健一|けんいち}さんだけだとしたら、{犯人|はんにん}は{健一|けんいち}さんなのではないか」。{私|わたし}はそう{思|おも}ったが、{口|くち}には{出|だ}さなかった。

{一面|いちめん}{真|ま}っ{白|しろ} = white all over; {事務所|じむしょ} = office (lesson 11); かいた = painted
(its usual kanji is outside N3); {掛|か}けてある = has been hung (lesson 27's kanji).

<details>
<summary>Questions on part 1 (answers inside)</summary>

1. Which painting has gone, and why does it matter? — 「{夏|なつ}の{海|うみ}」, one of three small
   paintings in the studio; it was the father's favourite.
2. Who has keys to the studio? — Kenichi has the key; a spare key is kept in a kitchen drawer.
3. Who lives in the house? — Kenichi, his youngest sister Yumi (a university student) and the
   housekeeper, Ms Tamura.
4. What does the narrator suspect, and how sure is she? — That Kenichi did it, because he alone
   has the key. It's a supposition (としたら) and a soft guess (のではないか), and she keeps it to
   herself.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Translation of part 1</summary>

That morning the town was white all over. The snow, which had kept falling until about midnight,
had turned the gardens and the roads completely white. It was just after eight when the phone in
the office rang.

"This is Aoki. My father's painting has disappeared."

The voice on the phone was Kenichi, eldest son of the painter Tadashi Aoki, who had died the year
before. The detective, Mr Morikawa, took a sip of coffee and answered, "I'll come at once."

The Aokis' house is an old one, twenty minutes' walk from the station. Upstairs is the father's
studio, where three small paintings hung. One of them, a picture of the sea called "Summer Sea",
was missing this morning, Kenichi said. It was the painting his father had treasured most.

Only Kenichi has the key to the studio; a spare key is kept in a drawer in the kitchen. Besides
Kenichi, the youngest child, Yumi, a university student, lives in the house, and so does the
housekeeper, Ms Tamura.

"If Kenichi is the only one with the key, isn't he the culprit?" I thought so, but I didn't say
it out loud.

</details>

## Part 2: no footprints

> {家|いえ}に{着|つ}くと、{森川|もりかわ}さんはまず{庭|にわ}を{見|み}た。{雪|ゆき}の{上|うえ}には、あしあとが{一|ひと}つもなかった。{門|もん}から{入|い}り{口|ぐち}までの{道|みち}に、{家|いえ}に{入|はい}っていく{一人|ひとり}のあしあとがあるだけだ。
>
> 「{雪|ゆき}がやんだのは{十二時|じゅうにじ}ごろでしたね。とすると、それから{朝|あさ}まで、だれも{外|そと}から{来|き}ていないし、{外|そと}へ{出|で}てもいないことになります」
>
> {次|つぎ}に{健一|けんいち}さんの{話|はなし}を{聞|き}いた。{健一|けんいち}さんは{昨夜|さくや}、{仕事|しごと}で{東京|とうきょう}に{行|い}っていた。{雪|ゆき}で{電車|でんしゃ}が{止|と}まってしまい、{駅前|えきまえ}のホテルで{一晩|ひとばん}{過|す}ごして、{今朝|けさ}{帰|かえ}ってきたそうだ。ホテルの{人|ひと}も、それを{覚|おぼ}えているという。
>
> 「{帰|かえ}ってすぐ{絵|え}がないのに{気|き}がついて、{森川|もりかわ}さんに{電話|でんわ}しました。かぎはずっと{私|わたし}が{持|も}っていました。{由美|ゆみ}はまだ{寝|ね}ていたので、{話|はな}していません」
>
> {健一|けんいち}さんには{完全|かんぜん}なアリバイがあるように{見|み}えた。
>
> お{手伝|てつだ}いの{田村|たむら}さんは、{夜中|よなか}の{二時|にじ}ごろ、{二階|にかい}で{物音|ものおと}がしたような{気|き}がしたと{言|い}う。「でも、{古|ふる}い{家|いえ}ですから、{風|かぜ}の{音|おと}だったかもしれません。{今朝|けさ}{台所|だいどころ}に{行|い}くと、{引|ひ}き{出|だ}しが{少|すこ}し{開|あ}いていました。どの{絵|え}がなくなったのか、{私|わたし}はまだ{知|し}りませんけど」
>
> だれかがあいかぎを{使|つか}ったに{違|ちが}いない、と{私|わたし}は{思|おも}った。でも、だれが？

とすると = in that case (lesson 19); 〜ことになる = it means that (N4); {一晩|ひとばん}{過|す}ごす = to
spend a night.

<details>
<summary>Questions on part 2 (answers inside)</summary>

1. What does the snow tell the detective? — There are no footprints in the garden and only one
   line going in on the path, and the snow stopped at midnight, so nobody came in from outside or
   went out during the night: the culprit was inside the house. (The line on the path is Kenichi's,
   from this morning.)
2. Why does Kenichi seem to be in the clear? — He spent the night at a hotel near the station in
   Tokyo when the trains stopped, and the hotel staff remember him: an alibi.
3. What did Ms Tamura notice? — A noise upstairs at about two in the morning (she isn't sure:
   〜ような{気|き}がした, かもしれない) and, in the morning, the kitchen drawer slightly open.
4. Who knows which painting has gone? — Kenichi and the detective's team. Kenichi hasn't told
   Yumi, and Ms Tamura says she doesn't know which one it is.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Translation of part 2</summary>

When we reached the house, Mr Morikawa looked at the garden first. There wasn't a single
footprint in the snow. On the path from the gate to the door there was only one line of
footprints, going into the house.

"The snow stopped at about midnight, didn't it? In that case, nobody came in from outside, or went
out, between then and the morning."

Next we heard Kenichi's story. Last night he had gone to Tokyo for work. The trains stopped
because of the snow, so he spent the night at a hotel near the station and came home this
morning. The hotel staff remember him, he said.

"As soon as I got back I noticed the painting had gone and phoned you. I had the key with me the
whole time. Yumi was still asleep, so I haven't told her."

Kenichi seemed to have a perfect alibi.

The housekeeper, Ms Tamura, said she had a feeling she heard a noise upstairs at about two in the
night. "But it's an old house, so it might have been the wind. When I went into the kitchen this
morning, the drawer was a little open. I still don't know which painting has gone, though."

Someone must have used the spare key, I thought. But who?

</details>

## Part 3: what Yumi said

> {最後|さいご}に、{由美|ゆみ}さんが{二階|にかい}から{下|お}りてきた。{目|め}が{少|すこ}し{赤|あか}く、{寝不足|ねぶそく}のように{見|み}えた。
>
> 「{昨夜|さくや}は{早|はや}く{寝|ね}たので、{何|なに}も{聞|き}いていません。{朝|あさ}{起|お}きたら、みんなが{下|した}で{大|おお}きな{声|こえ}で{話|はな}していて…。まさか、{父|ちち}の『{夏|なつ}の{海|うみ}』がなくなるなんて」
>
> {由美|ゆみ}さんはそう{言|い}って、{下|した}を{向|む}いた。
>
> {私|わたし}は{田村|たむら}さんを{疑|うたが}い{始|はじ}めていた。{夜中|よなか}に{起|お}きていたのは{田村|たむら}さんだけだ。いつも{台所|だいどころ}にいる{田村|たむら}さんなら、あいかぎのある{場所|ばしょ}もよく{知|し}っているはずだ。
>
> 「{森川|もりかわ}さん、{犯人|はんにん}は{田村|たむら}さんなのではないでしょうか」
>
> {小|ちい}さな{声|こえ}で{言|い}うと、{森川|もりかわ}さんは{首|くび}を{横|よこ}にふった。
>
> 「{田村|たむら}さんが{犯人|はんにん}だとしたら、{物音|ものおと}のことや{引|ひ}き{出|だ}しのことを、わざわざ{私|わたし}たちに{話|はな}すでしょうか。それより、{今|いま}の{由美|ゆみ}さんの{言葉|ことば}に、{大切|たいせつ}な{手|て}がかりがありましたよ」

{下|お}りる = to come down (stairs); {首|くび}を{横|よこ}にふる = to shake one's head; わざわざ = go out
of one's way to (lesson 5).

<details>
<summary>Stop and think (answer inside)</summary>

What was the clue in Yumi's words? — She named the painting: 『{夏|なつ}の{海|うみ}』. There were three
paintings in the studio, Kenichi hadn't told her anything, and Ms Tamura didn't know which one had
gone. Someone who had slept all night and heard nothing couldn't have known.

Why does the detective doubt that Ms Tamura did it? — If she were the culprit
(〜だとしたら), she would hardly go out of her way to mention the noise and the open drawer.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Translation of part 3</summary>

Last of all, Yumi came downstairs. Her eyes were a little red, and she looked as if she hadn't
slept enough.

"I went to bed early last night, so I didn't hear anything. When I got up this morning, everyone
was talking loudly downstairs... I never thought Dad's 'Summer Sea' would go missing."

Yumi said this and looked down.

I had begun to suspect Ms Tamura. She was the only one who had been up in the night. Always in the
kitchen, she must know exactly where the spare key is kept.

"Mr Morikawa, couldn't the culprit be Ms Tamura?"

When I said this in a low voice, he shook his head.

"If Ms Tamura were the culprit, would she go out of her way to tell us about the noise and the
drawer? More to the point, there was an important clue in what Yumi just said."

</details>

## Part 4: the answer

> {森川|もりかわ}さんは{由美|ゆみ}さんの{前|まえ}に{立|た}った。
>
> 「{由美|ゆみ}さん、アトリエには{絵|え}が{三点|さんてん}ありました。{健一|けんいち}さんは、どの{絵|え}がなくなったか、まだあなたに{話|はな}していません。{田村|たむら}さんも{知|し}りませんでした。{一晩中|ひとばんじゅう}{寝|ね}ていたあなたが、どうして『{夏|なつ}の{海|うみ}』だと{知|し}っていたんですか」
>
> {由美|ゆみ}さんの{顔|かお}が{真|ま}っ{青|さお}になった。しばらくして、{由美|ゆみ}さんは{小|ちい}さな{声|こえ}で{話|はな}し{始|はじ}めた。
>
> 「{兄|あに}が、あの{絵|え}を{売|う}るつもりだと{知|し}ったんです。{父|ちち}が{一番|いちばん}{愛|あい}していた{絵|え}なのに…。だから{夜中|よなか}にあいかぎでアトリエに{入|はい}って、{私|わたし}の{部屋|へや}にかくしました。{盗|ぬす}むつもりはありませんでした」
>
> {健一|けんいち}さんは{何|なに}も{言|い}わずに{妹|いもうと}を{見|み}ていたが、やがて「{悪|わる}かった。{売|う}るのはやめるよ」と{言|い}った。
>
> {帰|かえ}り{道|みち}、{私|わたし}は{森川|もりかわ}さんに{聞|き}いた。「{最初|さいしょ}から{由美|ゆみ}さんだと{分|わ}かっていたんですか」
>
> 「まさか。あしあとがなかったから、{家|いえ}の{中|なか}の{人|ひと}に{違|ちが}いないとは{思|おも}いました。でも、なぞを{解|と}いたのは{由美|ゆみ}さんの{一言|ひとこと}ですよ。{人|ひと}はうそをつくとき、{知|し}りすぎていることを{話|はな}してしまうものです」
>
> {森川|もりかわ}さんはそう{言|い}って、{白|しろ}い{息|いき}をはいた。

{一晩中|ひとばんじゅう} = all night (lesson 1); {真|ま}っ{青|さお} = deathly pale (N4); やがて = before
long; 〜ものです = that's how people are (lesson 9); {息|いき}をはく = to breathe out.

<details>
<summary>Questions on part 4 (answers inside)</summary>

1. Why did Yumi take the painting? — She found out Kenichi meant to sell it, and it was the
   painting their father loved most.
2. Where was the painting? — Hidden in Yumi's room. She used the spare key in the night (the noise
   at two, the open drawer).
3. Did the detective know from the start? — No (まさか). The missing footprints only told him it
   was someone inside the house; Yumi's slip told him who.
4. How does the story end for the painting? — Kenichi apologizes and gives up selling it.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Translation of part 4</summary>

Mr Morikawa stood in front of Yumi.

"Yumi, there were three paintings in the studio. Kenichi hasn't told you which one has gone, and
Ms Tamura didn't know either. You slept all night, so how did you know it was 'Summer Sea'?"

Yumi went pale. After a while she began to speak in a small voice.

"I found out my brother was going to sell that painting. When it was the one Dad loved most...
So in the night I went into the studio with the spare key and hid it in my room. I never meant to
steal it."

Kenichi looked at his sister without saying anything, but before long he said, "I'm sorry. I won't
sell it."

On the way back I asked Mr Morikawa, "Did you know it was Yumi from the start?"

"Not at all. Because there were no footprints, I was sure it was someone in the house. But what
solved the mystery was that one thing Yumi said. When people lie, they end up saying things they
know too much about."

With that, he breathed out a cloud of white breath.

</details>

## The guessing grammar in the story

| In the story | Pattern | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| {健一|けんいち}さんだけだとしたら | としたら (19) | a supposition |
| {犯人|はんにん}は{健一|けんいち}さんなのではないか | のではないか (19) | a soft suspicion |
| とすると、…ことになります | とすると (19) | a step in reasoning: in that case |
| アリバイがあるように{見|み}えた | ように{見|み}える (17) | an impression, maybe wrong |
| {物音|ものおと}がしたような{気|き}がした | ような{気|き}がする (17) | a vague feeling |
| {風|かぜ}の{音|おと}だったかもしれません | かもしれない (N4) | a possibility |
| あいかぎを{使|つか}ったに{違|ちが}いない | に{違|ちが}いない (17) | a firm conclusion from a clue |
| {場所|ばしょ}もよく{知|し}っているはずだ | はず (N4) | a deduction from facts |
| まさか、…なくなるなんて | まさか (19), なんて (20) | disbelief and surprise |

Notice that the narrator's guesses get firmer as the story goes on (のではないか → に{違|ちが}いない →
はずだ), yet only the spare-key one is right; the detective's reasoning uses としたら to test each
idea.

## Key points

- A mystery is a good place to watch guessing grammar at work: としたら tests an idea,
  のではないか suggests one, に{違|ちが}いない and はず sound sure, まさか refuses to believe.
- Story words: {手|て}がかり, アリバイ, なぞ, すいりする, あしあと, あいかぎ, {物音|ものおと}.
- 〜{点|てん} counts paintings and works of art: {絵|え}が{三点|さんてん}.

lessons.title: Haiku and seasonal words
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

A haiku (はいく) is a poem of seventeen sounds in three parts, 5-7-5, that usually holds a season
word. It's often called the shortest poetic form in the world, and in Japan it's everywhere:
many newspapers print readers' haiku every week, schoolchildren write them, and a well-known tea
company prints prize-winning haiku on its bottles. This lesson shows you how a haiku is built, how to count
its sounds, what season words do, and three famous haiku by the old masters, with a modern
paraphrase of each. At the end you write one.

はいく is in kana here because its first kanji is outside N3; so is く (a single verse; its kanji is
outside N3 too).

## Five, seven, five: counting the sounds

A haiku counts morae (the beats of Japanese, which you've been counting for pitch accent since
N5), not syllables. The rules are the ones for pitch:

| Kana | Counts as | Example |
|---|---|---|
| each ordinary kana | 1 | {花|はな} = は・な (2) |
| small ゃ, ゅ, ょ | 0 (part of the kana before) | きょう = きょ・う (2) |
| small っ | 1 | とって = と・っ・て (3) |
| ん | 1 | みんな = み・ん・な (3) |
| ー and long vowels | 1 | {名月|めいげつ} = め・い・げ・つ (4) |

So "five, seven, five" means seventeen beats: ふ・る・い・け・や (5) / か・わ・ず・と・び・こ・む (7) /
み・ず・の・お・と (5).

A line with one beat too many is {字余|じあま}り (literally "extra characters"). Poets do it on
purpose sometimes, and readers accept it; too short is much rarer.

## Season words: きご

Most traditional haiku include a season word, a きご ({季語|きご}; the first kanji is outside N3):
a word that tells the reader which season the poem is set in, and brings that season's feeling
with it. Poets use season-word dictionaries that list thousands of them.

| Season | Season words |
|---|---|
| Spring | {菜|な}の{花|はな} (rape blossom), かわず (frog, an old word), さくら, {春|はる}の{海|うみ} |
| Summer | ほたる (firefly), せみ (cicada), {夕立|ゆうだち} (a sudden evening shower) |
| Autumn | {名月|めいげつ} (the harvest moon), もみじ (red leaves), {七夕|たなばた}, {秋|あき}の{暮|く}れ (an autumn evening) |
| Winter | {雪|ゆき}, こがらし (a cold wintry wind) |

One surprise: the haiku seasons follow the old calendar, so spring starts in early February and
autumn in early August. {七夕|たなばた} fell in early autumn in the old calendar, so it still counts
as an autumn word, even where it's now held on 7 July (some places hold it on 7 August). New Year
has its own section in most season-word dictionaries.

Many haiku also have a cutting word, {切|き}れ{字|じ}, that makes a pause and adds feeling: や
(like a sigh, "ah, …"), かな (wonder, at the end), けり (at the end, "it was so"). You'll see や in two
of the haiku below and かな in one.

## Three classic haiku

These three are by the best-known poets of the Edo period. They're centuries old and free to
quote; the paraphrases in modern Japanese and English are this course's own. Words whose kanji
are outside N3 are in kana.

### Bashō: the old pond

ばしょう (1644–1694) travelled the country and wrote what many people call the most famous haiku
of all:

> {古池|ふるいけ}やかわず{飛|と}びこむ{水|みず}の{音|おと}

| Line | Text | Morae |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | {古池|ふるいけ}や | ふ・る・い・け・や (5) |
| 2 | かわず{飛|と}びこむ | か・わ・ず・と・び・こ・む (7) |
| 3 | {水|みず}の{音|おと} | み・ず・の・お・と (5) |

Season word: かわず (frog), spring. Cutting word: や.

Modern paraphrase: {古|ふる}い{池|いけ}がある。かえるがそこに{飛|と}びこんで、{水|みず}の{音|おと}がした。
そのあと、また{静|しず}かになった。

English: An old pond. A frog jumps in: the sound of water.

The poem doesn't say "and then it was quiet again"; it doesn't need to. The single sound makes
the silence around it stronger, and that's the {情景|じょうけい} (scene) the reader is left with.

### Buson: rape blossom

ぶそん (1716–1784) was a painter as well as a poet, and you can see it:

> {菜|な}の{花|はな}や{月|つき}は{東|ひがし}に{日|ひ}は{西|にし}に

| Line | Text | Morae |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | {菜|な}の{花|はな}や | な・の・は・な・や (5) |
| 2 | {月|つき}は{東|ひがし}に | つ・き・は・ひ・が・し・に (7) |
| 3 | {日|ひ}は{西|にし}に | ひ・は・に・し・に (5) |

Season word: {菜|な}の{花|はな} (yellow rape blossom), spring. Cutting word: や. The particle は is
read わ and counts as one mora, like any kana.

Modern paraphrase: {一面|いちめん}に{菜|な}の{花|はな}がさいている。{東|ひがし}の{空|そら}には{月|つき}が{出|で}て、
{西|にし}の{空|そら}には{日|ひ}がしずんでいく。

English: Rape blossom everywhere; the moon in the east, the sun in the west.

A whole spring evening in seventeen sounds: a field of yellow flowers, the moon rising on one side
and the sun setting on the other, as if the poet stood in the middle of a painting.

### Issa: the harvest moon

いっさ (1763–1828) wrote many haiku about children, small animals and everyday life:

> {名月|めいげつ}をとってくれろと{泣|な}く{子|こ}かな

| Line | Text | Morae |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | {名月|めいげつ}を | め・い・げ・つ・を (5) |
| 2 | とってくれろと | と・っ・て・く・れ・ろ・と (7) |
| 3 | {泣|な}く{子|こ}かな | な・く・こ・か・な (5) |

Season word: {名月|めいげつ}, autumn. Cutting word: かな. くれろ is an old dialect form of
くれ (give me), so とってくれろ is "get it for me".

Modern paraphrase: きれいな{満月|まんげつ}が{出|で}ている。「あの{月|つき}を{取|と}って」と、{子供|こども}が
{泣|な}いている。

English: "Get me the harvest moon!" the child cries.

Funny and tender at once: the moon is so bright and close that a small child thinks you could
reach up and take it.

## Writing a haiku

1. Choose a season and one season word. {雪|ゆき}, {名月|めいげつ}, さくら, せみ…
2. Pick one moment. Something you saw or heard today: a sound, a colour, a small movement.
   Haiku are about showing, not explaining feelings.
3. Write it in three parts, 5-7-5. Count the morae on your fingers. If a line is off by one,
   try another word, or accept a {字余|じあま}り.
4. Cut it. Put a pause after the first or second part (や, or simply a noun that stops the
   sentence). Leave something for the reader to imagine.
5. Read it aloud. The {表現|ひょうげん} (wording) should sound natural, not like a sentence chopped
   into pieces.

Here's one written for this course, about the snow in the mystery story:

> {雪|ゆき}の{朝|あさ}あしあと{一|ひと}つ{門|もん}からの

ゆ・き・の・あ・さ (5) / あ・し・あ・と・ひ・と・つ (7) / も・ん・か・ら・の (5). Season word: {雪|ゆき},
winter. "A snowy morning: one line of footprints, from the gate." Who made them, and why only
one line? The haiku doesn't say.

## Dialogue: the haiku contest

Kaito and his grandmother, who belongs to a haiku circle, talk at the kitchen table.

```dialogue
# A haiku for school
かいと: おばあちゃん、{学校|がっこう}ではいくを{書|か}かなきゃいけないんだけど、{難|むずか}しいよ。
= Grandma, I have to write a haiku for school, but it's hard.
そぼ: そう？まず、きごを{一|ひと}つ{選|えら}んでごらん。{今|いま}は{秋|あき}だから、{名月|めいげつ}はどう？
= Is it? First, choose a season word. It's autumn, so how about the harvest moon?
かいと: {名月|めいげつ}か…。{昨日|きのう}の{夜|よる}、{月|つき}がすごくきれいだった。
= The harvest moon... Last night the moon was really beautiful.
そぼ: そのとき、{何|なに}が{聞|き}こえた？{何|なに}が{見|み}えた？
= What could you hear then? What could you see?
かいと: {犬|いぬ}が{鳴|な}いてた。あと、{池|いけ}に{月|つき}が{浮|う}かんでるみたいだった。
= A dog was barking. And the moon looked like it was floating on the pond.
そぼ: いいね。それを{五|ご}・{七|しち}・{五|ご}にしてみよう。
= Nice. Let's try to make that five-seven-five.
かいと: {名月|めいげつ}や{池|いけ}に{浮|う}かんで…{何|なん}だろう。
= "The harvest moon, floating on the pond"... what next?
そぼ: {音|おと}を{数|かぞ}えてごらん。{名月|めいげつ}や、で{五|いつ}つ。{池|いけ}に{浮|う}かんで、は？
= Count the sounds. 「{名月|めいげつ}や」 is five. What about 「{池|いけ}に{浮|う}かんで」?
かいと: い・け・に・う・か・ん・で…{七|なな}つ！あと{五|いつ}つだ。
= I-ke-ni-u-ka-n-de... seven! Five more.
そぼ: {最後|さいご}は{犬|いぬ}の{声|こえ}にしたら？
= Why not end with the dog's bark?
かいと: 「{犬|いぬ}が{鳴|な}く」で{五|いつ}つ。{名月|めいげつ}や{池|いけ}に{浮|う}かんで{犬|いぬ}が{鳴|な}く。できた！
= 「{犬|いぬ}が{鳴|な}く」 is five. 「{名月|めいげつ}や{池|いけ}に{浮|う}かんで{犬|いぬ}が{鳴|な}く」. Done!
そぼ: {情景|じょうけい}が{目|め}に{浮|う}かぶね。{次|つぎ}は、おばあちゃんのサークルにも{出|だ}してみる？
= I can picture the scene. Next time, shall we enter it in Grandma's circle?
```

〜てごらん = try (doing), said to a child; {数|かぞ}える = to count; ～みたいだった = looked like
(N4); {目|め}に{浮|う}かぶ = to picture.

## Key points

- はいく: seventeen morae, 5-7-5, usually with a season word (きご) and often a cutting word
  (や, かな, けり).
- Count morae as for pitch accent: small ゃゅょ don't count; っ, ん and long vowels do. A line that runs
  over its count is {字余|じあま}り.
- Season words follow the old calendar: {七夕|たなばた} and {名月|めいげつ} are autumn, {菜|な}の{花|はな} and
  かわず spring, {雪|ゆき} winter.
- ばしょう's old pond, ぶそん's rape blossom, いっさ's harvest moon: one moment, shown, not
  explained.
- New words: はいく, きご, {字余|じあま}り, {名月|めいげつ}, {情景|じょうけい} ({表現|ひょうげん} is from lesson 12).

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you
complete the lesson.

lessons.title: Passing on requests: ように言う, てもらいたい, とおりに
topics: てもらいたい and ていただきたい
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

This module is about words that travel: what someone asked you to do, what you heard, what a
word means, how to say it politely to a customer and how to say it to a friend. Lessons 21–23
pass words on (requests, news, definitions), lesson 24 adds the keigo of shops and offices, and
lesson 25 gathers casual speech in one place.

This lesson starts with requests. In N4 you could quote someone's exact words in a **[[quotation]]**
with と:
「{待|ま}ってください」と{言|い}われた. At N3 you also report the request itself, without the exact
words, with 〜ように{言|い}う:

{先生|せんせい}に、{明日|あした}{早|はや}く{来|く}るように{言|い}われました。 — The teacher told me to come early tomorrow.

You'll also say what you want others to do (〜てもらいたい, 〜ていただきたい), follow instructions
"just as" they say (〜{通|とお}りに), and make wishes (〜ますように). The theme is technology: phones,
apps, settings and the instructions that come with them, which are full of exactly these patterns.

## Reporting a request: 〜ように{言|い}う

To report a request, an instruction or a warning, put the verb in the dictionary form (or the ない
form) before ように, then a verb of saying:

| Request | Reported with ように |
|---|---|
| 「{早|はや}く{来|き}てください。」 | {早|はや}く{来|く}るように{言|い}われた (I was told to come early) |
| 「{遅|おく}れないでください。」 | {遅|おく}れないように{言|い}われた (I was told not to be late) |
| 「ファイルを{保存|ほぞん}してね。」 | ファイルを{保存|ほぞん}するように{頼|たの}んだ (I asked them to save the file) |
| 「パスワードを{教|おし}えないで。」 | パスワードを{教|おし}えないように{注意|ちゅうい}された (I was warned not to give my password out) |

The verbs that go after ように are the verbs of asking and telling: {言|い}う, {頼|たの}む (ask a favour),
{伝|つた}える (pass on), {注意|ちゅうい}する (warn), お{願|ねが}いする (request), {書|か}いてある (it says, in
writing), and their passives ({言|い}われる, {頼|たの}まれる, {注意|ちゅうい}される).

The person who receives the request takes に:

{部長|ぶちょう}は{私|わたし}に、{資料|しりょう}をいんさつするように{言|い}いました。 — The department head told me to print the documents.

{母|はは}に、{寝|ね}る{前|まえ}にスマホを{見|み}ないように{言|い}われています。 — My mother has told me not to look at my phone before bed.

{田中|たなか}さんに、{明日|あした}の{会議|かいぎ}に{来|く}るように{伝|つた}えてください。 — Please tell Tanaka to come to tomorrow's meeting.

{説明書|せつめいしょ}には、{使|つか}う{前|まえ}にじゅうでんするように{書|か}いてあります。 — The manual says to charge it before using it.

Two things change when you report a request with ように:

- **The politeness goes.** ください, ね and ます don't go before ように: ×{来|き}てくださいように.
  The dictionary form carries the request; the politeness of your own sentence is set by the verb
  at the end ({言|い}われました, {言|い}われた).
- **The person changes.** 「{明日|あした}{来|き}てください」, said to you, becomes {明日|あした}{来|く}るように
  {言|い}われた: there's no "you" any more, just the action asked for.

### ように or と?

と quotes words or reports a statement; ように reports what someone was asked to *do*. With the
same verb they mean different things:

{田中|たなか}さんは{明日|あした}{来|く}ると{言|い}いました。 — Tanaka said he would come tomorrow. (a statement)

{田中|たなか}さんに{明日|あした}{来|く}るように{言|い}いました。 — I told Tanaka to come tomorrow. (a request)

You can always quote the request directly instead: 「{明日|あした}{来|き}てください」と{言|い}いました.
That keeps the exact words and their politeness. Use ように when the gist matters more than the
wording, which is most of the time when you pass a message on.

A strong order can also be quoted with the imperative (N4 taught you to recognize it): {早|はや}く
{寝|ね}ろと{言|い}われた (I was told to go to bed, roughly). ように is softer and much more common in
polite reports.

### ように after a verb you already know

You met three other uses of ように in N4. They look similar but don't take a verb of saying:

| Pattern | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| 〜ようになる | come to (change) | {日本語|にほんご}で{入力|にゅうりょく}できるようになった |
| 〜ようにする | make a point of | {毎晩|まいばん}じゅうでんするようにしている |
| 〜ように、… | so that | {忘|わす}れないように、メモした |
| 〜ように{言|い}う | tell (someone) to | {忘|わす}れないように{言|い}われた |

The last one is this lesson's: ように + a verb of saying, asking or warning.

## I'd like you to: 〜てもらいたい, 〜ていただきたい

> **Review (N4 lesson 7).** 〜てほしい = I want someone to do something; the person takes に:
> {早|はや}く{元気|げんき}になってほしい. It's direct, so with superiors you ask instead: 〜ていただけませんか.

〜てもらいたい means the same as 〜てほしい: "I'd like (someone) to…". It's built from 〜てもらう
(have someone do something) + たい. 〜ていただきたい is the humble version, built on いただく:

{弟|おとうと}に、パソコンの{使|つか}い{方|かた}を{教|おし}えてもらいたい。 — I'd like my brother to show me how to use the computer.

{皆|みな}さんにアンケートに{答|こた}えていただきたいと{思|おも}います。 — I would like to ask you all to fill in a questionnaire.

ここではスマホを{使用|しよう}しないでいただきたい。 — I must ask you not to use smartphones here.

| Pattern | Feel | Typical use |
|---|---|---|
| 〜てほしい | direct, personal | friends, family, saying how you feel |
| 〜てもらいたい | a little firmer, more matter-of-fact | colleagues, written explanations |
| 〜ていただきたい | polite, formal | speeches, notices, a boss to staff |

The difference between 〜てほしい and 〜てもらいたい is small, and speakers vary; 〜てもらいたい
can sound slightly more like a demand. 〜ていただきたい is polite in form, but it is still a
statement of *your* wish. Said straight to a customer or a superior, it can sound like an order,
so it usually comes with と{思|おも}います or as a softened request: 〜ていただけませんか, 〜ていただけると
{助|たす}かります (it would help if you could…). It's at home in announcements and speeches, where
one speaker addresses a group.

The negative is 〜ないでもらいたい / 〜ないでいただきたい: ここに{自転車|じてんしゃ}を{置|お}かないでもらいたい
(I'd like people not to leave bicycles here). That's often a complaint.

## Just as: 〜{通|とお}りに, 〜{通|どお}りに

{通|とお}り means "the way, as (something goes)". It follows a noun with の, or a verb in the
dictionary or た form:

| Before it | Form | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| noun + の | 〜の{通|とお}りに | {説明書|せつめいしょ}の{通|とお}りに | as the manual says |
| noun directly | 〜{通|どお}りに | {予定|よてい}{通|どお}りに | according to plan |
| verb (dictionary) | 〜{通|とお}りに | {私|わたし}が{言|い}う{通|とお}りに | as I tell you (now) |
| verb (た form) | 〜た{通|とお}りに | {習|なら}った{通|とお}りに | as I was taught |

{説明書|せつめいしょ}の{通|とお}りにやったら、うまくいった。 — When I did it as the manual said, it worked.

{電車|でんしゃ}は{時間|じかん}{通|どお}りに{着|つ}いた。 — The train arrived on time.

{画面|がめん}に{出|で}た{通|とお}りに{入力|にゅうりょく}してください。 — Type it in exactly as it appears on the screen.

{思|おも}った{通|とお}り、{彼|かれ}は{来|こ}なかった。 — Just as I thought, he didn't come.

Two small points:

- Straight after a noun, {通|とお}り becomes {通|どお}り (the voicing you saw in {大声|おおごえ}):
  {予定|よてい}{通|どお}り, いつも{通|どお}り (as usual), {時間|じかん}{通|どお}り. After の it stays
  {通|とお}り.
- The dictionary form and the た form both work after verbs. The dictionary form is usual for what's
  happening now or always ({私|わたし}が{言|い}う{通|とお}りに、やってみて); the た form for something said
  or done earlier ({先生|せんせい}が{言|い}った{通|とお}りに).

〜{通|とお}りだ and 〜{通|とお}りです end a sentence: その{通|とお}りです (exactly, that's right). And
{次|つぎ}の{通|とお}りです means "as follows", the line before a list in a notice.

This {通|とお}り is the same kanji as N4's {通|とお}り (street), and both come from {通|とお}る (to pass
along): a street is the way you go along, and {説明書|せつめいしょ}の{通|とお}り is the way the manual
goes.

## Wishes: 〜ますように

〜ますように (at the end of a sentence, often with a falling, soft voice) is a wish or a prayer: "may…",
"I hope…". It's what people write on shrine prayer boards and say before an exam:

{試験|しけん}に{合格|ごうかく}できますように。 — Please let me pass the exam.

{明日|あした}{晴|は}れますように。 — I hope it's sunny tomorrow.

{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}りませんように。 — Please don't let it rain.

おばあちゃんが{早|はや}く{元気|げんき}になりますように。 — I hope Grandma gets well soon.

It usually takes the polite ます form, even in casual speech and private wishes: the wish is addressed, in a
way, to the gods or to fate. Put the potential before it for your own efforts ({合格|ごうかく}できますように).

## Words for devices and the internet

Japanese device words are a mix of loanwords and Sino-Japanese compounds, and the instructions
use both. A few families:

| Doing | Words |
|---|---|
| Starting and stopping | {起動|きどう}する (start up), {再起動|さいきどう}する (restart), でんげんを{入|い}れる / {切|き}る (switch on / off), {初期化|しょきか}する (reset to factory settings) |
| Files and data | {保存|ほぞん}する (save), さくじょする (delete), {開|ひら}く / {閉|と}じる (open / close), ダウンロードする, {更新|こうしん}する (update, refresh) |
| Typing | {入力|にゅうりょく}する (enter), へんかんする (convert kana to kanji), {文字化|もじば}け (garbled text) |
| Messages and calls | {送信|そうしん}する (send), {着信|ちゃくしん} (incoming call), {発信|はっしん}する (call out), {通話|つうわ} (a call), {通知|つうち} (notification) |
| Settings | せってい, {変|か}える, {元|もと}に{戻|もど}す (put back), ロックを{解除|かいじょ}する (unlock), {手動|しゅどう} / {自動|じどう} |

{開|ひら}く and {閉|と}じる are the pair for books, files and apps; for doors and windows, N5's
{開|あ}ける and {閉|し}める. {開|ひら}く is also "to hold" an event: {会|かい}を{開|ひら}く.

{機能|きのう} (function) sounds like {昨日|きのう} (yesterday): {機能|きのう} falls after the first mora
(き\のう), {昨日|きのう} falls after the second (きの\う). Type きのう and convert, and the IME offers both.

## Kanji

Thirteen kanji for machines, messages and change. Several of them spell verbs you know in kana.

### Machines and messages

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 機 | machine; occasion | キ | | 16 | {機能|きのう}, {機種|きしゅ}, {飛行機|ひこうき}, {機会|きかい} (an opportunity) |
| 信 | believe; message | シン | | 9 | {信|しん}じる, {信号|しんごう}, {通信|つうしん}, {送信|そうしん}, {着信|ちゃくしん}, {返信|へんしん} |
| 報 | report, news | ホウ | | 12 | {情報|じょうほう}, {天気予報|てんきよほう}, {報道|ほうどう} (lesson 22), {速報|そくほう} (news flash) |
| 保 | keep, protect | ホ | | 9 | {保存|ほぞん}, {保険|ほけん}, {保育園|ほいくえん} (nursery school) |

### Pushing, going back and closing

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 押 | push | | お(す) | 8 | {押|お}す, {押|お}し{入|い}れ (a futon cupboard) |
| 再 | again | サイ, サ | | 6 | {再生|さいせい}, {再起動|さいきどう}, {再来週|さらいしゅう} (lesson 25) |
| 戻 | go back | | もど(る), もど(す) | 7 | {戻|もど}る, {戻|もど}す, {払|はら}い{戻|もど}し (a refund) |
| 閉 | close | ヘイ | と(じる), し(める), し(まる) | 11 | {閉|と}じる, {閉|し}める, {閉|し}まる, {閉店|へいてん} (closing, of a shop) |
| 返 | return | ヘン | かえ(す) | 7 | {返|かえ}す, {返事|へんじ}, {返信|へんしん}, {返品|へんぴん} |

### Continuing, attaching and changing

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 続 | continue | ゾク | つづ(く), つづ(ける) | 13 | {続|つづ}く, {続|つづ}ける, {続|つづ}き, {手続|てつづ}き, {連続|れんぞく} (lesson 22) |
| 付 | attach | | つ(ける) | 5 | {付|つ}ける, {気|き}を{付|つ}ける, {付|つ}き{合|あ}う, {受付|うけつけ}, {日付|ひづけ} (date) |
| 変 | change; strange | ヘン | か(わる), か(える) | 9 | {変|へん}, {大変|たいへん}, {変|か}わる, {変|か}える, {変更|へんこう} |
| 更 | renew | コウ | | 7 | {更新|こうしん}, {変更|へんこう}, {夜更|よふ}かし (lesson 25) |

Carried words you can now write with kanji: {押|お}す, {戻|もど}る, {閉|し}める, {閉|し}まる,
{返|かえ}す, {返事|へんじ}, {返信|へんしん}, {続|つづ}く, {続|つづ}ける, {手続|てつづ}き, {気|き}を{付|つ}ける,
{付|つ}き{合|あ}う, {受付|うけつけ} (with lesson 24's 受), {変|へん}, {大変|たいへん}, {変更|へんこう},
{信|しん}じる, {信号|しんごう}, {情報|じょうほう} (with lesson 10's 情), {天気予報|てんきよほう} (with lesson 24's
予), {保険|ほけん} (with lesson 26's 険), {飛行機|ひこうき} (with lesson 2's 飛) and {押|お}し{入|い}れ.

Notes:

- 閉 has three kun'yomi. {閉|し}める / {閉|し}まる are the door pair (transitive / intransitive, N4
  lesson 8); {閉|と}じる is for books, eyes, files and apps. Only the okurigana tell you which:
  {閉|し}める has め, {閉|と}じる has じ.
- 再 is サイ in most words and サ in {再来週|さらいしゅう}, {再来月|さらいげつ} and {再来年|さらいねん}
  ("the one after next").
- 付 spells N5's つける when it means "to attach, to put on": ファイルを{付|つ}ける, {気|き}を{付|つ}ける.
  When つける means "to switch on" (a light, the TV), this course keeps it in kana, as many writers
  do: {電気|でんき}をつける.
- 変 is ヘン in {変|へん} (strange) and {大変|たいへん}, and か in {変|か}わる / {変|か}える. Don't mix
  {変|か}える (to change, group 2) with {帰|かえ}る (to go home, group 1): {変|か}えます, {帰|かえ}ります.
- 機 also means "occasion, opportunity": {機会|きかい} (a chance). The other きかい, machine (N4),
  needs a second kanji that is outside N3, so it stays in kana.

Memory notes (hooks, not etymology):

- 押: the "hand" shape on the left, pressing down on a box: push.
- 戻: a door (戸) with a big (大) person going back through it.
- 閉: a gate (門) with a bar (才) across it: closed.
- 返: 反 (turn over, lesson 9) on the "road" shape that runs along the bottom: turn back along the
  road, return.
- 続: the "thread" shape on the left and 売 (sell) on the right: a seller who keeps the thread
  going, continuing.
- 機: a tree (木) on the left, as in many wooden things: a machine, once built of wood.
- 付: the thin "person" shape on the left, with a hand reaching out to stick something on: attach.

```trace
機信報保押再戻閉返続付変更
```

## Dialogue: Grandpa's new phone

Misaki, a university student, is visiting her grandfather, who has just bought a smartphone.
They speak casually; he uses a slightly old-fashioned plain style.

```dialogue
# A new phone
おじいさん: みさき、ちょっと{見|み}てくれないか。このスマホ、{急|きゅう}に{動|うご}かなくなったんだ。
= Misaki, could you have a look? This phone suddenly stopped working.
みさき: いいよ。どうしたの？
= Sure. What's wrong?
おじいさん: {店|みせ}の{人|ひと}に{毎晩|まいばん}じゅうでんするように{言|い}われたから、ちゃんとやってるんだけどな。
= The man at the shop told me to charge it every night, and I've been doing it properly.
みさき: うん。…あ、{画面|がめん}が{止|と}まってるね。{一回|いっかい}、{再起動|さいきどう}してみよう。この{横|よこ}のボタンを{長|なが}く{押|お}して。
= Right… oh, the screen's frozen. Let's restart it once. Press and hold this button on the side.
おじいさん: {押|お}したよ。{何|なに}か{出|で}てきた。
= I've pressed it. Something's come up.
みさき: 「{再起動|さいきどう}」っていうのをタップして。そうそう、その{通|とお}り。
= Tap the one that says "Restart". Yes, that's it.
おじいさん: お、{動|うご}いた。でも、メールの{字|じ}が{小|ちい}さくて{読|よ}めないんだよ。
= Oh, it's working. But the letters in my email are too small to read.
みさき: じゃ、せっていで{大|おお}きくしよう。{私|わたし}が{言|い}う{通|とお}りにやってみて。まず、ここを{開|ひら}いて…。
= Then let's make them bigger in the settings. Do what I tell you. First, open this…
おじいさん: {待|ま}った{待|ま}った。もう{少|すこ}しゆっくり{言|い}ってくれ。
= Hold on, hold on. Say it a bit more slowly.
みさき: ごめん。じゃ、{紙|かみ}に{書|か}いとくから、{書|か}いた{通|とお}りにやってね。
= Sorry. I'll write it down on paper for you, so do it the way I've written it.
おじいさん: {助|たす}かるよ。それから、{知|し}らない{人|ひと}からのメールは{開|ひら}かないように、お{父|とう}さんに{注意|ちゅうい}されたんだけど、どれが{知|し}らない{人|ひと}のか{分|わ}からなくてな。
= That's a help. Oh, and your dad warned me not to open emails from people I don't know, but I can't tell which ones are from strangers.
みさき: {名前|なまえ}が{出|で}ないのは、{開|ひら}かないほうがいいよ。{迷|まよ}ったら、{私|わたし}に{転送|てんそう}して。
= Better not to open the ones with no name. If you're not sure, forward them to me.
おじいさん: ありがとう。みさきにもっと{近|ちか}くに{住|す}んでもらいたいなあ。
= Thank you. I wish you lived nearer, Misaki.
みさき: ふふ。じゃあ、{来月|らいげつ}またすぐ{来|く}るね。{次|つぎ}はビデオ{通話|つうわ}も{教|おし}えてあげる。
= Ha ha. Then I'll come again next month. Next time I'll show you video calls too.
```

{待|ま}った{待|ま}った is a set, slightly old-fashioned "hold on!" (from {待|ま}つ); 〜な at the end of
his lines is an older man's soft sentence ending (lesson 25). お{父|とう}さん here is Misaki's father,
the grandfather's son: Japanese families often call each other by the name the youngest would use.
{転送|てんそう}する = to forward (lesson 24). {迷|まよ}う = to be unsure, to get lost (N4, now with lesson
9's kanji).

## Reading: an email from the systems team

An office email, in the です/ます style. Notice how the writer passes on the boss's instructions.

> {件名|けんめい}：パソコンの{更新|こうしん}について
>
> {社員|しゃいん}の{皆|みな}さん
>
> システム{係|がかり}の{木村|きむら}です。{来週|らいしゅう}の{月曜日|げつようび}から、{会社|かいしゃ}のパソコンのソフトを{最新|さいしん}のものに{更新|こうしん}することになりました。{部長|ぶちょう}から、{全員|ぜんいん}に{次|つぎ}のことを{伝|つた}えるように{言|い}われましたので、お{知|し}らせします。
>
> まず、{金曜日|きんようび}の{夕方|ゆうがた}までに、{大切|たいせつ}なファイルを{保存|ほぞん}しておいてください。{更新|こうしん}の{途中|とちゅう}で、パソコンが{何回|なんかい}か{再起動|さいきどう}します。{画面|がめん}に{何|なに}が{表示|ひょうじ}されても、でんげんは{切|き}らないようにしてください。
>
> {次|つぎ}に、{月曜日|げつようび}の{朝|あさ}パソコンを{起動|きどう}すると、{新|あたら}しいパスワードを{入力|にゅうりょく}するように{表示|ひょうじ}されます。パスワードは、このメールに{付|つ}けた{説明書|せつめいしょ}の{通|とお}りに{作|つく}ってください。{前|まえ}と{同|おな}じパスワードは{使|つか}えません。
>
> また、{更新|こうしん}の{後|あと}は、{音量|おんりょう}や{通知|つうち}のせっていが{元|もと}に{戻|もど}ってしまうことがあります。その{場合|ばあい}は、それぞれで{直|なお}していただきたいと{思|おも}います。
>
> {分|わ}からないことがあったら、{内線|ないせん}205{番|ばん}までお{電話|でんわ}ください。ただ、{月曜日|げつようび}の{午前中|ごぜんちゅう}は{電話|でんわ}が{多|おお}くなりそうなので、{急|いそ}がない{質問|しつもん}はメールで{送|おく}っていただけると{助|たす}かります。
>
> よろしくお{願|ねが}いします。

{係|かかり} (がかり after a word) = the person or section in charge (lesson 11's kanji); {全員|ぜんいん} =
everyone, all members; {途中|とちゅう} = in the middle of (lesson 1); それぞれ = each (person); {直|なお}す
= to fix, to put right; {内線|ないせん} = extension (lesson 24); ただ = but, only.

<summary>Translation</summary>

Subject: Updating the computers

To all staff,

This is Kimura from the systems team. From next Monday, we'll be updating the software on the
company computers to the latest version. The department head has asked me to pass the following
on to everyone, so here it is.

First, please save your important files by Friday evening. During the update, your computer will
restart several times. Whatever appears on the screen, please don't switch it off.

Next, on Monday morning, when you start your computer, it will ask you to enter a new password.
Please make the password as described in the manual attached to this email. You can't use the
same password as before.

Also, after the update, settings such as the volume and notifications may go back to how they
were. If that happens, I'd ask you to change them back yourselves.

If there's anything you don't understand, please call extension 205. However, there will
probably be a lot of calls on Monday morning, so it would help if you could send questions that
aren't urgent by email.

Thank you.

</details>

## Say it

```speak
{明日|あした}{早|はや}く{来|く}るように{言|い}われました。
= I was told to come early tomorrow.
{田中|たなか}さんに、{電話|でんわ}するように{伝|つた}えてください。
= Please tell Tanaka to call.
{説明書|せつめいしょ}の{通|とお}りにやってみてください。
= Please try doing it as the manual says.
{予定|よてい}{通|どお}りに{終|お}わりました。
= It finished as planned.
{皆|みな}さんにも{手伝|てつだ}っていただきたいと{思|おも}います。
= I'd like to ask all of you to help as well.
{試験|しけん}に{合格|ごうかく}できますように。
= Please let me pass the exam.
```

## Common mistakes

- Politeness before ように: ×{来|き}てくださいように{言|い}われた. Use the dictionary form:
  {来|く}るように{言|い}われた.
- ように for a statement: ×{彼|かれ}は{来|く}るように{言|い}った for "He said he'd come". That's と:
  {来|く}ると{言|い}った. 〜ように{言|い}う only reports a request or instruction.
- Mixing up the two people. {先生|せんせい}に{来|く}るように{言|い}われた: the teacher told *me*.
  {先生|せんせい}に{来|く}るように{言|い}った: I told the teacher.
- 〜{通|とお}り after a noun without の: ×{説明書|せつめいしょ}{通|とお}りに read とおりに. Directly after a
  noun it's {通|どお}り ({説明書|せつめいしょ}{通|どお}りに); with の, {通|とお}り.
- 〜ていただきたいです straight to a superior: it states your wish. Ask: 〜ていただけませんか.
- {閉|と}じる for a door: {窓|まど}を{閉|し}めてください, not ×{閉|と}じてください.

## Key points

- Verb (dictionary / ない form) + ように + {言|い}う, {頼|たの}む, {伝|つた}える, {注意|ちゅうい}する: reports a
  request. ください and ます drop out. と reports statements.
- 〜てもらいたい ≈ 〜てほしい; 〜ていただきたい is the humble version, a stated wish, so soften it with
  と{思|おも}います or ask with 〜ていただけませんか.
- Noun + の{通|とお}りに, noun + {通|どお}りに, verb + {通|とお}りに: just as. その{通|とお}りです: exactly.
- 〜ますように: a wish or prayer, usually with ます.
- New kanji: 機 信 報 保 押 再 戻 閉 返 続 付 変 更.
