questions.explanation: お{忙|いそが}しいところすみません apologizes for taking your time, so you reassure the speaker: いいえ、だいじょうぶですよ. Apologizing for being busy turns the meaning round, and the other two answer thanks and questions about your health.

questions.topic: ところに and ところを
questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: Just as I was about to go out, a friend came round.
questions.explanation: 〜ようとしているところに: just as I was about to. The arrival comes after it. ところを would need a verb of seeing or catching.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: I lent him a book and never got it back.
questions.explanation: 〜たきり + a negative: {貸|か}したきり、{返|かえ}してもらっていません. 〜てもらっていない is "haven't had it done for me (yet)". The two objects ({彼|かれ}に, {本|ほん}を) can come in either order.

questions.stem:
Read the recipe and answer.

{焼|や}きおにぎり（{二人分|ふたりぶん}）

ご{飯|はん}{二杯|にはい}、しょうゆ{大|おお}さじ{一杯|いっぱい}、さとう{小|こ}さじ{半分|はんぶん}

① ご{飯|はん}が{熱|あつ}いうちに、{丸|まる}くにぎります。

② しょうゆとさとうをまぜておきます。

③ フライパンを{中火|ちゅうび}で{熱|ねっ}して、おにぎりを{焼|や}きます。

④ {両面|りょうめん}が{焼|や}けたところに、②をぬって、もう{一度|いちど}さっと{焼|や}きます。

⑤ {焼|や}きたてがおいしいですが、{冷|さ}めてもおいしく{食|た}べられます。

When do you brush on the soy sauce mixture?
choices: While the rice is still hot.
After the rice balls have cooled.
questions.explanation: ④ {両面|りょうめん}が{焼|や}けたところに、②をぬって: once both sides are done, brush on the mixture from step ② and grill them briefly again. Shaping the rice while it's hot is step ①.

questions.topic: につれて and にしたがって
questions.stem: {年|とし}を{取|と}る___、{朝|あさ}{早|はや}く{目|め}が{覚|さ}めるようになりました。 (As I've got older, I've started waking up early.)
questions.explanation: "As A changes, B changes" is 〜につれて: getting older brings a change in when you wake up. について is "about", にとって "for, from the viewpoint of", and によって "depending on, by means of" (module 3).

questions.topic: とともに and 一方だ
questions.stem: {物|もの}の{値段|ねだん}は{上|あ}がる___。 (Prices just keep going up.)
questions.explanation: Dictionary form + {一方|いっぽう}だ: keeps on going in one direction, usually for the worse. {上|あ}がるところだ is "is about to go up", つもりだ is a person's intention, and ことだ gives advice.

questions.stem: この{本|ほん}は、___、おもしろくなります。 (The more you read this book, the more interesting it gets.)
questions.explanation: "The more…, the more…" is the ば form + the dictionary form + ほど: {読|よ}めば{読|よ}むほど. たら, と and ても can't make this pattern.

questions.stem: {部屋|へや}は___いいです。 (The bigger the room, the better.)
choices: {広|ひろ}いなら{広|ひろ}いほど
{広|ひろ}ければ{広|ひろ}いほど
questions.explanation: An い-adjective's ば form is 〜ければ: {広|ひろ}ければ{広|ひろ}いほど. ×{広|ひろ}いば isn't a form, くて is the て form, and なら is for な-adjectives ({静|しず}かなら{静|しず}かなほど).

questions.topic: につれて and にしたがって
questions.stem: {係|かかり}の{人|ひと}の{指示|しじ}___、{外|そと}に{出|で}てください。 (Please go outside following the staff's instructions.)
questions.explanation: "Following (an instruction)" is にしたがって. につれて and とともに are about changes happening together, and ほど is degree; none of them can mean "in accordance with".

questions.topic: につれて and にしたがって
questions.stem: Which sentence is natural?
choices: {年|とし}を{取|と}るにつれて、{旅行|りょこう}しましょう。
{明日|あした}は{寒|さむ}くなる{一方|いっぽう}です。
{人口|じんこう}が{減|へ}るにつれて、{店|みせ}も{少|すく}なくなりました。
{説明|せつめい}につれて、{書|か}いてください。
questions.explanation: Two changes moving together: the population falls, and the shops become fewer. After につれて a suggestion (〜ましょう) doesn't fit, 〜{一方|いっぽう}だ needs a change that keeps going (not one cold day), and "following the explanation" is {説明|せつめい}にしたがって.

questions.topic: とともに and 一方だ
questions.stem: What does this sentence mean? {大学|だいがく}の{卒業|そつぎょう}とともに、ふるさとに{帰|かえ}りました。
choices: When I graduated from university, I went back to my hometown.
I went back to my hometown with my university friends.
I went back to my hometown so that I could graduate.
I will go back to my hometown after graduating.
questions.explanation: After an event, とともに is "at the same time as": on graduating, I went home. "With my friends" would need people before とともに ({友|とも}だちとともに), and the verb is past, so it isn't a plan.

questions.stem: {学生|がくせい}の{三分|さんぶん}の{一|いち}が{留学生|りゅうがくせい}です。 How many of the students are international students?
questions.explanation: 〜{分|ぶん}の〜 is a fraction with the bottom number first: {三分|さんぶん}の{一|いち} is one third. Thirty per cent would be {三割|さんわり} or {三十|さんじゅう}パーセント.

questions.stem: {子供|こども}の{数|かず}の___で、{村|むら}の{小学校|しょうがっこう}がなくなりました。
questions.explanation: A school closes because the number of children has gone down: {減少|げんしょう} (decrease). {増加|ぞうか} is the opposite, {平和|へいわ} is peace, and {共通|きょうつう} is "in common".

questions.stem: Which is closest in meaning? {住民|じゅうみん}の{大半|たいはん}が{反対|はんたい}しています。
choices: ほとんどの{住民|じゅうみん}が{反対|はんたい}しています。
{一部|いちぶ}の{住民|じゅうみん}が{反対|はんたい}しています。
{住民|じゅうみん}{全員|ぜんいん}が{反対|はんたい}しています。
{住民|じゅうみん}の{半分|はんぶん}だけが{反対|はんたい}しています。
questions.explanation: {大半|たいはん} is "the greater part, most", so ほとんど is closest. {一部|いちぶ} is only some, {全員|ぜんいん} is everyone, and {半分|はんぶん}だけ is just half.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses {平気|へいき} correctly?
choices: {平気|へいき}な{土地|とち}に{家|いえ}を{建|た}てました。
この{国|くに}は{戦争|せんそう}がなくて{平気|へいき}です。
{寒|さむ}いのは{平気|へいき}ですから、コートはいりません。
{今日|きょう}は{平気|へいき}なので、{会社|かいしゃ}に{行|い}きます。
questions.explanation: {平気|へいき} is "fine with it, not bothered": the cold doesn't bother me. Flat land is {平|たい}らな{土地|とち}, a country without war is {平和|へいわ}, and a working day is {平日|へいじつ}.

questions.stem: How is 現在 read? 現在、この{町|まち}の{人口|じんこう}は{三万人|さんまんにん}です。
questions.explanation: {現在|げんざい} (at present): 現 is ゲン, with a voiced げ, and 在 is ザイ. あらわ is the kun reading in {現|あらわ}れる, which isn't used in compounds like this.

questions.stem: Which kanji is right? この{町|まち}の{人口|じんこう}は［へって］います。
questions.explanation: へる (decrease) is 減る. 増 is read ふ(える) or ま(す), 低 is ひく(い), and 少 is すく(ない) or すこ(し); none of them is へる.

questions.stem: How is 平等 read?
questions.explanation: {平等|びょうどう} (equality) is one of the few words where 平 is read ビョウ; elsewhere it's usually ヘイ ({平和|へいわ}, {平日|へいじつ}). 等 is ドウ here.

questions.stem: Listen. What is happening to the town's population?

audio.text: このまちのじんこうは、へるいっぽうです。

questions.explanation: {人口|じんこう}は{減|へ}る{一方|いっぽう}です: it just keeps going down. 〜{一方|いっぽう}だ is a change that keeps going in one direction.

questions.stem: Listen. What share of the members are women?

audio.text: かいいんのさんわりがじょせいです。

questions.explanation: {会員|かいいん}の{三割|さんわり}が{女性|じょせい}です: 〜{割|わり} counts tenths, so {三割|さんわり} is 30%.

questions.stem: Listen. Which is the best reply?

audio.text: さいきん、もののねだんがあがるいっぽうですね。

choices: {本当|ほんとう}ですね。{困|こま}りますね。
はい、やすくなりましたね。
いいえ、あがるいっぽうです。
questions.explanation: "Prices just keep going up these days, don't they?" The natural reply agrees and sympathizes. やすくなりました contradicts it, いいえ followed by the same words makes no sense, and おかげさまで answers a question about your health or success.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: The more you practise, the better you get.
questions.explanation: ば form + dictionary form + ほど: {練習|れんしゅう}すればするほど, then the result. たら can't make the "the more…" pattern.

questions.topic: につれて and にしたがって
questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: As the population falls, the number of shops is falling too.
questions.explanation: The driving change comes first with につれて, then the change that follows it. について ("about") doesn't link two changes.

questions.stem:
Read and answer.

{市|し}が{二十代|にじゅうだい}から{七十代|ななじゅうだい}の{市民|しみん}{千人|せんにん}に{聞|き}いたところ、「この{町|まち}が{好|す}き」と{答|こた}えた{人|ひと}は{全体|ぜんたい}の{七割|ななわり}でした。{年代|ねんだい}{別|べつ}に{見|み}ると、{年代|ねんだい}が{上|うえ}になるほど「{好|す}き」の{割合|わりあい}が{高|たか}く、{七十代|ななじゅうだい}では{九割|きゅうわり}でした。しかし、{二十代|にじゅうだい}では{半数|はんすう}だけで、「{仕事|しごと}が{少|すく}ない」「{遊|あそ}ぶ{所|ところ}がない」という{声|こえ}が{多|おお}かったそうです。{市|し}はこの{結果|けっか}を{見|み}て、{若|わか}い{人|ひと}のための{仕事|しごと}を{増|ふ}やすことにしました。

Which is true?
choices: Ninety per cent of all the people asked like the town.
Most people in their twenties like the town.
The older the age group, the higher the share who like the town.
Fewer older people answered than younger people.
questions.explanation: {年代|ねんだい}が{上|うえ}になるほど「{好|す}き」の{割合|わりあい}が{高|たか}く: the older the group, the higher the share. Ninety per cent is only for people in their seventies (overall it's {七割|ななわり}, 70%), and in their twenties it's only {半数|はんすう}, half. Nothing is said about how many of each age answered.

questions.topic: ようとする and ようとしない
questions.stem: {家|いえ}を___とき、{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}りだしました。 (Just as I was about to leave the house, it started to rain.)
questions.explanation: "Just as I was about to" is the volitional + とした + とき: {出|で}ようとしたとき. {出|で}たふり is pretending to have left, {出|で}たつもり is thinking you'd left, and {出|で}ることにした is deciding to leave, which isn't "about to".

questions.topic: ようとする and ようとしない
questions.stem: {父|ちち}は{歯|は}が{痛|いた}いのに、{歯医者|はいしゃ}に{行|い}こうと___。 (Dad has toothache, but he won't go to the dentist.)
questions.explanation: "Won't, refuses to" is the volitional + としない: {行|い}こうとしません. と{言|い}いません would be "doesn't say 'let's go'", and なりません and みません don't follow the volitional.

questions.stem: ドアにかぎをかけた___でしたが、かけていませんでした。 (I thought I'd locked the door, but I hadn't.)
questions.explanation: 〜たつもり is what you believed you had done: "I thought I'd locked it". ふり is pretending (and needs をする), ところでした would be "I had just locked it", and ことでした doesn't fit.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I meant to go to bed early (but I didn't)"?
choices: {早|はや}く{寝|ね}たつもりでした。
{早|はや}く{寝|ね}たふりをしました。
{早|はや}く{寝|ね}ることにしています。
{早|はや}く{寝|ね}るつもりでした。
questions.explanation: Dictionary form + つもりだった is an intention that didn't come true. {寝|ね}たつもりでした is "I thought I'd gone to bed (or slept)", {寝|ね}たふり is pretending to be asleep, and {寝|ね}ることにしています is a rule you keep.

questions.topic: ふりをする and たことにする
questions.stem: {病気|びょうき}___ふりをして、{学校|がっこう}を{休|やす}みました。
questions.explanation: A noun takes の before ふり: {病気|びょうき}のふり. な is for な-adjectives ({元気|げんき}なふり), and だ and で don't go before ふり.

questions.topic: ふりをする and たことにする
questions.stem: {今|いま}の{話|はなし}は、{聞|き}かなかった___にします。 (I'll treat what you just said as something I never heard.)
questions.explanation: 〜なかったことにする: treat it as not having happened. ふり takes をする, not にする, and つもり and ところ don't make this pattern.

questions.topic: なるべく and わざと
questions.stem: {遠|とお}いところから、___お{見舞|みま}いに{来|き}てくれて、ありがとう。
questions.explanation: Thanking someone for going to the trouble is わざわざ. わざと is "on purpose" (as opposed to by accident), and it would sound as if the visit had a hidden motive. なるべく is "as much as possible", and たまに is "now and then".

questions.topic: なるべく and わざと
questions.stem: {医者|いしゃ}：「___お{酒|さけ}を{飲|の}まないようにしてください。」 (Please try not to drink alcohol as far as you can.)
questions.explanation: なるべく + 〜ないようにする: avoid it as far as possible. わざと and わざわざ are about intention and effort, and しょっちゅう (all the time) contradicts the advice.

questions.stem: {昨日|きのう}は{三時間|さんじかん}しか{寝|ね}ていないので、{今日|きょう}は___です。
questions.explanation: Three hours' sleep means you haven't slept enough: {寝不足|ねぶそく}. {満腹|まんぷく} is a full stomach, {運動不足|うんどうぶそく} is not enough exercise, and {息切|いきぎ}れ is being out of breath.

questions.stem: Which is closest in meaning? {今日|きょう}は{体調|たいちょう}がよくないです。
choices: {今日|きょう}は{具合|ぐあい}が{悪|わる}いです。
{今日|きょう}は{天気|てんき}が{悪|わる}いです。
{今日|きょう}は{仕事|しごと}がうまくいきません。
{今日|きょう}は{時間|じかん}がありません。
questions.explanation: {体調|たいちょう} is how your body feels, so {体調|たいちょう}がよくない is "I don't feel well", the same as {具合|ぐあい}が{悪|わる}い. The others are about the weather, work and time.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses {痛|いた}む correctly?
choices: {頭|あたま}を{痛|いた}んでいます。
{雨|あめ}の{日|ひ}は、{古|ふる}いけががよく{痛|いた}みます。
{痛|いた}む{薬|くすり}を{飲|の}みました。
{転|ころ}んで、{足|あし}を{痛|いた}みました。
questions.explanation: {痛|いた}む is intransitive: the part that hurts is the subject (けがが{痛|いた}む). It doesn't take を, and a painkiller is {痛|いた}み{止|ど}め, not a "hurting medicine".

questions.stem: How is 頭痛 read? {朝|あさ}から頭痛がします。
questions.explanation: {頭痛|ずつう} (headache): 頭 is ズ here, and 痛 is ツウ. トウ is another on'yomi of 頭 ({先頭|せんとう}), but not in this word.

questions.stem: Which kanji is right? {昨日|きのう}の{夜|よる}はよく［ねむれ］ませんでした。
questions.explanation: ねむる (to sleep) is 眠る, so ねむれ is 眠れ. 寝 is read ね ({寝|ね}る, to go to bed), 民 is the part on the right of 眠 but means "people", and 休 is やす(む).

questions.stem: How is 息子 read?
questions.explanation: {息子|むすこ} (son) is a special reading: the word is read むすこ, whatever the kanji would normally give. 息 alone is いき (breath).

questions.stem: Listen. What happened?

audio.text: くすりをのんだつもりでしたが、まだのんでいませんでした。

choices: The speaker took the medicine twice.
The speaker has decided not to take the medicine.
The speaker thought they had taken the medicine, but hadn't.
The speaker is going to take the medicine now.
questions.explanation: {飲|の}んだつもりでした: "I thought I had taken it", followed by まだ{飲|の}んでいませんでした, "I still hadn't taken it".

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker's brother doing?

audio.text: おとうとは、ねているふりをしています。

choices: Just about to go to sleep.
Trying to sleep, but he can't.
questions.explanation: {寝|ね}ているふりをしています: he's pretending to be asleep. "About to sleep" would be {寝|ね}ようとしています.

questions.stem: Listen. Which is the best reply?

audio.text: きのうから、あたまがいたいんです。

choices: おめでとうございます。
だいじょうぶですか。{薬|くすり}はありますか。
questions.explanation: "I've had a headache since yesterday": the natural reply shows concern. The other three are set phrases for celebrations, leaving home and finishing a meal.

questions.topic: ようとする and ようとしない
questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: Dad just won't go to the doctor.
questions.explanation: The volitional + としない: {行|い}こうとしません, "won't go". どうしても (no matter what) strengthens it and can come in several places before the verb.

questions.topic: ふりをする and たことにする
questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: I actually knew, but I pretended not to.
questions.explanation: 〜ないふりをする: pretend not to. つもり doesn't take をする; it's つもりだ or つもりで.

questions.stem:
Read the clinic's notice and answer.

さくら{内科|ないか}からのお{知|し}らせ

{十二月|じゅうにがつ}から、インフルエンザのよぼうちゅうしゃを{始|はじ}めます。{予約|よやく}が{必要|ひつよう}ですので、お{電話|でんわ}か{受付|うけつけ}で{予約|よやく}してください。{当日|とうじつ}、{熱|ねつ}が{三十七度|さんじゅうななど}{五分|ごぶ}{以上|いじょう}ある{方|かた}は、ちゅうしゃができません。また、{体調|たいちょう}が{悪|わる}いときは、{無理|むり}をしないで{日|ひ}を{変|か}えてください。{料金|りょうきん}は{一回|いっかい}{三千五百円|さんぜんごひゃくえん}です。{六十五歳|ろくじゅうごさい}{以上|いじょう}の{方|かた}は、{料金|りょうきん}の{一部|いちぶ}を{市|し}が{払|はら}います。

What should you do if you feel unwell on the day of your appointment?
choices: Come anyway and tell the reception desk.
Change the appointment to another day.
questions.explanation: {体調|たいちょう}が{悪|わる}いときは、{無理|むり}をしないで{日|ひ}を{変|か}えてください: if you're unwell, don't push yourself; change the day. The reception desk is only for making bookings, and the city helps pay only for people aged 65 and over.

questions.stem: What is intonation, as this lesson uses the word?
choices: The high and low pitch inside each word
The rise and fall over a whole phrase, which shows the speaker's attitude
The difference between long and short vowels
How loudly each syllable is said
questions.explanation: Intonation is the melody of the whole phrase: a rise to ask, a fall to state. The high and low inside a word is pitch accent (N4 lesson 05h1), which stays in place under the intonation.

questions.stem: A friend says 「コーヒー、{飲|の}まない？」 with a rise at the end. What do they mean?
questions.explanation: A negative question with a rise is a friendly offer or invitation. Said with a fall, the same words would be a statement: "I'm not drinking (coffee)". "Did you drink it?" would be past: {飲|の}んだ？

questions.stem: Your colleague keeps saying 「はい、はい」 while you explain a plan. What does it most likely mean?
questions.explanation: Aizuchi like はい and うん mean "I'm following you", not "I agree". The listener may still disagree when you've finished.

questions.stem: Why is it especially important to give aizuchi on the phone?
choices: Because it's rude to say はい face to face.
Because silence can sound as if the line has gone dead or you disapprove.
Because phone calls must be short.
Because aizuchi are only used on the phone.
questions.explanation: On the phone there's no nodding, so short signals like はい and ええ show you're still there and listening. A long silence makes the speaker ask もしもし？ or {聞|き}いてる？

questions.stem: You want to ask a stranger the way. Which filler is the most natural way to begin?
choices: なんか、{駅|えき}はどこですか。
まあ、{駅|えき}はどこですか。
さすが、{駅|えき}はどこですか。
あのう、すみません。{駅|えき}はどこですか。
questions.explanation: あのう gently warns the listener that a question is coming, and it's polite. なんか is a casual "like", まあ softens an answer you're giving, and さすが is praise.

questions.stem: 「{仕事|しごと}、どう？」「___、なんとかやってるよ。」 Which filler softens the answer ("well, I'm getting by")?
questions.explanation: まあ is "well, sort of": it keeps the answer from sounding too strong. へえ and なるほど are a listener's reactions, and あのう opens a question or request.

questions.stem: In fast speech, 「{山田|やまだ}って{人|ひと}、{知|し}ってる？」 What does って stand for here?
questions.explanation: Before a noun, って is a short という: {山田|やまだ}という{人|ひと}, "a person called Yamada". And {知|し}ってる is {知|し}っている. At the end of a sentence, 〜って can stand for と{言|い}った (he said…).

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker mean?

audio.text: ちょっとまってて。すぐいくから。

choices: I waited a while, but I'm going now.
I'll be a little late, so go ahead.
Wait a moment, I'm coming right away.
questions.explanation: {待|ま}ってて is the fast form of {待|ま}っていて, "wait (there)", and すぐ{行|い}くから is "because I'm coming right away".

questions.stem: Listen to the listener's reply. What is the listener expressing?

audio.text: へえ、そうなんですか。

choices: Interest and surprise at something new
questions.explanation: へえ shows surprise or interest, and そうなんですか is "oh, is that so?" for new information. If they already knew, they might say そうですね; if they didn't hear, え？ or すみません、もう{一度|いちど}.

questions.stem: Listen. Which is the best reply?

audio.text: あのう、ちょっとよろしいですか。

choices: はい、よろしくお{願|ねが}いします。
はい、{何|なん}でしょうか。
questions.explanation: ちょっとよろしいですか is "have you got a moment?", so the natural answer is はい、{何|なん}でしょうか (yes, what is it?). よろしくお{願|ねが}いします is said when meeting or asking a favour, and どういたしまして answers thanks.

questions.stem:
Read and answer.

{会議|かいぎ}で、{相手|あいて}の{会社|かいしゃ}の{人|ひと}がずっと「はい、はい」と{言|い}いながら{聞|き}いていたので、{私|わたし}は{計画|けいかく}に{賛成|さんせい}してくれたと{思|おも}いました。でも{次|つぎ}の{日|ひ}、「{今回|こんかい}はちょっと……」というメールが{来|き}て、びっくりしました。{日本人|にほんじん}の{友|とも}だちに{話|はな}すと、「はいは『{聞|き}いています』という{意味|いみ}だよ」と{教|おし}えてくれました。

({賛成|さんせい}: agreement; {今回|こんかい}はちょっと……: "this time it's a bit…", a polite no)

Why was the writer surprised?
choices: The writer thought はい meant agreement, but the plan was turned down.
The other company agreed to the plan straight away.
The writer's friend didn't know what はい meant.
questions.explanation: The writer took the repeated はい as agreement ({賛成|さんせい}してくれたと{思|おも}いました), but the next day came a polite refusal. The friend explains that はい here means "I'm listening".

questions.stem:
Read and answer.

{妹|いもうと}は{話|はな}すとき、「なんか」をよく{使|つか}います。「なんか、お{腹|なか}すいた」「なんか、この{店|みせ}いいね」と、{一日|いちにち}に{何十回|なんじっかい}も{言|い}います。{来週|らいしゅう}、{妹|いもうと}はアルバイトのめんせつがあります。{母|はは}は「めんせつでは、なんかを{使|つか}わないほうがいいよ」と{言|い}いました。

(めんせつ: interview)

Why does the mother give this advice?
choices: Because なんか is rude to older people.
Because なんか is a casual filler that sounds out of place in an interview.
Because なんか can only be used in writing.
questions.explanation: As a filler, なんか is a casual "like, kind of": fine with friends, but it can sound unprepared in a job interview. It isn't rude in itself, and it's a word of speech, not writing.

questions.stem: What is the main difference between a せんとう and an {温泉|おんせん}?
choices: A せんとう is only for men.
An {温泉|おんせん} is always outdoors.
A せんとう is a neighbourhood public bath; an {温泉|おんせん} uses water that comes from the ground.
A せんとう is always free.
questions.explanation: A せんとう is a public bath in town; an {温泉|おんせん} is a hot spring. Both have men's and women's sides, many {温泉|おんせん} also have indoor baths, and せんとう charge a fee set by the prefecture.

questions.stem: What should you do before you get into the {湯船|ゆぶね}?
choices: Pour water over yourself and wash.
Put your towel into the water.
Put on a pair of slippers.
questions.explanation: First かけ{湯|ゆ}, then wash at the washing area, and only then get into the bath. The towel stays out of the water, and milk is for afterwards.

questions.stem: Where should your small towel be while you're soaking in the bath?
choices: In the water, around your body
Under the water, so it stays warm
On your head or by the side of the bath
questions.explanation: Towels never go in the bath water. People put them on their heads or on the edge. You keep the small towel with you, to wipe yourself down before going back to the changing room.

questions.stem: {長|なが}く{入|はい}りすぎて、のぼせてしまいました。 What happened?
choices: I stayed in too long and felt faint from the heat.
questions.explanation: のぼせる is to feel dizzy and hot in the face from staying in hot water too long. Get out, sit down and drink some water.

questions.stem: A sign says 「いれずみのある{方|かた}は、ごえんりょください。」 What does it mean?
choices: People with tattoos should please refrain from using the bath.
People with tattoos must pay more.
Please show your tattoos at the desk.
questions.explanation: ごえんりょください is a polite "please refrain": people with tattoos are asked not to come in. えんりょ (holding back) is from N4.

questions.stem: How is 男湯 read?
questions.explanation: {男湯|おとこゆ} (the men's bath) uses two kun readings: おとこ + ゆ. The women's bath is {女湯|おんなゆ}.

questions.stem: Which statement about tattoos and baths in Japan is the most accurate?
choices: Rules vary a lot from place to place, so it's best to check first.
Every bath in Japan refuses people with tattoos.
Every bath in Japan welcomes people with tattoos.
Only visitors from abroad are allowed in with tattoos.
questions.explanation: Many hot-spring hotels refuse tattoos, many せんとう don't, and some allow small tattoos under a sticker. Because it varies, read the notice or ask before you pay.

questions.stem: Listen to the announcement. What are bathers asked to do?

audio.text: タオルは、ゆぶねにいれないでください。

choices: Keep their towels out of the bath water.
Use the towels by the bath.
Leave their towels in the changing room.
questions.explanation: タオルは{湯船|ゆぶね}に{入|い}れないでください: please don't put towels in the bath.

questions.stem: Listen. Which curtain should a man use today?

audio.text: きょうは、あかいのれんがおとこゆです。

choices: Neither: the men's bath is closed.
questions.explanation: {今日|きょう}は、{赤|あか}いのれんが{男湯|おとこゆ}です: today the red curtain is the men's bath. Some baths swap the sides on different days, which is why you should read the kanji, not just the colour.

questions.stem:
Read the notice and answer.

ひまわり{湯|ゆ}のごあんない

・{午後|ごご}{三時|さんじ}から{夜|よる}{十一時|じゅういちじ}まで。{月曜日|げつようび}はお{休|やす}みです。

・{大人|おとな}{五百五十円|ごひゃくごじゅうえん}、{中学生|ちゅうがくせい}{四百円|よんひゃくえん}、{小学生|しょうがくせい}{二百円|にひゃくえん}。

・タオルはいちまい{百円|ひゃくえん}でお{貸|か}しします。

・サウナは{別|べつ}に{二百円|にひゃくえん}かかります。

An adult rents one towel and uses the sauna. How much do they pay in all?
questions.explanation: {大人|おとな}{五百五十円|ごひゃくごじゅうえん} + towel {百円|ひゃくえん} + sauna {二百円|にひゃくえん} = 850 yen. {別|べつ}に means "separately, on top".

questions.stem:
Read and answer.

{友|とも}だちと{山|やま}の{温泉|おんせん}に{行|い}った。ろてんぶろは{気持|きも}ちがよかったが、{話|はな}しているうちに{長|なが}く{入|はい}りすぎて、のぼせてしまった。だついじょで{少|すこ}し{休|やす}んで、{冷|つめ}たい{水|みず}を{飲|の}んだら、{元気|げんき}になった。{次|つぎ}は{時間|じかん}を{決|き}めて{入|はい}ろうと{思|おも}う。

What happened to the writer?
choices: They got cold in the outdoor bath.
They talked so long that they missed the last bus.
They lost track of time while chatting, stayed in too long and felt faint.
They weren't allowed into the outdoor bath.
questions.explanation: {話|はな}しているうちに{長|なが}く{入|はい}りすぎて、のぼせてしまった: while chatting, they stayed in too long and got light-headed (lesson 1's 〜ているうちに). Rest and cold water helped.

questions.stem: Which of these is good manners at a public bath?
choices: Wiping yourself down before going back to the changing room
Washing your hair in the bath itself
Swimming a few lengths when the bath is empty
Putting your towel in the water to keep it warm
questions.explanation: Wiping yourself down keeps the changing room floor dry. Washing happens at the washing area, never in the bath, and towels stay out of the water. No swimming, even in an empty bath.

questions.topic: おかげで and せいで
questions.stem: Choose the best word: {友|とも}だちが{手伝|てつだ}ってくれた___、{雪|ゆき}かきが{早|はや}く{終|お}わった。
questions.explanation: The friend's help led to a good result, so the grateful おかげで fits: {手伝|てつだ}ってくれたおかげで. せいで blames a cause for a bad result, and finishing early isn't bad. ことから reasons from evidence or explains a name, and わけで doesn't join a cause to its result like this.

questions.topic: おかげで and せいで
questions.stem: Choose the correct form: {台風|たいふう}___、{旅行|りょこう}が{中止|ちゅうし}になってしまった。
questions.explanation: After a noun, せい takes の, like any noun: {台風|たいふう}のせいで. A bare noun + せいで is missing の, な is only for な-adjectives ({静|しず}かなせいで), and のせいに goes with する ("blame it on"), not with a result like {中止|ちゅうし}になった.

questions.stem: Which sentence is natural?
choices: {雨|あめ}なので、{家|いえ}にいてください。
{雨|あめ}のせいで、{家|いえ}にいてください。
{雨|あめ}のおかげで、{家|いえ}にいましょう。
{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}ったことから、{家|いえ}にいてください。
questions.explanation: A request can follow ので: {雨|あめ}なので、{家|いえ}にいてください. おかげで and せいで report a result that has happened, so they can't be followed by a request or an invitation, and ことから reasons from a fact ("from the fact that…") rather than giving a reason for a request.

questions.stem: In which sentence does ため mean "because" rather than "in order to" or "for"?
choices: {試験|しけん}に{合格|ごうかく}するために、{毎日|まいにち}{勉強|べんきょう}している。
{健康|けんこう}のために、{毎朝|まいあさ}{歩|ある}いている。
{大雪|おおゆき}のため、{電車|でんしゃ}が{止|と}まっています。
{家族|かぞく}のために、{料理|りょうり}を{作|つく}った。
questions.explanation: Nobody chooses heavy snow, and the trains being stopped is its result: this is cause ため, "owing to the heavy snow". The other three are N4's purpose ため: studying in order to pass, walking for your health, cooking for your family. Each has a chosen action after ため.

questions.stem: Choose the best words: {秋|あき}になると{山|やま}が{赤|あか}くなる___、「{赤山|あかやま}」と{呼|よ}ばれている。
questions.explanation: The sentence explains how the mountain got its name, which is the classic job of ことから: "because it turns red, it's called Red Mountain". せいで and おかげで judge a result as bad or good, which a name isn't, and のに (although) would make the name a surprise.

questions.stem: Choose the best word: {何度|なんど}も{話|はな}し{合|あ}った___、{全員|ぜんいん}が{賛成|さんせい}した。
questions.explanation: The た form + {結果|けっか} gives the outcome of a process: "as a result of talking it over many times, everyone agreed". せいで would blame the talks for a bad result, ことから reasons from evidence, and うちに needs the dictionary or ている form ({話|はな}し{合|あ}っているうちに). {賛成|さんせい} (agreement) is lesson 28's word.

questions.stem: Choose the best word: {大雨|おおあめ}で{川|かわ}の{水|みず}が___、{町|まち}に{入|はい}ってきた。
questions.explanation: Water that comes over a river's banks into the town あふれる (overflows). こおる is to freeze, {積|つ}もる is what snow and dust do as they pile up, and {散|ち}る is what petals and leaves do as they fall.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses {倒|たお}れる correctly?
choices: {強|つよ}い{風|かぜ}が、{木|き}を{倒|たお}れた。
{強|つよ}い{風|かぜ}で、{木|き}が{倒|たお}れた。
{子供|こども}がコップを{倒|たお}れた。
{雪|ゆき}が{三十|さんじゅっ}センチ{倒|たお}れた。
questions.explanation: {倒|たお}れる is intransitive: the thing that falls is the subject, {木|き}が{倒|たお}れた. With を you need the transitive partner {倒|たお}す ({風|かぜ}が{木|き}を{倒|たお}した, {子供|こども}がコップを{倒|たお}した). Snow piling up is {積|つ}もる.

questions.topic: おかげで and せいで
questions.stem: What does this mean? {雨|あめ}のせいか、{今日|きょう}は{客|きゃく}が{少|すく}ない。
choices: Perhaps because of the rain, there are few customers today.
It's definitely the rain's fault that there are few customers today.
Thanks to the rain, there are few customers today.
Even though it's raining, there are few customers today.
questions.explanation: 〜せいか adds doubt: "maybe it's because of…". The speaker guesses that the rain is the cause. A sure cause would be {雨|あめ}のせいで, "thanks to" would be おかげで, and "even though" would be のに.

questions.stem: How is 吹雪 read in this sentence? {昨日|きのう}は吹雪で、{外|そと}に{出|で}られなかった。
questions.explanation: {吹雪|ふぶき} (snowstorm) is a special reading of the whole word: neither kanji is read like this anywhere else. The other choices put together ordinary readings of 吹 (ふ(く), スイ) and 雪 (ゆき, セツ).

questions.stem: Which kanji is は (leaf) in this sentence? {秋|あき}になると、___の{色|いろ}が{変|か}わる。
questions.explanation: The leaf is {葉|は}, with the grass shape on top. {歯|は} (tooth) sounds the same but is a different word, and {草|くさ} (grass) and {石|いし} (stone) are read differently.

questions.stem: How is 落 read in this word? 落とし物
questions.explanation: {落|お}とし{物|もの} (something dropped, N5's おとしもの) is 落 read お, with とし as okurigana: {落|お}とす (to drop). らく is its on'yomi, and おち and おと would put okurigana inside the kanji's reading.

questions.stem: Listen. Why was the trip cancelled?

audio.text: たいふうのせいで、りょこうがちゅうしになりました。

questions.explanation: {台風|たいふう}のせいで、{旅行|りょこう}が{中止|ちゅうし}になりました: "because of the typhoon, the trip was cancelled". せいで marks a cause with a bad result. Heavy snow would be {大雪|おおゆき}, and a power cut ていでん.

questions.stem: Listen. How does the speaker feel about what the friend did?

audio.text: ともだちがてつだってくれたおかげで、はやくおわりました。

choices: Annoyed: the friend got in the way
Grateful: the friend's help made it quicker
questions.explanation: {手伝|てつだ}ってくれたおかげで、{早|はや}く{終|お}わりました: "thanks to my friend helping, it was over quickly". おかげで and 〜てくれた both show gratitude. Annoyance would be せいで, and "maybe" would be せいか.

questions.stem: Listen to the station announcement. What is happening?

audio.text: おおあめのため、でんしゃがとまっております。

choices: Trains are running late because of strong wind.
Trains are running as normal despite the rain.
Trains are stopped because of heavy rain.
The station is closed for building work.
questions.explanation: {大雨|おおあめ}のため、{電車|でんしゃ}が{止|と}まっております: "owing to heavy rain, trains are stopped". ため is the formal "because" of announcements, and 〜ております is the polite 〜ています. Strong wind would be {強風|きょうふう}.

questions.topic: おかげで and せいで
questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: Thanks to the sun coming out, the snow melted quickly.
questions.explanation: The cause comes first, as a clause in the た form, then おかげで: {太陽|たいよう}が{出|で}たおかげで. The result follows: {雪|ゆき}が{早|はや}くとけた. {早|はや}く can also come before {雪|ゆき}が. せいで would blame the sun, but the snow melting is good news here. (とける = to melt.)

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: This town is called "Snow Country" because it gets so much snow.
questions.explanation: 〜ことから explains how a name came about: {雪|ゆき}が{多|おお}いことから、「{雪国|ゆきぐに}」と{呼|よ}ばれている. The topic この{町|まち}は can open the sentence or come after the ことから clause. おかげで would present the name as a lucky result.

questions.stem:
Read the school notice and answer.

{生徒|せいと}の{皆|みな}さんへ
{台風|たいふう}が{近|ちか}づいているため、{明日|あした}の{午前|ごぜん}は{休校|きゅうこう}とします。{午前|ごぜん}{十時|じゅうじ}に{大雨|おおあめ}や{強風|きょうふう}の{警報|けいほう}が{出|で}ていなければ、{午後|ごご}{一時|いちじ}までに{登校|とうこう}してください。{警報|けいほう}が{出|で}ている{場合|ばあい}は、{一日|いちにち}{休校|きゅうこう}です。{台風|たいふう}のえいきょうで{電車|でんしゃ}が{遅|おく}れることもあるので、{気|き}をつけて{来|き}てください。

({休校|きゅうこう} = school closure; {登校|とうこう}する = to come to school)

When should students come to school tomorrow?
choices: By 1 p.m., if no warning is in force at 10 a.m.
Not at all, whatever the weather
At 10 a.m., if the trains are running
questions.explanation: The morning is cancelled ({午前|ごぜん}は{休校|きゅうこう}). If there's no heavy rain or strong wind warning at 10 a.m. (〜{警報|けいほう}が{出|で}ていなければ), students come by 1 p.m. ({午後|ごご}{一時|いちじ}までに{登校|とうこう}). The notice mentions trains only to say they may be late. The first ため is the formal "because": the typhoon is the cause.

questions.stem:
Read the school notice again.

{生徒|せいと}の{皆|みな}さんへ
{台風|たいふう}が{近|ちか}づいているため、{明日|あした}の{午前|ごぜん}は{休校|きゅうこう}とします。{午前|ごぜん}{十時|じゅうじ}に{大雨|おおあめ}や{強風|きょうふう}の{警報|けいほう}が{出|で}ていなければ、{午後|ごご}{一時|いちじ}までに{登校|とうこう}してください。{警報|けいほう}が{出|で}ている{場合|ばあい}は、{一日|いちにち}{休校|きゅうこう}です。{台風|たいふう}のえいきょうで{電車|でんしゃ}が{遅|おく}れることもあるので、{気|き}をつけて{来|き}てください。

At 10 a.m. there is a strong wind warning. What happens?
questions.explanation: {警報|けいほう}が{出|で}ている{場合|ばあい}は、{一日|いちにち}{休校|きゅうこう}です: if a warning is in force, the school is closed for the whole day. Coming at 1 p.m. is only for the case with no warning. えいきょうで (because of the effects) is another neutral "because".

questions.stem: Match each pattern to what it adds.
choices: a cause with a good result
a cause with a bad result
questions.explanation: おかげで is grateful (good result), せいで blames (bad result), せいか guesses at a cause, ため is the neutral "because" of notices and the news, and ことから reasons from a fact or explains a name. "In order to" is the purpose ため, which the cause ため isn't.

questions.stem: Choose the best words: 「{田中|たなか}さんは{十年|じゅうねん}アメリカに{住|す}んでいたそうですよ。」「それで{英語|えいご}が{上手|じょうず}な___ね。」
questions.explanation: The new fact explains something the speaker had noticed, so it's わけだ: "so that's why his English is good". わけがない would deny it strongly ("there's no way"), わけではありません would deny it softly ("it's not that…"), and わけにはいきません is "can't, for social reasons".

questions.stem: Choose the best words: お{金|かね}がない___が、{高|たか}いものは{買|か}わないことにしている。
questions.explanation: The speaker denies the conclusion a listener might draw: "it's not that I have no money". That's わけではない. わけがない ("there's no way I have no money") is too strong and doesn't fit が…, わけにはいかない is about what you can't allow yourself to do, and わけだ would mean "so I have no money".

questions.stem: Choose the best words: 「{明日|あした}までに{十万円|じゅうまんえん}{貸|か}してくれない？」「そんなお{金|かね}、ある___よ！」
questions.explanation: The answer is a strong, emotional "no way": あるわけない (casual わけがない). あるわけだ would mean "so I've got it", あるわけにはいかない makes no sense with ある, and ことだ gives advice.

questions.stem: Which sentence is natural?
choices: {足|あし}が{痛|いた}くて、{歩|ある}くわけにはいかない。
{明日|あした}は{大事|だいじ}な{会議|かいぎ}があるから、{休|やす}むわけにはいかないだ。
{明日|あした}は{大事|だいじ}な{会議|かいぎ}があるから、{休|やす}むわけにはいかない。
{明日|あした}は{大事|だいじ}な{会議|かいぎ}があるから、{休|やす}まないわけにはいかない。
questions.explanation: わけにはいかない is "can't, because it wouldn't be right": with an important meeting, you can't take the day off. A sore foot is a physical inability, which needs the potential ({歩|ある}けない). わけにはいかない doesn't take だ, and {休|やす}まないわけにはいかない would mean "I have to take the day off", the opposite of what the meeting suggests.

questions.stem: Choose the best ending: {部長|ぶちょう}にさそわれたので、{飲|の}み{会|かい}に___。
choices: {行|い}かないわけにはいかない
questions.explanation: Being invited by the department head is a social reason to go: {行|い}かないわけにはいかない, "I can't not go" (so I have to). {行|い}くわけにはいかない says the opposite (I can't go), {行|い}かないわけだ would conclude that you don't go, and {行|い}くわけではない ("it's not that I go") doesn't follow from the invitation. (さそう = to invite.)

questions.stem: Which sentence means "Not all Japanese people use cash"?
choices: {日本人|にほんじん}がみんな{現金|げんきん}を{使|つか}うわけではない。
{日本人|にほんじん}はみんな{現金|げんきん}を{使|つか}わない。
{日本人|にほんじん}がみんな{現金|げんきん}を{使|つか}うわけがない。
{日本人|にほんじん}はみんな{現金|げんきん}を{使|つか}うわけだ。
questions.explanation: わけではない after みんな is partial negation: it denies "all", so some do and some don't. みんな…{使|つか}わない says nobody does, わけがない says it's impossible that everyone does (much stronger), and わけだ concludes that everyone does.

questions.stem: Choose the best word: 「{山田|やまだ}さん、{今日|きょう}は{休|やす}みだって。」「{昨日|きのう}、{雨|あめ}にぬれて{帰|かえ}ったからね。」「それで{休|やす}んだ___か。」
questions.explanation: The third speaker has just heard the reason and says "so that's why she's off": それで{休|やす}んだわけか (casual question-like ending, わけか). はず doesn't end a sentence with か like this, ものか means "as if (I would)!", and ことか is "how…!".

questions.stem: Choose the best word: {今月|こんげつ}は{支出|ししゅつ}が{収入|しゅうにゅう}より{多|おお}くて、___になってしまった。
questions.explanation: Spending ({支出|ししゅつ}) more than you earn ({収入|しゅうにゅう}) puts you in the red: {赤字|あかじ}. {黒字|くろじ} is the opposite (in the black), {残高|ざんだか} is an account balance, and {財産|ざいさん} is property.

questions.stem: Which is closest in meaning? {駅前|えきまえ}の{店|みせ}が{値上|ねあ}げした。
choices: {駅前|えきまえ}の{店|みせ}の{値段|ねだん}が{高|たか}くなった。
{駅前|えきまえ}の{店|みせ}の{値段|ねだん}が{安|やす}くなった。
{駅前|えきまえ}の{店|みせ}が{新|あたら}しくなった。
{駅前|えきまえ}の{店|みせ}の{客|きゃく}が{増|ふ}えた。
questions.explanation: {値上|ねあ}げ is a seller raising prices, so the shop's prices went up. {値下|ねさ}げ would be the second choice. The shop being renewed or getting more customers says nothing about its prices.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses {余|あま}る correctly?
choices: {銀行|ぎんこう}でお{金|かね}を{余|あま}った。
{友|とも}だちに{本|ほん}を{余|あま}った。
パーティーの{料理|りょうり}がたくさん{余|あま}った。
{電車|でんしゃ}に{余|あま}って、{遅|おく}れてしまった。
questions.explanation: {余|あま}る is intransitive: what's left over is the subject, {料理|りょうり}が{余|あま}った (there was food left over). It can't take を ({余|あま}った with お{金|かね}を or {本|ほん}を), and it has nothing to do with missing a train ({乗|の}り{遅|おく}れる).

questions.stem: How is 経済 read in this sentence? {日本|にほん}の経済は、{少|すこ}しずつよくなっている。
questions.explanation: {経済|けいざい} (economy) is 経 ケイ + 済 サイ, which becomes ざい after ケイ. The unvoiced けいさい misses that change, and キョウ and へ are not readings of 経 in this word.

questions.stem: Which kanji is はら in this sentence? {現金|げんきん}で___います。 (I'll pay in cash.)
questions.explanation: {払|はら}う (to pay) is written 払: the hand shape on the left and ム on the right. {私|わたし} (I) has the grain shape on the left, {仕事|しごと}'s 仕 has the person shape, and {打|う}つ (to hit, lesson 15) has the hand shape with a different right side.

questions.stem: Type the reading of 値段 in hiragana: この値段は{高|たか}すぎる。
questions.explanation: {値段|ねだん} (price) is 値 read ね, its kun'yomi, + 段 だん. It's N4's ねだん, now written with lesson 7's kanji.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker mean?

audio.text: それでこんなにたかいわけですね。

choices: It can't possibly be that expensive.
I can't buy something so expensive.
Now I see why it's so expensive.
questions.explanation: それでこんなに{高|たか}いわけですね: "so that's why it's this expensive". それで…わけです explains a fact the speaker has just understood. "It can't be" would be わけがない, "it isn't really" わけではない.

questions.stem: Listen. Why isn't the speaker buying it?

audio.text: おかねがないわけじゃないけど、いまはかいません。

choices: They have no money at all.
It isn't a lack of money: they just won't buy it now.
questions.explanation: お{金|かね}がないわけじゃないけど、{今|いま}は{買|か}いません: "it's not that I don't have money, but I won't buy it now". わけじゃない denies the obvious reason (no money) without giving another.

questions.stem: Listen. Which reply fits best?

audio.text: あした、だいじなかいぎがあるから、やすむわけにはいかないんです。

choices: じゃあ、ゆっくり{休|やす}んでください。
よかったですね。{休|やす}めて。
そうですか。{大変|たいへん}ですね。
{会議|かいぎ}はないんですか。
questions.explanation: {明日|あした}、{大事|だいじ}な{会議|かいぎ}があるから、{休|やす}むわけにはいかないんです: "I've got an important meeting tomorrow, so I can't take the day off". A sympathetic そうですか。{大変|たいへん}ですね fits. The others assume the speaker can rest or that there's no meeting.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: It's not that I dislike shopping; I just don't have time.
questions.explanation: きらい is a な-adjective, so it takes な before わけ: きらいなわけではありません. が then adds the real reason, {時間|じかん}が ないんです. わけが would make わけがありません ("there's no way"), which doesn't fit "it's not that…".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: It's borrowed money, so I have to pay it back.
questions.explanation: "Have to" here is "can't not": the ない form + わけにはいかない, {返|かえ}さないわけにはいかない. {返|かえ}す + わけにはいかない would mean "I can't pay it back", the opposite.

questions.stem:
Read the blog post and answer.

{先月|せんげつ}から、{買|か}い{物|もの}はほとんどスマホで{払|はら}っている。{便利|べんり}だが、{困|こま}ったこともある。{使|つか}ったお{金|かね}が{目|め}に{見|み}えないので、つい{使|つか}いすぎてしまうのだ。{今月|こんげつ}は{給料日|きゅうりょうび}の{一週間前|いっしゅうかんまえ}に、{残高|ざんだか}が{三千円|さんぜんえん}になってしまった。{現金|げんきん}のほうがいいというわけではないが、{来月|らいげつ}からは{一週間|いっしゅうかん}ごとによさんを{決|き}めて、アプリで{確|たし}かめることにした。

(つい = without meaning to; よさん = budget)

Why does the writer spend too much?
choices: They can't see the money they're spending.
The app charges a fee for each payment.
Prices have gone up this month.
questions.explanation: {使|つか}ったお{金|かね}が{目|め}に{見|み}えないので、つい{使|つか}いすぎてしまう: because the money spent isn't visible, the writer ends up overspending. Fees, prices and a lost wallet aren't mentioned.

questions.stem:
Read the blog post again.

{先月|せんげつ}から、{買|か}い{物|もの}はほとんどスマホで{払|はら}っている。{便利|べんり}だが、{困|こま}ったこともある。{使|つか}ったお{金|かね}が{目|め}に{見|み}えないので、つい{使|つか}いすぎてしまうのだ。{今月|こんげつ}は{給料日|きゅうりょうび}の{一週間前|いっしゅうかんまえ}に、{残高|ざんだか}が{三千円|さんぜんえん}になってしまった。{現金|げんきん}のほうがいいというわけではないが、{来月|らいげつ}からは{一週間|いっしゅうかん}ごとによさんを{決|き}めて、アプリで{確|たし}かめることにした。

What has the writer decided to do?
choices: Go back to paying only in cash.
Set a budget for each week and check it in the app.
Move money into a second account.
questions.explanation: {一週間|いっしゅうかん}ごとによさんを{決|き}めて、アプリで{確|たし}かめることにした: a weekly budget, checked in the app. {現金|げんきん}のほうがいいというわけではない says cash isn't the answer, so the writer isn't going back to it.

questions.stem: Choose the best words: {心配|しんぱい}する___よ。{書類|しょるい}は{来週|らいしゅう}{出|だ}してもいいそうだから。
questions.explanation: The speaker reassures the listener: "there's no need to worry". That's the dictionary form + ことはない. ものだ would say worrying is what one is supposed to do, ことにする is deciding to do it, and わけだ concludes that you worry.

questions.stem: Choose the best words: 「{今日中|きょうじゅう}に{終|お}わりますか。」「{終|お}わら___が、{少|すこ}し{急|いそ}がないと{難|むずか}しいですね。」
questions.explanation: The answer is a hesitant yes: "it's not that it won't be finished, but…". That's 〜ないことはない. ないわけです and ないはずです would say it won't be finished, which clashes with the "but", and ないことにします is a decision not to.

questions.stem: Choose the best words: {安|やす}い{店|みせ}が、いつも{一番|いちばん}{安|やす}い___。
questions.explanation: "A cheap shop isn't necessarily always the cheapest": 〜とは{限|かぎ}らない denies "always". ことはない ("there's no need") doesn't fit a statement about prices, わけだ would conclude that it is always cheapest, and ものだ would call it a general truth.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: {高|たか}い{薬|くすり}は{必|かなら}ずしもよくきく。
{必|かなら}ずしも{明日|あした}{来|き}てください。
{高|たか}い{薬|くすり}が{必|かなら}ずしもよくきくわけではない。
{必|かなら}ずしも{毎日|まいにち}{歩|ある}くことにした。
questions.explanation: {必|かなら}ずしも ("necessarily") needs a negative later in the sentence: 〜わけではない, 〜とは{限|かぎ}らない or 〜ない. Without one it's wrong, and it can't go with a request or a decision. For "be sure to come", use {必|かなら}ず. (きく = to work, of medicine.)

questions.stem: Choose the best ending: ネットで{予約|よやく}したので、{一時間|いちじかん}もならば___。
choices: なければならなかった
questions.explanation: Booking online spared the speaker an hour's queue: ならばないで{済|す}んだ, "I didn't have to queue". {住|す}む is "to live" (same sound, different kanji). Having to queue doesn't follow from booking online, and ないこともなかった ("it's not that I didn't") makes no sense here. (ならぶ = to queue, N4.)

questions.stem: What does this mean? {申|もう}し{込|こ}んだことは{申|もう}し{込|こ}んだけど、まだ{返事|へんじ}が{来|こ}ない。
choices: I did apply, but I haven't had a reply yet.
I've never applied, so there's no reply.
There's no need to apply, because nobody replies.
I'll apply as soon as I get a reply.
questions.explanation: A ことは A けど admits something and then limits it: "I did apply, but…". The た form here is the applying itself, not "have never" (that would be {申|もう}し{込|こ}んだことはない), and nothing says there's no need to apply.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "There's no need to go to the city office"?
choices: {市役所|しやくしょ}に{行|い}ったことはありません。
{市役所|しやくしょ}に{行|い}かないことはありません。
{市役所|しやくしょ}に{行|い}くことにしました。
{市役所|しやくしょ}に{行|い}くことはありません。
questions.explanation: The dictionary form + ことはない is "no need". With the た form it's "I've never been", with the ない form it's "it's not that I don't go", and ことにしました is a decision to go.

questions.stem: Choose the best word: {申|もう}し{込|こ}みの___は{金曜日|きんようび}です。それを{過|す}ぎると、{受|う}け{付|つ}けられません。
questions.explanation: A date after which applications aren't accepted is a time limit, {期限|きげん}. {限度|げんど} is a limit on an amount, {記号|きごう} is a symbol, and {資格|しかく} is a qualification.

questions.stem: Which is closest in meaning? {予約|よやく}は{不要|ふよう}です。
choices: {予約|よやく}しなくてもいいです。
{予約|よやく}しなければなりません。
{予約|よやく}はもう{終|お}わりました。
questions.explanation: {不要|ふよう} is "not needed", so you don't have to book: {予約|よやく}しなくてもいい. It doesn't say booking is required, over or impossible.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses {要|い}る correctly?
choices: {部屋|へや}に{田中|たなか}さんが{要|い}ります。
{写真|しゃしん}を{要|い}ってください。
{申|もう}し{込|こ}みに{写真|しゃしん}は{要|い}りません。
{明日|あした}は{家|いえ}に{要|い}ます。
questions.explanation: {要|い}る means "to be needed" and is group 1: {要|い}りません. Being somewhere is いる (group 2: います), written in kana, so the sentences about Mr Tanaka and staying home are wrong, and {要|い}る isn't used with を as a request.

questions.stem: How is 確認 read in this sentence? {名前|なまえ}と{住所|じゅうしょ}を確認してください。
questions.explanation: {確認|かくにん} (confirmation) is 確 カク + 認 ニン. たし is the kun'yomi of 確 ({確|たし}か), used only with okurigana, and 認 is never イン or ジン.

questions.stem: Which kanji is the first kanji of ひつよう (necessary)? {写真|しゃしん}はひつようですか。
questions.explanation: {必要|ひつよう} (necessary) is written 必: 心 with a stroke cutting through it. 心 alone is こころ (heart), and 引 (pull) and 比 (compare, lesson 4) aren't read ひつ.

questions.stem: In 申込書, the okurigana are left out. What does 申 stand for in this word?
questions.explanation: {申込書|もうしこみしょ} is {申|もう}し{込|こ}み + {書|しょ} with the okurigana し and み dropped, so 申 is read もうし and 込 こみ. もう leaves out the し, シン is 申's on'yomi (not used here), and さる isn't a reading of 申 at this level.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker doing?

audio.text: しんぱいすることはありませんよ。まだじかんはありますから。

choices: Warning the listener that it's too late
Reassuring the listener that there's still time
questions.explanation: {心配|しんぱい}することはありませんよ。まだ{時間|じかん}はありますから: "there's no need to worry; there's still time". ことはありません with the dictionary form reassures. "Never worried" would be {心配|しんぱい}したことはありません.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker think about going?

audio.text: いけないことはないけど、ちょっととおいですね。

choices: They'd love to go: it's close.
They could go, but it's a bit far.
questions.explanation: {行|い}けないことはないけど、ちょっと{遠|とお}いですね: "it's not that I can't go, but it's a bit far". The double negative is a reluctant yes, and the けど adds the doubt.

questions.stem: Listen. What happened?

audio.text: でんわいっぽんですみました。

choices: A single phone call was enough.
They had to make a lot of phone calls.
They couldn't get through on the phone.
questions.explanation: {電話|でんわ}{一本|いっぽん}で{済|す}みました: "it was settled with one phone call". 〜で{済|す}む is "it only took…". ({一本|いっぽん} counts phone calls.)

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: Expensive things aren't necessarily good.
questions.explanation: {必|かなら}ずしも goes before what it limits, and the sentence ends with the negative it needs: いいとは{限|かぎ}らない. {必|かなら}ずしも can also open the sentence. いいことは would start the 〜ことは〜が pattern, which doesn't fit.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: Thanks to checking early, I didn't have to rewrite it.
questions.explanation: The cause with a good result takes おかげで (lesson 6), and what you were spared is 〜ずに{済|す}む: {書|か}き{直|なお}さずに {済|す}んだ. {書|か}き{直|なお}さずに is the ず form of {書|か}き{直|なお}さない (lesson 10). せいで would blame the checking.

questions.stem:
Read the notice and answer.

{市民|しみん}プール：{夏|なつ}の{水泳教室|すいえいきょうしつ}の{申|もう}し{込|こ}み
{申|もう}し{込|こ}みは{七月|しちがつ}{一日|ついたち}から{十日|とおか}までです。ホームページから{申|もう}し{込|こ}めるので、{窓口|まどぐち}に{来|く}る{必要|ひつよう}はありません。{定員|ていいん}は{三十人|さんじゅうにん}で、{申|もう}し{込|こ}みが{多|おお}い{場合|ばあい}はちゅうせんになります。{申|もう}し{込|こ}んでも{必|かなら}ず{参加|さんか}できるとは{限|かぎ}りませんので、ご{注意|ちゅうい}ください。{結果|けっか}は{十五日|じゅうごにち}までにメールでお{知|し}らせします。

({水泳教室|すいえいきょうしつ} = swimming class; ちゅうせん = a draw)

Do you have to go to the counter to apply?
choices: Yes: only applications at the counter are accepted.
No: you can apply on the website.
Only if more than thirty people apply.
questions.explanation: ホームページから{申|もう}し{込|こ}めるので、{窓口|まどぐち}に{来|く}る{必要|ひつよう}はありません: you can apply online, so there's no need to come to the counter. The results come by email.

questions.stem:
Read the notice again.

{市民|しみん}プール：{夏|なつ}の{水泳教室|すいえいきょうしつ}の{申|もう}し{込|こ}み
{申|もう}し{込|こ}みは{七月|しちがつ}{一日|ついたち}から{十日|とおか}までです。ホームページから{申|もう}し{込|こ}めるので、{窓口|まどぐち}に{来|く}る{必要|ひつよう}はありません。{定員|ていいん}は{三十人|さんじゅうにん}で、{申|もう}し{込|こ}みが{多|おお}い{場合|ばあい}はちゅうせんになります。{申|もう}し{込|こ}んでも{必|かなら}ず{参加|さんか}できるとは{限|かぎ}りませんので、ご{注意|ちゅうい}ください。{結果|けっか}は{十五日|じゅうごにち}までにメールでお{知|し}らせします。

What does the notice warn applicants about?
choices: The class may be cancelled in bad weather.
questions.explanation: {申|もう}し{込|こ}んでも{必|かなら}ず{参加|さんか}できるとは{限|かぎ}りません: even if you apply, you can't necessarily take part, because there may be a draw. Fees, weather and photos aren't mentioned.

questions.stem: Choose the best word: {悪|わる}いことをしたら、すぐにあやまる___です。
questions.explanation: べき follows the dictionary form and takes だ / です straight after it: あやまるべきです (you should apologize). べき doesn't take な before です, and ことにです and ようにです aren't possible endings.

questions.stem: Which sentence correctly says "You shouldn't talk loudly on the train"?
choices: {電車|でんしゃ}の{中|なか}で{大声|おおごえ}で{話|はな}さないべきだ。
{電車|でんしゃ}の{中|なか}で{大声|おおごえ}で{話|はな}すべきない。
{電車|でんしゃ}の{中|なか}で{大声|おおごえ}で{話|はな}さないべきではない。
{電車|でんしゃ}の{中|なか}で{大声|おおごえ}で{話|はな}すべきではない。
questions.explanation: The negative of べきだ is べきではない, after the dictionary form: {話|はな}すべきではない. ない can't go before べき, and べき needs では before ない. The third choice would be a double negative ("shouldn't not talk").

questions.stem: Choose the correct form: もっと{早|はや}く{相談|そうだん}___だった。 (I should have asked for advice sooner.)
questions.explanation: With する, べき comes after the dictionary form する, which is often shortened to す: {相談|そうだん}すべき (or {相談|そうだん}するべき). The other forms take the wrong part of する. べきだった is "should have".

questions.stem: Choose the best word: {子供|こども}のころは、{毎日|まいにち}この{川|かわ}で{泳|およ}いだ___だ。
questions.explanation: The た form + ものだ looks back on something you used to do often: "I used to swim in this river every day". ことだ gives advice, はずだ an expectation, and わけだ an explanation or conclusion.

questions.stem: Choose the best word: {日本語|にほんご}が{上手|じょうず}になりたければ、{毎日|まいにち}{話|はな}す___だ。
questions.explanation: "If you want to get good, the thing to do is…" is advice: the dictionary form + ことだ. ところだ is "about to", わけだ an explanation or conclusion, and はずだ an expectation; none of them gives advice.

questions.stem: Which sentence states a rule (a requirement), not an opinion or advice?
choices: {電車|でんしゃ}に{乗|の}るには、きっぷを{買|か}わなければならない。
お{年寄|としよ}りには{席|せき}をゆずるべきだ。
{人|ひと}の{話|はなし}は{最後|さいご}まで{聞|き}くものだ。
{毎日|まいにち}{少|すこ}しずつ{練習|れんしゅう}することだ。
questions.explanation: 〜なければならない states a requirement: you can't ride without a ticket. べきだ is the speaker's judgement, ものだ presents a social norm, and ことだ gives advice.

questions.stem: Choose the best words: このマンションでは、ごみは{朝|あさ}{八時|はちじ}までに{出|だ}す___。
questions.explanation: このマンションでは points to the building's rule: ことになっている, "it's the rule that…". ことにしている is a personal habit, ものだった looks back on the past, and べきだった is "should have", a regret.

questions.stem: Which sentence is natural?
choices: {非常口|ひじょうぐち}の{前|まえ}には、{決|けっ}して{物|もの}を{置|お}いてください。
{非常口|ひじょうぐち}の{前|まえ}には、{決|けっ}して{物|もの}を{置|お}かないでください。
{決|けっ}して{非常口|ひじょうぐち}の{場所|ばしょ}を{確認|かくにん}しましょう。
{非常口|ひじょうぐち}は{決|けっ}して{便利|べんり}です。
questions.explanation: {決|けっ}して ("never, by no means") needs a negative: {置|お}かないでください. It can't go with a positive request, a suggestion or a positive statement. (It's lesson 28's word; here it's taught as a pattern.)

questions.stem: Choose the best word: {電車|でんしゃ}の{中|なか}で{電話|でんわ}で{話|はな}すのは、マナー___だと{考|かんが}える{人|ひと}が{多|おお}い。
questions.explanation: Breaking the rules of manners is マナー{違反|いはん}. {制度|せいど} is an official system, {常識|じょうしき} is common sense (マナー{常識|じょうしき} isn't a phrase), and {方法|ほうほう} is a method.

questions.stem: Which is closest in meaning? {借|か}りたものを{返|かえ}すのは{当|あ}たり{前|まえ}だ。
choices: {借|か}りたものは{返|かえ}さなくてもいい。
{借|か}りたものを{返|かえ}すのは{難|むずか}しい。
{借|か}りたものを{返|かえ}すのは、ふつうのことだ。
{借|か}りたものを{返|かえ}すのは{恥|は}ずかしい。
questions.explanation: {当|あ}たり{前|まえ} is "only natural, obvious": of course you return what you borrow. That's ふつうのこと (an ordinary, expected thing). It doesn't say returning is optional, hard or embarrassing.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses {迷子|まいご} correctly?
choices: {道|みち}が{迷子|まいご}で、よく{分|わ}からない。
デパートで{子供|こども}が{迷子|まいご}になった。
{電車|でんしゃ}が{迷子|まいご}で{遅|おく}れた。
{私|わたし}はよく{迷子|まいご}するのが{好|す}きだ。
questions.explanation: {迷子|まいご} is a lost child (or, jokingly, a lost adult), and the verb is {迷子|まいご}になる. A road or a train can't be a {迷子|まいご}, and there's no verb ×{迷子|まいご}する. For yourself losing your way, N4's {道|みち}に{迷|まよ}う is usual.

questions.stem: How is 常識 read in this sentence? そんなことは常識だ。
questions.explanation: {常識|じょうしき} (common sense) is 常 ジョウ + 識 シキ. つね is 常's kun'yomi ({常|つね}に), not used in this word; しょく belongs to other kanji ({食|しょく}), and 常 starts with a voiced ジョ.

questions.stem: Which kanji is ちが in this sentence? {二|ふた}つの{国|くに}では、マナーが___う。
questions.explanation: {違|ちが}う (to differ) is 違. The other three also sit on the "moving" shape: {達|たっ} (lesson 15), {遠|とお}い (far, N4) and {運|うん} (luck, N4), but none is read ちが.

questions.stem: How is 守 read in 留守 (being out)?
questions.explanation: {留守|るす} is 留 ル + 守 ス. シュ is 守's other on'yomi, まも its kun'yomi in {守|まも}る, and もり belongs to {子守|こもり} (babysitting), not to this word.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker saying?

audio.text: よるはしずかにするものですよ。

choices: It's always quiet here at night.
I used to be quiet at night.
At night you're supposed to keep quiet.
You must never come here at night.
questions.explanation: {夜|よる}は{静|しず}かにするものですよ: "at night you're supposed to keep quiet". ものです presents it as common sense. "Used to" would need the た form ({静|しず}かにしたものです).

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker talking about?

audio.text: こどものころ、よくこのこうえんであそんだものです。

choices: Something they often did as a child
Something they plan to do with their children
A rule about using the park
One visit to the park yesterday
questions.explanation: {子供|こども}のころ、よくこの{公園|こうえん}で{遊|あそ}んだものです: "as a child I often played in this park". The た form + ものです with よく is a fond memory of a habit, not one event or a rule.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker doing?

audio.text: わからないときは、えんりょしないできくことです。

choices: Giving advice: ask when you don't understand
Explaining a rule of the building
questions.explanation: {分|わ}からないときは、えんりょしないで{聞|き}くことです: "when you don't understand, the thing to do is ask without holding back". The dictionary form + ことです gives advice.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: You should think about the people around you.
questions.explanation: 〜のことを{考|かんが}える is "to think about (someone)", and べきだ follows the dictionary form: {考|かんが}えるべきだ. べきではない would mean "shouldn't".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: When I was a student, I used to talk with my friends until morning.
questions.explanation: The た form + ものだ is the nostalgic "used to": {話|はな}したものだ. {朝|あさ}まで and {友|とも}だちと can swap places. ことだ would make it advice, which doesn't fit a memory.

questions.stem:
Read the opinion and answer.

{優先席|ゆうせんせき}は、お{年寄|としよ}りや、{体|からだ}の{具合|ぐあい}が{悪|わる}い{人|ひと}のための{席|せき}だ。{空|あ}いていても{座|すわ}るべきではない、と{考|かんが}える{人|ひと}もいる。しかし{私|わたし}は、{空|あ}いているなら{座|すわ}ってもかまわないと{思|おも}う。{大切|たいせつ}なのは、{必要|ひつよう}な{人|ひと}が{来|き}たら、すぐに{席|せき}をゆずることだ。だから、{優先席|ゆうせんせき}ではスマホばかり{見|み}ないで、まわりに{気|き}を{配|くば}るものだ。

({優先席|ゆうせんせき} = priority seat; {気|き}を{配|くば}る = to pay attention to others)

What is the writer's opinion?
choices: You should never sit in a priority seat.
It's fine to sit in an empty priority seat, as long as you give it up when someone needs it.
Priority seats should be for elderly people only.
People should stand on trains whenever they can.
questions.explanation: The writer disagrees with people who say you shouldn't sit even when it's empty ({座|すわ}るべきではない): {空|あ}いているなら {座|すわ}ってもかまわない. What matters is giving up the seat at once (ゆずることだ) and watching the people around you (〜ものだ).

questions.stem: Choose the correct form: {朝|あさ}ご{飯|はん}を___に{家|いえ}を{出|で}た。 (I left without eating breakfast.)
questions.explanation: The ず form replaces ない with ず: {食|た}べない → {食|た}べず, and 〜ずに is "without doing". ず doesn't keep ない ({食|た}べないず) or join to the く of なく, and {食|た}べる has no ら.

questions.stem: Choose the correct form: {全然|ぜんぜん}{勉強|べんきょう}___に{試験|しけん}を{受|う}けてしまった。
questions.explanation: する is the one irregular verb: its ず form is せず, not ×しず (from しない). So {勉強|べんきょう}せずに, "without studying".

questions.stem: Choose the best words: {終電|しゅうでん}がないから、タクシーで{帰|かえ}る___。
questions.explanation: With no last train, a taxi is the only option left: the dictionary form + しかない, "there's nothing for it but to". ことはない ("no need"), わけがない ("no way") and べきではない ("shouldn't") don't follow from having no train.

questions.stem: Choose the best word: {試験|しけん}の{結果|けっか}が{気|き}になって___。
questions.explanation: After a て form, しょうがない says a feeling is unbearable: {気|き}になってしょうがない, "I can't stop worrying about it". しかない follows the dictionary form, ようがない the ます stem, and わけにはいかない the dictionary or ない form; none of them goes after a て form.

questions.stem: Choose the best ending: その{話|はなし}を{聞|き}いて、{泣|な}か___。
choices: ずにはいられなかった
questions.explanation: The ず form + にはいられない is "can't help doing": {泣|な}かずにはいられなかった, "I couldn't help crying". ず can't make a request, べき can't follow ない, and the た form + ものだ (used to) doesn't fit one moment.

questions.stem: Choose the best word: {住所|じゅうしょ}が{分|わ}からないので、{手紙|てがみ}の{出|だ}し___。
questions.explanation: The ます stem + ようがない is "there's no way to": {出|だ}しようがない, "there's no way to send it". The other patterns don't join to a ます stem: しかない takes the dictionary form ({出|だ}すしかない), てしょうがない the て form, and ずにはいられない the ず form.

questions.stem: Which sentence is wrong?
choices: {忘|わす}れずに{持|も}ってきてください。
{答|こた}えが{分|わ}からず、{困|こま}った。
questions.explanation: ず can't make a request on its own: "please don't forget" is {忘|わす}れないでください. 〜ずに can come before a request verb, though ({忘|わす}れずに{持|も}ってきてください: please don't forget to bring it), and 〜ず、 links a cause in writing ({分|わ}からず、{困|こま}った).

questions.stem: Choose the best words: {試合|しあい}に{負|ま}けて、{弟|おとうと}はずっと___いる。
questions.explanation: After losing a match, you feel down: {落|お}ち{込|こ}んでいる. {喜|よろこ}ぶ (to be pleased), {感心|かんしん}する (to be impressed) and ほっとする (to feel relieved) don't fit a defeat.

questions.stem: Which is closest in meaning? {試験|しけん}が{終|お}わって、ほっとした。
choices: {試験|しけん}が{終|お}わって、{安心|あんしん}した。
{試験|しけん}が{終|お}わって、がっかりした。
{試験|しけん}が{終|お}わって、{腹|はら}が{立|た}った。
{試験|しけん}が{終|お}わって、きんちょうした。
questions.explanation: ほっとする is to feel the pressure go: relieved, close to {安心|あんしん}する. がっかりする is disappointed, {腹|はら}が{立|た}つ is angry, and きんちょうする is nervous, the feeling ほっとする ends.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses {怖|こわ}がる correctly?
choices: {私|わたし}は{今|いま}、とても{怖|こわ}がります。
この{話|はなし}はとても{怖|こわ}がる。
{妹|いもうと}は{犬|いぬ}を{怖|こわ}がる。
{怖|こわ}がる{天気|てんき}ですね。
questions.explanation: 〜がる describes how someone else shows a feeling: {妹|いもうと}は{犬|いぬ}を{怖|こわ}がる (my sister is scared of dogs). For your own fear right now, say {怖|こわ}いです; a story or the weather is {怖|こわ}い, not {怖|こわ}がる.

questions.stem: How is 笑顔 read in this sentence? {母|はは}はいつも笑顔で{迎|むか}えてくれる。
questions.explanation: {笑顔|えがお} (a smiling face) reads 笑 as え and 顔 as がお: かお becomes がお as the second part of a word. わらい is the noun {笑|わら}い, and しょうがん puts the on'yomi together, which this word doesn't use.

questions.stem: Which kanji is かな in this sentence? {犬|いぬ}が{死|し}んで、とても___しかった。
questions.explanation: {悲|かな}しい (sad) is 悲: lesson 9's 非 on top of 心 (heart). 非 alone is ヒ (not), {感|かん} is "feel" and {恐|おそ}ろしい "terrifying"; they share the heart at the bottom but aren't read かな.

questions.stem: How is 怒 read in 怒鳴る (to shout)?
questions.explanation: {怒鳴|どな}る uses 怒's on'yomi ド and 鳴's kun'yomi な: どなる. おこ and いか are its kun'yomi in {怒|おこ}る and {怒|いか}り.

questions.stem: Listen. What will the speaker do?

audio.text: しゅうでんがないから、あるいてかえるしかない。

choices: Walk home: there's no other way
questions.explanation: {終電|しゅうでん}がないから、{歩|ある}いて{帰|かえ}るしかない: "there's no last train, so I have no choice but to walk home". しかない leaves only one option.

questions.stem: Listen. How does the speaker feel?

audio.text: あしたのりょこうがたのしみでしょうがない。

choices: They don't want to go on the trip.
They're really looking forward to the trip.
They can't go on the trip after all.
questions.explanation: {明日|あした}の{旅行|りょこう}が{楽|たの}しみでしょうがない: "I'm so looking forward to tomorrow's trip I can hardly stand it". てしょうがない makes a feeling unbearably strong; here the feeling is a happy one ({楽|たの}しみ).

questions.stem: Listen. Which reply fits best?

audio.text: すみません、かさをもたずにきてしまって…。

choices: じゃあ、これを{使|つか}ってください。
かさを{持|も}ってきてよかったですね。
そのかさ、どこで{買|か}ったんですか。
{二本|にほん}も{持|も}ってきたんですか。
questions.explanation: かさを{持|も}たずに{来|き}てしまって: "I came without an umbrella". The natural reply offers one: じゃあ、これを{使|つか}ってください. The other replies assume the speaker brought an umbrella.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: I ended up leaving the house without saying anything.
questions.explanation: 〜ずに is "without doing": {何|なに}も{言|い}わずに. Then {家|いえ}を{出|で}てしまった, with 〜てしまう for the regret. 〜なくて gives a cause, not "without".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: The shop is closed, so I have no choice but to wait until tomorrow.
questions.explanation: しかない follows the dictionary form: {待|ま}つしかありません (polite). The ない form ({待|ま}たない) can't come before しかない.

questions.stem:
Read the letter to an advice column and answer.

{最近|さいきん}、{仕事|しごと}のことが{気|き}になってしかたがありません。{夜|よる}も{眠|ねむ}れず、{休|やす}みの{日|ひ}も{会社|かいしゃ}のメールを{見|み}ずにはいられません。{家族|かぞく}に{話|はな}しても、「{気|き}にしすぎだよ」と{言|い}われるだけです。こんな{自分|じぶん}が{情|なさ}けなくて、{落|お}ち{込|こ}んでしまいます。どうすればいいでしょうか。

What is the writer's problem?
choices: They don't have enough work to do.
They can't stop thinking about work, even at night and on days off.
Their family won't let them read their email.
questions.explanation: {仕事|しごと}のことが{気|き}になってしかたがありません: work is constantly on their mind. They can't sleep ({眠|ねむ}れず) and can't help checking work email on days off ({見|み}ずにはいられません). Their family only says they worry too much.

questions.stem: Match each verb to its ず form. (The verbs are in kana because answers in a list can't show furigana.)
questions.explanation: Replace ない with ず: {食|た}べない → {食|た}べず, {行|い}かない → {行|い}かず, {来|こ}ない → {来|こ}ず. する is irregular: せず, not ×しず.

questions.stem: What is a かいらんばん?
choices: A clipboard of notices passed from house to house
A rota for cleaning the school
The list of rubbish days kept on the fridge
questions.explanation: かいらんばん is a folder or clipboard of notices from the residents' association that each household reads, signs or stamps, and passes on to the next house. In many places it now also comes by email or app.

questions.stem: The かいらんばん arrives at your door. What are you expected to do?
choices: Keep it until the end of the month.
Take it back to the city office.
Read it, sign or stamp it, and pass it on within a day or two.
questions.explanation: The custom is to read it and pass it on quickly: {読|よ}んだら、すぐに{次|つぎ}の{家|いえ}に{回|まわ}すものです. Keeping it for a long time holds up the whole street.

questions.stem: What does {当番|とうばん} mean in ごみ{置|お}き{場|ば}の{当番|とうばん}?
questions.explanation: {当番|とうばん} is your turn on a rota: here, your turn to look after the rubbish collection point. The fee is {会費|かいひ}, a drill くんれん, and the meeting hall {集会所|しゅうかいじょ}.

questions.stem: Which statement about {町内会|ちょうないかい} matches the lesson?
choices: Every resident is required by law to join.
Only people who own their house can join.
Joining is voluntary, though in many places most households join.
It is part of the city office.
questions.explanation: Residents' associations are voluntary groups run by the residents; many households join and pay a small fee, but it isn't a legal duty and the association isn't the city office. Customs vary from place to place.

questions.stem: ぼうさいの{日|ひ} (Disaster Prevention Day), when many drills are held, is on which date?
questions.explanation: 1 September is ぼうさいの{日|ひ}, the anniversary of the Great Kantō earthquake of 1923, and many towns hold drills around then. Other drills are held in spring or autumn.

questions.stem:
Read the notice and answer.

{町内|ちょうない}そうじのお{知|し}らせ
{日時|にちじ}：{十一月|じゅういちがつ}{十日|とおか}{午前|ごぜん}{八時|はちじ}から（{雨|あめ}の{場合|ばあい}は{十七日|じゅうしちにち}） {集合|しゅうごう}：{第二公園|だいにこうえん}の{入口|いりぐち} {持|も}ち{物|もの}：ぐんて、{飲|の}み{物|もの} ごみぶくろと{道具|どうぐ}は{町内会|ちょうないかい}で{用意|ようい}しますので、{持|も}ってくる{必要|ひつよう}はありません。

(ぐんて = cotton work gloves)

What should you bring?
choices: Work gloves and something to drink
questions.explanation: {持|も}ち{物|もの} (what to bring) lists ぐんて and {飲|の}み{物|もの}. The bags and tools are provided, so there's no need to bring them ({持|も}ってくる{必要|ひつよう}はありません).

questions.stem:
Read the notice again.

{町内|ちょうない}そうじのお{知|し}らせ
{日時|にちじ}：{十一月|じゅういちがつ}{十日|とおか}{午前|ごぜん}{八時|はちじ}から（{雨|あめ}の{場合|ばあい}は{十七日|じゅうしちにち}） {集合|しゅうごう}：{第二公園|だいにこうえん}の{入口|いりぐち} {持|も}ち{物|もの}：ぐんて、{飲|の}み{物|もの}

If it rains on 10 November, when is the clean-up?
questions.explanation: （{雨|あめ}の{場合|ばあい}は{十七日|じゅうしちにち}）: in case of rain, it moves to the 17th.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker ask you to do?

audio.text: かいらんばんは、よんだらすぐにつぎのいえにまわしてください。

choices: Pass the clipboard on soon after reading it
Read the clipboard aloud at the meeting
Bring the clipboard back to them
questions.explanation: かいらんばんは、{読|よ}んだらすぐに{次|つぎ}の{家|いえ}に{回|まわ}してください: "once you've read the clipboard, please pass it straight on to the next house".

questions.stem: Listen. Where and when do people meet?

audio.text: こんどのにちようびは、まちのそうじのひです。はちじにこうえんにあつまってください。

choices: At the park, at eight on Sunday
At the station, at eight on Sunday
At the park, at four on Saturday
At the meeting hall, at eight on Monday
questions.explanation: {今度|こんど}の{日曜日|にちようび} (this coming Sunday) is the clean-up day, and {八時|はちじ}に{公園|こうえん}に{集|あつ}まってください: gather at the park at eight.

questions.stem: A neighbour tells you: {参加|さんか}しないといけないわけではありませんよ。 What does she mean?
choices: There's no way you can take part.
You don't absolutely have to take part.
questions.explanation: わけではない softens: "it's not that you have to take part" (lesson 7). The clean-up isn't compulsory, though it's good to go.

questions.stem: You can't come to the clean-up. Which is the polite thing to say to the organizer?
choices: その{日|ひ}は{参加|さんか}するわけがないです。
すみません、その{日|ひ}は{用事|ようじ}があって{参加|さんか}できないんです。
{皆|みな}さんも{参加|さんか}することはありません。
{参加|さんか}しないべきです。
questions.explanation: Apologize and give a reason with んです: {用事|ようじ}があって{参加|さんか}できないんです. わけがない ("no way I'd go") is rude, telling others there's no need to go isn't your place, and ×しないべき isn't a correct form.

questions.stem: What does ボランティアをする mean?
choices: to take part in a disaster drill
to move to a new neighbourhood
questions.explanation: ボランティア is both a volunteer and voluntary work, so ボランティアをする is "to volunteer". The fee is {会費|かいひ}, and a drill is くんれん.

questions.stem: A flat listing says ペット{相談|そうだん}. What does it mean?
choices: Pets may be allowed: ask first.
Any pet is welcome, no questions asked.
questions.explanation: {相談|そうだん} is "consultation", so ペット{相談|そうだん} means "pets negotiable": ask before you sign. ペット{不可|ふか} is "no pets" and ペット{可|か} "pets allowed" ({可|か} is outside the N3 list).

questions.stem: According to the lesson, what must dog owners in Japan do every year?
choices: Register the dog with the city again
Take the dog to a training course
Have the dog vaccinated against rabies
questions.explanation: Dogs are registered with the city once in their life, but the rabies injection is every year. Pet insurance is private and optional, and training isn't required by law. Details vary by city.

questions.stem: Which word means an animal's cry, such as barking or mewing?
questions.explanation: {鳴|な}き{声|ごえ} uses the kanji of {鳴|な}く (an animal's or bird's cry). {泣|な}き{声|ごえ} sounds the same but is people crying, {大声|おおごえ} is a loud voice, and {笑|わら}い{声|ごえ} is laughter.

questions.stem: Choose the best word: {散歩|さんぽ}のときは、ふんを{持|も}ち{帰|かえ}る___だ。
questions.explanation: The speaker judges what's right: owners should take the droppings home, {持|も}ち{帰|かえ}るべきだ. わけがない ("no way") and ことはない ("no need") say the opposite, and ようがない follows the ます stem, not the dictionary form.

questions.stem: At a cat café, which of these is good manners?
choices: Picking up a cat that's asleep
Taking photos with the flash on
Waiting for a cat to come to you
Sharing your sandwich with the cats
questions.explanation: The café's rules ask you not to wake, hold or chase the cats, not to use a flash and not to give them human food: the thing to do is wait for them to come to you ({猫|ねこ}のほうから{来|く}るのを{待|ま}つものです).

questions.stem:
Read the café's rules and answer.

{二|に}、{寝|ね}ている{猫|ねこ}は{起|お}こさないでください。{猫|ねこ}は{一日|いちにち}の{半分|はんぶん}{以上|いじょう}{寝|ね}ています。 {三|さん}、{猫|ねこ}を{抱|だ}いたり、{追|お}いかけたりしないでください。{猫|ねこ}のほうから{来|く}るのを{待|ま}つものです。 {五|ご}、{猫|ねこ}に{人|ひと}の{食|た}べ{物|もの}をあげないでください。{店|みせ}で{売|う}っているおやつは{一回|いっかい}だけあげられます。

({抱|だ}く = to hold in your arms; おやつ = a treat)

Why does the card say not to wake the cats?
choices: They sleep for more than half the day.
The café is about to close.
questions.explanation: The reason follows the rule: {猫|ねこ}は{一日|いちにち}の{半分|はんぶん}{以上|いじょう}{寝|ね}ています (cats sleep more than half the day), so sleeping is normal for them and shouldn't be interrupted.

questions.stem:
Read the rules again.

{五|ご}、{猫|ねこ}に{人|ひと}の{食|た}べ{物|もの}をあげないでください。{店|みせ}で{売|う}っているおやつは{一回|いっかい}だけあげられます。

Can you give the cats a treat?
choices: Only when a member of staff is watching.
Yes, once, if it's a treat sold in the shop.
questions.explanation: Human food is out, but {店|みせ}で{売|う}っているおやつは{一回|いっかい}だけあげられます: you may give one of the shop's treats, once. Nothing is said about staff watching.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker's advice?

audio.text: さんぽのときは、リードをみじかくもつものですよ。

choices: Let the dog off the lead in the park.
Keep the lead short on walks.
Walk the dog twice a day.
Don't walk the dog at night.
questions.explanation: {散歩|さんぽ}のときは、リードを{短|みじか}く{持|も}つものですよ: "on walks you're supposed to hold the lead short". ものです states the common-sense rule.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker explaining?

audio.text: いぬは、しにとうろくすることになっています。

choices: A rule: dogs must be registered with the city.
A tip for training a dog.
That dogs aren't allowed in the city.
How to find a good vet.
questions.explanation: {犬|いぬ}は、{市|し}にとうろくすることになっています: "dogs have to be registered with the city". ことになっている states a rule set by others (lesson 9).

questions.stem: Choose the best word: {朝|あさ}と{夜|よる}に、{猫|ねこ}に___をやる。
questions.explanation: You give a cat its food, えさ, with やる (N4: to give to animals). A リード is a lead, しつけ is training, and a ワクチン is given by the vet, not twice a day.

questions.stem: Which word means "owner (of an animal)"?
questions.explanation: かいぬし comes from かう (to keep an animal) + ぬし (owner). じゅうい is a vet, {大家|おおや} (N4) a landlord, and {店員|てんいん} (N5) a shop assistant.

questions.stem: Many dog owners carry a bottle of water on walks. Why, according to the lesson?
choices: Because dogs must drink every ten minutes
To clean the lead after the walk
Because the city gives a fine to dogs without water
To rinse away the urine where the dog has gone
questions.explanation: Rinsing the spot after the dog has gone is a common courtesy to the neighbours, alongside picking up the droppings.

questions.stem: Choose the best phrase: "{父|ちち}は{医師|いし}___、{病院|びょういん}で{三十年|さんじゅうねん}{働|はたら}いてきました。"
questions.explanation: A role or capacity takes として: {医師|いし}として{働|はたら}く (to work as a doctor). にとって needs a judgement after it ({大切|たいせつ}だ, {難|むずか}しい), に{対|たい}して marks the target of an attitude, and について (about) would make no sense here.

questions.stem: Fill the blank: "{子供|こども}がいる{社員|しゃいん}___、{在宅勤務|ざいたくきんむ}はとてもありがたい{制度|せいど}です。"
questions.explanation: ありがたい (a welcome help) is a judgement, and the blank says whose point of view it is from: {社員|しゃいん}にとって. として would mean "in the role of employees with children", which doesn't fit an evaluation of the system, and に{対|たい}して would need an attitude or action aimed at the employees.

questions.stem: Which sentence is NOT natural Japanese?
choices: {私|わたし}にとって、{家族|かぞく}が{一番|いちばん}{大切|たいせつ}です。
この{本|ほん}は{初心者|しょしんしゃ}にとって{分|わ}かりやすい。
けいごは{外国人|がいこくじん}にとって{難|むずか}しい。
{母|はは}にとってケーキを{作|つく}りました。
questions.explanation: にとって is followed by a judgement, not by an action done for someone. "I made a cake for my mother" is {母|はは}のためにケーキを{作|つく}りました. The other three all have judgements after にとって: {大切|たいせつ}, {分|わ}かりやすい, {難|むずか}しい.

questions.stem: Fill the blank: "{課長|かちょう}は{部下|ぶか}___きびしいが、{自分|じぶん}にはもっときびしい。" (きびしい = strict)
questions.explanation: The section chief's strictness is aimed at his staff, so the target takes に{対|たい}して. {部下|ぶか}にとってきびしい would mean "hard from the staff's point of view", which doesn't match the second half (strict with himself), and として would make the staff his role.

questions.stem: Choose the correct form: "{兄|あに}は{会社員|かいしゃいん}___、{弟|おとうと}は{職人|しょくにん}だ。" (My older brother is an office worker, whereas my younger brother is a craftsman.)
questions.explanation: A noun before のに{対|たい}して takes な, as before N4's のに: {会社員|かいしゃいん}なのに{対|たい}して. ×{会社員|かいしゃいん}のに leaves out the な, ×だのに uses the wrong form, and に{対|たい}するのに mixes up the noun-modifying form with the contrast pattern.

questions.stem: Choose the correct form: "{社会人|しゃかいじん}___ {責任|せきにん}を{忘|わす}れないでください。"
questions.explanation: Before a noun ({責任|せきにん}), として needs の: {社会人|しゃかいじん}としての{責任|せきにん} (the responsibility of a working adult). Bare として can't modify a noun, and にとって / に{対|たい}して would also need a noun-modifying form, besides meaning something else.

questions.stem: Fill the blank: "{仕事|しごと}___ {考|かんが}え{方|かた}は、{人|ひと}によって{違|ちが}います。" (Attitudes to work differ from person to person.)
questions.explanation: The blank modifies the noun {考|かんが}え{方|かた}, and the meaning is "towards work", so the noun-modifying form of に{対|たい}して is needed: に{対|たい}する. に{対|たい}して itself can't go straight before a noun (に{対|たい}しての would also be possible). にとって and として give the wrong meaning and also lack の.

questions.stem: Choose the best word: "{熱|ねつ}があったので、{午後|ごご}は{会社|かいしゃ}を___しました。"
questions.explanation: {早退|そうたい}する is leaving work or school early, which is what you do with a temperature. {出勤|しゅっきん} is going to work, {転勤|てんきん} is a transfer to another office, and {交代|こうたい} is taking turns; none of them takes を{会社|かいしゃ} in this sense.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses {任|まか}せる correctly?
choices: この{仕事|しごと}は{私|わたし}に{任|まか}せてください。
{雨|あめ}に{任|まか}せて、{試合|しあい}が{中止|ちゅうし}になった。
{毎朝|まいあさ}、{電車|でんしゃ}で{会社|かいしゃ}に{任|まか}せます。
{給料|きゅうりょう}を{任|まか}せて、{車|くるま}を{買|か}いました。
questions.explanation: {任|まか}せる is "to leave (a task) to someone": person に task を{任|まか}せる. この{仕事|しごと}は{私|わたし}に{任|まか}せてください is "please leave this job to me". The others use it for causes, commuting or saving money, which it doesn't mean.

questions.stem: "{田中|たなか}さんは{来月|らいげつ}{退職|たいしょく}します。" Which sentence is closest in meaning?
choices: {田中|たなか}さんは{来月|らいげつ}、{別|べつ}の{支社|ししゃ}に{行|い}きます。
{田中|たなか}さんは{来月|らいげつ}、{長|なが}い{休|やす}みを{取|と}ります。
{田中|たなか}さんは{来月|らいげつ}、{会社|かいしゃ}に{入|はい}ります。
{田中|たなか}さんは{来月|らいげつ}、{会社|かいしゃ}を{辞|や}めます。
questions.explanation: {退職|たいしょく}する is leaving one's job (including retiring), so it matches {会社|かいしゃ}を{辞|や}める. Going to another branch is {転勤|てんきん}, a long break is {休|やす}み, and joining a company is the opposite.

questions.stem: How is 責任 read? "この{仕事|しごと}の責任は{私|わたし}にあります。"
questions.explanation: {責任|せきにん} (responsibility): 責 is セキ and 任 is ニン. 任 is never にち (that's 日) and the word has no イン sound.

questions.stem: Which kanji is the きゅう of じきゅう (hourly pay)? "この{仕事|しごと}は じきゅう がいいです。"
questions.explanation: {時給|じきゅう} uses 給 (pay, supply), as in {給料|きゅうりょう} and {月給|げっきゅう}. 急 (sudden, hurry), 球 (ball, lesson 15) and 休 (rest) are other キュウ kanji.

questions.stem: Type the reading of 部屋 in hiragana: "{会議|かいぎ}は{三階|さんがい}の部屋で{行|おこな}います。"
questions.explanation: {部屋|へや} (room) is a special reading of the whole word: 部 is ブ elsewhere ({部長|ぶちょう}, {全部|ぜんぶ}), but this word is へや, an N5 word now written in kanji.

questions.stem: Listen. What is going to happen to the speaker?

audio.text: らいげつから、なごやししゃにてんきんすることになりました。

choices: She is being transferred to the Nagoya branch.
She is starting to work from home.
questions.explanation: {来月|らいげつ}から、{名古屋|なごや}{支社|ししゃ}に{転勤|てんきん}することになりました: from next month I'm being transferred to the Nagoya branch. {転勤|てんきん} is a move within the same company; changing companies would be {転職|てんしょく}.

questions.stem: Listen. Where will the speaker be working tomorrow?

audio.text: あしたはざいたくきんむなので、しゅっしゃしません。かいぎはオンラインでおねがいします。

questions.explanation: {明日|あした}は{在宅勤務|ざいたくきんむ}なので、{出社|しゅっしゃ}しません: tomorrow I'm working from home, so I won't come into the office; please make the meeting online. {在宅勤務|ざいたくきんむ} is working from home.

questions.stem: Listen to your colleague. What is the most natural reply?

audio.text: このしごと、わたしにまかせてもらえませんか。

choices: いいえ、どういたしまして。
それは{役|やく}に{立|た}ちましたね。
はい、{任|まか}せてもらいました。
じゃあ、お{願|ねが}いします。
questions.explanation: この{仕事|しごと}、{私|わたし}に{任|まか}せてもらえませんか means "could you leave this job to me?". The natural reply is to accept: じゃあ、お{願|ねが}いします. どういたしまして answers thanks, and the other two talk about the past.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: I attended the meeting as the company's representative.
questions.explanation: {私|わたし}は{会社|かいしゃ}の{代表|だいひょう}として{会議|かいぎ}に{出|で}ました。The role ({会社|かいしゃ}の{代表|だいひょう}) takes として and comes before the action. にとって would need a judgement, not an action, after it.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: For me, time with my family matters more than my salary.
questions.explanation: {私|わたし}にとって、{家族|かぞく}との{時間|じかん}のほうが{給料|きゅうりょう}より{大事|だいじ}です。にとって gives whose point of view the judgement {大事|だいじ}です is from. 〜より and 〜のほうが can come in either order.

questions.stem: Read the notice from a company: "{来月|らいげつ}から、{在宅勤務|ざいたくきんむ}のルールが{変|か}わります。{社員|しゃいん}は{週|しゅう}に{二日|ふつか}まで、{家|いえ}で{働|はたら}くことができます。ただし、{毎週|まいしゅう}{月曜日|げつようび}の{会議|かいぎ}には、{全員|ぜんいん}{出社|しゅっしゃ}してください。また、{新|あたら}しく{入|はい}った{社員|しゃいん}は、{最初|さいしょ}の{三|さん}か{月|げつ}は{在宅勤務|ざいたくきんむ}ができません。" Which is true for an employee who joined five years ago?
choices: They can work from home every day except Monday.
They can work from home up to two days a week, but must come in for the Monday meeting.
They can't work from home for three months.
They don't have to attend the Monday meeting in person.
questions.explanation: {週|しゅう}に{二日|ふつか}まで (up to two days a week) and {月曜日|げつようび}の{会議|かいぎ}には、{全員|ぜんいん}{出社|しゅっしゃ} (everyone comes in for the Monday meeting). The three-month rule is only for new employees ({新|あたら}しく{入|はい}った{社員|しゃいん}). ただし = however.

questions.stem: Read: "{私|わたし}は{去年|きょねん}まで{教師|きょうし}として{働|はたら}いていた。{今|いま}は{小|ちい}さなパン{屋|や}をしている。{給料|きゅうりょう}は{前|まえ}より{少|すく}ないが、{私|わたし}にとって、{毎朝|まいあさ}{客|きゃく}の{笑顔|えがお}を{見|み}られることは、お{金|かね}よりずっと{大切|たいせつ}だ。" What does the writer say?
choices: Being a teacher paid less than the bakery.
The writer wants to go back to teaching for the money.
Seeing customers smile matters more to the writer than money.
Customers have told the writer that the bread is too expensive.
questions.explanation: {私|わたし}にとって、…{笑顔|えがお}を{見|み}られることは、お{金|かね}よりずっと{大切|たいせつ}だ: for the writer, being able to see customers' smiles every morning matters far more than money. The bakery pays less, not more ({前|まえ}より{少|すく}ない). {教師|きょうし} = teacher and {笑顔|えがお} = smile (lessons 18 and 10).

questions.topic: について and に関して
questions.stem: In a chat with a friend, which is most natural? "{昨日|きのう}{見|み}た{映画|えいが}___ {話|はな}そうよ。"
questions.explanation: In casual speech "about" is について: {映画|えいが}について{話|はな}そう. に{関|かん}して means the same but is formal, so it sounds stiff in a chat. において is a formal "in, at", and をはじめ needs a group after it.

questions.topic: について and に関して
questions.stem: Choose the best phrase for a heading: "{留学|りゅうがく}___お{知|し}らせ" (a notice about studying abroad)
