questions.explanation: Before a noun (お{知|し}らせ), に{関|かん}して becomes に{関|かん}する, the usual form in headings: {留学|りゅうがく}に{関|かん}するお{知|し}らせ. The て form can't modify a noun, and を{中心|ちゅうしん}に / によって mean something else.

questions.stem: Fill the blank: "このゲームは{若者|わかもの}___ {人気|にんき}があります。" (This game is popular, mainly among young people.)
questions.explanation: "Mainly among" is を{中心|ちゅうしん}に: the centre of the group it is popular with. をはじめ would need a list or group after it (をはじめ、{多|おお}くの{人|ひと}に), において is "in, at" for events and fields, and について is "about".

questions.stem: Which sentence is NOT natural Japanese?
choices: {学長|がくちょう}をはじめ、{多|おお}くの{先生|せんせい}が{来|き}た。
すしをはじめ、{日本|にほん}の{料理|りょうり}は{世界|せかい}で{人気|にんき}だ。
{東京|とうきょう}をはじめ、{全国|ぜんこく}で{雪|ゆき}が{降|ふ}った。
{田中|たなか}さんをはじめ、{来|き}ました。
questions.explanation: をはじめ names a leading example and then a group. ×{田中|たなか}さんをはじめ、{来|き}ました has no group after it; it needs something like {田中|たなか}さんをはじめ、{研究室|けんきゅうしつ}の{全員|ぜんいん}が{来|き}ました. The other three follow をはじめ with a group ({多|おお}くの{先生|せんせい}, {日本|にほん}の{料理|りょうり}, {全国|ぜんこく}).

questions.stem: Fill the blank in this formal notice: "{次|つぎ}の{会議|かいぎ}は、{第一|だいいち}{会議室|かいぎしつ}___ {行|おこな}われます。"
questions.explanation: において is a formal で for where an event is held: {会議室|かいぎしつ}において{行|おこな}われる. について and に{関|かん}して mean "about", and を{中心|ちゅうしん}に means "centred on", none of which gives a place.

questions.topic: について and に関して
questions.stem: Choose the correct form: "{日本|にほん}の{歴史|れきし}___ {本|ほん}を{探|さが}しています。"
questions.explanation: Before a noun ({本|ほん}), について takes の: についての{本|ほん} (a book about…). Bare について can't modify a noun. によって (by, depending on) and において (in, at) don't mean "about". ({探|さが}す = to look for.)

questions.stem: Fill the blank: "{関東|かんとう}{地方|ちほう}では、{東京|とうきょう}を{中心|ちゅうしん}___、{強|つよ}い{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}っています。"
questions.explanation: The pattern is を{中心|ちゅうしん}に (or を{中心|ちゅうしん}として): heavy rain is falling with Tokyo at the centre. を{中心|ちゅうしん}の, を{中心|ちゅうしん}と and を{中心|ちゅうしん}が aren't forms of it; before a noun you would use を{中心|ちゅうしん}とした.

questions.stem: Choose the best word: "この{表|ひょう}は、{留学生|りゅうがくせい}の{数|かず}が{増|ふ}えていることを___います。"
questions.explanation: A table "shows" a fact: {示|しめ}している. {調|しら}べる is what a person does to find out, {解|と}く is solving a problem, and {表|あらわ}れる (to appear) is intransitive, so it can't take を.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses {参考|さんこう} correctly?
choices: {毎朝|まいあさ}、{参考|さんこう}で{大学|だいがく}に{行|い}きます。
{参考|さんこう}が{高|たか}くて、{買|か}えませんでした。
{先生|せんせい}の{話|はなし}は、とても{参考|さんこう}になりました。
{友|とも}だちと{参考|さんこう}して{遊|あそ}びました。
questions.explanation: {参考|さんこう}になる means "to be helpful, useful (as a reference)", and 〜を{参考|さんこう}にする is "to use as a reference". It isn't a means of transport, a price or an activity, so the other three make no sense.

questions.stem: Which kanji fits かいとう here? "アンケートの かいとう を{集|あつ}めて、{表|ひょう}にしました。"
questions.explanation: A reply to a survey or enquiry is {回答|かいとう}. {解答|かいとう} is the answer to a test question; they sound the same. 会答 and 改答 aren't words.

questions.stem: How is 内容 read? "メールの内容をもう{一度|いちど}{確|たし}かめてください。"
questions.explanation: {内容|ないよう} (contents): 内 is ナイ in compounds (うち is its kun reading, on its own) and 容 is ヨウ, with a long vowel. だい is 大 or 代, not 内.

questions.stem: Which kanji is the ちょう of きょうちょう (emphasis) and the しら of しらべる (to look up)?
questions.explanation: 調 is チョウ in {強調|きょうちょう} and {調子|ちょうし}, and しら(べる) in {調|しら}べる. 朝, 長 and 町 are also read チョウ, but none of them is しらべる. Like 論 and 課, it starts with 言 (words).

questions.stem: In which word is 表 read あらわ?
questions.explanation: {表|あらわ}す (to express, to stand for) uses the kun reading あらわ. In {発表|はっぴょう} and {代表|だいひょう} it's ヒョウ (ピョウ after っ), and 表 alone is ひょう (a table) or おもて (the front).

questions.stem: Listen to the teacher. How should students send questions about the exam?

audio.text: しけんにかんするしつもんは、メールでおねがいします。

questions.explanation: {試験|しけん}に{関|かん}する{質問|しつもん}は、メールでお{願|ねが}いします: please send questions about the exam by email. に{関|かん}する makes the phrase a noun modifier: questions concerning the exam.

questions.stem: Listen. What will this seminar mainly focus on?

audio.text: こんかいのゼミでは、データのよみかたをちゅうしんにべんきょうします。

questions.explanation: {今回|こんかい}のゼミでは、データの{読|よ}み{方|かた}を{中心|ちゅうしん}に{勉強|べんきょう}します: in this seminar we'll study mainly how to read data. を{中心|ちゅうしん}に gives the main focus.

questions.stem: Listen to the student. What is the most natural reply from the professor?

audio.text: すみません、このろんぶんについて、すこししつもんしてもいいですか。

choices: いいえ、{論文|ろんぶん}です。
はい、{質問|しつもん}されました。
それはよかったですね。
questions.explanation: The student asks: すみません、この{論文|ろんぶん}について、{少|すこ}し{質問|しつもん}してもいいですか (may I ask a few questions about this paper?). The natural reply grants permission: ええ、どうぞ. The other replies don't answer a request.

questions.topic: について and に関して
questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: This paper is about the lives of international students.
questions.explanation: この{論文|ろんぶん}は{留学生|りゅうがくせい}の{生活|せいかつ}について{書|か}かれています。The topic + について comes before the verb; において (in, at) would give a place, not a topic.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: Japan has many dishes that are popular around the world, sushi first among them.
questions.explanation: {日本|にほん}には、すしをはじめ、{世界|せかい}で{人気|にんき}がある{料理|りょうり}がたくさんあります。The leading example (すし) comes before をはじめ, and the group it belongs to ({料理|りょうり}) follows.

questions.stem: Read the library notice: "{四月|しがつ}から、{図書館|としょかん}の{開館|かいかん}{時間|じかん}が{変|か}わります。{平日|へいじつ}は{朝|あさ}{八時|はちじ}から{夜|よる}{十時|じゅうじ}まで、{土曜日|どようび}は{朝|あさ}{十時|じゅうじ}から{夕方|ゆうがた}{五時|ごじ}までです。{日曜日|にちようび}は{休|やす}みです。{開館|かいかん}{時間|じかん}に{関|かん}する{質問|しつもん}は、{受付|うけつけ}までお{願|ねが}いします。" You want to study in the library at 7 pm on a Saturday in May. What does the notice tell you?
choices: You need to ask at reception first.
The library is closed on Saturdays.
The library closes at 5 pm on Saturdays.
questions.explanation: {土曜日|どようび}は…{夕方|ゆうがた}{五時|ごじ}まで: on Saturdays it's open until 5 pm, so 7 pm is too late. Ten o'clock is the weekday closing time, and it's Sunday that it's closed. {開館|かいかん} = opening (of a library or museum).

questions.stem: Read: "{北山|きたやま}{大学|だいがく}の{学生|がくせい}{五百人|ごひゃくにん}に、{一日|いちにち}の{勉強|べんきょう}{時間|じかん}についてちょうさした。{一番|いちばん}{多|おお}かったのは「{一時間|いちじかん}から{二時間|にじかん}」で、{全体|ぜんたい}の{四割|よんわり}だった。「{三時間|さんじかん}{以上|いじょう}」と{答|こた}えた{学生|がくせい}は、{全体|ぜんたい}の{二割|にわり}で、{科学|かがく}の{学部|がくぶ}の{学生|がくせい}が{中心|ちゅうしん}だった。" Who mostly answered "three hours or more"?
questions.explanation: {科学|かがく}の{学部|がくぶ}の{学生|がくせい}が{中心|ちゅうしん}だった: they were mainly students in science faculties. 〜が{中心|ちゅうしん}だ is the plain-statement form of を{中心|ちゅうしん}に. The text doesn't mention first-years, part-time jobs or graduate students. 〜{割|わり} = tenths: {四割|よんわり} is 40%, {二割|にわり} 20%.

questions.topic: によって and による
questions.stem: Fill the blank: "{国|くに}___、あいさつの{仕方|しかた}が{違|ちが}います。"
questions.explanation: "Depending on" is によって, followed by a word of difference such as {違|ちが}う: {国|くに}によって{違|ちが}う (it differs from country to country). によると is "according to" and ends in hearsay, に{代|か}わって is "on behalf of", and に{反|はん}して is "contrary to".

questions.topic: によって and による
questions.stem: Which sentence correctly says "The Tale of Genji was written by Murasaki Shikibu"?
choices: 『げんじものがたり』は、むらさきしきぶによると{書|か}かれた。
『げんじものがたり』は、むらさきしきぶに{代|か}わって{書|か}かれた。
『げんじものがたり』は、むらさきしきぶによって{書|か}かれた。
『げんじものがたり』は、むらさきしきぶと{違|ちが}って{書|か}かれた。
questions.explanation: When a passive names the creator of a work, the creator takes によって: むらさきしきぶによって{書|か}かれた. によると would make her the source of a report, に{代|か}わって would mean someone wrote it on her behalf, and と{違|ちが}って (unlike) makes no sense here.

questions.stem: Choose the correct form: "{電話|でんわ}する___、メールを{送|おく}りました。" (Instead of calling, I sent an email.)
questions.explanation: After a verb in the plain form, {代|か}わり comes straight after it: {電話|でんわ}する{代|か}わりに. の{代|か}わりに is for nouns ({電話|でんわ}の{代|か}わりに), so ×{電話|でんわ}するの{代|か}わりに is wrong. によって and に{反|はん}して don't mean "instead of".

questions.stem: What does this sentence mean? "この{仕事|しごと}は{給料|きゅうりょう}が{高|たか}い{代|か}わりに、{休|やす}みが{少|すく}ない。"
choices: This job pays well, but on the other hand there are few days off.
This job pays well instead of giving bonuses.
This job has few days off, so the pay is low.
This job pays well because nobody takes days off.
questions.explanation: Here {代|か}わりに balances a good point against a bad one: the pay is high, and in return (on the other hand) there are few days off. It doesn't give a reason (that would be から or ので), and nothing is said about bonuses.

questions.stem: Fill the blank: "{社長|しゃちょう}___、{部長|ぶちょう}があいさつをしました。" (The department head gave the speech on the president's behalf.)
questions.explanation: "On behalf of, in place of" is に{代|か}わって: {社長|しゃちょう}に{代|か}わって. に{反|はん}して is "contrary to", によって would make the president the means or cause, and と{違|ちが}って is "unlike".

questions.topic: に反して and と違って
questions.stem: Fill the blank: "みんなの{予想|よそう}___、{小|ちい}さなチームが{優勝|ゆうしょう}しました。"
questions.explanation: A result that goes against what people expected takes に{反|はん}して: {予想|よそう}に{反|はん}して (contrary to predictions). に{代|か}わって would mean "on behalf of the prediction", によって would make the prediction the cause, and をはじめ needs a group after it.

questions.topic: に反して and と違って
questions.stem: Fill the blank: "{東京|とうきょう}___、{私|わたし}の{町|まち}は{夜|よる}とても{静|しず}かです。" (Unlike Tokyo, my town is very quiet at night.)
questions.explanation: "Unlike" is と{違|ちが}って: one thing differs from another. に{反|はん}して is for results that go against expectations or rules, not for comparing two places; によって and に{代|か}わって mean "depending on" and "in place of".

questions.stem: Choose the best word: "{冬|ふゆ}は、{日本|にほん}とロンドンの___は{九時間|くじかん}です。"
questions.explanation: The difference in clock time between two places is {時差|じさ}. {日本|にほん}とロンドンの{時間|じかん}は{九時間|くじかん} doesn't say "difference", {方式|ほうしき} is a method or system, and {両方|りょうほう} means "both".

questions.stem: Which sentence uses {慣|な}れる correctly?
choices: {友|とも}だちに{本|ほん}を{慣|な}れました。
{新|あたら}しい{仕事|しごと}に、やっと{慣|な}れました。
{雨|あめ}が{慣|な}れて、{寒|さむ}くなった。
{毎朝|まいあさ}、コーヒーを{慣|な}れます。
questions.explanation: {慣|な}れる is "to get used to", and what you get used to takes に: {仕事|しごと}に{慣|な}れる. It's intransitive, so it never takes を, and it isn't used of the weather.

questions.stem: "この{町|まち}の{名産|めいさん}はりんごです。" Which sentence is closest in meaning?
choices: この{町|まち}では、りんごが{安|やす}く{買|か}えます。
この{町|まち}は、りんごで{有名|ゆうめい}です。
この{町|まち}では、りんごを{作|つく}っていません。
この{町|まち}の{人|ひと}は、りんごをよく{食|た}べます。
questions.explanation: {名産|めいさん} is a famous local product, so the town is known for its apples: りんごで{有名|ゆうめい}です. Being cheap or eaten a lot isn't the same, and the third choice says the opposite.

questions.stem: How is 種類 read? "この{店|みせ}には、いろいろな種類のパンがあります。"
questions.explanation: {種類|しゅるい} (kind, type) is an N4 word now written in kanji: 種 is シュ (short vowel) and 類 is ルイ. たね is 種's kun reading, used on its own ({種|たね}, a seed).

questions.stem: Which kanji is しま (island)? "{日本|にほん}には しま がたくさんあります。"
questions.explanation: 島 is しま: a bird (鳥) perched on a mountain (山) in the sea. 鳥 is とり (bird), 場 is ば (place) and 馬 is うま (horse).

questions.stem: Type the reading of お土産 in hiragana: "{旅行|りょこう}のお土産を{買|か}いました。"
questions.explanation: お{土産|みやげ} (a souvenir, a present from a trip) is a special reading: the whole word is みやげ, though 土 and 産 are ド and サン elsewhere. It's N5's おみやげ, now written in kanji.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker say about tipping?

audio.text: くにによっては、レストランでチップをはらわなければなりません。

choices: You must always tip in restaurants.
In some countries you have to tip in restaurants.
Tipping is rude in every country.
questions.explanation: {国|くに}によっては、レストランでチップを{払|はら}わなければなりません: in some countries you have to tip in restaurants. によっては means "in some (cases)", so it isn't "always" or "every country".

questions.stem: Listen. How does the speaker usually keep in touch with family?

audio.text: でんわのかわりに、メッセージをおくることがおおいです。

questions.explanation: {電話|でんわ}の{代|か}わりに、メッセージを{送|おく}ることが{多|おお}いです: instead of phoning, I usually send messages. The phone is what she doesn't use.

questions.stem: Listen to the question. What is the most natural reply?

audio.text: もうにほんのせいかつにはなれましたか。

choices: いいえ、{慣|な}れてください。
はい、{生活|せいかつ}しました。
はい、だいたい{慣|な}れました。
questions.explanation: もう{日本|にほん}の{生活|せいかつ}には{慣|な}れましたか: have you got used to life in Japan yet? The natural answer is はい、だいたい{慣|な}れました (yes, mostly). The other replies don't answer the question.

questions.topic: によって and による
questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: In some countries you have to tip in restaurants.
questions.explanation: {国|くに}によっては、レストランでチップを{払|はら}わなければなりません。によっては (in some cases) comes first; the place (で) and the object (を) can come in either order before the verb.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: Instead of rice, I eat bread every morning.
questions.explanation: {毎朝|まいあさ}、{米|こめ}の{代|か}わりにパンを{食|た}べています。A noun takes の{代|か}わりに; {代|か}わって is for "on behalf of" (に{代|か}わって). The time word can come first or after the {代|か}わりに phrase.

questions.stem: Read: "{日本|にほん}に{来|き}て{一番|いちばん}びっくりしたのは{電車|でんしゃ}だ。{私|わたし}の{国|くに}と{違|ちが}って、{日本|にほん}の{電車|でんしゃ}はほとんど{遅|おく}れない。でも、{朝|あさ}はとても{込|こ}んでいる。それで{私|わたし}は、{電車|でんしゃ}の{代|か}わりに{自転車|じてんしゃ}で{大学|だいがく}に{通|かよ}うことにした。{雨|あめ}の{日|ひ}は{大変|たいへん}だが、いい{運動|うんどう}にもなる。" Why does the writer cycle to university?
choices: The writer's home country has no trains.
questions.explanation: でも、{朝|あさ}はとても{込|こ}んでいる。それで…{自転車|じてんしゃ}で{通|かよ}うことにした: the trains are very crowded in the morning, so the writer cycles. The trains are hardly ever late ({遅|おく}れない), unlike in the writer's country; money isn't mentioned. {込|こ}む = to be crowded.

questions.stem: Read the notice: "{国際|こくさい}{交流|こうりゅう}パーティーのお{知|し}らせ / {日時|にちじ}：{六月|ろくがつ}{十日|とおか}（{土|ど}）{午後|ごご}{六時|ろくじ}から / {場所|ばしょ}：{市民|しみん}センター / {参加費|さんかひ}：{五百円|ごひゃくえん}。{自分|じぶん}の{国|くに}の{料理|りょうり}を{一|ひと}つ{持|も}ってきた{方|かた}は、{無料|むりょう}です。" Ana is bringing a dish from her country. How much does she pay?
choices: 500 yen, plus the cost of the dish
questions.explanation: {自分|じぶん}の{国|くに}の{料理|りょうり}を{一|ひと}つ{持|も}ってきた{方|かた}は、{無料|むりょう}です: people who bring a dish from their own country get in free. {参加費|さんかひ} = the entry fee; {無料|むりょう} = free of charge.

questions.stem: Fill the blank: "{去年|きょねん}___、{今年|ことし}は{観光客|かんこうきゃく}が{二割|にわり}{増|ふ}えました。"
questions.explanation: The sentence compares this year with last year, so it's に{比|くら}べて (compared with). にかけて marks the end of a span (から〜にかけて), を{通|とお}して is "throughout, through", and において is a formal "in, at". {二割|にわり} = 20%.

questions.stem: Fill the blank in this forecast: "{明日|あした}は、{関東|かんとう}から{東北|とうほく}___、{雪|ゆき}が{降|ふ}るでしょう。"
questions.explanation: A loose span of area, as in forecasts, is から〜にかけて: {関東|かんとう}から{東北|とうほく}にかけて (from Kanto up through Tohoku). The others don't pair with から: に{比|くら}べて compares, を{通|とお}して is "throughout", and のうちで is "among".

questions.stem: Which sentence is NOT natural Japanese?
choices: {三月|さんがつ}から{四月|しがつ}にかけて、さくらがさきます。
{夜|よる}から{朝|あさ}にかけて、{強|つよ}い{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}ります。
{関西|かんさい}から{四国|しこく}にかけて、{台風|たいふう}が{通|とお}ります。
{店|みせ}は{九時|くじ}から{五時|ごじ}にかけて{開|あ}いています。
questions.explanation: Opening hours have exact ends, so they take から〜まで: {九時|くじ}から{五時|ごじ}まで{開|あ}いています. から〜にかけて is for spans with loose edges: seasons, nights, regions.

questions.stem: Fill the blank: "この{島|しま}は、{一年|いちねん}___ {温|あたた}かいです。" (This island is warm all year round.)
questions.explanation: "All through (a period)" is を{通|とお}して: {一年|いちねん}を{通|とお}して. にかけて needs から before it, に{比|くら}べて would compare the island with a year, and において (in, at) is for events and fields.

questions.stem: What does を{通|とお}して mean in "{友人|ゆうじん}を{通|とお}して、{今|いま}の{会社|かいしゃ}を{知|し}りました。"?
questions.explanation: With a person or a means, を{通|とお}して is "through, by way of": I found out about my current company through a friend. With a period of time ({一年|いちねん}を{通|とお}して) it would be "throughout".

questions.stem: Fill the blank (written style): "{日本|にほん}で___ {高|たか}い{山|やま}は、ふじさんです。"
questions.explanation: {最|もっと}も is the written "most": {日本|にほん}で{最|もっと}も{高|たか}い{山|やま} (the highest mountain in Japan). もっと means "more" and needs something to compare with; より and ほど mark what something is compared to and can't go before an adjective like this.

questions.stem: What does this sentence mean? "{京都|きょうと}ほど{古|ふる}い{寺|てら}が{多|おお}い{町|まち}はない。"
choices: Kyoto doesn't have many old temples.
Kyoto has fewer old temples than other cities.
There are old temples in Kyoto, but not many.
No city has as many old temples as Kyoto.
questions.explanation: A ほど〜はない means "nothing is as … as A", so it's a superlative: no city has as many old temples as Kyoto. The ない belongs to {町|まち}はない (there is no such city), not to Kyoto's temples.

questions.stem: Choose the best word: "{山|やま}を___と、{海|うみ}が{見|み}えてきます。"
questions.explanation: Crossing over a mountain is {山|やま}を{越|こ}える. {寄|よ}る (to drop in) takes に, {向|む}ける (to point something) needs an object you turn, and you can't swim a mountain.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses {訪|おとず}れる correctly?
choices: {電話|でんわ}で{友|とも}だちに{訪|おとず}れました。
{窓|まど}を{訪|おとず}れてください。
{毎朝|まいあさ}、{駅|えき}まで{訪|おとず}れて{歩|ある}きます。
{毎年|まいとし}、{多|おお}くの{人|ひと}がこの{島|しま}を{訪|おとず}れます。
questions.explanation: {訪|おとず}れる is "to visit (a place)", a written word, and the place takes を: この{島|しま}を{訪|おとず}れる. You can't visit by phone, it isn't a way of walking, and a window isn't visited.

questions.stem: "{京都|きょうと}まで{日帰|ひがえ}りで{行|い}きました。" Which sentence is closest in meaning?
choices: {京都|きょうと}に{行|い}って、その{日|ひ}のうちに{帰|かえ}りました。
{京都|きょうと}に{一週間|いっしゅうかん}いました。
{京都|きょうと}に{毎日|まいにち}{行|い}きました。
{京都|きょうと}から{帰|かえ}ってきませんでした。
questions.explanation: {日帰|ひがえ}り is a day trip: going and coming back on the same day. その{日|ひ}のうちに{帰|かえ}る says exactly that. A week, every day or not coming back are all different.

questions.stem: How is 景色 read? "ここから{見|み}る景色は、すばらしいです。"
questions.explanation: {景色|けしき} (scenery) is a special reading of the whole word, N5's けしき now in kanji. 景 is ケイ in other words ({風景|ふうけい}, {夜景|やけい}) and 色 is いろ or ショク, which is why the other choices look tempting.

questions.stem: Which kanji is the おう of おうだん (crossing)? "ここで{道|みち}を おうだん しないでください。"
questions.explanation: {横断|おうだん} uses 横 (side, across), as in {横|よこ} and {横切|よこぎ}る. 王 (king) and 押 (push) are also read オウ, and 構 (lesson 29) looks like 横 but is コウ.

questions.stem: Type the reading of 登山 in hiragana: "{夏|なつ}は{家族|かぞく}で登山をします。"
questions.explanation: {登山|とざん} (mountain climbing): 登 is read ト here, not トウ or のぼ(る), and 山 is ザン, voiced from サン. N5's {山登|やまのぼ}り means much the same in everyday speech.

questions.stem: Listen to the forecast. Where will it snow tomorrow?

audio.text: あしたは、かんとうからとうほくにかけて、ゆきがふるでしょう。

questions.explanation: {明日|あした}は、{関東|かんとう}から{東北|とうほく}にかけて、{雪|ゆき}が{降|ふ}るでしょう: tomorrow it will snow from Kanto up through Tohoku. から〜にかけて gives the area.

questions.stem: Listen to the guide. What does she say about the island?

audio.text: このしまは、いちねんをとおしてあたたかいので、ふゆでもおよげます。

choices: It's too cold to swim in winter.
It's warm all year round, so you can swim even in winter.
It's warm, but swimming isn't allowed.
questions.explanation: この{島|しま}は、{一年|いちねん}を{通|とお}して{温|あたた}かいので、{冬|ふゆ}でも{泳|およ}げます: the island is warm all year round, so you can swim even in winter.

questions.stem: Listen to your friend. What is the most natural reply?

audio.text: かえりに、ちょっとよりみちしていかない？

choices: うん、{寄|よ}り{道|みち}だったね。
いいえ、{帰|かえ}りません。
{道|みち}が{寄|よ}っていますよ。
questions.explanation: {帰|かえ}りに、ちょっと{寄|よ}り{道|みち}していかない？ is an invitation: shall we stop off somewhere on the way home? The natural reply accepts and asks where: いいね。どこに{寄|よ}る？ The others talk about the past or make no sense.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: Compared with last year, there are more tourists this year.
questions.explanation: {去年|きょねん}に{比|くら}べて、{今年|ことし}は{観光客|かんこうきゃく}が{増|ふ}えました。The thing compared with (+ に{比|くら}べて) and the topic ({今年|ことし}は) can come in either order; the change ({増|ふ}えました) comes last.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: The cherry blossoms are at their best from the end of March into April.
questions.explanation: {三月|さんがつ}の{終|お}わりから{四月|しがつ}にかけて、さくらが{見|み}ごろです。から marks the start of the span and にかけて its loose end; the subject さくらが can also come first.

questions.stem: Read the inn's notice: "チェックインは{午後|ごご}{三時|さんじ}から{七時|しちじ}まで、チェックアウトは{午前|ごぜん}{十時|じゅうじ}までです。{夕食|ゆうしょく}は{六時|ろくじ}からです。{七時|しちじ}より{遅|おそ}く{着|つ}く{方|かた}は、{前|まえ}の{日|ひ}までにお{電話|でんわ}ください。{十二月|じゅうにがつ}から{三月|さんがつ}にかけては、{雪|ゆき}のため、{駅|えき}からのバスは{一日|いちにち}{二回|にかい}だけになります。" You will arrive at 8 pm on 20 January. What should you do?
choices: Nothing: you can check in until ten.
Phone the inn by the day before.
Take the 8 pm bus from the station.
questions.explanation: {七時|しちじ}より{遅|おそ}く{着|つ}く{方|かた}は、{前|まえ}の{日|ひ}までにお{電話|でんわ}ください: anyone arriving after seven should phone by the day before. Check-in ends at seven, and the notice says only that buses run twice a day in winter, not when.

questions.stem: Read: "{北|きた}の{町|まち}と{南|みなみ}の{町|まち}を{比|くら}べると、{夏|なつ}は{南|みなみ}の{町|まち}のほうが{観光客|かんこうきゃく}が{多|おお}い。しかし{冬|ふゆ}は、スキーのため、{北|きた}の{町|まち}に{比|くら}べて、{南|みなみ}の{町|まち}は{観光客|かんこうきゃく}が{三割|さんわり}ぐらい{少|すく}ない。{一年|いちねん}を{通|とお}して{最|もっと}も{観光客|かんこうきゃく}が{多|おお}いのは、{北|きた}の{町|まち}の{二月|にがつ}だ。" When does the northern town get the most tourists?
questions.explanation: {一年|いちねん}を{通|とお}して{最|もっと}も{観光客|かんこうきゃく}が{多|おお}いのは、{北|きた}の{町|まち}の{二月|にがつ}だ: across the whole year, the busiest time is February in the northern town. In summer it's the southern town that has more tourists.

questions.stem: Fill the blank: "{試合|しあい}の{後|あと}、{立|た}てない___ {疲|つか}れていました。" (After the match I was so tired I couldn't stand.)
questions.explanation: Degree ("so … that") is ほど (or くらい) after the clause: {立|た}てないほど{疲|つか}れていた. さえ and こそ are emphatic particles that pick out one item, and せめて is an adverb, "at least".

questions.stem: Fill the blank: "{一回|いっかい}___ {勝|か}ちたいなあ。" (I'd like to win at least once.)
questions.explanation: Only くらい (ぐらい) marks a minimum, "at least, just": {一回|いっかい}くらい{勝|か}ちたい. {一回|いっかい}ほど would mean "about once", こそ would stress "once and no other number", and あまり doesn't fit after a number here.

questions.stem: Fill the blank: "{忙|いそが}しくて、{水|みず}を{飲|の}む{時間|じかん}___ありませんでした。"
questions.explanation: さえ picks out an extreme case: not even time to drink water (so certainly no time for anything else). こそ stresses something positive or important, ほど gives degree, and せめて is an adverb that can't follow a noun.

questions.stem: Choose the correct form: "{毎日|まいにち}{練習|れんしゅう}___、{必|かなら}ず{上達|じょうたつ}しますよ。" (As long as you practise every day, you're sure to improve.)
questions.explanation: With a する verb, さえ goes after the noun part and before すれば: {練習|れんしゅう}さえすれば. さえ replaces を, so ×をさえ is wrong; it can't come after the conditional (×すればさえ); and 〜ても means "even if", not "as long as".

questions.stem: Fill the blank: "{去年|きょねん}は{負|ま}けたけど、{今年|ことし}___ {優勝|ゆうしょう}したい。"
questions.explanation: "This year for sure" (after losing before) is こそ: {今年|ことし}こそ. {今年|ことし}さえ would be "even this year", which doesn't fit a wish to win; ほど and くらい give degree or amount.

questions.stem: What does this sentence mean? "{好|す}きだからこそ、{毎日|まいにち}{練習|れんしゅう}を{続|つづ}けられる。"
choices: Even though I love it, I can't keep practising every day.
I love it, but I only practise because I have to.
Because I practise every day, I've come to love it.
It's precisely because I love it that I can keep practising every day.
questions.explanation: 〜からこそ is "precisely because": the love is the reason, and こそ stresses that it's this reason and no other. The order is love → practice, not practice → love, and nothing is said about "having to".

questions.topic: あまり and せめて
questions.stem: Fill the blank: "きんちょうの___、{何|なに}も{言|い}えませんでした。" (I was so nervous I couldn't say anything.)
questions.explanation: Noun + のあまり is "so (much feeling) that": きんちょうのあまり (from sheer nerves). ×きんちょうのほど isn't used, and さえ / こそ would pick out the nerves as an example, not as the cause. (きんちょう = nervousness.)

questions.topic: あまり and せめて
questions.stem: Which sentence is NOT natural Japanese?
choices: せめて{一回|いっかい}は{勝|か}ちたい。
せめて{名前|なまえ}だけでも{教|おし}えてください。
{少|すく}なくとも{三百人|さんびゃくにん}のファンが{来|き}た。
せめて{三百人|さんびゃくにん}のファンが{来|き}た。
questions.explanation: せめて goes with wishes, hopes and requests (〜たい, 〜てください), not with plain facts. For "at least 300 fans came", use {少|すく}なくとも, as in the third sentence.

questions.stem: Choose the best word: "{一回戦|いっかいせん}で___してしまい、{大会|たいかい}はすぐに{終|お}わってしまった。"
questions.explanation: Being knocked out of a tournament is {敗退|はいたい}する: knocked out in the first round, so the tournament was over quickly. {優勝|ゆうしょう} is winning the whole thing, {上達|じょうたつ} is improving, and おうえん is cheering.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses {相手|あいて} correctly?
choices: {次|つぎ}の{試合|しあい}の{相手|あいて}は、{去年|きょねん}の{優勝|ゆうしょう}チームです。
{毎朝|まいあさ}、{相手|あいて}で{走|はし}っています。
この{相手|あいて}はとてもおいしいです。
{相手|あいて}を{三時|さんじ}に{始|はじ}めます。
questions.explanation: {相手|あいて} is the other side: an opponent, or the person you deal with. {次|つぎ}の{試合|しあい}の{相手|あいて} is "our opponent in the next match". It isn't a place, a food or an event you start.

questions.stem: How is 選手 read? "{彼|かれ}は{有名|ゆうめい}なサッカーの選手です。"
questions.explanation: {選手|せんしゅ} (player, athlete) is an N4 word now in kanji: 選 is セン (えら(ぶ) is its kun reading, in {選|えら}ぶ) and 手 is シュ here, not て.

questions.stem: Which kanji is the か of かつ (to win)? "{次|つぎ}の{試合|しあい}は、{絶対|ぜったい}に かち たい。"
questions.explanation: {勝|か}つ (to win) is 勝: the moon (月) and strength (力). 買 is か(う) (buy), 書 is か(く) (write) and 貸 is か(す) (lend): all か, but other verbs.

questions.stem: In which word is 最 read もっと?
questions.explanation: {最|もっと}も (most) uses the kun reading もっと(も). In {最高|さいこう}, {最後|さいご} and {最近|さいきん}, 最 is サイ.

questions.stem: Listen. When will the match be held?

audio.text: あしたさえはれれば、しあいはあります。

choices: As long as it's fine tomorrow
questions.explanation: {明日|あした}さえ{晴|は}れれば、{試合|しあい}はあります: as long as it's fine tomorrow, the match is on. さえ〜ば makes the weather the one condition.

questions.stem: Listen. What happened in the match?

audio.text: あまりにもあいてがつよくて、いってんもとれませんでした。

choices: The other side was so strong that they didn't score a single point.
questions.explanation: あまりにも{相手|あいて}が{強|つよ}くて、{一点|いってん}も{取|と}れませんでした: the other side was so strong that we couldn't get a single point. {一点|いってん}も + negative is "not even one point".

questions.stem: Listen to your teammate. What is the most natural reply?

audio.text: こんどこそ、かとうね！

choices: {今度|こんど}は{何|なん}ですか。
それはこまりましたね。
questions.explanation: {今度|こんど}こそ、{勝|か}とうね！ means "let's win this time for sure!". The natural reply agrees: うん、がんばろう！ (yeah, let's give it our all!). The others don't answer the call.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: As long as the weather is good, the match will go ahead.
questions.explanation: {天気|てんき}さえよければ、{試合|しあい}はあります。さえ follows the noun and comes before the conditional (よければ, from いい); the result comes after. こそ would stress the weather but can't make an "as long as" condition.

questions.topic: あまり and せめて
questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: I was so happy that I cried.
questions.explanation: {私|わたし}は、うれしさのあまり{泣|な}いてしまいました。Noun + のあまり gives the feeling that caused it; 〜てしまう shows it happened without meaning to. The topic {私|わたし}は can also come after the あまり phrase.

questions.stem: Read: "{私|わたし}は{子供|こども}のころ、{泳|およ}げなかった。{顔|かお}を{水|みず}につけることさえ{怖|こわ}かった。{十歳|じゅっさい}のとき、{水泳|すいえい}{教室|きょうしつ}に{入|はい}ると、コーチは「{毎日|まいにち}{少|すこ}しずつでいい。{続|つづ}けさえすれば、{必|かなら}ず{泳|およ}げるようになる」と{言|い}った。その{言葉|ことば}を{信|しん}じて{続|つづ}けた{結果|けっか}、{一年後|いちねんご}には{五十|ごじゅう}メートル{泳|およ}げるようになった。" What did the coach say?
choices: You must practise for hours every day.
As long as you keep at it, you'll learn to swim.
Swimming is only for strong children.
questions.explanation: {続|つづ}けさえすれば、{必|かなら}ず{泳|およ}げるようになる: as long as you keep going, you'll certainly be able to swim. The coach said a little each day is enough ({少|すこ}しずつでいい). Earlier, さえ in {顔|かお}を{水|みず}につけることさえ{怖|こわ}かった means even putting their face in the water frightened the writer.

questions.stem: Read the notice: "{市民|しみん}しょうぎ{大会|たいかい} / {日時|にちじ}：{十一月|じゅういちがつ}{三日|みっか}（{日|にち}）{午前|ごぜん}{九時|くじ}から / {参加費|さんかひ}：{大人|おとな}{千円|せんえん}、{中学生|ちゅうがくせい}{以下|いか}は{無料|むりょう} / {三位|さんい}までの{方|かた}には{記念品|きねんひん}があります。{初心者|しょしんしゃ}も{参加|さんか}できます。" A junior high school student wants to enter. How much does it cost?
choices: It depends on where they finish.
questions.explanation: {中学生|ちゅうがくせい}{以下|いか}は{無料|むりょう}: junior high school students and younger take part free. 1,000 yen is for adults. The top three ({三位|さんい}まで) get a {記念品|きねんひん} (a commemorative gift), but that doesn't change the fee.

questions.stem: In Japanese job hunting, what is a {内定|ないてい}?
questions.explanation: {内定|ないてい} is an informal job offer, given before graduation; {内定|ないてい}をもらう is "to get an offer". An information session is a {説明会|せつめいかい}, a company's form is an エントリーシート, and the tests are written tests.

questions.stem: In an interview, a student talks about the company they are applying to. Which word do they use for "your company"?
questions.explanation: In speech, the applicant says おんしゃ. きしゃ is the written word (for an entry sheet or an email), and {当社|とうしゃ} is what the company's own staff say about their company.

questions.stem: Which word does an applicant write in an entry sheet or an email for "your company"?
questions.explanation: In writing, it's きしゃ; おんしゃ is for speech. {当社|とうしゃ} is "our company" (said by its staff) and {本社|ほんしゃ} is a head office.

questions.stem: Fill the blank in this interview answer: "{大学|だいがく}では、サークルのリーダー___、{五十人|ごじゅうにん}のメンバーをまとめました。"
questions.explanation: A role takes として: サークルのリーダーとして (as the club's leader). にとって needs a judgement after it, に{対|たい}して would make the leader the target, and によって would make the leader the means. まとめる = to bring together, to lead.

questions.stem: Fill the blank: "{私|わたし}___、{働|はたら}くことは{人|ひと}の{役|やく}に{立|た}つことです。"
questions.explanation: The sentence says what working means from the speaker's point of view, so にとって: {私|わたし}にとって (for me). {私|わたし}として would be about the speaker's role, に{関|かん}して is "concerning", and をはじめ needs a group after it.

questions.stem: An entry sheet asks for your しぼう{動機|どうき}. What should you write?
choices: Why you want to join the company
questions.explanation: しぼう is your choice, what you hope for, and {動機|どうき} is a motive: しぼう{動機|どうき} is why you want to join. {第一|だいいち}しぼう is your first choice.

questions.stem: Which statement about the job-hunting calendar matches the lesson?
choices: Every company waits until 1 June to hold interviews.
Offers are only given in April, when work starts.
The timetable is a guideline that many companies don't keep to strictly.
Students usually apply to one company at a time.
questions.explanation: The government asks companies to follow a timetable (March, June, October), but it's a guideline: many companies start earlier, and informal offers often come before October. Students usually apply to many companies; April is when work starts, not when offers are made.

questions.stem: Listen. This is the end of an interview. What is the interviewer asking?

audio.text: さいごに、なにかしつもんはありますか。

questions.explanation: {最後|さいご}に、{何|なに}か{質問|しつもん}はありますか: finally, do you have any questions? Applicants usually prepare one or two good questions for this moment.

questions.stem: Listen. What happened?

audio.text: だいいちしぼうのかいしゃから、ないていをもらいました。

choices: She got an offer from her first-choice company.
She sent her first entry sheet.
She went to her first information session.
questions.explanation: {第一|だいいち}しぼうの{会社|かいしゃ}から、{内定|ないてい}をもらいました: I got an offer from my first-choice company. {第一|だいいち}しぼう is "first choice", and {内定|ないてい}をもらう is "to get an offer".

questions.stem: Listen to the interviewer. What is the most natural reply?

audio.text: それでは、じこしょうかいをおねがいします。

choices: はい、しょうかいしてください。
はい。{北山|きたやま}{大学|だいがく}の{木下|きのした}ともうします。
questions.explanation: じこしょうかいをお{願|ねが}いします asks you to introduce yourself, so you begin with your university and name: {北山|きたやま}{大学|だいがく}の{木下|きのした}ともうします. もうします is the humble "am called". どうぞよろしく ends an introduction; it isn't one.

questions.stem: Read the notice: "ミナト{商事|しょうじ}では、{来年|らいねん}{三月|さんがつ}に{卒業|そつぎょう}する{予定|よてい}の{方|かた}のために、オンラインの{会社|かいしゃ}{説明会|せつめいかい}を{行|おこな}います。{参加|さんか}の{方法|ほうほう}は、エントリーした{方|かた}にメールでお{知|し}らせします。エントリーシートは、この{説明会|せつめいかい}に{参加|さんか}した{方|かた}だけが{出|だ}すことができます。" Who can submit an entry sheet?
choices: Only people who attended the information session
Only people who graduated last March
questions.explanation: エントリーシートは、この{説明会|せつめいかい}に{参加|さんか}した{方|かた}だけが{出|だ}すことができます: only people who attended the session can submit one. Signing up (エントリー) gets you the email with joining details, but isn't enough on its own.

questions.stem: Read the email: "{木下|きのした}そうた{様|さま} / ミナト{商事|しょうじ}の{山田|やまだ}です。{先日|せんじつ}は、めんせつにお{越|こ}しいただき、ありがとうございました。{選考|せんこう}の{結果|けっか}、{木下|きのした}{様|さま}に{内定|ないてい}をお{出|だ}しすることになりました。{十月|じゅうがつ}{一日|ついたち}に{内定式|ないていしき}を{行|おこな}いますので、{本社|ほんしゃ}までお{越|こ}しください。" What is this email about?
choices: Sota must come for another interview on 1 October.
Sota has been offered a job and is invited to a ceremony on 1 October.
Sota must send his CV by 1 October.
questions.explanation: {内定|ないてい}をお{出|だ}しすることになりました: we have decided to offer you a job. {十月|じゅうがつ}{一日|ついたち}に{内定式|ないていしき}を{行|おこな}います: the offer ceremony is on 1 October. お{越|こ}しください is a polite "please come"; {選考|せんこう} = selection; {先日|せんじつ} = the other day.

questions.stem: Fill the blank: "{自転車|じてんしゃ}で{通勤|つうきん}すれば、{運動|うんどう}にもなるし、お{金|かね}もかからない。まさに___だ。"
choices: {一石二鳥|いっせきにちょう}
{十人十色|じゅうにんといろ}
questions.explanation: Two good results from one action (exercise and no fares) is {一石二鳥|いっせきにちょう}: two birds with one stone. {十人十色|じゅうにんといろ} is "everyone is different", {花|はな}よりだんご is "the practical over the pretty", and {急|いそ}がば{回|まわ}れ is "more haste, less speed".

questions.stem: A friend wants to quit a new job after only two months. Which proverb would you use to encourage them to stay?
choices: {一石二鳥|いっせきにちょう}
{石|いし}の{上|うえ}にも{三年|さんねん}
{十人十色|じゅうにんといろ}
questions.explanation: {石|いし}の{上|うえ}にも{三年|さんねん} (even a cold stone gets warm if you sit on it for three years) says patience pays off: a classic thing to say to someone new in a job.

questions.stem: What does {十人十色|じゅうにんといろ} mean?
choices: Ten people are better than one.
Everyone has their own tastes and ideas.
questions.explanation: {十人十色|じゅうにんといろ} is literally "ten people, ten colours": everyone is different, to each their own.

questions.stem: How is 十人十色 read?
choices: じゅうにんじゅうしょく
じゅうにんじゅういろ
questions.explanation: {十人十色|じゅうにんといろ}: {十人|じゅうにん} uses the usual じゅう, but {十色|といろ} uses the native readings と (ten) and いろ (colour). It's a reading you have to learn with the word.

questions.stem: In {急|いそ}がば{回|まわ}れ, いそがば is old grammar. What is it in modern Japanese?
questions.explanation: いそがば is a classical conditional: "if you hurry". Modern Japanese says {急|いそ}げば. {回|まわ}れ is the imperative of {回|まわ}る: go round.

questions.stem: {花|はな}よりだんご describes someone who…
choices: prefers practical things, such as food, to beauty
questions.explanation: {花|はな}よりだんご (dumplings rather than flowers) is said, usually with a smile, about people who care more about food or practical things than beauty, like people at a cherry-blossom party who only eat.

questions.stem: Which is a natural, casual way to bring a proverb into what you're saying?
questions.explanation: 〜って{言|い}うでしょう (or 〜って{言|い}うじゃない) is "as they say, don't they": {石|いし}の{上|うえ}にも{三年|さんねん}って{言|い}うでしょう. The other three don't introduce a saying.

questions.stem: Fill the blank: "それ___ {急|いそ}がば{回|まわ}れだよ。" (That's exactly what "more haste, less speed" means.)
questions.explanation: こそ picks out "that, and nothing else": それこそ〜だ is "that's exactly…". さえ (even), ほど (to the extent) and くらい (about, at least) don't give this emphasis.

questions.stem: Listen. How does the speaker feel?

audio.text: しけんにさんかいおちたけど、ななころびやおきだ。らいねんこそごうかくする。

choices: They're giving up on the exam.
They'll keep trying, and will pass next year for sure.
They passed on the third try.
They think the exam is too easy.
questions.explanation: {試験|しけん}に{三回|さんかい}{落|お}ちたけど、{七転|ななころ}び{八起|やお}きだ。{来年|らいねん}こそ{合格|ごうかく}する: I've failed three times, but fall seven times, get up eight; next year I'll pass for sure. こそ adds "this time for sure".

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker suggest?

audio.text: ちかみちはあぶないから、いそがばまわれで、おおきいみちをいこう。

choices: Taking the main road, because the short cut is dangerous
Taking the short cut to save time
Running so they won't be late
questions.explanation: {近道|ちかみち}は{危|あぶ}ないから、{急|いそ}がば{回|まわ}れで、{大|おお}きい{道|みち}を{行|い}こう: the short cut is dangerous, so, more haste less speed, let's take the main road.

questions.stem: Read: "{今週|こんしゅう}のことわざは「{花|はな}よりだんご」です。{春|はる}になると、{多|おお}くの{人|ひと}が{公園|こうえん}で{花見|はなみ}をします。でも、さくらを{見|み}るより、おべんとうを{食|た}べたり、{友|とも}だちと{話|はな}したりするほうが{楽|たの}しいという{人|ひと}も{少|すく}なくありません。{悪|わる}い{意味|いみ}で{使|つか}うこともありますが、たいていは{笑|わら}いながら{言|い}います。" How is this proverb usually said?
questions.explanation: たいていは{笑|わら}いながら{言|い}います: it's usually said with a laugh, though it can be used in a bad sense. {少|すく}なくありません = there are quite a few.

questions.stem: Read: "{兄|あに}は{料理|りょうり}が{好|す}きで、{弟|おとうと}はスポーツが{好|す}きだ。{妹|いもうと}は{一日中|いちにちじゅう}{本|ほん}を{読|よ}んでいる。{同|おな}じ{家|いえ}で{育|そだ}っても、{好|この}みは{本当|ほんとう}にいろいろだ。" Which saying sums this up best?
choices: {一石二鳥|いっせきにちょう}
{十人十色|じゅうにんといろ}
{石|いし}の{上|うえ}にも{三年|さんねん}
questions.explanation: Brothers and a sister from the same home, with completely different tastes: {十人十色|じゅうにんといろ}, everyone is different. The others are about double benefits, patience and taking the safe way.

questions.topic: っぽい and らしい
questions.stem: {三十歳|さんじゅっさい}にもなって、そんなことで{泣|な}くのは___よ。 (It's childish to cry over something like that at thirty.)
questions.explanation: {子供|こども}っぽい criticizes an adult for behaving like a child. {子供|こども}らしい is the tempting one, but it praises a child for being charmingly childlike, so it doesn't fit a grown-up. {子供|こども}{向|む}け means "made for children", and {気味|ぎみ} doesn't join {子供|こども}.

questions.stem: {今日|きょう}はちょっとかぜ___なので、{早|はや}く{寝|ね}ます。 (I've got a touch of a cold today.)
questions.explanation: かぜ{気味|ぎみ} is "a slight cold", a mild state right now, which is what {気味|ぎみ} expresses. がち is about something that happens often, and it follows a ます stem (かぜをひきがち: tends to catch colds), not かぜ alone. だらけ (covered in) and {的|てき} (-ic) make no sense here.

questions.stem: {冬|ふゆ}はあまり{外|そと}に{出|で}ないので、{運動|うんどう}{不足|ぶそく}になり___だ。
questions.explanation: なりがち: "tends to become". がち follows a ます stem (なり) and describes an unwelcome thing that happens easily in a situation (in winter). っぽい after a ます stem describes a character trait ({忘|わす}れっぽい), and なりっぽい isn't a word. だらけ and {向|む}き follow nouns.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses だらけ naturally?
choices: {庭|にわ}は{花|はな}だらけで、とてもきれいだ。
{雨|あめ}の{中|なか}で{遊|あそ}んで、{靴|くつ}がどろだらけになった。
この{店|みせ}はおいしいものだらけで、うれしい。
{彼女|かのじょ}はいつも{笑顔|えがお}だらけだ。
questions.explanation: だらけ means "covered in, full of" something unpleasant: shoes covered in mud is a typical use. With things you like (flowers, good food, smiles) it sounds as if they were a nuisance; say {花|はな}でいっぱい or おいしいものが{多|おお}い instead.

questions.stem: {市|し}が、{日本|にほん}に{住|す}む{外国人|がいこくじん}___の{生活|せいかつ}ガイドを{作|つく}った。 (a guide made for foreigners living in Japan)
questions.explanation: {向|む}け means "made for, aimed at" a target group, on purpose: the city made the guide for foreigners. {向|む}き is the tempting one, but it only says something suits a group by its nature, which misses the point of a guide written for them. っぽい and らしい describe resemblance, not a target.

questions.stem: Complete with a 〜{的|てき} word meaning "specifically, concretely": どんな{服|ふく}が{欲|ほ}しいのか、___に{教|おし}えてください。
questions.explanation: {具体的|ぐたいてき}に: specifically, in concrete terms. 〜{的|てき} makes a な-adjective, so before a verb it takes に: {具体的|ぐたいてき}に{教|おし}える.

questions.topic: っぽい and らしい
questions.stem: {子供|こども}は{子供|こども}___、{外|そと}で{元気|げんき}に{遊|あそ}んでほしい。 (I want children to be children and play outside.)
questions.explanation: N + らしい is "as X should be, typical of X", usually praise: {子供|こども}らしく (in a childlike way, as children should). {子供|こども}っぽく would criticize someone for being childish, which makes no sense about children. {気味|ぎみ} and がち don't follow {子供|こども}.

questions.stem: {妹|いもうと}は{知|し}らない{人|ひと}の{前|まえ}では、{何|なに}も{話|はな}せなくなる。かなりの___だ。
questions.explanation: {人見知|ひとみし}り is being shy with people you don't know, exactly what the first sentence describes. {社交的|しゃこうてき} (sociable) is the opposite; わがまま (spoilt) and {生意気|なまいき} (cheeky) are about attitude, not shyness.

questions.stem: {祖父|そふ}は{最近|さいきん}、{忘|わす}れっぽくなった。 Which is closest in meaning?
choices: {祖父|そふ}は{最近|さいきん}、{忘|わす}れたふりをする。
{祖父|そふ}は{最近|さいきん}、{一度|いちど}だけ{物|もの}を{忘|わす}れた。
{祖父|そふ}は{最近|さいきん}、{何|なに}も{忘|わす}れなくなった。
{祖父|そふ}は{最近|さいきん}、よく{物|もの}を{忘|わす}れる。
questions.explanation: {忘|わす}れっぽい (ます stem + っぽい) is "forgetful": forgetting things easily and often. Forgetting once is not a habit, and pretending to forget (ふりをする, lesson 5) is something else.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses {地味|じみ} correctly?
choices: {地味|じみ}の{日|ひ}は、{外|そと}で{遊|あそ}ぶのが{一番|いちばん}だ。
{地味|じみ}な{色|いろ}のスーツで、めんせつに{行|い}った。
{田中|たなか}さんは{地味|じみ}が{上手|じょうず}で、よく{絵|え}をかく。
{試験|しけん}に{地味|じみ}して、{合格|ごうかく}した。
questions.explanation: {地味|じみ} is a な-adjective, "plain, understated": a plain-coloured suit for an interview is a typical use. It isn't a kind of day, a skill or a verb, so the other three don't work.

questions.stem: {美容院|びよういん}で前髪を{少|すこ}し{切|き}ってもらった。 How is 「前髪」 read?
questions.explanation: {前髪|まえがみ} (fringe): {前|まえ} + {髪|かみ}, with かみ voiced to がみ. まえかみ forgets the voicing; ハツ is 髪's on'yomi ({長髪|ちょうはつ}), but this word uses the kun reading.

questions.stem: あの{人|ひと}は、せいかくがとても{明|あか}るい。 Which kanji is せいかく?
questions.explanation: {性格|せいかく} (personality) is 性 (nature) + 格. {正確|せいかく} is a real word read the same way, but it means "accurate" and can't be bright or cheerful. The other two aren't words.

questions.stem: In which word is 直 read ジキ?
questions.explanation: {正直|しょうじき} (honest) uses the on'yomi ジキ. {直前|ちょくぜん} uses the other on'yomi, チョク, and {直|なお}す / {直|なお}る use the kun reading なお.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker say?

audio.text: さいきん、ちょっとかぜぎみなんです。

choices: I've just got over a cold.
questions.explanation: {最近|さいきん}、ちょっとかぜ{気味|ぎみ}なんです: "Lately I've had a bit of a cold." {気味|ぎみ} is a slight state now. "Often" would be がち; "going around" would be かぜが{流行|はや}っている.

questions.topic: っぽい and らしい
questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker say about the bag?

audio.text: このかばん、やすっぽくみえるけど、じつはたかいんだよ。

choices: It was cheap, and it looks it.
It looks expensive, but it was cheap.
It looks cheap, but it's actually expensive.
questions.explanation: このかばん、{安|やす}っぽく{見|み}えるけど、{実|じつ}は{高|たか}いんだよ. {安|やす}っぽい is "cheap-looking"; {実|じつ}は (actually) introduces the truth: it's expensive.

questions.stem: Listen and choose the best reply.

audio.text: そのワンピース、すごくにあってるね。

choices: いいえ、{似|に}ていません。
うん、{似合|にあ}うといいね。
questions.explanation: そのワンピース、すごく{似合|にあ}ってるね ("That dress really suits you") is a compliment, so a pleased ほんとう？うれしい fits. {似|に}ていません confuses {似合|にあ}う (suit) with {似|に}る (resemble); どういたしまして answers thanks, not a compliment.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: When I'm busy, I tend to forget to eat.
questions.explanation: {忙|いそが}しいと、{食事|しょくじ}を{取|と}るのを{忘|わす}れがちだ。 がち joins the ます stem, so it's {忘|わす}れ + がち, not {忘|わす}れる + がち. The situation (when I'm busy) comes first.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: This programme is made for children, but it's fun for adults to watch too.
questions.explanation: この{番組|ばんぐみ}は{子供|こども}{向|む}けだが、{大人|おとな}が{見|み}ても{面白|おもしろ}い。 A programme is made for children on purpose, so it's {向|む}け; {向|む}き would only say it suits them.

questions.stem:
Read the notice from a hair salon.

【お{知|し}らせ】{来月|らいげつ}から、{初心者|しょしんしゃ}{向|む}けのヘアアレンジ{教室|きょうしつ}を{始|はじ}めます。{毎週|まいしゅう}{土曜日|どようび}の{午後|ごご}{二時|にじ}から{一時間|いちじかん}です。{髪|かみ}が{短|みじか}い{方|かた}も{参加|さんか}できます。{予約|よやく}は{電話|でんわ}で、{前|まえ}の{日|ひ}までにお{願|ねが}いします。{雨|あめ}の{日|ひ}は{予約|よやく}が{少|すく}なくなりがちなので、{当日|とうじつ}でも{入|はい}れることがあります。

Which is true?
choices: People who have never done it before can take part.
Only people with long hair can take part.
You have to book on the day of the class.
The class is held every day.
questions.explanation: {初心者|しょしんしゃ}{向|む}け means the class is aimed at beginners. People with short hair can take part too, you book by phone by the day before (on rainy days you may get in on the day: {当日|とうじつ}), and it's every Saturday, not every day.

questions.topic: っぽい and らしい
questions.stem:
Read the blog post.

{兄|あに}は{二十五歳|にじゅうごさい}だが、{顔|かお}つきが{子供|こども}っぽいので、よく{高校生|こうこうせい}に{間違|まちが}えられる。{本人|ほんにん}はそれを{気|き}にしていて、{最近|さいきん}ひげをのばし{始|はじ}めた。でも、{母|はは}は「ひげがあると、{安|やす}っぽく{見|み}える」と{言|い}う。{兄|あに}は{少|すこ}し{落|お}ち{込|こ}み{気味|ぎみ}だ。

Why did the brother start growing a beard?
choices: Because his mother told him to.
Because people often mistake him for a high-school student.
Because he felt a little down.
questions.explanation: His face looks childish ({子供|こども}っぽい), so people take him for a high-school student, and he minds ({気|き}にしていて): that's why he's growing a beard. His mother is against it (it looks {安|やす}っぽい), and feeling a bit down ({落|お}ち{込|こ}み{気味|ぎみ}) is the result, not the reason.

questions.stem: {前|まえ}にもこの{店|みせ}に{来|き}た___がする。 (I feel as if I've been to this shop before.)
questions.explanation: ような{気|き}がする: ような comes before a noun ({気|き}), so it's ような, not ように. みたい needs な before a noun (みたいな{気|き}がする), and そうな after {来|き}た would be hearsay ("I hear"), which doesn't fit a feeling.

questions.stem: {彼女|かのじょ}の{目|め}が{赤|あか}い。{泣|な}いた___。 (She looks as if she's been crying.)
questions.explanation: 〜ように{見|み}える takes a whole clause in any tense: {泣|な}いたように{見|み}える (looks as if she cried). The "looks" そう can't follow a past form ({泣|な}きそう means "about to cry"), and the other two aren't patterns.

questions.stem: あんなに{毎日|まいにち}{練習|れんしゅう}したのだから、{彼|かれ}はきっと{勝|か}つ___。
questions.explanation: Verb (plain) + に{違|ちが}いない: "he's sure to win". No だ goes before it, so だに{違|ちが}いない is wrong; に{違|ちが}う and の{違|ちが}いだ aren't the pattern.

questions.stem: Complete with the pattern that means "must be": あの{背|せ}の{高|たか}い{人|ひと}は、{彼女|かのじょ}のお{父|とう}さん___。
questions.explanation: After a noun, に{違|ちが}いない follows directly, with no だ: お{父|とう}さんに{違|ちが}いない. The polite form に{違|ちが}いありません is also accepted.

questions.stem: {式|しき}は{午後|ごご}{二時|にじ}から___。{招待状|しょうたいじょう}にそう{書|か}いてある。
questions.explanation: The time is written on the invitation, a fact, so はず fits: "it should be from two". に{違|ちが}いない is for your own conviction from clues, and sounds odd about a printed time; ような{気|き}がする is too vague, and だったっけ (was it again?) asks, while the second sentence answers.

questions.stem: 「えーと、{結婚式|けっこんしき}は{何曜日|なんようび}___？」「{土曜日|どようび}だよ。」 (trying to remember)
questions.explanation: だっけ asks about something you knew and have forgotten: "what day was the wedding again?". The other three don't make questions, and っぽい / らしい describe impressions, not recall.

questions.stem: Which use of っけ is natural?
choices: (to a stranger in the street) すみません、{駅|えき}はどこだっけ？
(to a colleague) {明日|あした}の{会議|かいぎ}、{何時|なんじ}からでしたっけ？
(meeting someone for the first time) はじめまして。お{名前|なまえ}は{何|なん}だっけ？
(in a town you've never visited) ここはどこだっけ？
questions.explanation: っけ is for things you once knew and want to recall or check, like a meeting time you were told; でしたっけ is its polite form. A stranger's directions, a new person's name and a town you've never been to are new information, so っけ doesn't fit.

questions.stem: {二人|ふたり}は{大学|だいがく}のサークルで___、{三年後|さんねんご}に{結婚|けっこん}した。
questions.explanation: {出会|であ}う is to meet someone for the first time: they met at a club and married three years later. {招|まね}く (invite), {抱|だ}く (hold) and {結|むす}ぶ (tie) all need an object and don't describe two people meeting.

questions.stem: {彼|かれ}とは{気|き}が{合|あ}う。 Which is closest in meaning?
choices: {彼|かれ}とはよくけんかをする。
{彼|かれ}のことがよく{分|わ}からない。
{彼|かれ}とは{性格|せいかく}や{考|かんが}え{方|かた}が{合|あ}う。
{彼|かれ}には{会|あ}ったことがない。
questions.explanation: {気|き}が{合|あ}う is "to get on, be on the same wavelength": your personalities and ways of thinking match. Quarrelling, not understanding him and never having met him are the opposite or unrelated.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses {断|ことわ}る correctly?
choices: パーティーにさそわれたが、{用事|ようじ}があって{断|ことわ}った。
{雨|あめ}が{断|ことわ}って、{空|そら}が{晴|は}れた。
{駅|えき}で{友|とも}だちと{断|ことわ}って、{家|いえ}に{帰|かえ}った。
{寝|ね}る{前|まえ}に、{電気|でんき}を{断|ことわ}った。
questions.explanation: {断|ことわ}る is to turn down an invitation or request. Rain stops (やむ), you part from a friend ({別|わか}れる), and you switch off a light ({消|け}す).

questions.stem: となりの夫婦は、いつもなかがよさそうだ。 How is 「夫婦」 read?
questions.explanation: {夫婦|ふうふ} (married couple): 夫 is read フウ here, with a long vowel. ふふ drops it; {夫妻|ふさい} and {夫人|ふじん} are other words with 夫 read フ.

questions.stem: {来月|らいげつ}、{友|とも}だちの{結婚式|けっこんしき}にしょうたいされた。 Which kanji is しょうたい?
questions.explanation: {招待|しょうたい} (invitation) is 招 (beckon, invite: {招|まね}く) + 待 (wait, receive: {待|ま}つ). 持 (hold) looks like 待 but has the hand radical on the left; 正待 and 招対 aren't words.

questions.stem: In which word is 婦 read プ?
questions.explanation: After ん, 婦's フ becomes プ: {新婦|しんぷ} (bride). It's フ in {夫婦|ふうふ}, {主婦|しゅふ} and {婦人|ふじん} (woman, lady).

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker doing?

audio.text: しきは、なんじからだったっけ。

choices: Trying to remember what time the ceremony starts.
Telling someone what time the ceremony starts.
Complaining that the ceremony is late.
Asking whether there will be a ceremony.
questions.explanation: {式|しき}は、{何時|なんじ}からだったっけ: "What time did the ceremony start again?" っけ shows the speaker once knew and is trying to recall it.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker say?

audio.text: かれはつかれているようにみえるけど、ほんとうはげんきなんだよ。

choices: He's tired, but he looks fine.
He looks tired, but he's actually fine.
questions.explanation: {彼|かれ}は{疲|つか}れているように{見|み}えるけど、{本当|ほんとう}は{元気|げんき}なんだよ. ように{見|み}える is how it looks; {本当|ほんとう}は gives the reality: he's fine.

questions.stem: Listen and choose the best reply.

audio.text: あれ？まえに、どこかでおあいしたようなきがするんですけど。

choices: そうですか。{会|あ}いたいですね。
ええ、{先月|せんげつ}の{結婚式|けっこんしき}でお{会|あ}いしましたよね。
いいえ、{何|なに}もしていません。
questions.explanation: The speaker says "I feel as if we've met somewhere before". The natural reply confirms where: at last month's wedding. はい、{気|き}がします repeats words without answering, and the other two miss the point.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: I have a feeling I've met him somewhere before.
questions.explanation: {彼|かれ}には{前|まえ}にどこかで{会|あ}ったような{気|き}がする。 ような comes before the noun {気|き}; ように would need a verb after it. The time and place phrase can also come first.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: Her eyes are red; she looks as if she's been crying.
questions.explanation: {目|め}が{赤|あか}くて、{彼女|かのじょ}は{泣|な}いたように{見|み}える。 A past clause takes ように{見|み}える; the "looks" そう can't follow {泣|な}いた.

questions.stem:
Read the invitation.

{山田|やまだ}{健|けん}{様|さま}
このたび、{私|わたし}たちは{結婚|けっこん}することになりました。ささやかではございますが、ひろうえんを{開|ひら}きたいと{思|おも}います。お{忙|いそが}しいところ{恐|おそ}れ{入|い}りますが、ぜひおいでください。 {日時|にちじ}：{六月|ろくがつ}{十日|とおか}（{土|ど}）{午後|ごご}{一時|いちじ}から {場所|ばしょ}：ホテル{青葉|あおば}　{三階|さんがい} お{返事|へんじ}は{五月|ごがつ}{二十日|はつか}までにお{願|ねが}いします。

What does the couple ask Mr Yamada to do by 20 May?
choices: Book a room at the hotel.
Give a speech at the reception.
Reply to say whether he can come.
questions.explanation: お{返事|へんじ}は{五月|ごがつ}{二十日|はつか}までに: they want his reply by 20 May. The reception is on 10 June at the hotel; nothing is said about rooms, speeches or gifts. ささやか = modest; {恐|おそ}れ{入|い}りますが = we're sorry to trouble you, but.

questions.stem:
Read the diary entry.

{今日|きょう}は{結婚記念日|けっこんきねんび}だ。{朝|あさ}、{夫|おっと}は{何|なに}も{言|い}わずに{会社|かいしゃ}に{行|い}った。{忘|わす}れているに{違|ちが}いないと{思|おも}って、{一日中|いちにちじゅう}{少|すこ}し{悲|かな}しかった。でも、{夜|よる}{帰|かえ}ってきた{夫|おっと}は、{大|おお}きな{花束|はなたば}を{持|も}っていた。「{忘|わす}れるわけないだろう」と{笑|わら}っていた。

Why was the writer sad during the day?
choices: She was sure her husband had forgotten their anniversary.
Her husband had gone to work very early.
Her husband forgot to buy flowers.
She had forgotten their anniversary herself.
questions.explanation: {忘|わす}れているに{違|ちが}いないと{思|おも}って: she was convinced he'd forgotten, because he left without a word. In fact he came home with flowers: "As if I'd forget!" ({忘|わす}れるわけない, lesson 7).

questions.stem: {弟|おとうと}は{自分|じぶん}では{何|なに}もしない___、{人|ひと}にはもんくばかり{言|い}う。
questions.explanation: くせに criticizes someone: he does nothing himself, yet he's always complaining about others. にしては (for a…) and {割|わり}に (considering) compare a result with an expectation, and ながらも is a formal "although" that doesn't carry the blame. もんく = complaint.

questions.stem: {毎日|まいにち}{練習|れんしゅう}した___、{試合|しあい}に{負|ま}けてしまった。 (I practised every day, and I still lost.)
questions.explanation: The speaker is talking about their own effort, with disappointment: that's のに. くせに is the tempting one, but it blames someone else and isn't used about yourself. にしては and ばかりか don't mean "even though".

questions.topic: にしては and 割に
questions.stem: {初|はじ}めて___、とても{上手|じょうず}に{焼|や}けましたね。 (For a first try, you've baked it really well.)
questions.explanation: {初|はじ}めてにしては: "for a first time", the result is better than you'd expect. くせに would be a complaint, ながら doesn't follow {初|はじ}めて, and {上|うえ}に adds a point (lesson 20).

questions.topic: にしては and 割に
questions.stem: この{店|みせ}のラーメンは、{値段|ねだん}が{高|たか}い___、{量|りょう}が{少|すく}ない。
questions.explanation: {割|わり}に can follow an い-adjective: {高|たか}い{割|わり}に (for something so expensive) the portion is small. にしては doesn't normally follow an adjective, くせに is for criticizing people, and ばかりか (not only) would need a second point in the same direction.

questions.stem: {残念|ざんねん}___、{今年|ことし}の{運動会|うんどうかい}は{中止|ちゅうし}になりました。
questions.explanation: {残念|ざんねん}ながら (unfortunately) is a set phrase: a な-adjective stem + ながら, "although it's a pity". The others don't follow {残念|ざんねん} this way.

questions.stem: Complete the wish with two kana: {夏休|なつやす}みがもっと{長|なが}ければ___のに。 (I wish the summer holidays were longer.)
questions.explanation: 〜ばいいのに: "I wish…". {長|なが}ければいいのに says the holidays aren't as long as you'd like. 〜ばよかったのに is for the past: もっと{早|はや}く{言|い}えばよかったのに.

questions.stem: ___、{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}っても、{試合|しあい}は{行|おこな}われます。
questions.explanation: たとえ〜ても: "even if": the match goes ahead even if it rains. なかなか goes with negatives, ぜひ with wishes and requests, and まさか means "surely not".

questions.stem: {熱|ねつ}が{出|で}たので、お{昼|ひる}で{学校|がっこう}を___した。
questions.explanation: {早退|そうたい} is leaving school (or work) early: at noon, because of a fever. {欠席|けっせき} is the tempting one, but it means not coming at all, so it doesn't fit "at noon". {出席|しゅっせき} and {登校|とうこう} are being there and arriving.

questions.stem: あの{子|こ}は{覚|おぼ}えが{早|はや}い。 Which is closest in meaning?
choices: よく{物|もの}を{忘|わす}れる。
すぐに{物事|ものごと}を{覚|おぼ}える。
questions.explanation: {覚|おぼ}え here is the ability to learn, so {覚|おぼ}えが{早|はや}い is "quick to learn". It has nothing to do with getting up early or running; forgetting is the opposite. {物事|ものごと} = things.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses {欠|か}ける correctly?
choices: {彼|かれ}は{能力|のうりょく}はあるが、やる{気|き}に{欠|か}けている。
{毎朝|まいあさ}めがねを{欠|か}けて、{新聞|しんぶん}を{読|よ}む。
{友|とも}だちに{電話|でんわ}を{欠|か}けたが、{出|で}なかった。
{雨|あめ}の{日|ひ}は、{学校|がっこう}を{欠|か}けた。
questions.explanation: {欠|か}ける is "to lack, be missing": 〜に{欠|か}ける (lacking in). Putting on glasses and making a call use N5's かける, a different verb; missing school is {休|やす}む or {欠席|けっせき}する.

questions.stem: 生徒たちは{体育館|たいいくかん}に{集|あつ}まった。 How is 「生徒」 read?
questions.explanation: {生徒|せいと} (pupil): 生 is セイ and 徒 is ト, with a short o. せいとう would be another word (a political party), and しょう / いき are other readings of 生.

questions.stem: テストをもう{一度|いちど}{見|み}たら、あやまりが{見|み}つかった。 Which is あやまり?
questions.explanation: {誤|あやま}り (error) is 誤 with the okurigana り. 語 and 説 share the words radical (言) but mean "language" and "explain" ({語|かた}り is a different word, "telling a story"); 誤まり puts one kana too many outside the kanji.

questions.stem: In which word is 苦 read にが?
questions.explanation: {苦手|にがて} (not good at) uses にが, as in {苦|にが}い (bitter). {苦|くる}しい and {苦|くる}しむ use くる, and {苦労|くろう} uses the on'yomi ク.

questions.stem: Listen. How does the speaker feel?

audio.text: しってるくせに、おしえてくれないんだから。

choices: Surprised that the other person doesn't know.
Annoyed that the other person won't tell them.
questions.explanation: {知|し}ってるくせに、{教|おし}えてくれないんだから: "You know perfectly well, and you won't tell me!" くせに carries the complaint, and 〜んだから at the end adds exasperation.

questions.topic: にしては and 割に
questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker say about the restaurant?

audio.text: このみせは、ねだんのわりに、りょうがおおいね。

choices: It's expensive, and the portions are small.
It gives you a lot of food for the price.
The portions are small for the price.
questions.explanation: この{店|みせ}は、{値段|ねだん}の{割|わり}に、{量|りょう}が{多|おお}いね: "considering the price, the portions are big". {量|りょう}が{多|おお}い is "a lot"; {少|すく}ない would be "little".

questions.stem: Listen and choose the best reply.

audio.text: もっとはやく、いってくれればよかったのに。

choices: うん、{早|はや}く{言|い}ったよ。
ごめん。なかなか{言|い}えなかったんだ。
じゃあ、もっと{早|はや}く{来|き}てね。
questions.explanation: もっと{早|はや}く{言|い}ってくれればよかったのに: "If only you'd told me sooner" is a complaint about the listener, so an apology with a reason fits. Saying you did tell them early contradicts it, and the other two don't answer it.

questions.topic: にしては and 割に
questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: For a first time, she did really well.
questions.explanation: {彼女|かのじょ}は{初|はじ}めてにしては、とても{上手|じょうず}にできた。 にしては follows the noun {初|はじ}めて; くせに would turn praise into a complaint. The topic {彼女|かのじょ}は can also come after the にしては phrase.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: Even if it rains, I'll go.
questions.explanation: たとえ{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}っても、{私|わたし}は{行|い}きます。 たとえ goes with the ても form, not たら. {私|わたし}は can also come first.

questions.stem:
Read the notice from a primary school.

【{運動会|うんどうかい}のお{知|し}らせ】
{十月|じゅうがつ}{五日|いつか}（{土|ど}）に{運動会|うんどうかい}を{行|おこな}います。たとえ{小雨|こさめ}でも{行|おこな}いますが、{強|つよ}い{雨|あめ}の{場合|ばあい}は{次|つぎ}の{日|ひ}に{変|か}わります。{当日|とうじつ}の{朝|あさ}{六時|ろくじ}に、{学校|がっこう}のホームページでお{知|し}らせします。おべんとうと{水|みず}を{持|も}たせてください。{体調|たいちょう}が{悪|わる}く、{欠席|けっせき}や{早退|そうたい}をする{場合|ばあい}は、たんにんにれんらくしてください。

If it rains heavily on 5 October, what happens?
choices: Sports day moves to the next day.
Sports day is cancelled for this year.
Sports day is held in the gym.
questions.explanation: {強|つよ}い{雨|あめ}の{場合|ばあい}は{次|つぎ}の{日|ひ}に{変|か}わります: in heavy rain it moves to the next day. It goes ahead in light rain ({小雨|こさめ}), which is the tempting answer. {場合|ばあい} = in the case of; {体調|たいちょう} = how you feel.

questions.topic: にしては and 割に
questions.stem:
Read the essay.

{兄|あに}は{高校|こうこう}のころ、{勉強|べんきょう}しない{割|わり}にせいせきがよかった。{私|わたし}は{毎日|まいにち}{遅|おそ}くまで{勉強|べんきょう}しているのに、{兄|あに}ほどの{点|てん}が{取|と}れない。{母|はは}は「お{兄|にい}ちゃんは{覚|おぼ}えが{早|はや}かったのよ」と{言|い}う。でも、{兄|あに}によると、{実|じつ}は{夜中|よなか}にこっそり{勉強|べんきょう}していたそうだ。「{勉強|べんきょう}しているところを{見|み}られるのが{恥|は}ずかしかったんだ」と{笑|わら}っていた。

What was the truth about the brother?
choices: He went to cram school after school.
He learned everything from their mother.
questions.explanation: {実|じつ}は{夜中|よなか}にこっそり{勉強|べんきょう}していた: he actually studied secretly at night, because he was embarrassed to be seen studying. The mother's view (quick to learn) and "never studied" are what people believed. こっそり = secretly.

questions.topic: としたら and とすれば
questions.stem: その{話|はなし}が{本当|ほんとう}___、{大変|たいへん}なことだ。 (If that story is true, it's serious.)
questions.explanation: A noun or な-adjective takes だ before としたら: {本当|ほんとう}だとしたら. Without だ the sentence breaks (noun + としたら is a different use, "from the standpoint of"), and な / の don't go before と.

questions.topic: としたら and とすれば
questions.stem: Which sentence is natural?
choices: {駅|えき}に{着|つ}いたとしたら、{電話|でんわ}してください。
{駅|えき}に{着|つ}くとしたら、{電話|でんわ}してください。
{駅|えき}に{着|つ}いたら、{電話|でんわ}してください。
{駅|えき}に{着|つ}いたとすれば、{電話|でんわ}してください。
questions.explanation: Arriving at the station is a real, expected event, so plain たら fits: "when you get to the station, call me". としたら and とすれば make it a supposition, as if arriving were in doubt, which sounds strange before a simple request.

questions.topic: もしかしたら and まさか
questions.stem: ___、{犯人|はんにん}はもう{遠|とお}くに{逃|に}げたかもしれない。
questions.explanation: もしかしたら goes with かもしれない: "perhaps the culprit has already fled far away". まさか expresses disbelief, いったい needs a question word, and {決|けっ}して goes with negatives.

questions.topic: もしかしたら and まさか
questions.stem: ___、{彼|かれ}がうそをついているとは{思|おも}わなかった。 (I never imagined he was lying.)
questions.explanation: まさか〜とは{思|おも}わなかった: "I never imagined that…". もしかしたら would be a possibility, not disbelief; たとえ goes with ても, and いったい with a question word.

questions.topic: はずがない and わけがない
questions.stem: かぎをかけて{出|で}かけたのだから、ドアが{開|あ}いている___。
questions.explanation: I locked it, so it can't be open: a conclusion from a fact, はずがない. に{違|ちが}いない says the opposite ("it must be open"), もしかして doesn't end a sentence, and まさか isn't used with だ like this.

questions.stem: {彼|かれ}は{何|なに}か{知|し}っている___と{思|おも}う。 (I suspect he knows something.)
questions.explanation: 〜のではないかと{思|おも}う: "I think it may be that…", a soft suspicion. のではなく means "not… but", ではなかった is a plain past negative, and としたら (supposing) can't be followed by と{思|おも}う.

questions.stem: Fill in one kana: {犯人|はんにん}は{家|いえ}の{中|なか}の{人|ひと}___のではないだろうか。
questions.explanation: A noun (or な-adjective) takes な before のではないか / のではないだろうか: {人|ひと}なのではないだろうか, "could it be someone in the house?"

questions.stem: {店|みせ}の{物|もの}をお{金|かね}を{払|はら}わずに{持|も}って{帰|かえ}るのは、___という{犯罪|はんざい}だ。
questions.explanation: Taking goods from a shop without paying is {万引|まんび}き (shoplifting). ひき{逃|に}げ is hit and run, さぎ is fraud, {殺人|さつじん} is murder.

questions.stem: {警察|けいさつ}は{男|おとこ}をたいほした。 Which is closest in meaning?
choices: {男|おとこ}は{警察|けいさつ}から{逃|に}げた。
{男|おとこ}は{警察|けいさつ}に{通報|つうほう}した。
{男|おとこ}は{警察官|けいさつかん}になった。
{男|おとこ}は{警察|けいさつ}に{捕|つか}まった。
questions.explanation: たいほする is "to arrest", so the man was caught by the police: {捕|つか}まった. Escaping, reporting and becoming an officer are different things.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses {疑|うたが}う correctly?
choices: {分|わ}からないことがあったら、{先生|せんせい}に{疑|うたが}ってください。
{警察|けいさつ}は、となりの{男|おとこ}が{犯人|はんにん}ではないかと{疑|うたが}っている。
{明日|あした}は{雨|あめ}が{疑|うたが}う。
{彼|かれ}の{話|はなし}を{疑|うたが}って、すぐに{信|しん}じた。
questions.explanation: {疑|うたが}う is "to suspect, doubt": the police suspect the man next door. You ask ({聞|き}く) a teacher, rain doesn't doubt, and doubting a story and believing it at once contradict each other.

questions.stem: 警察官が{二人|ふたり}、{現場|げんば}に{来|き}た。 How is 「警察官」 read?
questions.explanation: {警察官|けいさつかん}: {警察|けいさつ} (police) + 官 (official, カン). Nothing changes at the joins: no voicing (がん, ざつ) and no small っ.

questions.stem: {犯人|はんにん}はまだつかまっていない。 Which is つかまって?
questions.explanation: {捕|つか}まる (to be caught) is written with 捕. 追 (chase: {追|お}う), 探 (search: {探|さが}す) and 逃 (escape: {逃|に}げる) are other crime-story kanji with different readings.

questions.stem: In which word is 盗 read トウ?
questions.explanation: {盗難|とうなん} (theft) uses the on'yomi トウ. The other three are forms of the verb {盗|ぬす}む, read with the kun reading ぬす.

questions.topic: もしかしたら and まさか
questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker mean?

audio.text: まさか、かれがはんにんだとは、おもわなかった。

choices: They always thought he was the culprit.
They think he might be the culprit.
They don't think there is a culprit.
They never imagined he was the culprit.
questions.explanation: まさか{彼|かれ}が{犯人|はんにん}だとは{思|おも}わなかった: "I never imagined he was the culprit": he turned out to be, and the speaker is shocked.

questions.topic: もしかしたら and まさか
questions.stem: Listen. How sure is the speaker?

audio.text: もしかしたら、はんにんはまだちかくにいるかもしれません。

choices: Not sure: it's only a possibility.
Sure that the culprit has gone.
Sure that there is no culprit.
questions.explanation: もしかしたら…かもしれません is a weak guess: "the culprit may still be nearby". Nothing in it is certain.

questions.topic: としたら and とすれば
questions.stem: Listen and choose the best reply.

audio.text: それがほんとうだとしたら、たいへんですね。

choices: はい、{本当|ほんとう}としました。
いいえ、{大変|たいへん}でした。
ええ。まだ{本当|ほんとう}かどうか{分|わ}かりませんけど。
どうぞ、お{大事|だいじ}に。
questions.explanation: "If that's true, it's serious" leaves open whether it's true, so a reply that agrees and adds "we don't know yet if it's true" fits. The first reply misuses としたら, the second changes the tense and contradicts, and お{大事|だいじ}に is for someone who's ill.

questions.topic: としたら and とすれば
questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: If what he says is true, the culprit is someone else.
questions.explanation: {彼|かれ}の{話|はなし}が{本当|ほんとう}だとしたら、{犯人|はんにん}はほかにいる。 The noun {本当|ほんとう} needs だ before としたら, so the tile without だ is the trap.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: Who on earth did a thing like this?
questions.explanation: いったいだれがこんなことをしたんだろう。 いったい strengthens the question word だれ; it usually comes just before it, though だれがいったい is possible too. まさか doesn't go with questions like this.

questions.stem:
Read the police notice.

【さぎに{注意|ちゅうい}！】{警察官|けいさつかん}や{銀行|ぎんこう}の{人|ひと}のふりをして、「あなたのカードが{犯罪|はんざい}に{使|つか}われています」と{電話|でんわ}をかけてくるさぎが{増|ふ}えています。{警察官|けいさつかん}が{電話|でんわ}でカードの{番号|ばんごう}を{聞|き}くことは、{決|けっ}してありません。もしかしたらさぎかもしれないと{思|おも}ったら、すぐに{電話|でんわ}を{切|き}って、{家族|かぞく}かけいさつしょに{相談|そうだん}してください。

What should you do if you think a call might be a scam?
choices: Give your card number so the police can check it.
Go to the bank at once.
Hang up and talk to your family or the police.
questions.explanation: すぐに{電話|でんわ}を{切|き}って、{家族|かぞく}かけいさつしょに{相談|そうだん}してください: hang up and consult your family or the police station. The notice says officers never ask for card numbers by phone. ふりをする = pretend (lesson 5); {相談|そうだん} = consultation.

questions.stem:
Read the diary entry.

{今朝|けさ}、{駅|えき}でさいふをなくした。{盗|ぬす}まれたのではないかと{思|おも}って、すぐ{交番|こうばん}に{行|い}った。{警官|けいかん}に{事情|じじょう}を{話|はな}していると、{電話|でんわ}が{鳴|な}った。{駅|えき}の{人|ひと}からで、{電車|でんしゃ}の{座席|ざせき}の{下|した}にさいふが{落|お}ちていたそうだ。お{金|かね}もカードも、そのまま{残|のこ}っていた。{盗|ぬす}まれたのではなく、{自分|じぶん}で{落|お}としていたのだ。

What had really happened to the wallet?
choices: The writer had dropped it on the train.
Someone had stolen it at the station.
A police officer had found it.
The money had been taken from it.
questions.explanation: It was found under a seat on the train, with everything still in it: the writer had dropped it ({自分|じぶん}で{落|お}としていた). The theft was only a suspicion ({盗|ぬす}まれたのではないか), and it was station staff, not the police, who called.

questions.topic: だけでなく and ばかりか
questions.stem: この{映画|えいが}は{子供|こども}___、{大人|おとな}も{楽|たの}しめる。
questions.explanation: A だけでなく B も: "not only children, adults too". {上|うえ}に doesn't follow a bare noun (it needs の: {子供|こども}の{上|うえ}に, and means "on top of being"), なんて would sneer at children, and ことか is an exclamation that needs a question word.

questions.topic: だけでなく and ばかりか
questions.stem: Which sentence is natural?
choices: {歌|うた}うばかりか、おどってください。
{彼|かれ}は{歌|うた}がうまいばかりか、{曲|きょく}まで{作|つく}る。
この{店|みせ}は{安|やす}いばかりか、まずい。
questions.explanation: ばかりか builds to something more striking in the same direction, often with まで: he sings well and even writes songs. It can't be followed by a request (おどってください), and it doesn't join opposite points (cheap but bad, rain but sunny).

questions.topic: はもちろん and 上に
questions.stem: このアニメは、{子供|こども}___、{大人|おとな}にも{人気|にんき}がある。
questions.explanation: A はもちろん、B も: popular with adults too, and with children of course. なんか would belittle children, ことか needs a question word, and のに (even though) makes no sense here.

questions.topic: はもちろん and 上に
questions.stem: このホテルは{駅|えき}から{近|ちか}い___、{部屋|へや}も{広|ひろ}い。
questions.explanation: {上|うえ}に adds a second good point to a first one: close to the station, and roomy too. のに and くせに would set the two points against each other, and にしては (for a…) doesn't follow an adjective.

questions.stem: {合格|ごうかく}の{知|し}らせを{聞|き}いて、___うれしかったことか。 (How happy I was!)
questions.explanation: ことか as an exclamation goes with a question word of degree: どんなにうれしかったことか, "how happy I was!". たとえ goes with ても, まさか with disbelief, もしかしたら with かもしれない.

questions.topic: なんて and なんか
questions.stem: {彼|かれ}が{歌手|かしゅ}になる___、{思|おも}わなかった。 (I never thought he'd become a singer.)
questions.explanation: After a clause, なんて shows surprise: "that he'd become a singer, I never thought". ばかりか and {上|うえ}に add a second point, and ことか ends an exclamation; none of them fits before {思|おも}わなかった.

questions.topic: だけでなく and ばかりか
questions.stem: Fill in one kana: {彼女|かのじょ}は{歌|うた}もうまけれ___、ダンスも{上手|じょうず}だ。
questions.explanation: 〜も〜ば〜も lists two features: {歌|うた}もうまければ、ダンスも{上手|じょうず}だ (she sings well, and dances well too). うまければ is the ば form of うまい.

questions.stem: {好|す}きな{小説|しょうせつ}が{映画|えいが}になった。でも、{映画|えいが}より___の{小説|しょうせつ}のほうが{面白|おもしろ}い。
questions.explanation: {原作|げんさく} is the original work a film is based on: the original novel is better than the film. {主役|しゅやく} is the lead role, {観客|かんきゃく} the audience, {再放送|さいほうそう} a rerun.

questions.stem: この{作品|さくひん}は、{色|いろ}の{使|つか}い{方|かた}が{優|すぐ}れている。 Which is closest in meaning?
choices: {色|いろ}の{使|つか}い{方|かた}が{少|すこ}し{変|へん}だ。
{色|いろ}の{使|つか}い{方|かた}が{古|ふる}い。
{色|いろ}の{使|つか}い{方|かた}がとても{上手|じょうず}だ。
{色|いろ}の{使|つか}い{方|かた}が{優|やさ}しい。
questions.explanation: {優|すぐ}れる (to excel): the use of colour is excellent. Watch the kanji: {優|やさ}しい (kind, gentle) uses the same kanji with a different reading and meaning.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses {鳴|な}る correctly?
choices: {映画|えいが}の{途中|とちゅう}で、{電話|でんわ}が{鳴|な}ってしまった。
{赤|あか}ちゃんが{夜中|よなか}に{鳴|な}った。
{鳥|とり}が{木|き}の{上|うえ}で{鳴|な}っている。
{彼|かれ}は{有名|ゆうめい}な{歌手|かしゅ}に{鳴|な}った。
questions.explanation: {鳴|な}る is for bells, phones and alarms: the phone rang in the middle of the film. A baby cries ({泣|な}く), a bird sings ({鳴|な}く), and becoming a singer is {歌手|かしゅ}になる. All sound alike; the kanji tell them apart.

questions.stem: {彼女|かのじょ}は{有名|ゆうめい}な女優だ。 How is 「女優」 read?
questions.explanation: {女優|じょゆう} (actress): 女 is ジョ, with a short vowel, and 優 is ユウ. じょうゆう lengthens the じょ; おんな is the kun reading, and ニョ is a rare on'yomi of 女.

questions.stem: {昨日|きのう}のドラマは、{生|なま}ほうそうだった。 Which is ほうそう?
questions.explanation: {放送|ほうそう} (broadcast) is 放 (release) + 送 (send): sending a programme out. 方 is also ホウ but means "direction", and 走 (run) is ソウ but doesn't fit.

questions.stem: In which word is 絵 read カイ?
questions.explanation: {絵画|かいが} (painting, formal) uses カイ. In {絵|え}, {絵本|えほん} and {絵|え}の{具|ぐ}, 絵 is read エ, which is in fact also an on'yomi.

questions.topic: はもちろん and 上に
questions.stem: Listen. Who can enjoy the film?

audio.text: このえいがは、こどもはもちろん、おとなもたのしめますよ。

questions.explanation: この{映画|えいが}は、{子供|こども}はもちろん、{大人|おとな}も{楽|たの}しめますよ: children of course, and adults too. はもちろん doesn't rank one above the other.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker say?

audio.text: さいしゅうかいをみて、どれだけないたことか。

choices: They want to know how much other people cried.
They haven't seen the final episode yet.
They cried a lot at the final episode.
questions.explanation: {最終回|さいしゅうかい}を{見|み}て、どれだけ{泣|な}いたことか: "how much I cried watching the final episode!" It sounds like a question, but ことか makes it an exclamation; no answer is expected.

questions.topic: なんて and なんか
questions.stem: Someone has just praised the speaker's singing. Listen. What does the speaker mean?

audio.text: いえいえ、わたしなんか、まだまだです。

choices: I'm nowhere near good enough yet.
questions.explanation: いえいえ、{私|わたし}なんか、まだまだです: "Oh no, someone like me still has a long way to go." なんか after {私|わたし} is modest, the usual way to answer a compliment.

questions.topic: だけでなく and ばかりか
questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: Not only is he a good singer, he even writes his own songs.
questions.explanation: {彼|かれ}は{歌|うた}がうまいばかりか、{自分|じぶん}で{曲|きょく}まで{作|つく}る。 ばかりか (not only) leads to まで (even); ばかりで would mean "only…". {自分|じぶん}で and {曲|きょく}まで can swap.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: How happy I was when I heard I'd passed!
questions.explanation: {合格|ごうかく}したと{聞|き}いて、どんなにうれしかったことか。 The exclamation is どんなに + plain form + ことか. 〜ことだ is advice (lesson 9), not an exclamation.

questions.stem:
Read the notice from a museum.

【{青山|あおやま}{美術館|びじゅつかん}より】{来月|らいげつ}から、{有名|ゆうめい}な{画家|がか}の{作品|さくひん}を{集|あつ}めたてんらんかいを{開|ひら}きます。{絵画|かいが}だけでなく、{画家|がか}が{使|つか}っていた{絵|え}の{具|ぐ}や{手紙|てがみ}もてんじします。{高校生|こうこうせい}までは{無料|むりょう}です。{毎週|まいしゅう}{金曜日|きんようび}は{夜|よる}{八時|はちじ}まで{開|あ}いています。{写真|しゃしん}はとってもかまいませんが、フラッシュは{使|つか}わないでください。

Which is true?
choices: High-school students and younger can get in free.
The museum is open until 8 pm every day.
questions.explanation: {高校生|こうこうせい}までは{無料|むりょう}: free up to high-school age. Paints and letters are shown as well as paintings (だけでなく), photos are allowed without flash, and late opening is on Fridays only.

questions.stem:
Read the letter to a radio programme.

{毎朝|まいあさ}この{番組|ばんぐみ}を{聞|き}いています。{仕事|しごと}に{行|い}く{前|まえ}、この{番組|ばんぐみ}の{音楽|おんがく}に{何度|なんど}{元気|げんき}をもらったことか。{先週|せんしゅう}{流|なが}れた{古|ふる}い{名曲|めいきょく}は、{亡|な}くなった{父|ちち}がよく{歌|うた}っていた{曲|きょく}でした。{聞|き}いているうちに{父|ちち}の{顔|かお}が{浮|う}かんできて、{目|め}が{熱|あつ}くなりました。{来週|らいしゅう}、もう{一度|いちど}あの{曲|きょく}を{流|なが}していただけないでしょうか。

What does the listener ask for?
choices: For the old song to be played again next week.
For their father's songs to be played every day.
For the programme to change its music.
For their letter to be read on air.
questions.explanation: {来週|らいしゅう}、もう{一度|いちど}あの{曲|きょく}を{流|なが}していただけないでしょうか: a polite request to play that song once more next week. {流|なが}す = to play (on the radio); 〜うちに = while (lesson 1); {目|め}が{熱|あつ}くなる = to feel tears coming.

questions.stem: In the story, why does the detective decide the culprit must be someone inside the house?
choices: There were no footprints in the snow, which had stopped at midnight.
The window of the studio was broken.
Kenichi admitted it on the phone.
questions.explanation: {雪|ゆき}の{上|うえ}には、あしあとが{一|ひと}つもなかった, and the snow stopped at about midnight: nobody came in or went out after that. The spare key was used but not missing, and nothing was broken.

questions.stem: Why does Kenichi seem to have an alibi?
choices: He was with Yumi all night.
He was asleep in his own room.
He spent the night at a hotel in Tokyo when the trains stopped.
He was talking to the detective on the phone.
questions.explanation: {雪|ゆき}で{電車|でんしゃ}が{止|と}まってしまい、{駅前|えきまえ}のホテルで{一晩|ひとばん}{過|す}ごした, and the hotel staff remember him. He only phoned the detective in the morning.

questions.stem: What was the clue that gave Yumi away?
choices: She named the missing painting, though nobody had told her which one it was.
She said she had heard a noise at two in the morning.
She had the studio key in her bag.
questions.explanation: There were three paintings, Kenichi hadn't told her, and Ms Tamura didn't know which one was gone, yet Yumi said 『{夏|なつ}の{海|うみ}』. Red eyes were only an impression, and it was Ms Tamura who mentioned the noise.

questions.stem: Why does the detective doubt that Ms Tamura is the culprit?
choices: She was out of the house that night.
She didn't know where the spare key was.
If she were the culprit, she wouldn't point out the noise and the open drawer herself.
questions.explanation: {田村|たむら}さんが{犯人|はんにん}だとしたら、…わざわざ{私|わたし}たちに{話|はな}すでしょうか: he tests the idea with としたら and finds it unlikely. In fact she knew where the key was and was in the house.

questions.stem: かぎを{持|も}っているのが{健一|けんいち}さんだけ___、{犯人|はんにん}は{健一|けんいち}さんなのではないか。
questions.explanation: The narrator supposes something (if Kenichi is the only one with a key) and draws a guess from it: だとしたら, with だ after the noun phrase. にしては and くせに don't set up a supposition, and なのに (even though) contradicts the guess that follows.

questions.stem: Which of the narrator's thoughts is the surest?
choices: {犯人|はんにん}は{健一|けんいち}さんなのではないか。
{風|かぜ}の{音|おと}だったかもしれない。
だれかがあいかぎを{使|つか}ったに{違|ちが}いない。
{物音|ものおと}がしたような{気|き}がした。
questions.explanation: に{違|ちが}いない is a firm conviction. のではないか is a soft suspicion, かもしれない a possibility, and ような{気|き}がした a vague feeling.

questions.stem: What does すいりする mean?
questions.explanation: すいりする is to reason something out from clues, what a detective does; すいり{小説|しょうせつ} is a mystery novel. To steal is {盗|ぬす}む, to hide かくす.

questions.stem: Type the story word for "a spare key" (four kana).
questions.explanation: あいかぎ: a duplicate key. In the story it was kept in a kitchen drawer, and Yumi used it in the night.

questions.stem: Listen. What did the detective find?

audio.text: ゆきのうえには、あしあとがひとつもなかった。

choices: Footprints leading to the back door.
No footprints at all in the snow.
questions.explanation: {雪|ゆき}の{上|うえ}には、あしあとが{一|ひと}つもなかった: not a single footprint. {一|ひと}つも + negative = not even one.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker suggesting?

audio.text: たむらさんがはんにんだとしたら、わざわざものおとのことをはなすでしょうか。

choices: Ms Tamura probably isn't the culprit.
Ms Tamura must be the culprit.
Ms Tamura heard nothing that night.
Ms Tamura made the noise herself.
questions.explanation: {田村|たむら}さんが{犯人|はんにん}だとしたら、わざわざ{物音|ものおと}のことを{話|はな}すでしょうか: "If she were the culprit, would she go out of her way to mention the noise?" The question expects "no", so she probably isn't.

questions.stem: Listen and choose the best reply.

audio.text: さいしょから、ゆみさんだとわかっていたんですか。

choices: いいえ、{由美|ゆみ}さんは{知|し}りません。
まさか。{最初|さいしょ}は{分|わ}かりませんでしたよ。
ええ、{由美|ゆみ}さんに{聞|き}いてください。
questions.explanation: "Did you know it was Yumi from the start?" まさか (not at all) followed by "I didn't know at first" answers it, as the detective does in the story. The other replies answer different questions.

questions.stem:
Read the passage.

{森川|もりかわ}さんの{事務所|じむしょ}に、また{電話|でんわ}がかかってきた。「{家|いえ}の{猫|ねこ}がいなくなったんです。もしかしたら、となりの{人|ひと}が{連|つ}れていったのではないかと…」。{森川|もりかわ}さんは{少|すこ}し{考|かんが}えてから{言|い}った。「{窓|まど}が{開|あ}いていたとしたら、{自分|じぶん}で{出|で}ていったのかもしれませんよ」

What does Mr Morikawa think?
choices: The neighbour must have taken the cat.
The cat may have gone out by itself.
The window must have been locked.
questions.explanation: {窓|まど}が{開|あ}いていたとしたら、{自分|じぶん}で{出|で}ていったのかもしれません: supposing the window was open, the cat may have left on its own. It's the caller who suspects the neighbour (のではないか); nobody is certain of anything. {連|つ}れていく = to take (a person or animal) along.

questions.stem: How many morae (beats) are there in がっこう?
questions.explanation: が・っ・こ・う: the small っ and the long う each count as a beat, so there are four.

questions.stem: How many morae are there in きょうしつ?
questions.explanation: きょ・う・し・つ: the small ょ belongs to き and doesn't count on its own, so there are four.

questions.stem: In a haiku, {名月|めいげつ} (the harvest moon) is a season word for which season?
questions.explanation: {名月|めいげつ} is the full moon of mid-autumn, one of the best-known autumn season words.

questions.stem: In traditional season-word lists, {七夕|たなばた} counts as which season, and why?
choices: Winter, because the stars are clearest then.
Spring, because it's a new beginning.
Autumn, because the haiku seasons follow the old calendar.
questions.explanation: The haiku seasons follow the old calendar, in which autumn starts in early August, so {七夕|たなばた} is an autumn word even though it feels like summer today.

questions.stem: What is {字余|じあま}り?
choices: A line with more sounds than the usual five or seven.
A haiku without a season word.
A haiku written in kanji only.
A cutting word such as や or かな.
questions.explanation: {字余|じあま}り (literally "extra characters") is a line that runs over its count. Poets sometimes do it on purpose. Cutting words are {切|き}れ{字|じ}.

questions.stem: Which haiku is ばしょう's?
choices: {菜|な}の{花|はな}や{月|つき}は{東|ひがし}に{日|ひ}は{西|にし}に
{古池|ふるいけ}やかわず{飛|と}びこむ{水|みず}の{音|おと}
{名月|めいげつ}をとってくれろと{泣|な}く{子|こ}かな
{雪|ゆき}の{朝|あさ}あしあと{一|ひと}つ{門|もん}からの
questions.explanation: The old pond is ばしょう's. The rape blossom is ぶそん's, the child and the moon いっさ's, and the snowy morning was written for this course.

questions.stem: In {名月|めいげつ}をとってくれろと{泣|な}く{子|こ}かな, what does the child want?
