questions.explanation: とってくれろ is an old dialect form of "get it for me": the child is crying for someone to fetch the harvest moon, as if it could be reached.

questions.stem: Which of these lines has seven morae?
questions.explanation: か・わ・ず・と・び・こ・む is seven. The other three are five-mora lines (the first and last lines of their haiku).

questions.stem: Listen to the haiku. What sound does it describe?

audio.text: ふるいけや、かわずとびこむ、みずのおと。

questions.explanation: {古池|ふるいけ}やかわず{飛|と}びこむ{水|みず}の{音|おと}: the sound of water as a frog jumps into an old pond.

questions.stem: Listen to the haiku. Where is the moon?

audio.text: なのはなや、つきはひがしに、ひはにしに。

choices: Above the flowers, hidden by clouds.
questions.explanation: {月|つき}は{東|ひがし}に{日|ひ}は{西|にし}に: the moon is in the east and the sun in the west, over a field of rape blossom.

questions.stem:
Read the notice.

【はいくコンテスト】テーマは「{秋|あき}」です。{秋|あき}のきごを{一|ひと}つ{入|い}れて、{五|ご}・{七|しち}・{五|ご}で{作|つく}ってください。{一人|ひとり}{三|みっ}つまで{送|おく}ることができます。しめきりは{十月|じゅうがつ}{三十一日|さんじゅういちにち}です。

How many haiku can one person send?
questions.explanation: {一人|ひとり}{三|みっ}つまで: up to three per person. まで sets the upper limit.

questions.stem:
Read the passage.

はいくを{作|つく}るときは、まずきごを{一|ひと}つ{選|えら}びます。{次|つぎ}に、{見|み}たことや{聞|き}いたことの{中|なか}から、{一|ひと}つの{場面|ばめん}を{選|えら}びます。{気持|きも}ちを{説明|せつめい}するより、{情景|じょうけい}を{見|み}せるほうが、{読|よ}む{人|ひと}の{心|こころ}に{残|のこ}ります。

According to the passage, what makes a haiku stay with the reader?
choices: Using as many season words as possible.
Making every line exactly the same length.
Showing the scene rather than explaining feelings.
questions.explanation: {気持|きも}ちを{説明|せつめい}するより、{情景|じょうけい}を{見|み}せるほうが…{心|こころ}に{残|のこ}ります: showing the scene stays with the reader more than explaining feelings. The passage says to choose one season word, not many.

questions.stem: Choose the form: 「{先生|せんせい}に、{明日|あした}{早|はや}く___ように{言|い}われました。」 (The teacher told me to come early tomorrow.)
questions.explanation: A reported request puts the dictionary form before ように: {来|く}るように{言|い}われました. The politeness of the original words (ください, ます) drops out, so {来|き}てくださいように and {来|き}ますように are wrong here, and {来|き}て can't come before ように at all.

questions.stem: What does 「{田中|たなか}さんに{明日|あした}{来|く}るように{言|い}いました。」 mean?
choices: Tanaka said he would come tomorrow.
I told Tanaka to come tomorrow.
Tanaka told me to come tomorrow.
I said I would come to see Tanaka tomorrow.
questions.explanation: 〜ように{言|い}う reports a request, and に marks the person who receives it: I told Tanaka to come. "Tanaka said he would come" is a statement, which needs と: {田中|たなか}さんは{来|く}ると{言|い}いました. "Tanaka told me" would be the passive, {田中|たなか}さんに{来|く}るように{言|い}われました.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "Yamashita said she would send the file"?
choices: {山下|やました}さんはファイルを{送|おく}るように{言|い}いました。
{山下|やました}さんはファイルを{送|おく}ってくださいと{言|い}いました。
{山下|やました}さんはファイルを{送|おく}ると{言|い}いました。
{山下|やました}さんはファイルを{送|おく}るようにしました。
questions.explanation: Yamashita's statement about her own plan is reported with と: {送|おく}ると{言|い}いました. {送|おく}るように{言|い}いました and {送|おく}ってくださいと{言|い}いました both mean she asked someone else to send it, and {送|おく}るようにしました means she made a point of sending it.

questions.stem: Choose the form: 「パスワードはだれにも___ように{注意|ちゅうい}されました。」 (I was warned not to tell anyone my password.)
questions.explanation: A negative request takes the plain ない form before ように: {教|おし}えないように. ないで and なくて are て-type forms and can't come before ように, and the ず form ({教|おし}えず) doesn't either.

questions.topic: てもらいたい and ていただきたい
questions.stem: You want your department head to check a document. Which is the most appropriate thing to say to them?
choices: この{資料|しりょう}を{確認|かくにん}してほしいです。
この{資料|しりょう}を{確認|かくにん}してもらいたいです。
この{資料|しりょう}を{確認|かくにん}するように{言|い}います。
この{資料|しりょう}を{確認|かくにん}していただけませんか。
questions.explanation: To a superior you ask, rather than state your wish: 〜ていただけませんか. 〜てほしいです and 〜てもらいたいです say what you want and sound like a demand when said to a boss's face, and 〜ように{言|い}います (I'll tell them to) is an instruction, not a request.

questions.stem: Type the missing word in hiragana: 「{電車|でんしゃ}は{予定|よてい}___に{着|つ}きました。」 (The train arrived as scheduled.)
questions.explanation: Straight after a noun, {通|とお}り is voiced: {予定|よてい}{通|どお}りに (according to plan). With の in between it stays {通|とお}り: {予定|よてい}の{通|とお}りに is possible but much less common.

questions.stem: Which completes the wish written on a shrine prayer board? 「{試験|しけん}に{合格|ごうかく}___ように。」
questions.explanation: A wish at the end of a sentence usually takes the polite ます form: {合格|ごうかく}できますように (please let me pass), the set form on prayer boards. できるように is most often the "so that" ように, with a main clause after it ({合格|ごうかく}できるように{勉強|べんきょう}する), and the て and た forms don't fit.

questions.stem: Choose the word that fits: 「{画面|がめん}が{止|と}まって{動|うご}かないときは、まず___してみてください。」
questions.explanation: When the screen is frozen, you restart: {再起動|さいきどう}する. {保存|ほぞん} (saving), {送信|そうしん} (sending) and {入力|にゅうりょく} (typing in) don't help with a frozen screen.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses {閉|と}じる correctly?
choices: {寒|さむ}いので、{水|みず}を{閉|と}じてください。
{部屋|へや}を{出|で}るときは、{電気|でんき}を{閉|と}じてください。
{読|よ}み{終|お}わったら、{本|ほん}を{閉|と}じてください。
うるさいので、{声|こえ}を{閉|と}じてください。
questions.explanation: {閉|と}じる is for books, eyes, files and apps: {本|ほん}を{閉|と}じる. Water is turned off with {止|と}める, lights with {消|け}す, and for a voice you'd say {声|こえ}を{小|ちい}さくする or {静|しず}かにする.

questions.stem: Which is closest in meaning to 「データを{保存|ほぞん}する」?
choices: データをさくじょする
データを{送信|そうしん}する
データを{残|のこ}しておく
questions.explanation: {保存|ほぞん}する is to save, to keep: {残|のこ}しておく (leave it there for later). さくじょする is the opposite (delete), {送信|そうしん}する is to send and {開|ひら}く is to open.

questions.stem: How is 押して read in 「このボタンを押してください。」?
questions.explanation: 押 is お(す), to push: おして. かえして is {返|かえ}して (give back), もどして is {戻|もど}して (put back) and とじて is {閉|と}じて (close).

questions.stem: Which kanji is used for もどす in 「せっていを{元|もと}にもどす」?
questions.explanation: もど(す) is written 戻す: a door (戸) and 大. 返す is read かえす (give back); 更 and 閉 are not used for this verb (閉 is と(じる), し(める)).

questions.stem: How is 再 read in 再来週 (the week after next)?
questions.explanation: 再 is サイ in most words ({再生|さいせい}, {再起動|さいきどう}), but サ in {再来週|さらいしゅう}, {再来月|さらいげつ} and {再来年|さらいねん}. ザイ is not a reading of 再.

questions.stem: Listen. What was the speaker asked to do?

audio.text: かちょうに、このしりょうをさんぶいんさつするようにいわれました。

choices: Send the documents to the section head
Print three copies of the document
questions.explanation: {課長|かちょう}に、この{資料|しりょう}を{三部|さんぶ}いんさつするように{言|い}われました: the section head told the speaker to print three copies (〜{部|ぶ} counts copies) of this document. Nothing is made or sent.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker's problem?

audio.text: せつめいしょのとおりにやったのに、うごきません。

choices: They followed the manual, but it doesn't work.
They lost the manual, so they can't use it.
They didn't read the manual, and it broke.
The manual is wrong, so they returned it.
questions.explanation: {説明書|せつめいしょ}の{通|とお}りにやったのに、{動|うご}きません: "I did it as the manual said, but it doesn't work". のに shows the result was unexpected. Nothing is said about losing or returning the manual.

questions.stem: Listen. A colleague says this to you. Which reply fits best?

audio.text: すみません、このファイル、ひらけないんですけど。

choices: はい、{開|あ}けてもいいですよ。
いったん{閉|と}じて、もう{一度|いちど}{開|ひら}いてみてください。
ありがとうございます。{助|たす}かりました。
questions.explanation: The colleague says the file won't open (ファイル、{開|ひら}けないんですけど), so suggesting they close it and try again fits. {開|あ}けてもいい gives permission to open a door or window, {閉|し}めておきました is about a door, and thanking them makes no sense.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: My mother told me not to look at my phone at night.
questions.explanation: {母|はは}に{夜|よる}はスマホを{見|み}ないように{言|い}われました. The person who made the request takes に with the passive {言|い}われました, and the request is the ない form + ように. {見|み}ないで can't come before ように. {母|はは}に and {夜|よる}は can swap, and {夜|よる}は can also follow スマホを.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: Please type it in exactly as it appeared on the screen.
questions.explanation: {画面|がめん}に{出|で}た{通|とお}りに{入力|にゅうりょく}してください. A verb in the た form goes straight before {通|とお}りに ("as it appeared"). ために (for the purpose of) doesn't fit after a past event.

questions.stem:
Read the notice and answer.

【{図書館|としょかん}からのお{知|し}らせ】{館内|かんない}のパソコンをご{利用|りよう}の{方|かた}へ。{使|つか}う{前|まえ}に、{受付|うけつけ}で{名前|なまえ}を{書|か}いてください。{使|つか}い{終|お}わったら、ファイルは{必|かなら}ずさくじょして、ログアウトしてください。{画面|がめん}が{動|うご}かなくなったときは、でんげんを{切|き}らないで、{近|ちか}くの{係|かかり}の{者|もの}に{声|こえ}をかけてください。

What should you do if the screen freezes?
choices: Tell a member of staff nearby
questions.explanation: The notice says not to switch it off (でんげんを{切|き}らないで) and to speak to a member of staff nearby ({近|ちか}くの{係|かかり}の{者|もの}に{声|こえ}をかけてください). It doesn't mention restarting; writing your name at reception is what you do before using it. {係|かかり}の{者|もの} = the person in charge (humble {者|もの}).

questions.topic: てもらいたい and ていただきたい
questions.stem:
Read the message and answer.

{課長|かちょう}に、{皆|みな}さんに{次|つぎ}のことを{伝|つた}えるように{頼|たの}まれました。{来週|らいしゅう}から{新|あたら}しいアプリを{使|つか}います。{金曜日|きんようび}までにインストールして、ログインできるか{確認|かくにん}しておいてください。できなかった{人|ひと}は、{木村|きむら}さんにメールしてください。{課長|かちょう}は「{月曜日|げつようび}の{朝|あさ}から、{全員|ぜんいん}に{使|つか}ってもらいたい」と{言|い}っていました。

What does the section head want?
choices: Kimura to install the app for everyone
Everyone to send Kimura an email
Everyone to log in on Monday morning for the first time
Everyone to be using the app from Monday morning
questions.explanation: {全員|ぜんいん}に{使|つか}ってもらいたい: the section head would like everyone to be using it from Monday morning. Only those who can't log in should email Kimura, and logging in should be checked by Friday, not first done on Monday.

questions.stem: At work, passing on a phone message: 「{田中|たなか}さんから{電話|でんわ}があって、{会議|かいぎ}に{少|すこ}し{遅|おく}れる___です。」
questions.explanation: 〜とのことです passes on a message from a named person, politely: {遅|おく}れるとのことです (he says he'll be late). んだって is casual and can't take です, and ようなです / みたいなです aren't possible endings (ような and みたいな come before a noun).

questions.stem: Telling a close friend some news: 「ねえ、{山本|やまもと}さん、{会社|かいしゃ}{辞|や}める___。」 (Apparently Yamamoto is leaving the company.)
questions.explanation: Between friends, the casual report is 〜んだって. とのことです and そうでございます are polite and formal, and ということだ belongs to news and writing; all three clash with the casual ねえ and the dropped particles.

questions.stem: Type the casual ending in hiragana: 「{明日|あした}、{休|やす}み___。」 (Apparently tomorrow's a day off.)
questions.explanation: After a noun, んだって needs な: {休|やす}みなんだって. Plain {休|やす}みだって and {休|やす}みって are also casual hearsay and are accepted. ×{休|やす}みだんだって is the common mistake.

questions.stem: Which sentence is natural?
choices: {私|わたし}は{明日|あした}{休|やす}むとのことです。
{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}るとのことになりました。
{部長|ぶちょう}は{会議|かいぎ}に{少|すこ}し{遅|おく}れるとのことです。
{明日|あした}は{休|やす}みとのことしています。
questions.explanation: とのことです reports someone else's message: {部長|ぶちょう}は…{遅|おく}れるとのことです. It can't report your own plans ({私|わたし}は{明日|あした}{休|やす}みます), and とのことになる / とのことしている aren't forms.

questions.topic: と言われている and といった
questions.stem: Which means "This temple is said to be the oldest in Japan"?
choices: この{寺|てら}は{日本|にほん}で{一番|いちばん}{古|ふる}いと{言|い}われた。
この{寺|てら}は{日本|にほん}で{一番|いちばん}{古|ふる}いように{言|い}われている。
この{寺|てら}は{日本|にほん}で{一番|いちばん}{古|ふる}いとのことしている。
この{寺|てら}は{日本|にほん}で{一番|いちばん}{古|ふる}いと{言|い}われている。
questions.explanation: "It is said" is 〜と{言|い}われている: what people in general say. {言|い}われた means someone once told the speaker, and ように{言|い}う reports a request, not a belief. とのことしている isn't a form.

questions.topic: と言われている and といった
questions.stem: Choose the phrase that fits: 「{会議|かいぎ}では、{政治|せいじ}、{経済|けいざい}、{教育|きょういく}（　　）{問題|もんだい}について{話|はな}し{合|あ}った。」
questions.explanation: 〜といった + noun lists examples: "issues such as politics, the economy and education". について and によって would need の before a noun ({教育|きょういく}についての{問題|もんだい}), and とのこと can't modify a noun this way.

questions.stem: In 「{八時|はちじ}{集合|しゅうごう}ということは、{七時|しちじ}には{家|いえ}を{出|で}なければならないということだ。」, what does the final ということだ do?
choices: It reports what someone said: "I hear that…"
questions.explanation: After ということは (so that means), the final ということだ states the conclusion the speaker has worked out: leaving at seven follows from meeting at eight. There's no source being reported, so it isn't hearsay here.

questions.stem: Choose the word that fits: 「{山田|やまだ}さんは{市長|しちょう}せんきょで___して、{来月|らいげつ}から{市長|しちょう}になる。」
questions.explanation: Becoming mayor next month means Yamada won the election: {当選|とうせん}した. {落選|らくせん} is losing, {報道|ほうどう} is news coverage, and {支持|しじ}する (to support) needs an object.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses {支|ささ}える correctly?
choices: {雨|あめ}を{支|ささ}えるために、かさを{持|も}っていった。
{電車|でんしゃ}に{遅|おく}れないように、{時間|じかん}を{支|ささ}えた。
{部屋|へや}が{暗|くら}いので、{電気|でんき}を{支|ささ}えてください。
{父|ちち}は{家族|かぞく}を{支|ささ}えるために{働|はたら}いている。
questions.explanation: {支|ささ}える is to support, to hold up: {家族|かぞく}を{支|ささ}える (to support a family). Rain, time and lights can't be "supported"; the other sentences need different verbs ({電気|でんき}をつける, for example).

questions.stem: Which is closest in meaning to {実際|じっさい}は in 「{安|やす}いと{聞|き}いていたが、{実際|じっさい}はけっこう{高|たか}かった。」?
questions.explanation: {実際|じっさい}は is "in fact, in reality", contrasting what you heard with what was true: {本当|ほんとう}は. {最初|さいしょ}は (at first), たぶん (probably) and いつもは (usually) change the meaning.

questions.stem: How is 議論 read in 「{国会|こっかい}で議論が{続|つづ}いている。」?
questions.explanation: 議 is ギ and 論 is ロン: ぎろん (debate). ぎりん and ぎろう aren't readings of these kanji, and きろん lacks the voicing of ギ.

questions.stem: Which kanji spell しゅしょう in 「しゅしょうが{記者会見|きしゃかいけん}を{開|ひら}いた」?
questions.explanation: The prime minister is 首相: 首 (head, as in {首都|しゅと}) and 相 (minister; read ショウ here). 主, 守 and 想 sound similar in other words but aren't used here.

questions.stem: How is 相 read in 相手 (the other person)?
questions.explanation: 相 is あい in {相手|あいて} and {相変|あいか}わらず, ソウ in {相談|そうだん}, and ショウ in {首相|しゅしょう}. さが is not a reading of 相.

questions.stem: Listen to the message. What will happen?

audio.text: ぶちょうは、かいぎにじゅっぷんほどおくれるとのことです。

choices: The meeting will start ten minutes early.
The department head will be about ten minutes late for the meeting.
The department head wants everyone to arrive ten minutes late.
questions.explanation: {部長|ぶちょう}は、{会議|かいぎ}に{十分|じゅっぷん}ほど{遅|おく}れるとのことです: a message that the department head will be about ten minutes late. ほど = about. Nobody else is asked to do anything.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker telling their friend?

audio.text: えきまえのふるいビル、こわされるんだって。

choices: They want the old building by the station knocked down.
The old building by the station was knocked down yesterday.
They asked someone to knock down the building.
Apparently the old building by the station is going to be knocked down.
questions.explanation: {駅前|えきまえ}の{古|ふる}いビル、こわされるんだって: こわされる is the passive (will be knocked down) and んだって passes on what the speaker heard. It isn't past, and it isn't the speaker's wish or request.

questions.stem: Listen. A friend says this to you. Which reply fits best?

audio.text: らいしゅうは、ずっとあめなんだって。

choices: ということは、キャンプは{中止|ちゅうし}かな。
いいえ、{雨|あめ}じゃありません。
{雨|あめ}に{降|ふ}られたんですか。
はい、そう{言|い}いましょう。
questions.explanation: The friend passes on a forecast: it'll rain all next week. ということは draws the obvious conclusion: so the camping trip's probably off. The other replies deny the news, ask about the past, or misunderstand って as a request to say something.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: We're told the results will be made public next month.
questions.explanation: {結果|けっか}は{来月|らいげつ}{公表|こうひょう}されるとのことです. The plain passive {公表|こうひょう}される comes straight before とのことです. The time can also come first. ように would turn it into a reported request.

questions.stem: Build the casual sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: Apparently that shop is closing down next month.
questions.explanation: あの{店|みせ}、{来月|らいげつ}{閉店|へいてん}するんだって. Casual speech drops は after {店|みせ}. After a verb, んだって joins directly; なんだって is for nouns and な-adjectives.

questions.stem:
Read the news item and answer.

{市|し}の{発表|はっぴょう}によると、{来年|らいねん}の{四月|しがつ}から、{市内|しない}のバスの{料金|りょうきん}が{大人|おとな}{二百円|にひゃくえん}から{二百二十円|にひゃくにじゅうえん}に{上|あ}がるということだ。{子供|こども}の{料金|りょうきん}は{変|か}わらないとされている。{市長|しちょう}は{記者会見|きしゃかいけん}で、「{運転手|うんてんしゅ}が{足|た}りず、{料金|りょうきん}を{上|あ}げなければ{今|いま}の{路線|ろせん}を{続|つづ}けられない」と{説明|せつめい}した。

What will change next April?
choices: The adult bus fare will go up to 220 yen.
More bus drivers will be hired.
questions.explanation: ということだ reports the city's announcement: the adult fare goes from 200 to 220 yen. Children's fares won't change (とされている). The mayor says the routes can't continue without the rise, not that they will close, and nothing is said about hiring.

questions.stem:
Read the message slip and answer.

{西田|にしだ}さんへ　10:30 みどり{商事|しょうじ}のおかだ{様|さま}からお{電話|でんわ}がありました。{明日|あした}の{打|う}ち{合|あ}わせは、{先方|せんぽう}の{都合|つごう}で{三時|さんじ}からにしてほしいとのことです。{資料|しりょう}は{今日|きょう}{中|じゅう}にメールで{送|おく}ってもらえると{助|たす}かるとのことでした。{折|お}り{返|かえ}しのお{電話|でんわ}は{要|い}らないそうです。（かとう）

What does Ms Okada ask Nishida to do today?
choices: Come to Midori Trading at three
questions.explanation: {資料|しりょう}は{今日|きょう}{中|じゅう}にメールで{送|おく}ってもらえると{助|たす}かる: she'd be grateful for the documents by email today. The meeting is tomorrow at three, and she says no call back is needed ({要|い}らないそうです). {先方|せんぽう} = the other company.

questions.topic: というのは and とは
questions.stem: Complete the definition: 「「{鳥居|とりい}」というのは、{神社|じんじゃ}の{入|い}り{口|ぐち}にある{門|もん}___。」
questions.explanation: A definition with というのは usually ends with のことだ: {門|もん}のことです (it's the gate…). After a noun, こと needs の, and というより / と{言|い}っても can't end a sentence with です.

questions.topic: と言えば and というと
questions.stem: Choose the phrase that fits: 「{来月|らいげつ}、{京都|きょうと}に{行|い}くんです。」「{京都|きょうと}___、お{寺|てら}がたくさんありますね。」
questions.explanation: The second speaker picks up the topic and says what it brings to mind: {京都|きょうと}と{言|い}えば (speaking of Kyoto). と{言|い}っても would limit what was said, というより would say another word fits better, and とは defines a word.

questions.topic: といっても and というより
questions.stem: Choose the phrase that fits: 「{旅行|りょこう}に{行|い}った___、{日帰|ひがえ}りだよ。」 (I did go on a trip, but just for the day.)
questions.explanation: と{言|い}っても takes back part of what "a trip" might suggest: it was only a day trip. と{言|い}えば (speaking of) and というのは (defining, or "the reason is") don't fit, and というか (or rather) would need a better word after it.

questions.topic: といっても and というより
questions.stem: Type the missing phrase in hiragana: 「{今日|きょう}は{寒|さむ}い___、{痛|いた}い。」 (Today it isn't so much cold as painful.)
questions.explanation: 〜というより says another word fits better: {寒|さむ}いというより{痛|いた}い. In casual speech っていうより is also common.

questions.stem: Choose the verb: 「おばあちゃんのために、{心|こころ}を（　　）{作|つく}りました。」
questions.explanation: {心|こころ}を{込|こ}めて is the set phrase "with all my heart": {込|こ}める puts feelings into something. {込|こ}む (to be crowded) is intransitive, {入|はい}る can't take {心|こころ}を, and {加|くわ}える adds things or people, not feelings.

questions.topic: というのは and とは
questions.stem: In 「{今年|ことし}のお{正月|しょうがつ}は{実家|じっか}に{帰|かえ}りません。というのは、{仕事|しごと}が{休|やす}めないんです。」, what does というのは introduce?
choices: The reason for what was just said
A definition of お{正月|しょうがつ}
An example of a New Year custom
questions.explanation: At the start of a sentence, というのは gives the reason ("the thing is…"), and the sentence ends with んです. It's the position that tells you: after a word, というのは defines it.

questions.topic: といっても and というより
questions.stem: What does 「{彼女|かのじょ}は{静|しず}かというか、ちょっと{恥|は}ずかしがりなんだよね。」 mean?
choices: She's quiet, and she isn't shy at all.
She's quiet, or rather, a bit shy.
She says she's quiet, but she's shy.
Speaking of quiet people, she's shy.
questions.explanation: 〜というか searches for a better word: "quiet, or rather, a bit shy". It doesn't report what she says (that would be と{言|い}っている), and it doesn't contradict the first word.

questions.stem: Choose the word that fits: 「{日本|にほん}では{昔|むかし}から、{山|やま}や{木|き}にも___がいると{考|かんが}えられてきた。」
questions.explanation: What "lives" in mountains and trees is a god: {神様|かみさま}がいる. {行列|ぎょうれつ} (a queue), {伝説|でんせつ} (a legend) and {暮|く}らし (way of life) can't be the subject of いる here.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses {暮|く}らす correctly?
choices: {毎朝|まいあさ}、{新聞|しんぶん}を{暮|く}らしています。
{時計|とけい}が{止|と}まって、{暮|く}らさなくなった。
{雨|あめ}が{一日中|いちにちじゅう}{暮|く}らしていた。
{祖父母|そふぼ}はいなかで{楽|たの}しく{暮|く}らしている。
questions.explanation: {暮|く}らす is "to live (one's life)", and its subject is a person: {祖父母|そふぼ}は…{暮|く}らしている. Newspapers, clocks and rain can't 〜を{暮|く}らす or {暮|く}らす at all.

questions.stem: Which is closest in meaning to 「{約束|やくそく}を{完全|かんぜん}に{忘|わす}れていた。」?
choices: {約束|やくそく}を{全然|ぜんぜん}{覚|おぼ}えていなかった。
{約束|やくそく}を{少|すこ}しだけ{覚|おぼ}えていた。
{約束|やくそく}をわざと{忘|わす}れた。
{約束|やくそく}をすぐに{思|おも}い{出|だ}した。
questions.explanation: {完全|かんぜん}に{忘|わす}れていた = had completely forgotten, so it wasn't remembered at all. The other choices change the meaning (a little, on purpose, remembered quickly).

questions.stem: How is 神社 read in 「神社の{前|まえ}で{待|ま}ち{合|あ}わせた。」?
questions.explanation: 神社 is じんじゃ: 神 is ジン and 社 voices to ジャ. 神 is シン in {神道|しんとう} and {神話|しんわ}, but not here.

questions.stem: Which kanji is used for のこって in 「この{町|まち}には{古|ふる}い{伝説|でんせつ}がのこっている」?
questions.explanation: のこ(る) is 残る: {残|のこ}っている (remains). 続 is つづ(く), 列 has no kun'yomi at this level, and 暮 is く(らす).

questions.stem: How is 暮 read in 一人暮らし (living alone)?
questions.explanation: After another word, く becomes ぐ: {一人暮|ひとりぐ}らし. On its own it's {暮|く}らし. ぼ and ば aren't readings of 暮 at this level.

questions.stem: Listen. What is a mikoshi?

audio.text: みこしというのは、かみさまがのる、ちいさなじんじゃのようなものです。

choices: A small shrine-like thing that a god rides in
A tall gate at the entrance to a shrine
A dance held at the summer festival
A small shrine in people's homes
questions.explanation: みこしというのは、{神様|かみさま}が{乗|の}る、{小|ちい}さな{神社|じんじゃ}のようなものです: a mikoshi is "something like a small shrine that the god rides in". The gate is a {鳥居|とりい}.

questions.topic: といっても and というより
questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker mean?

audio.text: まつりといっても、まちのちいさなまつりですよ。

choices: It isn't a festival at all.
It's a festival, but only a small local one.
Speaking of festivals, the town has a big one.
The town festival is bigger than you think.
questions.explanation: {祭|まつ}りと{言|い}っても、{町|まち}の{小|ちい}さな{祭|まつ}りですよ: と{言|い}っても lowers expectations: it is a festival, but don't imagine anything big.

questions.topic: と言えば and というと
questions.stem: Listen. A friend says this to you. Which reply fits best?

audio.text: そういえば、あしたはたなばただね。

choices: はい、{言|い}えばいいですよ。
いいえ、{言|い}っていません。
そうだね。{願|ねが}いごと、もう{書|か}いた？
ということは、{今日|きょう}はたなばたじゃないね。
questions.explanation: そう{言|い}えば (come to think of it) brings up something just remembered: tomorrow is Tanabata, the star festival when people write wishes on paper strips. Agreeing and asking about the wish fits. The others take {言|い}えば literally or draw a pointless conclusion.

questions.topic: というのは and とは
questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: A torii is the gate at the entrance to a shrine.
questions.explanation: {鳥居|とりい}というのは、{神社|じんじゃ}の{入|い}り{口|ぐち}にある{門|もん}のことです. The word being defined takes というのは, the description goes before the noun {門|もん}, and のことです ends the definition. と{言|い}えば (speaking of) doesn't define.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: I made a cake for my grandmother with all my heart.
questions.explanation: {祖母|そぼ}のために{心|こころ}を{込|こ}めてケーキを{作|つく}りました. {心|こころ}を{込|こ}めて is one unit, and it can move around before the verb, as can {祖母|そぼ}のために and ケーキを. {込|こ}んで is from {込|こ}む (to be crowded).

questions.stem:
Read the text and answer.

{七五三|しちごさん}というのは、{子供|こども}の{成長|せいちょう}をいわう{行事|ぎょうじ}のことだ。{多|おお}くの{地方|ちほう}では、{男|おとこ}の{子|こ}は{三歳|さんさい}と{五歳|ごさい}、{女|おんな}の{子|こ}は{三歳|さんさい}と{七歳|ななさい}の{年|とし}の{十一月|じゅういちがつ}ごろ、{家族|かぞく}で{神社|じんじゃ}にお{参|まい}りする。{着物|きもの}を{着|き}て{写真|しゃしん}をとる{家族|かぞく}も{多|おお}い。{子供|こども}たちがもらう{細長|ほそなが}いあめは「ちとせあめ」と{呼|よ}ばれ、{長|なが}く{元気|げんき}に{生|い}きられるようにという{願|ねが}いが{込|こ}められている。

Which is true, according to the text?
choices: Boys usually go to the shrine at three and seven.
Families go to the shrine in January.
Girls usually go at three and seven.
The long sweets are a wish for good marks at school.
questions.explanation: In many regions girls go at three and seven ({女|おんな}の{子|こ}は{三歳|さんさい}と{七歳|ななさい}), boys at three and five, around November. The long, thin ちとせあめ carry a wish for a long, healthy life, not for school success. いわう = to celebrate.

questions.topic: というのは and とは
questions.stem:
Read the text and answer.

「{年中行事|ねんじゅうぎょうじ}」とは、{毎年|まいとし}{決|き}まった{時期|じき}に{行|おこな}われる{行事|ぎょうじ}のことである。{正月|しょうがつ}やおぼんのように{全国|ぜんこく}で{行|おこな}われるものもあれば、その{土地|とち}にしかない{祭|まつ}りもある。ただ、{最近|さいきん}は、{行事|ぎょうじ}と{言|い}っても、{家族|かぞく}で{特別|とくべつ}な{食事|しょくじ}をするだけという{家|いえ}も{増|ふ}えている。

What does the writer say about recent years?
choices: More families mark these events only with a special meal.
Local festivals are spreading across the whole country.
Fewer people know what New Year and Obon are.
Annual events are now held at different times each year.
questions.explanation: {行事|ぎょうじ}と{言|い}っても、{家族|かぞく}で{特別|とくべつ}な{食事|しょくじ}をするだけという{家|いえ}も{増|ふ}えている: "even when they keep an event, more families just have a special meal". と{言|い}っても limits what {行事|ぎょうじ} suggests. である is the written だ (lesson 26).

questions.topic: お〜です and でいらっしゃる
questions.stem: A receptionist tells a colleague: 「お{客様|きゃくさま}が{受付|うけつけ}で___。」 (A customer is waiting at reception.)
choices: お{待|ま}ちしております
questions.explanation: The customer is the one waiting, so the verb must be honorific: お{待|ま}ちです. お{待|ま}ちしております and お{待|ま}ちいたします are humble (they'd mean "we are waiting for you"), and {待|ま}たせていただきます is a humble request to make someone wait.

questions.topic: お〜です and でいらっしゃる
questions.stem: On the phone, checking a customer's name: 「{失礼|しつれい}ですが、{田中様|たなかさま}___か。」
questions.explanation: The honorific です for a person is でいらっしゃる: {田中様|たなかさま}でいらっしゃいますか. でございます is polite です, used for things (and for yourself), so it doesn't raise the customer. でおります and でまいります aren't forms of です.

questions.topic: させていただく and お〜いたす
questions.stem: To your boss: 「すみません、{明日|あした}は{休|やす}___いただけますか。」 (Could I take tomorrow off?)
questions.explanation: 〜させていただく uses the causative: {休|やす}む → {休|やす}ませる → {休|やす}ませていただけますか. Group 1 verbs take only せ; ×{休|やす}まさせて (with an extra さ) is a common slip. {休|やす}んでいただけますか would ask the boss to rest.

questions.stem: A caller asks for your colleague Nishida, who is out. What do you say?
choices: {西田|にしだ}はただいま{外出中|がいしゅつちゅう}でございます。
{西田|にしだ}さんはいらっしゃいません。
{西田様|にしださま}はお{出|で}かけです。
{西田|にしだ}さんは{外出中|がいしゅつちゅう}でいらっしゃいます。
questions.explanation: To an outsider, your own colleague is on your side: surname only, no さん or {様|さま}, and humble or polite forms: {西田|にしだ}はただいま{外出中|がいしゅつちゅう}でございます. The other choices raise him with honorifics, which you'd only do inside the company.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct keigo for "The professor said so"?
choices: {先生|せんせい}がそうおっしゃられました。
{先生|せんせい}がそうおっしゃいました。
{先生|せんせい}がそうお{言|い}いになりました。
{先生|せんせい}がそう{申|もう}されました。
questions.explanation: おっしゃる is already honorific: おっしゃいました. おっしゃられました adds a second honorific (double keigo). お{言|い}いに なる isn't used because {言|い}う has a special form, and {申|もう}す is humble, so it can't raise the professor.

questions.topic: ております and てまいります
questions.stem: A shop notice: 「ご{予約|よやく}はお{電話|でんわ}で{受|う}け{付|つ}け___。」 (We take bookings by phone.)
questions.explanation: The shop talks about its own actions courteously with 〜ております (humble 〜ています). ていらっしゃいます would raise the shop, てございます is the formal てあります (a prepared result: ご{用意|ようい}してございます), which doesn't fit an ongoing service, and てくださいます would mean someone else does it as a favour.

questions.stem: Type the humble verb in hiragana: 「もうしわけございません。その{件|けん}については___ません。」 (I'm afraid I don't know about that matter.)
questions.explanation: The humble negative of {知|し}る is {存|ぞん}じません. {知|し}りません is correct but not humble, and the honorific ご{存|ぞん}じ is for the other person's knowledge.

questions.stem: Choose the word that fits: 「もうしわけございません。その{日|ひ}は、もうお{部屋|へや}が{空|あ}いておりません。___となっております。」
questions.explanation: No rooms are free, so the hotel is fully booked: {満室|まんしつ}. {空室|くうしつ} is the opposite (a free room), {予約制|よやくせい} means "by reservation only", and {客室|きゃくしつ} just means a guest room.

questions.stem: Choose the word that fits: 「お___ですが、こちらにお{名前|なまえ}をご{記入|きにゅう}ください。」 (Sorry to trouble you, but please write your name here.)
questions.explanation: お{手数|てすう}ですが is the set phrase for asking someone to go to a little trouble. お{越|こ}し (coming), お{宅|たく} (your home) and お{客様|きゃくさま} (customer) don't make sense before ですが here.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses {取|と}り{寄|よ}せる correctly?
choices: {駅|えき}で{友|とも}だちを{取|と}り{寄|よ}せた。
その{本|ほん}は{今|いま}ございませんが、お{取|と}り{寄|よ}せできます。
{暑|あつ}いので、{窓|まど}を{取|と}り{寄|よ}せてください。
かぜをひいて、{熱|ねつ}を{取|と}り{寄|よ}せた。
questions.explanation: {取|と}り{寄|よ}せる is to order something in from elsewhere: a shop can order a book for you, お{取|と}り{寄|よ}せできます. People, windows and a fever can't be "ordered in".

questions.stem: How is 皆様 read in 「皆様、{本日|ほんじつ}はありがとうございます。」?
questions.explanation: 皆 is みな and 様 is さま: みなさま. 皆 isn't read かい at this level, みんな is the casual word (written in kana), and 様 is read よう only in {様子|ようす}.

questions.stem: Which kanji spell よやく in 「ごよやくはこちらでうけたまわります」?
questions.explanation: よやく is 予約: 予 (in advance) + 約 (promise). 束 is the ソク of {約束|やくそく}, 余 (ヨ, extra) is a different kanji, and 役 is ヤク as in {役割|やくわり}, but not in this word.

questions.stem: How is 様 read in 様子 (how things look)?
questions.explanation: 様 is ヨウ in {様子|ようす} and さま as a polite suffix ({皆様|みなさま}, お{客様|きゃくさま}). ざま and しょう aren't readings you need for 様.

questions.stem: Listen to the receptionist. Where is Nishida?

audio.text: もうしわけございません。にしだはただいまがいしゅつちゅうでございます。よじごろもどるよていです。

choices: Out of the office, back around four
questions.explanation: {西田|にしだ}はただいま{外出中|がいしゅつちゅう}でございます。{四時|よじ}ごろ{戻|もど}る{予定|よてい}です: he's out of the office and expected back around four. A meeting would be {会議中|かいぎちゅう}, and a call {電話中|でんわちゅう}.

questions.topic: お〜です and でいらっしゃる
questions.stem: Listen. What is the customer asked to do?

audio.text: おきゃくさま、こちらでしょうしょうおまちいただけますか。

questions.explanation: お{客様|きゃくさま}、こちらで{少々|しょうしょう}お{待|ま}ちいただけますか: a very polite request (お + stem + いただけますか) to wait here for a moment.

questions.stem: Listen. A customer says this to you in a shop. Which reply fits best?

audio.text: すみません、このかばん、ほかのいろはありますか。

choices: はい、お{買|か}いになりました。
わたくしがいらっしゃいます。
かしこまりました。お{待|ま}ちです。
もうしわけございません。ただいまございませんが、お{取|と}り{寄|よ}せできます。
questions.explanation: The customer asks if the bag comes in other colours. Staff apologize that there are none at the moment and offer to order one in. The others use keigo the wrong way round (いらっしゃる for yourself) or don't answer the question.

questions.topic: させていただく and お〜いたす
questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: Allow me to explain today's content.
questions.explanation: {本日|ほんじつ}の{内容|ないよう}を{説明|せつめい}させていただきます. The causative of {説明|せつめい}する is {説明|せつめい}させる, then the て form + いただきます. いたさせて isn't used: the causative of いたす isn't part of this pattern.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese, as said to a caller from another company.
questions.prompt: When Nishida gets back, I'll have him call you back.
questions.explanation: {西田|にしだ}が{戻|もど}りましたら、{折|お}り{返|かえ}しお{電話|でんわ}させます. To an outsider, your colleague gets no さん. {戻|もど}りましたら is the polite たら form, and させます (I'll have him do it) is the causative.

questions.stem:
Read the hotel notice and answer.

ホテルさくらをご{利用|りよう}いただき、ありがとうございます。チェックインは{午後|ごご}{三時|さんじ}から、チェックアウトは{午前|ごぜん}{十一時|じゅういちじ}までとなっております。{朝食|ちょうしょく}は{一階|いっかい}のレストランで、{六時半|ろくじはん}から{九時|くじ}までご{用意|ようい}しております。チェックアウトの{後|あと}も、{夕方|ゆうがた}{五時|ごじ}までフロントでおにもつをおあずかりいたします。ご{不明|ふめい}な{点|てん}がございましたら、{内線|ないせん}9{番|ばん}までお{電話|でんわ}ください。

You check out at eleven. Until what time can you leave your bag at the front desk?
questions.explanation: チェックアウトの{後|あと}も、{夕方|ゆうがた}{五時|ごじ}までフロントでおにもつをおあずかりいたします: the front desk keeps luggage until five. Three is check-in, nine is when breakfast ends, and eleven is check-out. おあずかりいたします (humble お〜いたす of N4's あずかる, to look after) is the hotel keeping your bags.

questions.topic: させていただく and お〜いたす
questions.stem:
Read the email from a shop and answer.

{先日|せんじつ}ご{注文|ちゅうもん}いただいた{商品|しょうひん}ですが、ただいまざいこがございません。もうしわけございませんが、{来週|らいしゅう}の{水曜日|すいようび}にお{送|おく}りすることになります。お{急|いそ}ぎの{場合|ばあい}は、{同|おな}じ{色|いろ}の{別|べつ}の{商品|しょうひん}にとりかえさせていただくこともできますので、ごれんらくいただけますでしょうか。

What does the shop offer a customer who is in a hurry?
choices: A different item in the same colour
A discount on the next order
questions.explanation: {同|おな}じ{色|いろ}の{別|べつ}の{商品|しょうひん}にとりかえさせていただくこともできます: they can exchange it for a different item in the same colour. Otherwise it will be sent next Wednesday, not this week. Nothing is said about money back or discounts.

questions.stem: What is the full form of やっといた in 「{宿題|しゅくだい}、もうやっといた。」?
questions.explanation: 〜とく / 〜といた is the contraction of 〜ておく / 〜ておいた: やっておいた (I've done it already, ready). The contraction of やっていた would be やってた, of やってしまった is やっちゃった, and やってみた has no contraction.

questions.stem: What is the full form of 「さいふ、{家|いえ}に{忘|わす}れてきちゃった。」?
choices: さいふを{家|いえ}に{忘|わす}れてきてしまった。
さいふを{家|いえ}に{忘|わす}れてきては。
さいふを{家|いえ}に{忘|わす}れてきている。
さいふを{家|いえ}に{忘|わす}れてきておいた。
questions.explanation: 〜ちゃった is 〜てしまった (with regret): {忘|わす}れてきてしまった, "I've gone and left my wallet at home". The casual sentence also drops を. 〜ては contracts to 〜ちゃ, not ちゃった; 〜ている becomes 〜てる and 〜ておいた becomes 〜といた.

questions.stem: もう{帰|かえ}らなきゃ means "I have to go home now". Type the full form of the missing part in hiragana: 「もう{帰|かえ}ら___ならない。」
questions.explanation: 〜なきゃ is the contraction of 〜なければ: {帰|かえ}らなければならない (I have to go home). 〜なくちゃ comes from 〜なくては, so なくては is accepted too.

questions.stem: Choose the ending: 「どうして{来|こ}なかったの？」「だって、さそわれなかった___。」 (Well, nobody invited me.)
questions.explanation: 〜んだもん gives a self-justifying reason, and it often follows だって: さそわれなかったんだもん. とく (ておく), ちゃう (てしまう) and なきゃ (なければ) are contractions of other endings and can't follow a past form like this.

questions.stem: Choose the ending: 「{分|わ}かった___。もう{何回|なんかい}も{言|い}わないで。」 (All right, I said I get it! Stop telling me over and over.)
questions.explanation: 〜ってば repeats something with impatience: {分|わ}かったってば (I said I get it!). もん gives a reason, and とく / てく are contractions of ておく / ていく, which need a て form.

questions.stem: Asking a close friend casually: "Are you off tomorrow?" Which is the most natural?
choices: {明日|あした}、{休|やす}みでございますか。
questions.explanation: Casual questions drop だ and か and rise at the end: {明日|あした}、{休|やす}み？ ×{休|やす}みだ？ and ×{休|やす}みだか？ aren't used, and でございますか is far too formal for a friend.

questions.stem: Someone gets ready to start a hard job and says to himself: 「よし、やる___！」 Which particle fits best?
questions.explanation: ぞ is a strong ending, used to yourself to fire yourself up: よし、やるぞ！ (Right, let's do this!). かしら is "I wonder", わね is soft and shares a feeling, and よね checks with someone else.

questions.stem: Choose the word that fits: 「ごめん、{急|きゅう}に___ができて、{今日|きょう}の{飲|の}み{会|かい}に{行|い}けなくなっちゃった。」
questions.explanation: Something that comes up suddenly and stops you going is {急用|きゅうよう} (urgent business). A {先約|せんやく} is an earlier plan, so it can't appear {急|きゅう}に; わりかん (splitting the bill) and {二次会|にじかい} (the after-party) don't fit.

questions.stem: Choose the word that fits: 「{予定|よてい}がなかったから、{駅|えき}の{近|ちか}くを___してた。」
questions.explanation: ぶらぶらする is to wander around with no particular aim: {駅|えき}の{近|ちか}くをぶらぶらする. ごろごろ is lying around at home, and わくわく / どきどき are feelings (excitement, a pounding heart), not ways of walking.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses {断|ことわ}る correctly?
choices: {雨|あめ}が{急|きゅう}に{断|ことわ}った。
{暑|あつ}いので、{窓|まど}を{断|ことわ}った。
{飲|の}み{会|かい}にさそわれたけど、バイトがあるから{断|ことわ}った。
{朝|あさ}ご{飯|はん}を{断|ことわ}って{食|た}べた。
questions.explanation: {断|ことわ}る is to turn down an invitation or a request: {飲|の}み{会|かい}を{断|ことわ}る. Rain, windows and breakfast can't be "turned down" in these sentences.

questions.stem: How is 昨日 read in 「昨日、{友|とも}だちと{遊|あそ}んだ。」?
questions.explanation: 昨日 has a special reading: きのう. おととい is {一昨日|おととい}, さくや is {昨夜|さくや} (last night), and きょう is {今日|きょう}.

questions.stem: Which kanji is used for あそんだ in 「{夜|よる}おそくまで{友|とも}だちとあそんだ」?
questions.explanation: あそ(ぶ) is 遊ぶ: {遊|あそ}んだ. 過 is す(ぎる), す(ごす), 送 is おく(る), and 達 has no kun'yomi at this level. All four share the "road" shape at the bottom left, which is why they look alike.

questions.stem: How is 末 read in 週末 (weekend)?
questions.explanation: In compounds 末 is マツ: {週末|しゅうまつ}, {月末|げつまつ}, {年末|ねんまつ}. On its own it's すえ ({今月|こんげつ}の{末|すえ}).

questions.stem: Listen. What is the friend saying?

audio.text: ごめん、きゅうようができちゃって、きょういけなくなった。

choices: Something urgent has come up, so they can't come today.
They forgot about today, so they'll be late.
They'll come today after finishing something urgent.
They want to change the plan to an urgent one.
questions.explanation: {急用|きゅうよう}ができちゃって、{今日|きょう}{行|い}けなくなった: something urgent came up (できちゃって = できてしまって), and now they can't go today. They aren't coming later.

questions.stem: Listen. What will the speaker do?

audio.text: これ、やっとくから、さきにかえってて。

choices: Ask the listener to finish this
Do this, so the listener can go home first
Wait until the listener comes back
questions.explanation: これ、やっとくから、{先|さき}に{帰|かえ}ってて = これ、やっておくから、{先|さき}に{帰|かえ}っていて: "I'll do this, so you go on home". The speaker stays; the listener goes.

questions.stem: Listen. A friend asks you this. You can't go. Which reply fits best?

audio.text: あした、ひま？えいがみにいかない？

choices: うん、もう{見|み}ちゃった。
ごめん、{明日|あした}はちょっと{先約|せんやく}があって…。
いいえ、ひまでございます。
questions.explanation: The friend asks if you're free and invites you to a film. Refusing gently, with ちょっと and a reason left hanging, is the natural reply. でございます is far too formal, and the other two answer a different question.

questions.stem: Build the casual sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: I'll buy the tickets, so go on ahead.
questions.explanation: チケット、{買|か}っとくから、{先|さき}に{行|い}ってて. {買|か}っとく = {買|か}っておく (buy in advance) and {行|い}ってて = {行|い}っていて. を is dropped after チケット. {買|か}っちゃう (てしまう) would add "and be done with it", which doesn't fit.

questions.stem: Build the casual sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: Well, I didn't know anything about that, did I!
questions.explanation: だって、そんなこと{知|し}らなかったんだもん. だって (but, because) opens the excuse and んだもん closes it. ってば would insist on something you'd already said, which doesn't fit with だって here.

questions.stem:
Read the chat and answer.

あや：{明日|あした}の{待|ま}ち{合|あ}わせ、{十時|じゅうじ}に{駅|えき}でいいんだよね？
りく：ごめん、ちょっと{遅|おく}れるかも。{朝|あさ}、{歯医者|はいしゃ}{行|い}かなきゃいけなくて。
あや：そっか。じゃあ、{先|さき}にお{店|みせ}{入|はい}っとくね。
りく：ありがと！{十一時|じゅういちじ}までには{着|つ}くから。
あや：りょうかい。{遅|おく}れたら、ランチおごってもらうからね（{笑|わら}）

Why might Riku be late?
choices: He has to go to the dentist in the morning.
He has to buy lunch first.
He doesn't know where the shop is.
He has to work until eleven.
questions.explanation: {歯医者|はいしゃ}{行|い}かなきゃいけなくて = {歯医者|はいしゃ}に{行|い}かなければいけなくて: he has to go to the dentist. He says he'll arrive by eleven; Aya jokes that he'll buy her lunch if he's late. おごる = to treat someone.

questions.stem:
Read the blog post and answer.

{先週|せんしゅう}の{土曜日|どようび}、ひさしぶりに{高校|こうこう}の{友|とも}だちと{会|あ}った。{三年|さんねん}ぶりだったのに、{会|あ}ったとたん{昔|むかし}みたいにしゃべり{始|はじ}めて、{気|き}がついたらもう{終電|しゅうでん}の{時間|じかん}だった。{二次会|にじかい}のカラオケも{行|い}きたかったけど、{次|つぎ}の{日|ひ}が{仕事|しごと}だったので{断|ことわ}った。{来月|らいげつ}またみんなで{集|あつ}まることになったので、{今|いま}から{楽|たの}しみだ。

Why didn't the writer go to karaoke?
choices: He had already missed the last train.
He had work the next day.
questions.explanation: {次|つぎ}の{日|ひ}が{仕事|しごと}だったので{断|ことわ}った: he turned it down because he had work the next day. He says he wanted to go, and the last-train time is what made him notice how late it was, not the reason he left.

questions.stem: Choose the word that fits: 「{祖母|そぼ}の___は、{半分|はんぶん}ぐらいしか{分|わ}からない。」 (I can only understand about half of my grandmother's dialect.)
questions.explanation: A grandmother's speech that you only half understand is her dialect: {方言|ほうげん}. {共通語|きょうつうご} is the Japanese everyone understands, {地元|じもと} is a home town, and {関東|かんとう} is the Tokyo region.

questions.stem: Which best describes {共通語|きょうつうご}?
choices: The old Japanese of the Edo period
The Japanese that people all over Japan understand
questions.explanation: {共通語|きょうつうご} is "common Japanese", based on Tokyo speech and understood everywhere; people switch to it with strangers. Kansai speech is かんさいべん, a {方言|ほうげん}.

questions.stem: In Kansai-ben, 「{分|わ}からへん」 means the same as…
questions.explanation: Kansai 〜へん replaces the ない of the negative: {分|わ}からへん = {分|わ}からない. It isn't past or a guess.

questions.stem: A Kansai speaker says 「そんなん、あかん。」 What does あかん mean?
questions.explanation: あかん is Kansai for だめ (no good, not allowed): そんなの、だめ. "Very" is めっちゃ, "really?" is ほんま？ and "thanks" is おおきに.

questions.stem: Which is true of めっちゃ, according to the lesson?
choices: It's used only by older people in Kyoto.
It began in Kansai and is now used by young people all over Japan.
It's a polite word for business.
questions.explanation: めっちゃ (very) started in Kansai and spread: young people use it as ordinary casual slang everywhere. The word mostly heard from older Kansai speakers is おおきに.

questions.stem: In Hiroshima dialect, what does 「{雨|あめ}じゃけん、かさ{持|も}ってきた？」 mean?
choices: It isn't raining, so did you leave your umbrella?
It's raining, so did you bring an umbrella?
If it rains, will you bring an umbrella?
questions.explanation: じゃ is Hiroshima's だ, and 〜けん means から (because): {雨|あめ}だから、かさ{持|も}ってきた？ じゃ here isn't the negative じゃない, and けん isn't a condition.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the Kansai speaker mean?

audio.text: それ、ほんまにええやん。

questions.explanation: ほんまに = {本当|ほんとう}に, ええ = いい, 〜やん = 〜じゃん: それ、{本当|ほんとう}にいいじゃん (that's really nice). No negative and no question here.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the Kansai speaker saying?

audio.text: あしたは、いかへんねん。

choices: I'm not going tomorrow, you see.
questions.explanation: {行|い}かへん = {行|い}かない, and 〜ねん = 〜んだ: {明日|あした}は{行|い}かないんだ (I'm not going tomorrow, you see).

questions.stem: Which statement about Kansai pitch accent matches the lesson?
choices: It's the same as Tokyo pitch, with a few different words.
It's a different system, and some word pairs come out roughly the other way round.
Kansai speech has no pitch accent at all.
It's the pitch marked in this course.
questions.explanation: The lesson describes Kansai pitch as a different system from Tokyo's, with pairs such as はし (chopsticks) and {橋|はし} (bridge) often said roughly the opposite way. The course marks Tokyo pitch.

questions.stem: Which Kansai word matches {本当|ほんとう}?
questions.explanation: ほんま = {本当|ほんとう} (ほんまに？ = really?). ちゃう is {違|ちが}う, ええ is いい and おおきに is ありがとう.

questions.stem:
Read the text and answer.

{大学|だいがく}に{入|はい}って、{関東|かんとう}から{来|き}た{友|とも}だちに、「どうして{関西|かんさい}の{人|ひと}は、いつも{話|はなし}を{面白|おもしろ}く{終|お}わらせようとするの？」と{聞|き}かれた。{言|い}われてみると、{確|たし}かに{私|わたし}たちは、{笑|わら}える{終|お}わり{方|かた}を{考|かんが}えながら{話|はな}していることが{多|おお}い。でも、それは{方言|ほうげん}というより、{地元|じもと}の{文化|ぶんか}なのだと{思|おも}う。

What does the writer think?
choices: Kanto people talk the same way.
Ending a story with a laugh is part of local culture, rather than of the dialect.
Kansai people should stop making jokes.
questions.explanation: {方言|ほうげん}というより、{地元|じもと}の{文化|ぶんか}なのだ: "not so much the dialect as the local culture". The writer agrees the habit exists ({言|い}われてみると、{確|たし}かに…) and doesn't criticize it.

questions.stem:
Read the text and answer.

{東北|とうほく}に{住|す}む{祖父|そふ}は、「{行|い}くべ」とよく{言|い}う。{初|はじ}めて{聞|き}いたときは{意味|いみ}が{分|わ}からなかったが、「{行|い}こう」という{意味|いみ}だと{母|はは}が{教|おし}えてくれた。{今|いま}では{私|わたし}も、{祖父|そふ}と{話|はな}すときだけ「{行|い}くべ」と{言|い}ってみる。{祖父|そふ}はそれを{聞|き}くと、いつもうれしそうに{笑|わら}う。

What does 「{行|い}くべ」 mean?
questions.explanation: The mother explains that {行|い}くべ means {行|い}こう (let's go): the Tohoku 〜べ often works like the volitional. The writer now uses it with the grandfather, who is pleased.

questions.stem: In a job interview, which word for "I" is safest for a learner?
questions.explanation: {私|わたし} (or {私|わたくし}) is right for anyone in a formal situation. おれ is rough and casual, あたし is casual and feminine, and わし sounds like an old man in a story.

questions.stem: In a manga, a character says 「わしは{知|し}らんのう。」 What kind of character is most likely speaking?
choices: A shop assistant talking to a customer
questions.explanation: わし, {知|し}らん (= {知|し}らない) and 〜のう are the role language of an old man or a wise master. A shop assistant would use keigo, and a schoolgirl would more likely say {私|わたし}, あたし or うち.

questions.stem: Which ending marks a samurai in comedies and historical stories?
questions.explanation: 〜でござる is the samurai of fiction (せっしゃは〜でござる). 〜ですわ is the rich young lady, 〜だぜ the tough young man, and 〜かしら an older or refined woman.

questions.stem: Which statement about やばい matches the lesson?
choices: It's polite enough for work emails.
It can mean "bad, uh-oh" or "amazing", depending on the situation.
It's used only by older people.
questions.explanation: やばい began as "dangerous, risky", and young people now also use it for something amazing; tone and situation tell you which. It's casual slang, not for work.

questions.stem: A friend tells a funny story, and you say 「それ、ウケる！」 What do you mean?
questions.explanation: In slang, ウケる (from {受|う}ける, "to go down well") means "that's funny". It's written in katakana in this sense; it has nothing to do with receiving or accepting here.

questions.stem: Which is the standard form to use in writing for "very tasty"?
questions.explanation: Before an adjective, the adverb form すごく is standard: すごくおいしい. すごいおいしい is very common in speech but is seen as incorrect in writing. The other two aren't used.

questions.stem: What is {役割語|やくわりご} (role language)?
choices: The keigo used by staff in shops
A regional dialect such as Kansai-ben
The words for jobs and positions in a company
A way of speaking that marks a type of character in fiction
questions.explanation: Role language is a speech style that tells you who a character is (an old man, a rich young lady, a samurai), mostly in fiction and translation, not the real speech of any group. Keigo and dialects are real speech.

questions.stem: A teacher tells you some surprising news. Which reply is appropriate?
choices: {先生|せんせい}、それ、ウケますね。
{先生|せんせい}、{本当|ほんとう}ですか。
questions.explanation: With a teacher, use neutral polite Japanese: {本当|ほんとう}ですか. マジ, ウケる and ガチ are casual slang; adding です doesn't make them polite.

questions.stem: Listen. How does the speaker feel?

audio.text: え、マジで？それ、ほんと？

questions.explanation: マジで？ (seriously?) and ほんと？ (really?) show surprise at what they've just heard.

questions.stem: Listen. What has happened?

audio.text: やばい、さいふ、いえにわすれてきた。

choices: The speaker bought a new wallet.
The speaker left their wallet at home.
questions.explanation: やばい here is "uh-oh": さいふを{家|いえ}に{忘|わす}れてきた (I've left my wallet at home). Nothing was found, bought or stolen.

questions.stem:
Read the text and answer.

アニメで{日本語|にほんご}を{覚|おぼ}えた{留学生|りゅうがくせい}が、{先生|せんせい}に「{明日|あした}も{来|く}るぜ！」と{言|い}って、{先生|せんせい}をびっくりさせたという{話|はなし}を{聞|き}いた。アニメのキャラクターの{話|はな}し{方|かた}は、{実際|じっさい}の{日本人|にほんじん}の{話|はな}し{方|かた}とは{違|ちが}うことが{多|おお}い。{日本語|にほんご}を{勉強|べんきょう}する{人|ひと}は、まず{自分|じぶん}のまわりの{人|ひと}の{話|はな}し{方|かた}をまねしたほうがいいだろう。

What does the writer advise learners to do?
choices: Copy the way people around them speak
Learn the speech of each character type
questions.explanation: まず{自分|じぶん}のまわりの{人|ひと}の{話|はな}し{方|かた}をまねしたほうがいい: copy the people around you first, because anime speech often differs from real speech. まねする = to imitate.

questions.stem:
Read the text and answer.

{最近|さいきん}、{若者|わかもの}の{間|あいだ}で「ガチ」という{言葉|ことば}がよく{使|つか}われている。「{本気|ほんき}で」「{本当|ほんとう}に」という{意味|いみ}で、「ガチで{疲|つか}れた」のように{使|つか}う。ただ、{目上|めうえ}の{人|ひと}に{使|つか}うと{失礼|しつれい}だと{感|かん}じる{人|ひと}も{多|おお}いので、{注意|ちゅうい}したほうがいい。

What does the text say about using ガチ?
choices: Be careful using it with people above you.
It has become polite enough for anyone.
questions.explanation: {目上|めうえ}の{人|ひと}に{使|つか}うと{失礼|しつれい}だと{感|かん}じる{人|ひと}も{多|おお}い: many people find it rude towards those above you, so take care. It means "seriously, really"; {疲|つか}れた is just the example. {本気|ほんき} = in earnest.

questions.stem: You are writing a report in the written style. Which sentence is correct?
choices: {今年|ことし}の{夏|なつ}は{暑|あつ}いである。
{今年|ことし}の{夏|なつ}は{例年|れいねん}より{暑|あつ}かった。
{今年|ことし}の{夏|なつ}は{暑|あつ}いであった。
{今年|ことし}の{夏|なつ}は{暑|あつ}かったです。
questions.explanation: An い-adjective ends a written-style sentence on its own: {暑|あつ}い, {暑|あつ}かった. である only follows nouns and な-adjectives, so {暑|あつ}いである and {暑|あつ}いであった are wrong. {暑|あつ}かったです is correct Japanese, but it is the polite style, which doesn't belong in a である report. ({例年|れいねん} = an average year.)

questions.stem: この{方法|ほうほう}だけでは{十分|じゅうぶん}___。 Choose the ending for a written report.
questions.explanation: The written negative after a noun or な-adjective is ではない: {十分|じゅうぶん}ではない. じゃない is the same thing in speech and never appears in a report; ではありません is the polite style. {十分|じゅうぶん} is a な-adjective, so the い-adjective ending くない is wrong.

questions.stem: {町|まち}の{人口|じんこう}は{年々|ねんねん}{減|へ}って___、{店|みせ}も{少|すく}なくなった。 Choose the written-style form for the blank.
questions.explanation: In writing, 〜ている joins the next clause as 〜ており、: {減|へ}っており、{店|みせ}も…. ×{減|へ}ってい、 is not used, and おる and いる are sentence endings: a comma after them doesn't join anything. (In speech you'd say {減|へ}っていて、.)

questions.stem: Which is the written-style version of 「{何|なに}もしないで{帰|かえ}った」?
choices: {何|なに}もしずに{帰|かえ}った
{何|なに}もさずに{帰|かえ}った
{何|なに}もしなくずに{帰|かえ}った
{何|なに}もせずに{帰|かえ}った
questions.explanation: The ず form of する is せず, so "without doing anything" is {何|なに}もせずに. ×しず and ×さず are common slips (other verbs take the ない stem: {食|た}べず, {行|い}かず, but する is irregular), and ず never follows なく.

questions.topic: のである and opinions in writing
questions.stem: 「{夜|よる}になっても{気温|きおん}が{下|さ}がらない。{町|まち}そのものが{熱|ねつ}をためているのである。」 What does のである do in the second sentence?
choices: It explains the reason behind the fact in the first sentence.
It turns the sentence into a question to the reader.
It shows that the writer is quoting someone else.
It makes the sentence more polite to the reader.
questions.explanation: のである is the written form of んです: it explains or gives the background. The first sentence states a fact; the second says why: "(the reason is that) the town itself is storing heat." It isn't a question (that would be のではないだろうか), a quotation (という / とのことだ) or polite (です / ます).

questions.topic: のである and opinions in writing
questions.stem: この{問題|もんだい}は、{国|くに}だけでなく{私|わたし}たち{一人|ひとり}{一人|ひとり}にも{責任|せきにん}がある___。 The writer wants to give an opinion modestly in a written essay. Choose the best ending.
questions.explanation: のではないだろうか ("isn't it the case that…?") is the usual modest opinion in written Japanese. んじゃないかな says the same thing in casual speech, and と{思|おも}います and でしょうね are polite style, so none of them fits a である essay.

questions.stem: A sign at a museum says: 「{十二歳|じゅうにさい}{未満|みまん}は{無料|むりょう}」. Who goes in free?
questions.explanation: {未満|みまん} means "under, less than" and doesn't include the number itself, so {十二歳|じゅうにさい}{未満|みまん} is 11 and under. "12 and under" would be {十二歳|じゅうにさい}{以下|いか}, and "12 and over" {十二歳|じゅうにさい}{以上|いじょう}.

questions.stem: {工場|こうじょう}から{流|なが}れてきた{水|みず}で、{川|かわ}の___が{進|すす}んだ。 Choose the word for the blank.
questions.explanation: おせん (pollution) is what spreads in a river when factory water flows into it: "the river's pollution got worse". {進歩|しんぽ} is progress (of science or society), {無事|ぶじ} means safe and sound, and {予想|よそう} is a prediction; none of them can be "caused" by dirty water.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses 「{深刻|しんこく}」 correctly?
choices: あの{人|ひと}はとても{深刻|しんこく}で、{約束|やくそく}は{必|かなら}ず{守|まも}る。
このケーキは{深刻|しんこく}においしい。
{水|みず}が{足|た}りないことが、{深刻|しんこく}な{問題|もんだい}になっている。
{今日|きょう}は{深刻|しんこく}な{天気|てんき}なので、{散歩|さんぽ}に{行|い}こう。
questions.explanation: {深刻|しんこく} describes a serious problem or situation: {深刻|しんこく}な{問題|もんだい}. A person who keeps their promises is {真面目|まじめ}, not {深刻|しんこく}; it can't mean "very" (that's {非常|ひじょう}に), and good weather for a walk is the opposite of anything {深刻|しんこく}.

questions.stem: {台風|たいふう}の{中|なか}、{船|ふね}は無事に{港|みなと}に{着|つ}いた。 How is 無事 read?
questions.explanation: 無事 is ぶじ, "safely": 無 is read ブ here (it is ム in {無理|むり} and {無料|むりょう}), and 事 is ジ. むじ mixes up the two readings of 無, and ないこと and むごと aren't readings of this word.

questions.stem: {夜|よる}になっても、きおんがなかなか{下|さ}がらない。 Which kanji are used for きおん?
questions.explanation: きおん (air temperature) is 気温: 気 (air, spirit) + 温 (warm, オン). 湯 (hot water) is a kitchen kanji, and 期 (period) and 機 (machine) are also read キ but don't make this word. The same 温 is in {温度|おんど} and {体温|たいおん}.

questions.stem: この{紙|かみ}の原料は{古|ふる}い{新聞|しんぶん}である。 How is 原料 read?
questions.explanation: 原料 (raw material) is げんりょう, with the on'yomi ゲン of 原 as in {原因|げんいん}. はら is 原's kun'yomi ({野原|のはら}), which isn't used here, and 料 has a long vowel: リョウ, as in {料理|りょうり}.

questions.stem: {体|からだ}が{十分|じゅうぶん}{休|やす}ま___、{病気|びょうき}になる{人|ひと}が{増|ふ}えた。 Type the written-style ending for the blank (meaning "not resting enough, and…"), in kana.
questions.explanation: The written negative join is the ず form: {休|やす}まない → {休|やす}まず、. In speech the same idea is {休|やす}まなくて、 or {休|やす}まないで、.

questions.stem: Listen. What did you hear?

audio.text: げんいんは、ひとつではない。

choices: There is more than one cause.
The cause is not yet known.
One of the causes has been found.
questions.explanation: {原因|げんいん}は{一|ひと}つではない: "the cause is not one", i.e. there are several causes. ではない is the written negative; listen for it at the end. Nothing is said about the cause being unknown or found.

questions.stem: Listen to the notice. Who can't go in?

audio.text: じゅうはっさいみまんのかたは、はいることができません。

questions.explanation: {十八歳|じゅうはっさい}{未満|みまん}の{方|かた} are people under 18 (17 and younger), and they can't go in. じゅうはっさい (18) is short; 80 would be はちじゅっさい. {未満|みまん} never includes the number itself.

questions.stem: Listen to the teacher. What does she want the students to do?

audio.text: レポートは、です・ますではなく、であるでかいてください。

choices: Write the report in the である style.
Write the report in the polite style.
Hand in the report next week.
questions.explanation: です・ますではなく、であるで{書|か}いてください: "not in です / ます but in である, please." The polite style is exactly what she doesn't want, and she says nothing about handwriting or the deadline.

questions.topic: のである and opinions in writing
questions.stem: Build the sentence in the written style.
questions.prompt: The cause is thought to be human activity.
questions.explanation: その{原因|げんいん}は{人間|にんげん}の{活動|かつどう}であると{考|かんが}えられる. The topic comes first, the noun phrase ends in である (written style; です would be polite), and と{考|かんが}えられる turns it into "it is thought that…".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in the written style.
questions.prompt: The temperature didn't fall even at night, and many people couldn't sleep.
questions.explanation: {夜|よる}も{気温|きおん}が{下|さ}がらず、{眠|ねむ}れない{人|ひと}が{多|おお}かった. 〜ず、 is the written negative join ("didn't fall, and…"); {下|さ}がり、 would say the temperature did fall. {夜|よる}も and {気温|きおん}が can change places.

questions.stem:
Read the passage and answer the question.
{昔|むかし}、{馬|うま}は{人|ひと}の{生活|せいかつ}になくてはならない{存在|そんざい}であった。{人|ひと}や{物|もの}を{運|はこ}び、{田|た}んぼでも{働|はたら}いた。しかし、{車|くるま}やきかいが{広|ひろ}まると、{馬|うま}の{仕事|しごと}は{急|きゅう}に{減|へ}った。{現在|げんざい}、{日本|にほん}で{見|み}られる{馬|うま}の{多|おお}くは、レースや{乗馬|じょうば}のための{馬|うま}である。{働|はたら}く{動物|どうぶつ}から、{楽|たの}しむための{動物|どうぶつ}へ。{馬|うま}と{人|ひと}との{関係|かんけい}は、この{百年|ひゃくねん}で{大|おお}きく{変|か}わったのである。 What change does the writer describe?
choices: Horses have almost disappeared from Japan.
Horses are now used more in rice fields than before.
Horses went from being working animals to animals kept for enjoyment.
Cars were invented because horses were too slow.
questions.explanation: The last two sentences sum it up: {働|はたら}く{動物|どうぶつ}から、{楽|たの}しむための{動物|どうぶつ}へ, "from animals that work to animals for enjoyment" (racing and riding, {乗馬|じょうば}). Horses are still seen (they haven't disappeared), their farm work decreased, and the text says nothing about why cars were invented. Notice the である endings and the closing のである, which states the conclusion.

questions.stem: In the lesson reading "Why towns get hot", how do plants help cool a town?
choices: They give off water from their leaves.
They block the wind between buildings.
They take in the heat from air conditioners.
They reflect sunlight like a white roof.
questions.explanation: The text says しょくぶつは{葉|は}から{水|みず}を{出|だ}し、まわりの{温度|おんど}を{下|さ}げる{働|はたら}きをしている: plants release water from their leaves and lower the temperature around them. White roofs are a separate method in the last paragraph, and the text mentions neither wind nor plants absorbing air-conditioner heat.

questions.stem: {来月|らいげつ}から{毎朝|まいあさ}ジョギングを___つもりだ。 Choose the best word for the blank.
questions.explanation: A planned start takes 〜{始|はじ}める: ジョギングをし{始|はじ}める. 〜{出|だ}す is for something that starts suddenly or without warning ({雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}り{出|だ}す), so it doesn't fit a plan made for next month. し{切|き}る (do completely) and し{直|なお}す (do again) don't mean "begin".

questions.stem: {空|そら}が{急|きゅう}に{暗|くら}くなって、{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}り___。 Choose the word for the blank.
questions.explanation: 〜{出|だ}す after a stem means a sudden start: {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}り{出|だ}した, it suddenly started raining (the sky had just gone dark). 〜{込|こ}む is "into", 〜{合|あ}う "each other" and 〜{切|き}る "completely", and none of them goes with rain starting.

questions.stem: {料理|りょうり}が{多|おお}すぎて、{全部|ぜんぶ}は{食|た}べ___。 Choose the ending for the blank (There's too much food; I can't eat it all).
questions.explanation: "Can't finish" is the potential negative of 〜{切|き}る: {食|た}べ{切|き}れない. {食|た}べ{切|き}らない means "(choose to) not eat it all", which doesn't fit "too much food". {食|た}べ{直|なお}す and {食|た}べ{込|こ}む aren't used here.

questions.stem: {名前|なまえ}を{間違|まちが}えたので、{書|か}き___。 Choose the word for the blank.
questions.explanation: I got the name wrong, so I rewrote it: {書|か}き{直|なお}した. 〜{直|なお}す is "do again, properly". {書|か}き{出|だ}す is "start writing" or "write out", {書|か}き{合|あ}う would be writing to each other, and {書|か}き{上|あ}がる is intransitive (a text "gets finished"; finishing it yourself is {書|か}き{上|あ}げる).

questions.stem: {困|こま}ったときは、みんなで{助|たす}け___ことが{大切|たいせつ}だ。 Choose the word for the blank.
questions.explanation: 〜{合|あ}う makes the action mutual: {助|たす}け{合|あ}う, to help each other. みんなで (all together) is the hint. {助|たす}け{出|だ}す means "to rescue (someone out of somewhere)", {助|たす}け{上|あ}げる is "to pull someone up to safety", and {助|たす}け{切|き}る isn't used.

questions.stem: {窓|まど}を{開|あ}け___で{出|で}かけてしまった。 Choose the word for the blank (I went out and left the window open).
questions.explanation: Stem + っぱなし is "left in that state": {開|あ}けっぱなしで{出|で}かけた, went out with the window left open. {開|あ}けかけ would be "half-opened", {開|あ}けすぎ "opened too much", and ながら needs a verb to follow it ({開|あ}けながら{出|で}かける is "go out while opening"), so none of them says "left open".

questions.stem: {山田|やまだ}さんは、{会議|かいぎ}は{三時|さんじ}からだと{思|おも}い{込|こ}んでいた。 What does this tell us about Mr Yamada?
choices: He hoped the meeting would start at three.
He told everyone the meeting was at three.
He was sure it started at three, but he was probably wrong.
He remembered correctly that it started at three.
questions.explanation: {思|おも}い{込|こ}む is "to be convinced", usually of something that turns out to be wrong. 〜と{思|おも}い{込|こ}んでいた suggests he found out otherwise. It isn't a hope ({思|おも}う / ほしい), something he told others ({言|い}う), or a correct memory.

questions.stem: {台風|たいふう}に___、{水|みず}や{食|た}べ{物|もの}を{買|か}っておいた。 Choose the word for the blank.
questions.explanation: 〜に{備|そな}える is "to prepare for": {台風|たいふう}に{備|そな}えて, in preparation for the typhoon. 〜を{除|のぞ}いて means "except for", {抜|ぬ}く "to pull out" and {散|ち}らす "to scatter"; none of them explains buying water and food in advance.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses 「{見直|みなお}す」 correctly?
choices: テストを{出|だ}す{前|まえ}に、{答|こた}えをよく{見直|みなお}した。
{駅|えき}で{偶然|ぐうぜん}{友|とも}だちと{見直|みなお}して、{話|はなし}をした。
{毎朝|まいあさ}テレビでニュースを{見直|みなお}している。
{猫|ねこ}が{見直|みなお}して、{逃|に}げていった。
questions.explanation: {見直|みなお}す is "to look over again, to check": {答|こた}えを{見直|みなお}す before handing in a test. Meeting a friend by chance is {会|あ}う, ordinary watching is {見|み}る, and the cat sentence makes no sense with {見直|みなお}す.

questions.stem:
A notice in a block of flats:
{住|す}んでいる{皆様|みなさま}へ。ごみ{置|お}き{場|ば}が{散|ち}らかっていて{困|こま}っています。{段|だん}ボールは{小|ちい}さくたたんで、{水曜日|すいようび}の{朝|あさ}{八時|はちじ}までに{出|だ}してください。いすやたななどの{家具|かぐ}は、ごみ{置|お}き{場|ば}に{置|お}かないでください。{市|し}に{電話|でんわ}で{申|もう}し{込|こ}んでから、{決|き}められた{日|ひ}に{出|だ}すことになっています。 You want to throw away an old shelf. What should you do?
choices: Fold it small and put it out by 8 on Wednesday morning.
Phone the city first and put it out on the day you are given.
Leave it at the collection point on any day.
Take it apart and put it in a cardboard box.
questions.explanation: A shelf (たな) is furniture ({家具|かぐ}), and the notice says furniture must not be left at the collection point: you apply to the city by phone ({市|し}に{電話|でんわ}で{申|もう}し{込|こ}んでから) and put it out on the day you are given. Folding small by Wednesday morning is the rule for cardboard boxes only.

questions.stem: {寒|さむ}いので、{夜|よる}は雨戸を{閉|し}めた。 How is 雨戸 read?
questions.explanation: 雨戸 (storm shutter) is あまど: 雨 becomes あま in compounds ({雨水|あまみず}), and 戸 (と) is voiced to ど after another word, as in {引|ひ}き{戸|ど}. あめと keeps neither change, and うこ uses on'yomi that this word doesn't have.

questions.stem: {庭|にわ}に{自転車|じてんしゃ}の［おきば］を{作|つく}った。 Which kanji are used for おきば?
questions.explanation: おきば (a place to keep something) is 置き場: 置 (put, お(く)) + 場 (place, ば). 起 (お(きる), get up) sounds the same but means something else, 葉 is a leaf, and 押 is お(す), not お(く).

questions.stem: {夕|ゆう}ご{飯|はん}のあと、{家族|かぞく}は居間でテレビを{見|み}た。 How is 居間 read?
questions.explanation: 居間 (living room) is いま: 居 is read い, as in the verb いる, and 間 is ま, as in {間|ま}に{合|あ}う. きょま uses 居's on'yomi キョ, which isn't used here, and いあいだ reads 間 as あいだ.

questions.stem: {買|か}った{野菜|やさい}を{全部|ぜんぶ}___ましょう。 Type the compound verb that means "use up", in its ます stem (kana or kanji).
questions.explanation: 〜{切|き}る means "completely": {使|つか}う → {使|つか}い{切|き}る, to use up. Before ましょう it takes the ます stem: {使|つか}い{切|き}りましょう.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker asking?

audio.text: でんきを、つけっぱなしにしないでください。

choices: Please don't leave the light on.
Please don't turn the light off.
questions.explanation: {電気|でんき}をつけっぱなしにしないでください: っぱなし is "left on", and しないでください asks you not to do it. So it's "don't leave the light on", not a request to switch it on or off.

questions.stem: Listen. What did you hear?

audio.text: このたなは、ひとりではもちあげられません。

choices: One person put this shelf together.
This shelf is light enough for one person.
This shelf can only be assembled by one person.
One person can't lift this shelf.
questions.explanation: このたなは、{一人|ひとり}では{持|も}ち{上|あ}げられません: {持|も}ち{上|あ}げる (to lift) in the potential negative, "can't be lifted by one person". There's no {組|く}み{立|た}てる (assemble) in the sentence, and the shelf is heavy, not light.

questions.stem: Listen. At the city office, a man asks you a question. Choose the best reply.

audio.text: すみません。このもうしこみしょ、どこにかきこめばいいですか。

choices: はい、{書|か}き{直|なお}しました。
いいえ、{取|と}り{出|だ}しません。
こちらに、お{名前|なまえ}とご{住所|じゅうしょ}をお{願|ねが}いします。
じゃあ、{話|はな}し{合|あ}いましょう。
questions.explanation: He asks where he should write on the application form ({申込書|もうしこみしょ}、どこに{書|か}き{込|こ}めばいいですか). The natural reply shows him where and what to write: "here, your name and address, please." Saying you rewrote something, refusing to take something out or suggesting a discussion doesn't answer "where".

questions.stem: Build the sentence.
questions.prompt: We talked it over as a family and decided to move.
questions.explanation: {家族|かぞく}で{話|はな}し{合|あ}って、{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}すことに{決|き}めた. {話|はな}し{合|あ}う (to talk over together) joins the decision with the て form; 〜ことに{決|き}める is "decide to…". {話|はな}し{出|だ}す would be "start talking (suddenly)".

questions.stem: Build the sentence.
questions.prompt: Yesterday I went out and left the window open.
questions.explanation: {昨日|きのう}は{窓|まど}を{開|あ}けっぱなしで{出|で}かけてしまった. 〜っぱなしで is "with … left (open)", and 〜てしまった adds regret. {開|あ}けかけ would mean "half-opened".

questions.stem: In the lesson reading "Living with fewer things", what had the writer wrongly believed ({思|おも}い{込|こ}んでいた)?
choices: That there were too many things because the house was small.
That cleaning would always take a long time.
That a detached house would be too expensive.
That DIY was too difficult to try.
questions.explanation: The essay says {物|もの}が{多|おお}いのは{家|いえ}がせまいからだと{思|おも}い{込|こ}んでいた: "I was convinced I had too many things because the house was small". The real problem was the habit of keeping everything. The other answers aren't in the text: cleaning now takes ten minutes, and the writer enjoyed the first try at DIY.

questions.stem: {天気予報|てんきよほう}では{晴|は}れだった。___、{午後|ごご}から{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}り{出|だ}した。 Choose the word for the blank.
questions.explanation: What happened (rain) went against what was expected (the forecast said sunny), so the link is ところが. ところで changes the subject ("by the way"), それとも offers a choice in a question, and その{上|うえ} adds a point in the same direction.

questions.stem: {明日|あした}は{雨|あめ}かもしれない。___、{予定|よてい}{通|どお}り{出|で}かけよう。 Choose the word for the blank.
questions.explanation: The second sentence is a suggestion (〜よう), so the contrast must be でも (or しかし). ところが only reports an unexpected fact and can't introduce a plan or suggestion. そのため would make the rain the reason for going, and なぜなら needs a reason ending in からだ.

questions.stem: Build the sentence.
questions.prompt: What matters in learning a foreign language is to keep at it every day.
questions.explanation: {外国語|がいこくご}を{学|まな}ぶ{上|うえ}で{大切|たいせつ}なのは、{毎日|まいにち}{続|つづ}けることだ. The dictionary form + {上|うえ}で means "in doing"; the た form ({学|まな}んだ{上|うえ}で) would mean "after learning", which isn't the idea here.

questions.stem: この{部屋|へや}は{駅|えき}に{近|ちか}い。___、{広|ひろ}くて{明|あか}るい。 Choose the word for the blank.
questions.explanation: Close to the station is a good point, and spacious and bright are more good points, so the link adds: その{上|うえ} (on top of that). ところが and {一方|いっぽう} would set up a contrast, and {結局|けっきょく} (in the end) needs a process leading to an outcome.

questions.stem: {何年|なんねん}も{使|つか}ってきたけれど、___パソコンが{動|うご}かなくなってしまった。 Choose the word for the blank.
questions.explanation: After many years, the computer finally died: とうとう (in the end, after a long time) fits a result that was feared, and 〜てしまった shows regret. やっと is for something you were waiting for, so it would sound as if you wanted it to break. むしろ (rather) and {更|さら}に (further) don't fit.

questions.stem: よく{考|かんが}えた___、お{返事|へんじ}します。 Choose the words for the blank (I'll give you my answer after thinking it over carefully).
questions.explanation: The た form + {上|うえ}で means "after doing (and on that basis)": think it over first, then answer. うちに (while) and ところに (just when) are about timing within an action, and ために after a past form would give a reason ("because I thought"), which doesn't fit.

questions.stem: {彼|かれ}は{怒|おこ}っているのではない。___、{心配|しんぱい}しているのだ。 Choose the word for the blank.
questions.explanation: むしろ (rather, if anything) corrects the first idea: he isn't angry; rather, he's worried. しかも adds a further point, それとも offers a choice in a question, and そこで says what someone did as a result.

questions.stem:
Read the passage and choose the word for （　）.
{最近|さいきん}、{自転車|じてんしゃ}で{通勤|つうきん}する{人|ひと}が{増|ふ}えている。{健康|けんこう}にいいし、お{金|かね}もかからない。（　）、{雨|あめ}の{日|ひ}は{大変|たいへん}だし、{車|くるま}とぶつかる{危険|きけん}もある。{自転車|じてんしゃ}{通勤|つうきん}を{始|はじ}める{上|うえ}で{大切|たいせつ}なのは、{無理|むり}をしないことである。
questions.explanation: The passage gives the good side (healthy, costs nothing), then the bad side (rainy days, the risk of being hit by a car). {一方|いっぽう} (on the other hand) puts the second side next to the first. その{上|うえ} and しかも would add more good points, and つまり would sum up, which the next sentence doesn't do.

questions.stem: A test instruction says 「（　）に{入|い}るものとして、{最|もっと}も{適当|てきとう}なものを{選|えら}びなさい。」 What does {適当|てきとう}な mean here?
questions.explanation: In writing and in test instructions, {適当|てきとう} means "suitable, appropriate": choose the most suitable item. In everyday speech it often means "careless, half-hearted" ({適当|てきとう}にやる), but that can't be the meaning of an exam instruction.

questions.stem: {会社|かいしゃ}をやめるという{大|おお}きな___をする{前|まえ}に、{家族|かぞく}とよく{話|はな}し{合|あ}った。 Choose the word for the blank.
questions.explanation: Leaving the company is a big, hard decision: {大|おお}きな{決断|けつだん}をする. {欠点|けってん} is a drawback, {立場|たちば} a standpoint and {程度|ていど} a degree; none of them is something you "make" before talking it over.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses 「{断|ことわ}る」 correctly?
choices: {雨|あめ}が{断|ことわ}って、{試合|しあい}が{中止|ちゅうし}になった。
{忙|いそが}しかったので、パーティーの{招待|しょうたい}を{断|ことわ}った。
{電気|でんき}を{断|ことわ}ってから{寝|ね}た。
{美容院|びよういん}で{髪|かみ}を{短|みじか}く{断|ことわ}ってもらった。
questions.explanation: {断|ことわ}る is "to turn down, to refuse": {招待|しょうたい}を{断|ことわ}る, to decline an invitation. Rain stopping is やむ, switching off a light is {消|け}す, and having your hair cut is {切|き}ってもらう.

questions.stem: その{計画|けいかく}に賛成する{人|ひと}は{少|すく}なかった。 How is 賛成 read?
questions.explanation: 賛成 (agreement, being in favour) is さんせい: 賛 is サン and 成 is セイ. 成 is never read ジョウ in this word, and ざん has a voiced sound that isn't there.

questions.stem: {行|い}くかどうか、［はんだん］するのは{君|きみ}だ。 Which kanji are used for はんだん?
questions.explanation: はんだん (judgement) is 判断: 判 (judge, ハン) + 断 (cut off, decide, ダン). 半 (half) and 反 (against) are also read ハン, and 段 (step) is also ダン, but they make other words ({半分|はんぶん}, {反対|はんたい}, {階段|かいだん}).

questions.stem: {留学|りゅうがく}しようと決心した。 How is 決心 read?
questions.explanation: 決心 is けっしん: 決 (ケツ) shortens to けっ before し, as in {決|けっ}して. けつしん keeps the full ケツ, きめ is the kun of the verb {決|き}める, and 心 isn't voiced here.

questions.stem: Type the formal, written conjunction that means "that is, namely" (the written version of つまり), in kana.
questions.explanation: すなわち is the written つまり: {日本|にほん}の{首都|しゅと}、すなわち{東京|とうきょう} (the capital of Japan, that is, Tokyo). In speech つまり is far more common.

questions.stem: Listen. What happened?

audio.text: あめはすぐやむとおもった。ところが、よるまでふりつづけた。

choices: The rain stopped soon, as expected.
It didn't rain at all that day.
The rain only started at night.
The rain went on until night, against expectations.
questions.explanation: {雨|あめ}はすぐやむと{思|おも}った。ところが、{夜|よる}まで{降|ふ}り{続|つづ}けた: the speaker expected it to stop, but (ところが) it kept raining until night ({降|ふ}り{続|つづ}ける, keep falling). It didn't stop or start at night.

questions.stem: Listen. Why is the speaker against the plan?

audio.text: わたしは、そのけいかくにはんたいです。なぜなら、ひようがかかりすぎるからです。

questions.explanation: なぜなら introduces the reason, and the sentence ends in からです: {費用|ひよう}がかかりすぎる, it costs too much ({費用|ひよう} = cost, expenses). Time, danger and other people's views aren't mentioned.

questions.stem: Listen to your friend. Choose the best reply.

audio.text: ぼく、いなかにすみたいんだけど、どうおもう？

choices: ところで、{何|なに}を{食|た}べる？
いいえ、{住|す}みませんでした。
{確|たし}かに{静|しず}かでいいね。でも、{車|くるま}がないと{不便|ふべん}かも。
それとも{賛成|さんせい}です。
questions.explanation: He asks what you think about him moving to the countryside. The natural reply admits a point and adds a reservation: {確|たし}かに〜。でも〜. ところで changes the subject, the second reply doesn't answer the question, and それとも can't start a statement like that.

questions.stem: Build the sentence.
questions.prompt: I'd like to decide after talking it over with my family.
questions.explanation: {家族|かぞく}と{話|はな}し{合|あ}った{上|うえ}で{決|き}めたいと{思|おも}います. "After doing" is the た form + {上|うえ}で; {話|はな}し{合|あ}う{上|うえ}で would mean "in talking it over".

questions.stem: In the lesson reading "Choosing the countryside", why does the writer tell the story of the friend who moved to a mountain village?
choices: To show that moving to the country is always a mistake.
To admit a drawback, and then argue that you should look into a place carefully before choosing it.
To persuade readers to stay in the city.
To complain about the winter weather in the mountains.
questions.explanation: The story comes after {確|たし}かに (admitting the other side: country life can be hard). The next paragraph answers it with しかし and むしろ: the story shows, rather, how important it is to look into a place in advance ({前|まえ}もってよく{調|しら}べる). The writer is in favour of country life, not against it.

questions.stem: In lesson 29's Text 1 (the station notice about the east exit), what does the notice say about the lift?
choices: It can't be used while the work is going on.
It can be used even during the work.
It is the part of the station being repaired.
It is only at the west exit.
questions.explanation: The note after なお says {構内|こうない}のエレベーターは{工事|こうじ}{中|ちゅう}も{使|つか}えます: the lift inside the station can be used during the work too. The work is on the east exit's stairs ({階段|かいだん}), not the lift. なお often introduces exactly this kind of extra detail, so read it carefully.

questions.stem: In Text 2 (the teacher's email), who has to send the teacher an email?
choices: Students who can't come on Thursday.
Students who have lost their essay sheet.
Students who have torn their essay sheet.
questions.explanation: {木曜日|もくようび}に{来|こ}られない{人|ひと}は、{月曜日|げつようび}までにメールで{知|し}らせてください: only those who can't come on Thursday must email (by Monday). Students who tore or lost the sheet simply get a new one in class ({新|あたら}しいものを{渡|わた}します).

questions.stem: In Text 3 ("Pointing and calling"), why do people make mistakes in work they know well, according to the writer?
choices: They assume everything is fine without looking properly.
They are usually too tired to concentrate.
They don't know the rules of the job well enough.
They are too shy to speak aloud.
questions.explanation: {人|ひと}は{慣|な}れた{仕事|しごと}ほど、よく{見|み}ないで「だいじょうぶだ」と{思|おも}い{込|こ}んでしまう: the more familiar the work, the more people assume it's fine without looking. Tiredness and rules aren't mentioned, and shyness comes up only in the writer's last paragraph, about trying it at home.

questions.stem: In Text 3, what does the writer suggest at the end?
choices: That only railway staff should use the method.
That you should check things with your eyes only.
That you should ask someone else to check for you.
That readers try pointing and calling at home before going out.
questions.explanation: The last paragraph says the method can be used at home too ({家|いえ}でも{使|つか}える) and suggests pointing at the gas and the windows and saying よし before going out (〜てみてはどうだろうか, "why not try…?"). The whole point of the text is that looking alone isn't enough.

questions.stem: In Text 4 ("The reserved seat"), why was the old woman sitting in the writer's seat?
choices: She had booked the same seat by mistake.
She felt ill and needed to sit down.
She had an unreserved ticket and didn't know the difference.
She was keeping the seat for her daughter.
questions.explanation: Her ticket was for an unreserved seat ({自由席|じゆうせき}のきっぷ), and {違|ちが}いを{知|し}らなかったらしい: apparently she didn't know the difference between reserved and unreserved seats. She hadn't booked, wasn't ill, and her daughter lives in another town.

questions.stem: In Text 4, what did the woman give the writer before getting off?
choices: A small paper crane she had folded.
Some of the food she had made.
questions.explanation: {赤|あか}い{紙|かみ}で{折|お}った、{小|ちい}さなつる: a small crane folded from red paper. She had folded many for the baby and gave one to the writer. The food and the baby clothes were in her bags, but she didn't give them away.

questions.stem: Text 4 ends: 「{最初|さいしょ}から{予約|よやく}した{席|せき}に{座|すわ}っていたら、この{景色|けしき}もきっと、ただの{雪|ゆき}の{景色|けしき}だっただろう。」 What does the writer mean?
choices: The writer regrets not sitting down from the start.
The writer will book seats earlier next year.
The snowy view was not very beautiful.
Meeting the woman made the ordinary snowy view feel special.
questions.explanation: If the writer had simply sat in the booked seat, the view would have been "just a snowy view". In other words, giving up the seat and meeting the woman (and the crane in the writer's hand) gave the view a meaning. 〜ていたら、〜だっただろう describes what would have happened otherwise; it isn't a regret.

questions.stem: Look at Text 5 (the price list for the town pool). Mr Nakamura and his nine-year-old daughter go in at 6.30 p.m. on a Saturday. How much do they pay in all?
questions.explanation: Saturday prices: adult 500 yen, primary-school child 150 yen (650 in all). They go in after 6 p.m., so the price is halved ({午後|ごご}{六時|ろくじ}{以降|いこう}…{半分|はんぶん}): 250 + 75 = 325 yen. 650 forgets the evening rule, and 400 and 250 use the wrong prices.

questions.stem: Look at Text 5 again. On a Wednesday at 3 p.m., Ms Ito goes to the pool with her 13-year-old son and her 5-year-old daughter. How much do they pay?
questions.explanation: It's a weekday ({平日|へいじつ}) before 6 p.m., so there's no discount: adult 400 yen + middle-school son 200 yen + daughter under primary-school age free ({小学生|しょうがくせい}{未満|みまん}は{無料|むりょう}) = 600 yen. 700 charges the girl as a primary-school child, and 750 uses the weekend prices.

questions.stem: {駅|えき}の構内では、たばこを{吸|す}わないでください。 How is 構内 read?
questions.explanation: 構内 (inside the station, on the premises) is こうない: 構 is コウ (as in {結構|けっこう}) and 内 is ナイ. かまえ is a kun reading of 構 that isn't used here, and うち is the kun reading of 内.

questions.stem: {約束|やくそく}を破ってはいけない。 How is 破って read?
questions.explanation: {破|やぶ}る (to break a promise, to tear) is やぶる, so the て form is やぶって. ハ is 破's on'yomi, used only in compounds, and やぶれる is the intransitive verb, whose て form would be やぶれて, not やぶれって.

questions.stem: {一晩|ひとばん}で{雪|ゆき}が［つもった］。 Which is the correct way to write つもった?
questions.explanation: つもる (to pile up, of snow) is 積もる: 積 (pile up) with the okurigana もる. 積った leaves out the も, and 責 (responsibility) and 席 (seat) are other kanji read セキ, not つ.

questions.stem: チケットは___でも{買|か}えますが、{事前|じぜん}に{買|か}うと{安|やす}くなります。 Choose the word for the blank.
questions.explanation: {当日|とうじつ} is "on the day (itself)": tickets can be bought on the day, but they're cheaper in advance ({事前|じぜん}に). {以降|いこう} needs a time before it ({八時|はちじ}{以降|いこう}), {先着|せんちゃく} is "first come, first served", and {必着|ひっちゃく} is a deadline for something to arrive.

questions.stem: A sign says 「ご{利用|りよう}の{際|さい}は、{受付|うけつけ}でお{名前|なまえ}を{書|か}いてください。」 What does ご{利用|りよう}の{際|さい}は mean?
questions.explanation: 〜の{際|さい}(は) is the formal "when, at the time of": "when you use (this facility), please write your name at reception." It doesn't mean after (〜た{後|あと}), instead of (〜{代|か}わりに) or because (〜ので).

questions.stem: {年末|ねんまつ}の指定席は、もう{売|う}り{切|き}れだった。 Type the reading of 指定席 in kana.
questions.explanation: 指定席 (reserved seat) is していせき: 指 (シ, point to) + 定 (テイ, fix) + 席 (セキ, seat). Its opposite is {自由席|じゆうせき} (unreserved seat).

questions.stem: Listen to the announcement on the platform. What is it about?

audio.text: おしらせします。ゆきのため、とっきゅうは、やくさんじゅっぷんおくれています。なお、じゆうせきは、いちごうしゃとにごうしゃです。

choices: The express has been cancelled because of the snow.
The reserved seats are sold out.
The express is about 30 minutes late because of snow.
questions.explanation: {雪|ゆき}のため、{特急|とっきゅう}は、{約|やく}{三十分|さんじゅっぷん}{遅|おく}れています: because of the snow, the express is running about thirty minutes late. The part after なお is an extra note: unreserved seats are in cars 1 and 2. Nothing is cancelled, sold out or closed.

questions.stem: Listen. A classmate tells you about next week's class. When and where is it?

audio.text: らいしゅうのクラス、すいようびじゃなくて、もくようびになったんだって。きょうしつは、さんがいのだいにきょうしつ。

choices: Wednesday, classroom 2 on the third floor.
Thursday, classroom 3 on the second floor.
Thursday, classroom 2 on the third floor.
Wednesday, classroom 3 on the second floor.
