questions.explanation: {水曜日|すいようび}じゃなくて、{木曜日|もくようび}になったんだって: not Wednesday but Thursday (〜んだって, "I heard"). The room is {三階|さんがい}の{第二|だいに}{教室|きょうしつ}, classroom 2 on the third floor. Don't mix up the floor (さんがい) and the room number (だいに).

questions.stem: Listen. A stranger on a train asks you something. Choose the best reply.

audio.text: すみません、ここ、すわってもかまいませんか。

choices: いいえ、{構|かま}いました。
{結構|けっこう}{座|すわ}りました。
questions.explanation: The question is a request for permission: {座|すわ}っても{構|かま}いませんか, "do you mind if I sit here?". The natural reply is ええ、どうぞ (yes, go ahead). {構|かま}う is almost always negative, so {構|かま}いました is wrong, and the other two don't answer a request.

questions.stem: Build the sentence from a notice.
questions.prompt: When using it, please write your name at reception.
questions.explanation: ご{利用|りよう}の{際|さい}は、{受付|うけつけ}でお{名前|なまえ}を{書|か}いてください. 〜の{際|さい}は (when…) comes first, as the topic of the instruction; 〜の{際|さい}に is also correct here.

questions.stem: Build the sentence.
questions.prompt: Please point to where we are now on the map.
questions.explanation: {地図|ちず}の{上|うえ}で、{今|いま}いる{場所|ばしょ}を{指|さ}してください. {指|さ}す is "to point at"; {今|いま}いる modifies {場所|ばしょ} (the place where we are now). The phrase {地図|ちず}の{上|うえ}で can also come after the object.

questions.stem: How long is the JLPT N3's language knowledge (grammar) and reading section?
questions.explanation: At N3, grammar and reading share one 70-minute test section. Vocabulary has its own 30 minutes and listening 40 minutes. 55 minutes is the grammar and reading time at N4.

questions.stem: A test taker scores 30 in language knowledge (vocabulary and grammar), 50 in reading and 18 in listening: 98 in all. What is the result?
choices: Fail: listening is under the sectional pass mark of 19.
Fail: the total must be at least 100.
Pass: the high reading score makes up for listening.
questions.explanation: To pass N3 you need both the overall pass mark (95 of 180) and at least 19 in each of the three scoring sections. 98 is over 95, but 18 in listening is under 19, so the result is a fail. No section can make up for another.

questions.stem:
Sentence composition. Which word goes in the ★ position?
{駅|えき}に ＿＿ ＿＿ ★ ＿＿ {降|ふ}り{出|だ}した。
questions.explanation: The sentence is {駅|えき}に{着|つ}いたとたんに{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}り{出|だ}した (the moment I got to the station, it started to rain): {着|つ}いた + とたん + に + {雨|あめ}が. The third blank, ★, is に. Build the whole sentence first, then count to the ★.

questions.stem: {先生|せんせい}が{教|おし}えてくださった___、{合格|ごうかく}できました。 Choose the words for the blank.
questions.explanation: A good result (passing) thanks to someone's help takes おかげで (lesson 6). せいで blames someone for a bad result, くせに complains about a person (lesson 18), and わりに means "considering" (lesson 18); none of them fits thanking the teacher.

questions.stem: {私|わたし}___、この{仕事|しごと}は{何|なに}より{大切|たいせつ}だ。 Choose the words for the blank.
questions.explanation: にとって gives the viewpoint of an evaluation: "for me, this job matters more than anything" (lesson 11). として is a role ("as a teacher"), について is "about", and に{対|たい}して is "towards, against"; with {大切|たいせつ}だ only にとって works.

questions.stem: {弟|おとうと}は{答|こた}えを{知|し}っている___、{教|おし}えてくれない。 Choose the word for the blank (and the speaker is annoyed about it).
questions.explanation: くせに is "even though" with blame: he knows the answer and still won't tell me (lesson 18). ために gives a purpose or reason, ように a goal, and ことに (as in {残念|ざんねん}なことに) comments on a feeling; none of them expresses the complaint.

questions.stem: {練習|れんしゅう}すれ___する___、{上手|じょうず}になる。 Choose the words for the two blanks (The more you practise, the better you get).
questions.explanation: "The more…, the more…" is 〜ば〜ほど (lesson 4): {練習|れんしゅう}すればするほど. The first verb is in the ば form and the second in the dictionary form + ほど. まで, だけ and たら don't make this pattern.

questions.stem:
Read the passage and choose the word for （　）.
{日本語|にほんご}の{勉強|べんきょう}を{始|はじ}めて、{三年|さんねん}になる。{最初|さいしょ}はひらがなも{読|よ}めなかった。（　）、{今|いま}では{新聞|しんぶん}の{記事|きじ}も{少|すこ}し{読|よ}めるようになった。
questions.explanation: Couldn't read hiragana at first, can now read some newspaper articles: the two sentences contrast, so しかし fits. ところで changes the subject, それとも offers a choice in a question, and その{上|うえ} adds a point in the same direction.

questions.stem: {練習|れんしゅう}ではできたのに、___ではうまくいかなかった。 Choose the word for the blank.
questions.explanation: {本番|ほんばん} is "the real thing": I could do it in practice, but not in the actual test. {満点|まんてん} is full marks, {正解|せいかい} the correct answer and {目安|めやす} a rough guide; none of them contrasts with {練習|れんしゅう}.

questions.stem: A test instruction says: 「{次|つぎ}の{問|と}いに{対|たい}する{答|こた}えとして{最|もっと}もよいものを、1・2・3・4から{一|ひと}つ{選|えら}びなさい。」 What are you told to do?
choices: Choose the best answer to each question from 1 to 4.
Write the answer to each question in your own words.
Choose all the correct answers from 1 to 4.
Put the answers 1 to 4 in the right order.
questions.explanation: {最|もっと}もよいものを…{一|ひと}つ{選|えら}びなさい: choose the one best answer. {問|と}い is the written word for a question, and 〜に{対|たい}する{答|こた}え is "the answer to". Nothing asks you to write, choose several or put things in order.

questions.stem: この{書類|しょるい}は、{二階|にかい}の窓口に{出|だ}してください。 How is 窓口 read?
questions.explanation: 窓口 (counter, service window) is まどぐち: {窓|まど} + {口|くち}, voiced to ぐち after another word, as in {出口|でぐち}. Carried words in kanji like this one are typical N3 kanji-reading questions.

questions.stem: {遅|おく}れた理由を{説明|せつめい}してください。 How is 理由 read?
questions.explanation: 理由 (reason) is りゆう, with a long ゆう (由 is ユウ here). りよう is {利用|りよう} (use), and りゅう has a small ゅ that isn't there; listen for the three separate morae り・ゆ・う.

questions.stem: {山|やま}の{上|うえ}から、きれいな［けしき］が{見|み}えた。 Which kanji are used for けしき?
questions.explanation: けしき (view, scenery) is 景色, a special reading taught in lesson 14: the kanji are read ケイ and シキ but the word is けしき. 式 (ceremony), 軽 (light) and 計 (measure) have similar sounds but make other words.

questions.stem: {漢字|かんじ}のテストで100{点|てん}、つまり___を{取|と}った。 Type the word for "full marks", in kana or kanji.
questions.explanation: {満点|まんてん} is "full marks, a perfect score": {満|まん} (full) + {点|てん} (point). Its partner on the JLPT is {合格点|ごうかくてん}, the pass mark.

questions.stem: Listen. When will they meet tomorrow?

audio.text: じゃあ、あしたはくじにえきでね。あ、でも、しけんはくじはんからだから、やっぱりはちじはんにしよう。

choices: At half past eight, at the station.
At half past nine, at the test centre.
At eight, at the test centre.
questions.explanation: The first plan is nine at the station, but the speaker remembers the test starts at half past nine and changes it: やっぱり{八時半|はちじはん}にしよう. In task questions the last decision counts, and やっぱり is the signal.

questions.stem: Listen. What went badly in the test, and why?

audio.text: きのうのしけん、どっかいはよかったんだけど、ちょうかいがぜんぜんだめだったんだ。はやすぎて。

choices: Reading, because the texts were too long.
Vocabulary, because the kanji were difficult.
Listening, because it was too quiet.
Listening, because it was too fast.
questions.explanation: {読解|どっかい}はよかった (reading was fine), but ちょうかいが{全然|ぜんぜん}だめだった (listening was hopeless), and the reason comes last: {速|はや}すぎて, it was too fast. Key-point questions often put the reason at the end.

questions.stem: Listen to your friend. Choose the best reply.

audio.text: しけん、どうだった？

choices: いいえ、どういたしまして。
はい、{試験|しけん}でした。
まあまあかな。ちょうかいが{難|むずか}しかった。
questions.explanation: {試験|しけん}、どうだった？ asks how the test went, so the reply gives an impression: まあまあかな (so-so) and a detail. どういたしまして answers a thank-you, はい、{試験|しけん}でした doesn't say how it went, and {試験|しけん}にしよう is a suggestion.

questions.stem: Build the sentence.
questions.prompt: It's better to have a good rest the day before the test.
questions.explanation: {試験|しけん}の{前日|ぜんじつ}は、ゆっくり{休|やす}んだほうがいい. Advice with ほうがいい takes the た form ({休|やす}んだ), and {前日|ぜんじつ} is "the day before".

questions.stem: Build the sentence.
questions.prompt: I was able to pass thanks to the teacher helping me.
questions.explanation: {先生|せんせい}が{手伝|てつだ}ってくださったおかげで、{合格|ごうかく}できました. 〜てくださる is the respectful 〜てくれる, and おかげで gives the good result; せいで would blame the teacher.

questions.stem:
Read the passage and answer the question.
{外国語|がいこくご}を{学|まな}ぶ{上|うえ}で{最|もっと}も{大切|たいせつ}なのは{何|なん}だろうか。{文法|ぶんぽう}だと{言|い}う{人|ひと}もいれば、{単語|たんご}だと{言|い}う{人|ひと}もいる。{確|たし}かに、どちらも{必要|ひつよう}である。しかし、{私|わたし}は{毎日|まいにち}{少|すこ}しずつでも{続|つづ}けることが{何|なに}より{大切|たいせつ}だと{考|かんが}える。{一度|いちど}にたくさん{勉強|べんきょう}しても、{続|つづ}けなければ、すぐに{忘|わす}れてしまうからである。 What does the writer think matters most?
choices: Continuing every day, even a little.
Studying a lot at one time.
questions.explanation: After {確|たし}かに (admitting that grammar and words are both needed), しかし turns to the writer's view: {毎日|まいにち}{少|すこ}しずつでも{続|つづ}けることが{何|なに}より{大切|たいせつ}だ. The last sentence gives the reason with 〜からである. Studying a lot at once is what the writer warns against.

questions.stem: In "The watch in the drawer", why did the narrator go to her grandfather's shop?
choices: To sort out the inside of the shop before it was closed.
To open the shop again under her own name.
To sell the clocks to a dealer.
To have a watch of her own repaired.
questions.explanation: Part 1: the family decided to close the shop, and she used her summer holiday to sort it out ({店|みせ}の{中|なか}をせいりすることになった). She only thinks about keeping it open at the very end.

questions.stem: Why had all the clocks in the shop stopped?
choices: They were broken and waiting to be repaired.
The narrator had stopped them to sell them.
Nobody had wound them since her grandfather went into hospital.
The electricity had been cut off.
questions.explanation: {祖父|そふ}が{入院|にゅういん}してから、ねじをまく{人|ひと}がだれもいなかったのだ: they are wind-up clocks, and since her grandfather went into hospital no one had wound them. The のだ explains the stopped hands.

questions.stem: What did the paper attached to the box say?
choices: The watch had been repaired and was to be kept until Mr Morita collected it.
Mr Morita had paid in advance.
The watch should be thrown away after thirty years.
questions.explanation: {直|なお}し{終|お}わり (repair finished) and {取|と}りに{来|こ}られるまで、あずかること (keep it until he comes for it). The narrator wonders exactly why he never came, and why her grandfather didn't throw it away (すてずに{待|ま}ち{続|つづ}けた).

questions.stem: Why couldn't the narrator find Mr Morita near the harbour?
choices: The notebook gave the wrong district.
He had died many years earlier.
The harbour had been closed down.
New flats stood there, and he had moved far away about thirty years before.
questions.explanation: At the address there were new blocks of flats ({新|あたら}しいマンションが{建|た}っていて), and the baker explains that he had suddenly moved far away about thirty years earlier ({急|きゅう}に{遠|とお}くの{町|まち}へ{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}していった). He is still alive, in a care home.

questions.stem: What did the woman at the bakery reveal about Mr Morita and the narrator's grandfather?
choices: They were old friends who sometimes talked until late at night.
They had quarrelled about the price of the repair.
Mr Morita had worked in the shop as a young man.
questions.explanation: おじいさんとは{古|ふる}い{友|とも}だちで、{夜|よる}おそくまで{話|はな}し{込|こ}んでいることもあった: old friends who sometimes got deep into conversation until late (〜{込|こ}む, lesson 27). The narrator then thinks that this may be why the watch couldn't be thrown away.

questions.stem: On the night before the visit, why didn't the narrator wind the watch?
choices: She didn't know how to wind it.
She felt that Mr Morita should be the one to set it going again.
She was afraid of breaking it.
The daughter had asked her not to.
questions.explanation: この{時計|とけい}をもう{一度|いちど}{動|うご}かすのは、{私|わたし}ではなく{森田|もりた}さんであるべきだという{気|き}がしたからだ: she felt it ought to be him (〜であるべきだ, the written べきだ). She does know how to wind clocks: she winds the big wall clock in part 6.

questions.stem: Why had Mr Morita never collected the watch?
choices: He had forgotten all about it.
He thought the shop had closed.
He had to move suddenly for work just after his wife died, and going back would have brought back memories of her.
questions.explanation: The daughter's letter says he had to move suddenly for work ({仕事|しごと}の{都合|つごう}で{急|きゅう}に{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}す), and he himself says he felt that going would make him think of his wife. It stayed on his mind ({心|こころ}に{残|のこ}っていた), so he hadn't forgotten.

questions.stem: What promise does Mr Morita say he can at last keep ({約束|やくそく}が{果|は}たせる)?
choices: That he would always keep the watch going.
That he would visit the shop every year.
That he would give the watch to his daughter.
That he would pay the narrator's grandfather back.
questions.explanation: {妻|つま}と{約束|やくそく}したんだよ。この{時計|とけい}は、ずっと{動|うご}かしておくって: he promised his wife that he would always keep this watch going. {果|は}たせる is the potential of {果|は}たす (to fulfil).

questions.stem: 「{引|ひ}き{出|だ}しを{開|あ}けたところ、{小|ちい}さな{箱|はこ}が{出|で}てきた。」 What does 〜たところ mean here?
choices: "I was just about to open the drawer, when…"
"When I opened the drawer, (I found that) a small box came out."
"I had just opened the drawer for the first time."
"The place where I opened the drawer…"
questions.explanation: た form + ところ (lesson 3) means "when I did…, I found (an unexpected result)": she opened the drawer, and a box turned up. "About to" would be 〜るところ, and "had just" 〜たところだ at the end of a sentence; it isn't a place here.

questions.stem: 「このまま{帰|かえ}るわけにはいかないと{思|おも}ったのである。」 What does the narrator mean?
choices: She had no way of getting back to Tokyo.
She didn't want to go back to her job.
She felt she couldn't in good conscience just go home like this.
Her company had told her not to come back yet.
questions.explanation: 〜わけにはいかない (lesson 7) is "can't, for moral or social reasons": she could go, but leaving with the watch unreturned felt wrong. It isn't a practical impossibility, and it was she who asked her company for more time ({会社|かいしゃ}には{少|すこ}し{無理|むり}を{言|い}った).

questions.stem: Listen to a line from the story. What does the speaker mean?

audio.text: あのとき、とりにいけなかったことが、ずっとこころにのこっていたんだ。

choices: Not being able to go and collect it back then had stayed on his mind all along.
He had always remembered where he left it.
He went to collect it, but the shop was closed.
He had never once thought about it.
questions.explanation: あのとき{取|と}りに{行|い}けなかったことが、ずっと{心|こころ}に{残|のこ}っていたんだ: the fact that he couldn't go and fetch it then "remained in his heart" all this time. {心|こころ}に{残|のこ}る is to stay on your mind.

questions.stem: Listen to the grandfather's favourite saying. What does it mean?

audio.text: とけいは、たいせつにすれば、ひとよりながくいきるんだよ。

choices: Clocks are more important than people.
People who look after clocks live longer.
Old clocks are worth a lot of money.
If you look after a clock, it will last longer than a person.
questions.explanation: {時計|とけい}は、{大切|たいせつ}にすれば、{人|ひと}より{長|なが}く{生|い}きるんだよ: if you take care of a clock (〜ば), it "lives" longer than a person (〜より). It's the clock that lasts, not the person who looks after it.

questions.stem: On vertical げんこうようし, where does the title usually go?
choices: On the first line, starting a few squares down.
On the last line, at the bottom.
On the second line, ending one square before the bottom.
In the margin above the first line.
questions.explanation: The {題名|だいめい} goes on the first line, a few squares down (two or three are common). The second line, ending one square before the bottom, is for your name.

questions.stem: How do you start a new paragraph on げんこうようし?
choices: Leave an empty line, then start at the top.
Start on a new line and leave the first square blank.
Carry on in the same line after a blank square.
Start on a new line at the very top square.
questions.explanation: Each {段落|だんらく} starts on a new line ({改行|かいぎょう}) with the first square left blank. Empty lines between paragraphs aren't used, and the blank square is what shows the reader a new paragraph has begun.

questions.stem: Your sentence ends exactly at the bottom of a line, so the 。 would fall in the top square of the next line. What do you do?
choices: Write 。 in the top square of the next line.
Write it in the last square of the line, together with the last character (or just below it).
Start the whole sentence again on a new line.
questions.explanation: 。 and 、 (and a closing 」) never start a line. The usual rule is to squeeze the mark into the last square with the last character, or write it just below the last square. Leaving it out or rewriting the sentence isn't needed.

questions.stem: On げんこうようし, how many squares does the word きっぷ take?
questions.explanation: Every kana takes a square, including the small っ: き・っ・ぷ is three squares. (In vertical writing the small っ sits in the top right of its square.) The same goes for small ゃ, ゅ, ょ and the long-vowel mark ー.

questions.stem: Which sentence does NOT belong in an essay written in the である style?
choices: {紙|かみ}の{本|ほん}は{集中|しゅうちゅう}しやすい。
{電子|でんし}の{本|ほん}にも{利点|りてん}はある。
でも、{紙|かみ}の{本|ほん}のほうがいいと{思|おも}います。
{目的|もくてき}に{合|あ}わせて{選|えら}ぶべきである。
questions.explanation: でも is spoken, and と{思|おも}います is the polite style: both break a である essay. Write しかし、{紙|かみ}の{本|ほん}のほうがよいと{考|かんが}える. The other three are in the plain or である style.

questions.stem: In an essay, which word should start a sentence that contrasts with the one before?
questions.explanation: しかし is the written "however". でも, だけど and けど are spoken, and けど can't start a sentence at all in careful writing.

questions.stem: In the model essay, what is the writer's view?
choices: Children should be encouraged to read paper books.
Nobody should read books on a smartphone.
Adults should stop reading on the way to work.
questions.explanation: The opening says {子供|こども}には{紙|かみ}の{本|ほん}をすすめたいと{考|かんが}える, and the ending repeats it in new words. The writer grants that e-books are convenient, especially for adults commuting, so the view isn't against e-books in general.

questions.stem: In the model essay, what is the second reason for paper books?
choices: They can be shared with friends.
Their content stays in your head more easily.
questions.explanation: {第二|だいに}に、{紙|かみ}の{本|ほん}は{内容|ないよう}が{頭|あたま}に{残|のこ}りやすい, because hands and eyes remember where things were on the page (〜からである). Lightness is an advantage of e-books, and price and sharing aren't mentioned.

questions.stem: In the model essay, what does the sentence starting with もちろん do?
choices: It adds a third reason for paper books.
It sums up the whole essay.
It admits a point for the other side.
questions.explanation: もちろん、{電子|でんし}の{本|ほん}にも{利点|りてん}はある gives the other side its due (like {確|たし}かに, lesson 28) before the conclusion. The summing-up comes in the last paragraph with つまり.

questions.stem: Listen to the teacher. What are the instructions for the essay?

audio.text: さくぶんは、よんひゃくじいないで、であるちょうでかいてください。

choices: Up to 400 characters, in the である style.
At least 400 characters, in the polite style.
Up to 400 characters, in the です/ます style.
questions.explanation: {作文|さくぶん}は、{四百字|よんひゃくじ}{以内|いない}で、である{調|ちょう}で{書|か}いてください: within (not more than) 400 characters, in the である style. 〜{以内|いない} is "within", and である{調|ちょう} is the である style (lesson 26).

questions.stem: Listen to the teacher. What does she tell the students to do?

audio.text: だんらくのはじめは、ひとますあけてください。

choices: Leave an empty line between paragraphs.
Leave one square blank at the start of each paragraph.
Write the title one square from the top.
Leave a square between family name and given name.
questions.explanation: {段落|だんらく}のはじめは、{一|ひと}マス{空|あ}けてください: leave one square (マス) empty at the start of a paragraph. She doesn't mention empty lines, the title or names.

questions.stem: まず___をして、{間違|まちが}いを{直|なお}してから、げんこうようしに{書|か}き{写|うつ}した。 Choose the word for the blank.
questions.explanation: You write a {下書|したが}き (draft) first, correct the mistakes, then copy it out neatly. {改行|かいぎょう} is a new line, {題名|だいめい} the title and {結|むす}び the ending; none of them is something you "do first and then correct".

glossary.definition: A short word in hiragana that follows a word or ends a sentence and shows its role: は (topic), が (subject), を (object), に, で, と, も, か, ね, よ… Particles do the work of English word order and prepositions.

Characters taken from Chinese that carry a meaning as well as a sound. Japanese writes most nouns and the stems of verbs and adjectives in kanji, and the grammar in kana: {若者|わかもの}, {若|わか}い. This course writes a word in kanji when all its kanji are on the N5, N4 and N3 lists (649 in all).
Small kana printed above kanji to show how they are read: {途中|とちゅう}. This course puts furigana on every kanji except one that a question is testing, and you can switch them off.
A kanji reading that comes from the Chinese pronunciation it was borrowed with, used mostly in words of two or more kanji: 初 is ショ in {初心者|しょしんしゃ}. Kanji tables write on'yomi in katakana.
A kanji reading that is a native Japanese word, often used when the kanji stands alone or with okurigana: 初 read はじ in {初|はじ}めて, 夢 read ゆめ. Kanji tables write kun'yomi in hiragana.
The kana written after a kanji to finish a word, usually the part that changes in conjugation: the い of {若|わか}い, the やす of {冷|ひ}やす. Kanji tables show them in brackets: ひ(やす).

The unit of timing in Japanese, one beat: each kana is a mora, small ゃゅょ belong to the kana before them, and っ, ん and the second half of a long vowel count on their own. {途中|とちゅう} has three (と・ちゅ・う). Pitch accent and haiku are counted in morae.

The pattern of high and low pitch on the morae of a word. In standard (Tokyo) Japanese, a word is marked by the mora after which the pitch falls, or 0 if it never falls: {命|いのち:1}, {若者|わかもの:0}. Some words differ only in accent: {雨|あめ:1} (rain) and [あめ:0] (candy).
The rise and fall of the voice over a whole phrase, which shows the speaker's attitude: そう？ with a rise asks, そう。 with a fall states. It sits on top of each word's pitch accent.
An adjective that ends in い and changes its own ending: {細|こま}かい, {細|こま}かくない, {細|こま}かかった, {細|こま}かくて, {細|こま}かければ. いい uses よ- in its other forms (よくない).
An adjective that takes な before a noun ({平和|へいわ}な{町|まち}) and behaves like a noun with だ / です: {平和|へいわ}だ, {平和|へいわ}じゃない, {平和|へいわ}で, {平和|へいわ}なら. A few end in い (きれい) but are still な-adjectives.
The form that joins a verb, adjective or noun to what follows: {寝|ね}て, {飲|の}んで, {細|こま}かくて, {静|しず}かで. It links actions, gives reasons and builds many patterns: 〜ている, 〜てしまう, 〜てはじめて, 〜てからでないと.
The polite form of a verb ending in ます, ません, ました or ませんでした: {渡|わた}します, {冷|さ}めません. The part before ます is the ます stem.
A verb's ます form without ます: {食|た}べ, {焼|や}き, し. Many patterns are built on it: 〜たい, 〜ながら, 〜かける ({食|た}べかけ), 〜たて ({焼|や}きたて), and compounds such as {飛|と}び{乗|の}る.
The plain non-past form of a verb, as it appears in a dictionary: {飛|と}ぶ, {冷|ひ}やす, する, {来|く}る. Many patterns follow it: 〜たびに, 〜{一方|いっぽう}だ, 〜ことにする, 〜つもり.
The plain negative of a verb: {忘|わす}れない, {降|ふ}らない, しない, {来|こ}ない. It builds 〜ないうちに (before it happens), 〜ないで and 〜なければ.
The plain past of a verb, made with the same sound changes as the て form: {飛|と}んだ, {寝|ね}た, した. It builds 〜たとたん, 〜たところ, 〜たきり, 〜たことにする and 〜たら.

The forms without です / ます: dictionary form, ない form, た form, なかった form, and だ for nouns and な-adjectives. Used in casual speech, in the だ style of diaries and essays, and before grammar words such as うちに, つもり, こと and と{思|おも}う.
Speech and writing that end in です or ます, used with people you don't know well, people above you, and in most public situations. The safe default for a learner.
Verbs whose last sound moves through the vowel rows: {渡|わた}す → {渡|わた}さない, {渡|わた}します, {渡|わた}せる, {渡|わた}そう. Some verbs ending in -iる or -eる are group 1 too: {帰|かえ}る, {入|はい}る, {減|へ}る, {若返|わかがえ}る.
Verbs ending in -iる or -eる that drop る before an ending: {冷|さ}める → {冷|さ}めない, {冷|さ}めます, {冷|さ}めて; {生|い}きる → {生|い}きられる.
The two irregular verbs する and {来|く}る, and every する compound ({成長|せいちょう}する, {期待|きたい}する). Potential: できる, {来|こ}られる; volitional: しよう, {来|こ}よう.
The verb form meaning "can": group 1 changes the last u-sound to e + る ({渡|わた}せる), group 2 adds られる ({生|い}きられる), する becomes できる, {来|く}る becomes {来|こ}られる. It conjugates as a group 2 verb.
The plain "let's" form, which also states an intention: {行|い}こう, {寝|ね}よう, しよう, {来|こ}よう. With とする it means "try to, be about to" ({寝|ね}ようとした), and with としない "won't".
An "if" form. Japanese has four (と, ば, たら, なら; N4). The ば form is also the first half of 〜ば〜ほど, "the more…, the more…": {読|よ}めば{読|よ}むほど.

The verb form for having something done to you: group 1 a-sound + れる ({呼|よ}ばれる), group 2 られる ({見|み}られる), される, {来|こ}られる. It can also show that something happened to your cost: {雨|あめ}に{降|ふ}られた (I got caught in the rain).
The verb form for making or letting someone do something: group 1 a-sound + せる ({飲|の}ませる), group 2 させる ({食|た}べさせる), させる, {来|こ}させる.
A verb that acts on an object marked with を: {冷|ひ}やす (to chill something), {増|ふ}やす, {渡|わた}す. Many come in pairs with an intransitive partner: {冷|ひ}やす / {冷|ひ}える.
A verb with no object: something happens by itself. {冷|ひ}える (to get cold), {増|ふ}える, {焼|や}ける, {冷|さ}める. Its partner is transitive: {冷|ひ}える / {冷|ひ}やす.
A verb that follows a て form and adds a meaning instead of its own: 〜ている, 〜ておく, 〜てしまう, 〜てみる, 〜てくる, 〜ていく, 〜てあげる / くれる / もらう. Auxiliary verbs are written in kana.
A word that turns a clause into a noun so it can take a particle: こと and の. {歩|ある}くことにした (decided to walk), {食|た}べたことにする (treat it as eaten).
A noun that has lost most of its own meaning and works as grammar: こと, もの, ところ, とき, ため, はず, わけ, つもり, うち, ほう, ふり. Formal nouns are written in kana.
A clause that says when something happens: 〜とき, 〜うちに, 〜{間|あいだ}に, 〜{前|まえ}に, 〜たびに, 〜たとたん. Its verb is usually in the plain form even in a polite sentence: {若|わか}いうちに{旅行|りょこう}したいです.
The short responses a listener keeps giving to show they are following: はい, ええ, うん, へえ, そうなんですか, なるほど. They mean "I'm listening", not "I agree", and are especially frequent on the phone.
A word that fills a pause while you think: えーと (searching), あのう (a polite opening), まあ (softening), なんか (a casual "like"), その (looking for a word).

A written-style negative form of the verb: the ない form with ない replaced by ず ({食|た}べず, {行|い}かず; する → せず, {来|く}る → {来|こ}ず). 〜ずに means the same as 〜ないで ("without doing"), 〜ず、 links clauses in writing, and it survives in set phrases such as {思|おも}わず and {相変|あいか}わらず. It isn't a conjugation drill form in this course.

Denying "all" or "always" rather than the whole statement: "not all, not always, not necessarily". In Japanese it's made with 〜わけではない, 〜とは{限|かぎ}らない, {必|かなら}ずしも〜ない, or は after a word like {全部|ぜんぶ}: {全部|ぜんぶ}{分|わ}かるわけではない (I don't understand all of it) as against {全然|ぜんぜん}{分|わ}からない (I don't understand any of it).

The part of a sentence, usually its ending, that shows the speaker's attitude to what is said: how sure they are (〜でしょう, 〜はずだ, 〜かもしれない), and whether they think it should or must happen (〜べきだ, 〜ものだ, 〜ことだ, 〜なければならない, 〜たほうがいい). The same fact can carry different modality: {行|い}く, {行|い}くべきだ, {行|い}くはずだ.

A particle and a verb form (usually a て form) that have fused into one unit and work like a single particle: として (as), にとって (for, from the viewpoint of), に{対|たい}して (towards), について (about), に{関|かん}して (concerning), によって (depending on, by), に{比|くら}べて (compared with), を{通|とお}して (through). Most are formal or written. Some are written in kana by custom (として, にとって, について, によって); the ones whose verb keeps its meaning keep its kanji (に{対|たい}して, に{関|かん}して). Before a noun each has a noun-modifying form.

The form a compound particle takes before a noun, because a て form can't modify a noun directly. Most add の to the て form (として → としての, について → についての: {社会人|しゃかいじん}としての{責任|せきにん}); the ones built on a verb that keeps its meaning usually take its dictionary form (に{対|たい}して → に{対|たい}する, に{関|かん}して → に{関|かん}する, によって → による: {人|ひと}による{違|ちが}い).

A particle whose job is to put weight on a word rather than to show its role in the sentence. さえ (even: {水|みず}さえ{飲|の}めなかった; as long as: {練習|れんしゅう}さえすれば) and こそ (this very one: {今度|こんど}こそ) are the N3 ones; しか (only, with a negative) and も (even, too) are close relatives. They usually replace が and を and can follow other particles (にさえ, にこそ).

A piece that can't stand on its own and is added to the end of a word to make a new word. Japanese has many: 〜っぽい ({子供|こども}っぽい, childish), 〜{気味|ぎみ} (かぜ{気味|ぎみ}, a touch of a cold), 〜がち ({忘|わす}れがち, tends to forget), 〜だらけ ({間違|まちが}いだらけ, full of mistakes), 〜{的|てき} ({個人的|こじんてき}な, personal), 〜{向|む}け ({子供|こども}{向|む}け, made for children), and N4's 〜さ and 〜{方|かた}.

Drawing a conclusion from clues you notice yourself: the light is on, so someone must be in. Japanese marks inference with ようだ / みたいだ (it seems), らしい when the clue is something heard, and, when you're sure, に{違|ちが}いない (it must be). Compare hearsay, which only passes on what someone told you.

Passing on information you got from someone else without claiming it as your own knowledge: "I hear that…, apparently…". Japanese uses plain form + そうだ ({明日|あした}は{雨|あめ}だそうだ), らしい, casual 〜って and 〜んだって, and in writing 〜ということだ and 〜とのことだ.

Granting a point and then saying the result holds anyway: "although…, even if…, even so…". Japanese has many concessive patterns, each with its own feeling: のに (surprise, regret), くせに (blame), 〜ながら(も) (formal "although"), 〜ても and たとえ〜ても (even if), 〜たって (casual), それにしても (even so).

A situation you suppose for the sake of argument, without saying it's true: "supposing that…, if it's true that…". Japanese uses 〜としたら, 〜とすれば and 〜とすると after the plain form (nouns and な-adjectives take だ): その{話|はなし}が{本当|ほんとう}だとしたら (if that story is true). For real conditions, たら and ば are used instead.
A guess made without full evidence. Japanese softens it with もしかしたら / もしかすると…かもしれない (perhaps, it may be), だろう (probably), and 〜のではないか (I suspect that…); はず and に{違|ちが}いない are much surer.

The general name for the Japanese that shows respect. It is usually divided into polite language (です, ます, ございます), honorific language, which raises the person who acts (いらっしゃる, お{待|ま}ちになる, お{待|ま}ちです), and humble language, which lowers yourself or your side (まいる, お{送|おく}りいたします, 〜させていただく). Who gets keigo depends on status and on whether the person is inside or outside your group.
The kind of keigo that is polite to the listener without raising or lowering anyone: です and ます, and at the top of the scale ございます (for ある) and でございます (for です, used about things).

The kind of keigo that raises the person who does the action: a customer, a teacher, a boss, someone outside your company. Special verbs (いらっしゃる, おっしゃる, めしあがる, ごらんになる, なさる), お + ます stem + になる, the short お + ます stem + です (お{待|ま}ちです), でいらっしゃる for people, and the light honorific 〜られる. Never used about yourself or, to outsiders, about your own side.

The kind of keigo that lowers you, or someone on your side, when your action involves a person you respect: special verbs (まいる, {申|もう}す, いたす, いただく, うかがう, {存|ぞん}じる, うけたまわる), お + ます stem + する / いたす, and 〜させていただく. まいる, おる, {申|もう}す and いたす are also used just to be courteous to the listener, as in announcements: {電車|でんしゃ}がまいります, 〜ております.

お or ご put before a word only to make it sound refined, not to raise anyone: お{茶|ちゃ}, ご{飯|はん}, お{手洗|てあら}い. Unlike the respectful お/ご of お{宅|たく} (your home) or ご{家族|かぞく} (your family), it can be used for your own things. Usually お with native words and ご with Sino-Japanese words, with exceptions such as お{電話|でんわ}.

Passing on what someone else said or wrote without quoting the exact words, and without vouching for it yourself: 〜そうだ, 〜ということだ, 〜とのことです, 〜んだって and, for requests, 〜ように{言|い}う. Politeness markers such as ください drop out, and the speaker's own sentence sets the politeness.

Someone's words repeated as they were said, usually in 「」 and followed by と and a verb of saying: 「{待|ま}ってください」と{言|い}われた. In casual speech, って replaces と. Compare reported speech, which gives only the gist.

A shortened form of casual speech that squeezes sounds together: 〜てる (〜ている), 〜とく (〜ておく), 〜ちゃう (〜てしまう), 〜なきゃ (〜なければ), 〜じゃん (〜じゃないか), 〜って (〜と, 〜という). Used with friends and family, not in writing or polite speech.

A small particle at the end of a sentence that adds the speaker's attitude rather than meaning: よ (telling), ね (sharing, checking), よね, な, さ, ぞ, ぜ, わ, かな, かしら. In casual speech they set the tone, and some suggest the speaker's gender or age.

A regional variety of Japanese ({方言|ほうげん}), such as Kansai-ben, with its own words, grammar and pitch accent. Most people also speak {共通語|きょうつうご}, the Japanese everyone understands, and switch to it with strangers.

A way of speaking that marks a type of character in fiction rather than a real group of speakers: わし and 〜じゃ for an old man, 〜わよ for a refined woman, 〜でござる for a samurai. Common in manga, anime and translations; recognize it, but don't use it in earnest.

The style of reports, essays, textbooks and editorials: plain forms, with である where speech has だ after nouns and な-adjectives (である, ではない, であった, であろう, であり). It isn't mixed with です / ます in one text, and it uses written words such as しかし, また and および. The plain だ style of diaries and news articles is a lighter written style.

The ます stem used to join two clauses in writing, where speech uses the て form: {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}り、{風|かぜ}が{吹|ふ}いた. Adjectives join with 〜く、 and nouns with 〜であり、; 〜ている becomes 〜ており、, and the negative join is the ず form: 〜ず、.

Numbers written with kanji ({一|いち}, {二|に}, {三|さん}, {十|じゅう}, {百|ひゃく}, {千|せん}, {万|まん}), used in vertical writing and in fixed words such as {一人|ひとり} and {第一|だいいち}. In vertical text they are often written digit by digit with 〇: {二〇二六年|にせんにじゅうろくねん}. Horizontal text mostly uses Arabic numerals.

A word at the start of a sentence that links it to the one before and shows how: contrast (しかし, ところが), addition (その{上|うえ}, しかも, {更|さら}に), reason and result (なぜなら, そのため, したがって), summing up (つまり, {要|よう}するに), changing the subject (ところで, さて). On the JLPT, "text grammar" questions often ask for one.

A verb made of the ます stem of one verb and a second verb: {書|か}き{直|なお}す, {取|と}り{出|だ}す. It conjugates like the second verb. Some second verbs form productive patterns (〜{出|だ}す "suddenly", 〜{込|こ}む "into", 〜{切|き}る "completely", 〜{直|なお}す "again", 〜{合|あ}う "each other"); other compounds have a meaning of their own and are learned as words ({思|おも}い{込|こ}む, {見直|みなお}す).

A JLPT reading task: a timetable, price list or notice, and a person with a situation. You find what that person needs by matching their conditions (day, time, age, number of people) against the rules, including the small print.

A JLPT grammar task: a sentence with four blanks, one marked ★, and four words to put in order; you choose the word that goes in the ★ position. This course's "build the sentence" questions train the same skill.
A JLPT grammar task: a passage with several blanks, where you choose the conjunction, grammar form or word that fits the flow of the text.

The Japanese-Language Proficiency Test, run by the Japan Foundation and Japan Educational Exchanges and Services, at five levels from N5 to N1. N3 has three scoring sections (vocabulary and grammar, reading, listening), each 0–60; a pass needs 95 of 180 and at least 19 in every section. All questions are multiple choice.

references.title: Casual speech and reporting (contractions, endings, って)
references.body:
Casual Japanese from N4 and N3 in one place (mainly lesson 25), with the casual ways of
reporting and quoting from lessons 21–23. Everything here is for friends and family.

## Contractions

| Full form | Casual | Example |
|---|---|---|
| 〜ている | 〜てる | {何|なに}{見|み}てるの？ |
| 〜ていく | 〜てく | かさ{持|も}ってく？ |
| 〜ておく / 〜でおく | 〜とく / 〜どく | {買|か}っとく, {読|よ}んどく |
| 〜ておいて | 〜といて | {聞|き}いといて |
| 〜てしまう / 〜でしまう | 〜ちゃう / 〜じゃう | {忘|わす}れちゃった, {飲|の}んじゃった |
| 〜ては / 〜では | 〜ちゃ / 〜じゃ | さわっちゃだめ |
| 〜なければ | 〜なきゃ | {帰|かえ}らなきゃ |
| 〜なくては | 〜なくちゃ | {急|いそ}がなくちゃ |
| 〜ないと (いけない) | 〜ないと | もう{寝|ね}ないと |
| 〜ければ / 〜れば | 〜けりゃ / 〜りゃ | {行|い}きゃいい |
| 〜のだ / 〜のです | 〜んだ / 〜んです | {行|い}きたいんだ |
| 〜じゃないか | 〜じゃん | いいじゃん |
| 〜でしょう | 〜でしょ | {無理|むり}でしょ |
| 〜ところ | 〜とこ | {今|いま}{行|い}くとこ |
| 〜ても / 〜でも | 〜たって / 〜だって | {今|いま}{行|い}ったって{遅|おそ}い |
| それは / これは | そりゃ / こりゃ | そりゃそうだ |
| そうか | そっか | そっか、{分|わ}かった |
| {本当|ほんとう} | ほんと | ほんと？ |

Ra-less potentials ({見|み}れる, {来|こ}れる, {寝|ね}れる for {見|み}られる, {来|こ}られる, {寝|ね}られる)
are very common in speech but still widely seen as incorrect: recognize them, use the full form.

## Quoting and reporting, casually

| Full | Casual | Example |
|---|---|---|
| 〜と{言|い}った / 〜と{言|い}っていた | 〜って({言|い}ってた) | {来|く}るって{言|い}ってた |
| 〜そうだ (hearsay) | 〜って, 〜んだって | やめるんだって |
| 〜という + noun | 〜っていう + noun | {山田|やまだ}っていう{人|ひと} |
| 〜というのは / 〜とは | 〜って | ゆかたって{何|なに}？ |
| ということは | ってことは | {雨|あめ}ってことは、{中止|ちゅうし}？ |
| 〜というか | 〜っていうか, ていうか | っていうか、もう{帰|かえ}らない？ |
| 〜と{言|い}っても | 〜って{言|い}っても | {近|ちか}いって{言|い}っても、{歩|ある}くと{二十分|にじゅっぷん} |
| 〜てくださいと{言|い}われた | 〜てって{言|い}われた | {来|き}てって{言|い}われた |

## Sentence endings

| Ending | What it does | Example |
|---|---|---|
| 〜もん / 〜もの | because (self-justifying, a little childish) | だって、{知|し}らなかったんだもん |
| 〜ってば | I said…! (impatient) | {分|わ}かったってば |
| 〜って (rising) | what did they say? / did you say…? | {何|なん}だって？ |
| 〜の (rising) | soft question, asking for an explanation | どこ{行|い}くの？ |
| 〜の (falling) | soft explanation | {頭|あたま}が{痛|いた}いの |
| 〜なよ, 〜な | casual "do it" (from 〜なさい) | {早|はや}く{寝|ね}なよ |

## Sentence-final particles

| Particle | Function | Feel |
|---|---|---|
| よ | tells something new | neutral |
| ね | checks, shares | neutral |
| よね | "right?" | neutral |
| な, なあ | to yourself; a man's softer ね | casual |
| さ | emphasis; filler (あのさ, それでさ) | casual, young |
| ぞ | strong, a warning, to yourself | masculine |
| ぜ | rough "come on" | masculine, mostly fiction |
| わ (falling) | soft emphasis | western Japan, and many speakers elsewhere |
| わ (rising), わよ, わね | soft emphasis | feminine, a little old-fashioned in Tokyo |
| かな / かしら | I wonder | かしら feminine, older |

## Leaving things out

- Particles は, が, を, へ drop when the meaning is clear: これ、おいしい; {学校|がっこう}{行|い}く？
  Particles with real meaning stay: で, と, から, まで, に (time, person).
- だ drops in casual questions ({休|やす}み？) and often in statements (きれい！). A bare だ at the
  end can sound blunt.
- Questions rise instead of taking か: {行|い}く？ Plain か at the end can sound rough.

## Casual or polite?

| Polite | Casual |
|---|---|
| {行|い}きますか。 | {行|い}く？ |
| {行|い}きません。 | {行|い}かない。 |
| そうですね。 | そうだね / そうね。 |
| {雨|あめ}ではありません。 | {雨|あめ}じゃない。 |
| {寒|さむ}いでしょう。 | {寒|さむ}いでしょ / {寒|さむ}いだろう。 |
| {待|ま}ってください。 | {待|ま}って。 |
| {来|き}てくれませんか。 | {来|き}てくれない？ |
| {分|わ}かりました。 | {分|わ}かった / りょうかい。 |
| すみません。 | ごめん / ごめんね。 |

references.title: Compound verbs
references.body:
A compound verb is the ます stem of one verb + a second verb (lesson 27). It conjugates like the
second verb: {書|か}き{直|なお}す → {書|か}き{直|なお}します, {書|か}き{直|なお}して, {書|か}き{直|なお}さない.
The patterns below can be built from many verbs; the compounds marked "word" have a meaning of
their own and are learned as vocabulary.

## Patterns

| Second verb | Adds | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| 〜{出|だ}す (1) | a sudden start (not for plans: use 〜{始|はじ}める) | {泣|な}き{出|だ}す, {笑|わら}い{出|だ}す, {降|ふ}り{出|だ}す, {走|はし}り{出|だ}す |
| 〜{出|だ}す (2) | out (of somewhere) | {取|と}り{出|だ}す (word), {飛|と}び{出|だ}す (word), {持|も}ち{出|だ}す, {運|はこ}び{出|だ}す |
| 〜{始|はじ}める | begin (neutral, planned) | {書|か}き{始|はじ}める, {通|かよ}い{始|はじ}める |
| 〜{込|こ}む (1) | into | {飛|と}び{込|こ}む, {運|はこ}び{込|こ}む, {持|も}ち{込|こ}む, {吸|す}い{込|こ}む, {書|か}き{込|こ}む (word) |
| 〜{込|こ}む (2) | deeply, for a long time | {話|はな}し{込|こ}む, {冷|ひ}え{込|こ}む |
| 〜{切|き}る | completely, to the end | {使|つか}い{切|き}る, {読|よ}み{切|き}る, {疲|つか}れ{切|き}る |
| 〜{切|き}れない | can't finish, too much | {食|た}べ{切|き}れない, {数|かぞ}え{切|き}れない |
| 〜{直|なお}す | again, properly | {書|か}き{直|なお}す, {考|かんが}え{直|なお}す, やり{直|なお}す, {見直|みなお}す (word) |
| 〜{合|あ}う | each other | {助|たす}け{合|あ}う, {話|はな}し{合|あ}う (word), {知|し}り{合|あ}い (noun) |
| 〜{上|あ}げる / 〜{上|あ}がる | up | {持|も}ち{上|あ}げる (word), {立|た}ち{上|あ}がる |
| 〜{上|あ}げる / 〜{上|あ}がる | finished, complete | {書|か}き{上|あ}げる, できあがる |
| 〜{続|つづ}ける | keep on | {降|ふ}り{続|つづ}ける, {待|ま}ち{続|つづ}ける |
| 〜{終|お}わる | finish | {読|よ}み{終|お}わる, {書|か}き{終|お}わる |
| 〜すぎる | too much | {食|た}べすぎる, {働|はたら}きすぎる |
| 〜かける | start to; half-done (lesson 3) | {読|よ}みかけの{本|ほん}, {言|い}いかけてやめる |

## Words of their own

| Compound | Meaning | Lesson |
|---|---|---|
| {思|おも}い{込|こ}む | to be convinced (usually wrongly) | 27 |
| {落|お}ち{込|こ}む | to feel down | 10 |
| {見直|みなお}す | to look over again; to think better of someone | 27 |
| {話|はな}し{合|あ}う | to discuss, talk things through | 27 |
| {取|と}り{出|だ}す | to take out | 27 |
| {取|と}り{付|つ}ける | to install, to fit | 27 |
| {取|と}り{除|のぞ}く | to remove | 27 |
| {取|と}り{消|け}す | to cancel | 24 |
| とりかえる | to replace, to exchange | 24 |
| {組|く}み{立|た}てる | to assemble | 27 |
| {持|も}ち{上|あ}げる | to lift | 27 |
| {飛|と}び{出|だ}す | to rush out | 27 |
| {書|か}き{込|こ}む | to write in, to fill in | 27 |
| {思|おも}い{出|だ}す | to remember | N4 |
| {似合|にあ}う | to suit | N4 |
| {引|ひ}っ{越|こ}す | to move house | N4 |

## Stem + っぱなし (left that way)

| Example | Meaning |
|---|---|
| {電気|でんき}をつけっぱなしにする | to leave the light on |
| {窓|まど}を{開|あ}けっぱなしで{出|で}かける | to go out leaving the window open |
| {水|みず}を{出|だ}しっぱなしにする | to leave the water running |
| {一日中|いちにちじゅう}{立|た}ちっぱなしだった | I was on my feet all day |

っぱなし is a noun: 〜っぱなしにする, 〜っぱなしで, 〜っぱなしだ. It is spoken and usually a
complaint.

references.title: Degree and emphasis (ほど, くらい, さえ, こそ, あまり)
references.body:
Lesson 15's words for degree and emphasis, with the related patterns from other lessons.

## Degree: ほど and くらい

| Pattern | Meaning | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| verb / adjective + ほど | so … that, to the point of | {泣|な}きたいほど{痛|いた}い (so painful I want to cry) | a little more formal than くらい |
| verb / adjective + くらい・ぐらい | so … that | {信|しん}じられないくらい{強|つよ}い (unbelievably strong) | everyday |
| noun + ほど | as much as | {宿題|しゅくだい}が{山|やま}ほどある (a mountain of homework) | |
| noun + くらい | at least, only (a minimum) | {一回|いっかい}くらい{勝|か}ちたい (at least once) | only くらい: ×{一回|いっかい}ほど in this sense |
| そのくらい / それくらい | that little, nothing much | そのくらい{気|き}にしないで | |
| number + ほど / くらい | about | {三十分|さんじゅっぷん}ほど / くらい | both |
| A は B ほど〜ない | A isn't as … as B | {兄|あに}は{私|わたし}ほど{速|はや}くない | N4 |
| A ほど〜はない | nothing is as … as A | {旅|たび}ほど{楽|たの}しいものはない | lesson 14 |
| 〜ば〜ほど | the more …, the more … | {練習|れんしゅう}すればするほど{上手|じょうず}になる | lesson 4 |
| 〜くらいなら | rather than (something you'd hate) | {負|ま}けるくらいなら{出|で}ない | to recognize |

ほど and くらい are grammar words and stay in kana; 〜{位|い} (lesson 15's kanji) is a rank.

## Emphatic particles: さえ and こそ

| Pattern | Meaning | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| noun + さえ | even (an extreme case) | {水|みず}さえ{飲|の}めなかった | replaces が and を; にさえ, とさえ, からさえ |
| noun + でさえ | even (a subject) | {先生|せんせい}でさえ{解|と}けない | stronger |
| noun + さえ + ば form | as long as | {天気|てんき}さえよければ | only this condition is needed |
| noun part of a する verb + さえすれば | as long as you … | {練習|れんしゅう}さえすれば | |
| ます stem + さえすれば | as long as you … | {投|な}げさえすれば | |
| て form + さえいれば | as long as you keep … | {笑|わら}ってさえいれば | |
| noun + こそ | this very one, for sure | {今度|こんど}こそ{勝|か}つ | replaces は, が, を; usually positive |
| 〜からこそ | precisely because | {好|す}きだからこそ{続|つづ}けられる | |
| 〜ときこそ | it's when … that | {苦|くる}しいときこそ{笑|わら}おう | |
| こちらこそ | likewise | 「よろしく。」「こちらこそ。」 | N5 set phrase |

## Too much: あまり

| Pattern | Meaning | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| あまりにも (あまりに) + adjective / verb | far too, so extremely | あまりにも{強|つよ}くて{勝|か}てなかった | |
| noun + のあまり | so (much feeling) that | きんちょうのあまり{何|なに}も{言|い}えなかった | often an unintended result |
| verb + あまり | wanting / thinking so much that | {勝|か}ちたいと{思|おも}うあまり、ルールを{忘|わす}れた | |
| あまりの + noun + に | because of the extreme … | あまりの{寒|さむ}さに{声|こえ}も{出|で}なかった | to recognize |
| あまり〜ない | not very | あまり{寒|さむ}くない | N5: a different use |

## The minimum: せめて and 少なくとも

| Word | Use | Example |
|---|---|---|
| せめて | at least (a wish, hope or request) | せめて{一回|いっかい}は{勝|か}ちたい |
| {少|すく}なくとも | at least (a fact, a number) | {少|すく}なくとも{三百人|さんびゃくにん}{来|き}た |

references.title: Formal phrases (compound particles)
references.body:
The compound particles of module 3 (lessons 11–14), with their noun-modifying forms and the
course's spelling. "Kana" means the phrase is written in kana by custom; "kanji" means its verb
keeps its meaning and keeps its kanji.

## Roles, viewpoints and targets (lesson 11)

| Phrase | Meaning | Example | Before a noun | Spelling |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| として | as, in the role of | {医師|いし}として{働|はたら}く (work as a doctor) | としての: {社会人|しゃかいじん}としての{責任|せきにん} | kana |
| としては | speaking as, X's position | {会社|かいしゃ}としては{困|こま}る (as a company, it's a problem for us) | | kana |
| にとって | for, from X's point of view (+ a judgement) | {私|わたし}にとって{大切|たいせつ}だ (it matters to me) | にとっての: {私|わたし}にとっての{幸|しあわ}せ | kana |
| に{対|たい}して | towards (the target of an attitude, a reply) | {客|きゃく}に{対|たい}してていねいだ (polite to customers) | に{対|たい}する (に{対|たい}しての): {仕事|しごと}に{対|たい}する{考|かんが}え{方|かた} | kanji |
| のに{対|たい}して | whereas | {兄|あに}は{会社員|かいしゃいん}なのに{対|たい}して、{弟|おとうと}は{職人|しょくにん}だ | | kanji |

## Topics, centres and settings (lesson 12)

| Phrase | Meaning | Example | Before a noun | Spelling |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| について | about | {歴史|れきし}について{調|しら}べる (research history) | についての: {日本|にほん}についての{本|ほん} | kana |
| に{関|かん}して | concerning (formal) | この{件|けん}に{関|かん}して (concerning this matter) | に{関|かん}する: {試験|しけん}に{関|かん}する{質問|しつもん} | kanji |
| を{中心|ちゅうしん}に(して) | centred on, mainly | {若者|わかもの}を{中心|ちゅうしん}に{人気|にんき}がある | を{中心|ちゅうしん}とした / とする: {東京|とうきょう}を{中心|ちゅうしん}とした{地方|ちほう} | kanji |
| をはじめ(として) | starting with, including (+ a group) | {学長|がくちょう}をはじめ、{多|おお}くの{先生|せんせい}が{来|き}た | をはじめとする: {京都|きょうと}をはじめとする{町|まち} | kana |
| において | in, at (formal: events, fields, periods) | {大|だい}ホールにおいて{行|おこな}う | における: この{分野|ぶんや}における{研究|けんきゅう} | kana |

## Depending on, instead of, contrary to (lesson 13)

| Phrase | Meaning | Example | Before a noun | Spelling |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| によって | depending on (+ {違|ちが}う, {変|か}わる) | {国|くに}によって{違|ちが}う | による: {国|くに}による{違|ちが}い | kana |
| によっては | in some (cases) | {店|みせ}によっては{使|つか}えない (some shops don't take it) | | kana |
| によって | by means of (formal) | {話|はな}し{合|あ}いによって{解決|かいけつ}する | による | kana |
| によって | by (the maker, in a passive) | ベルによって{発明|はつめい}された | による: ベルによる{発明|はつめい} | kana |
| によって | because of (news) | {台風|たいふう}によって{止|と}まった | による: {台風|たいふう}による{遅|おく}れ | kana |
| によると / によれば | according to (+ hearsay) | {天気予報|てんきよほう}によると{雨|あめ}だそうだ | | kana |
| の{代|か}わりに / {代|か}わりに | instead of; in exchange for | {電話|でんわ}の{代|か}わりにメールを{送|おく}る | | kanji |
| に{代|か}わって / に{代|か}わり | on behalf of, in place of | {社長|しゃちょう}に{代|か}わってあいさつする | に{代|か}わる: {人|ひと}に{代|か}わるロボット | kanji |
| に{反|はん}して | contrary to (expectations, rules) | {予想|よそう}に{反|はん}して{勝|か}った | に{反|はん}する: {予想|よそう}に{反|はん}する{結果|けっか} | kanji |
| と{違|ちが}って | unlike | {東京|とうきょう}と{違|ちが}って{静|しず}かだ | と{違|ちが}う: {日本|にほん}と{違|ちが}う{習慣|しゅうかん} | kanji |

## Comparing places and times (lesson 14)

| Phrase | Meaning | Example | Before a noun | Spelling |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| に{比|くら}べて / と{比|くら}べて | compared with (+ a comparison) | {去年|きょねん}に{比|くら}べて{増|ふ}えた | | kanji |
| から〜にかけて | from … through to (loose span) | {関東|かんとう}から{東北|とうほく}にかけて{雪|ゆき}が{降|ふ}る | から〜にかけての: {春|はる}から{夏|なつ}にかけての{旅|たび} | kana (かける) |
| を{通|とお}して / を{通|つう}じて | throughout (a period); through (a means, a person) | {一年|いちねん}を{通|とお}して{温|あたた}かい・{友人|ゆうじん}を{通|とお}して{知|し}る | を{通|とお}しての / を{通|つう}じての | kanji |
| で{最|もっと}も | the most (written) | {日本|にほん}で{最|もっと}も{高|たか}い{山|やま} | | kanji |

## Pairs that are easy to mix up

| | Use | Example |
|---|---|---|
| として / にとって | role / point of view of a judgement | {親|おや}として{心配|しんぱい}だ / {親|おや}にとって{大切|たいせつ}だ |
| にとって / に{対|たい}して | judgement from X's side / action or attitude aimed at X | {部下|ぶか}にとってありがたい / {部下|ぶか}に{対|たい}してきびしい |
| にとって / のために | judgement / for X's benefit (an action) | {母|はは}にとって{大事|だいじ}だ / {母|はは}のために{作|つく}る |
| について / に{関|かん}して | everyday / formal, notices and headings | {映画|えいが}について{話|はな}す / {留学|りゅうがく}に{関|かん}するお{知|し}らせ |
| によって / によると | depending on (+ difference) / according to (+ hearsay) | {天気|てんき}によって / {天気予報|てんきよほう}によると |
| から〜まで / から〜にかけて | exact ends / loose span | {九時|くじ}から{五時|ごじ}まで / {三月|さんがつ}から{四月|しがつ}にかけて |
| によって / を{通|とお}して | the means or cause / something you go through | {話|はな}し{合|あ}いによって / {友人|ゆうじん}を{通|とお}して |

## Rule of thumb for the noun-modifying form

Most compound particles add の to the て form: としての, にとっての, についての, を{通|とお}しての.
The ones whose verb keeps its own meaning usually take that verb's dictionary form, which sounds
more formal: に{対|たい}する, に{関|かん}する, による, に{反|はん}する, に{代|か}わる. For に{対|たい}して and
に{関|かん}して the の form is also heard; ×によっての is rare.

references.title: Impressions, guesses and emphasis
references.body:
Module 4 of Japanese N3 (lessons 16–20). Each row gives the meaning, how the pattern joins, an
example and a limit or two. "Plain" means the plain form (dictionary, ない, た, なかった forms).

## Impression suffixes (lesson 16)

| Pattern | Joins to | Meaning | Example | Watch out |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 〜っぽい | noun, colour, い-adj stem, ます stem | -ish; too much of; does easily | {子供|こども}っぽい, {黒|くろ}っぽい, {忘|わす}れっぽい | casual; often critical; conjugates as an い-adj |
| N + らしい | noun | typical of, as X should be | {春|はる}らしい{天気|てんき}, {子供|こども}らしい | usually praise; also "apparently" (N4) |
| N + みたいな | noun | like a… (casual) | {夢|ゆめ}みたいな{話|はなし} | before a noun; みたいに before a verb |
| 〜{気味|ぎみ} | noun, ます stem | a touch of, slightly (now) | かぜ{気味|ぎみ}, {疲|つか}れ{気味|ぎみ} | unwelcome states; read ぎみ |
| 〜がち | ます stem, some nouns | tends to, is apt to | {忘|わす}れがち, {病気|びょうき}がち | unwanted things only; usually with a situation |
| 〜だらけ | noun | covered in, full of | {間違|まちが}いだらけ, ごみだらけ | negative and messy; not for nice things |
| 〜{的|てき} | noun (mostly two kanji) | -ic, -al; 〜{的|てき}に: in terms of | {個人的|こじんてき}な, {性格的|せいかくてき}に | makes a な-adjective |
| 〜{向|む}き | noun | suited to (by nature) | {初心者|しょしんしゃ}{向|む}きの{山|やま} | also "facing": {南向|みなみむ}き |
| 〜{向|む}け | noun | made for, aimed at | {子供|こども}{向|む}けの{番組|ばんぐみ} | on purpose, for a target group |

## Impressions and certainty (lessons 17 and 19)

Roughly from surest to least sure; speakers don't all draw the lines in the same place.

| Pattern | Joins | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| 〜に{違|ちが}いない | plain; noun and な-adj without だ | must be (own conviction) | {彼|かれ}が{犯人|はんにん}に{違|ちが}いない |
| 〜はずだ (N4) | plain; な-adj な, noun の | should be (facts, plans) | {式|しき}は{二時|にじ}からのはずだ |
| 〜のではないか | plain; な-adj and noun + な | I suspect that (soft) | {犯人|はんにん}は{近所|きんじょ}の{人|ひと}なのではないか |
| 〜ようだ / みたいだ (N4) | plain; な-adj な / noun の (みたい: direct) | it seems (from clues) | だれかいるようだ |
| 〜ように{見|み}える | as ようだ | looks as if (an impression) | {怒|おこ}っているように{見|み}える |
| 〜ような{気|き}がする | as ようだ | I've a vague feeling that | {前|まえ}に{会|あ}ったような{気|き}がする |
| 〜とみえる | plain | it appears, judging by (written) | よほど{疲|つか}れていたとみえる |
| もしかしたら〜かもしれない | plain; noun and な-adj direct | perhaps, it may be | もしかしたら{雨|あめ}かもしれない |

## Denying a possibility (lessons 7, 19)

| Pattern | Based on | Example | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| 〜はずがない (N4) | facts, logic | かぎをかけたから、{開|あ}いているはずがない | calm deduction |
| 〜わけがない (lesson 7) | emphasis | そんな{人|ひと}と{結婚|けっこん}するわけがない | emotional; fits your own will |
| まさか〜 | disbelief | まさか{彼|かれ}が{犯人|はんにん}だとは{思|おも}わなかった | also まさか！ alone; combines with the other two |

## Supposing (lesson 19)

| Pattern | Use | Example |
|---|---|---|
| 〜としたら | supposing, if it's true (everyday) | {本当|ほんとう}だとしたら、{大変|たいへん}だ |
| 〜とすれば | supposing (logical, written) | {十時|じゅうじ}だとすれば、アリバイがある |
| 〜とすると / とすると、 | supposing; "in that case" at the start | とすると、{窓|まど}は{開|あ}いていたはずだ |
| いったい + question word | what on earth | いったい{何|なに}があったんだろう |

Nouns and な-adjectives take だ before としたら / とすれば / とすると. Real conditions use たら or ば.

## Against expectations (lesson 18)

| Pattern | Joins | Meaning | Limits |
|---|---|---|---|
| 〜のに (N4) | plain; な-adj and noun + な | even though (surprise, regret) | can be about yourself |
| 〜くせに | plain; な-adj な, noun の | even though (blame, contempt) | about someone else; not to superiors |
| 〜にしては | noun, plain verb | for a…, considering it's… | not usually after adjectives |
| 〜{割|わり}に(は) | noun の, plain verb / い-adj, な-adj な | considering, for (the price, age) | also in kana わりに |
| 〜ながら(も) | ます stem of state verbs, い-adj, な-adj stem, noun | although (formal) | with actions it means "while" |
| 〜ば〜のに | ば form | if… (but it isn't so) | wishes, regret, blame |
| たとえ〜ても | て form + も | even supposing | casual: 〜たって, 〜だって |
| どんなに〜ても | て form + も | no matter how | |

## Adding and emphasising (lesson 20)

| Pattern | Meaning | Example | Limits |
|---|---|---|---|
| 〜だけでなく / ばかりでなく…も | not only…but also | {子供|こども}だけでなく{大人|おとな}も | な-adj な |
| 〜ばかりか…(まで / さえ) | not only, but even | {歌|うた}うばかりか{曲|きょく}まで{作|つく}る | no requests or plans after it |
| A はもちろん、B も | B too, not to mention A | {子供|こども}はもちろん、{大人|おとな}も | |
| 〜{上|うえ}(に) | on top of that | {安|やす}い{上|うえ}においしい | same direction only |
| 〜も〜ば〜も | both… and | {歌|うた}もうまければダンスもうまい | casual: 〜も〜し〜も |
| どんなに / {何度|なんど}〜ことか | how…! | どんなにうれしかったことか | emotional, a bit literary |
| 〜なんて | belittling; surprise; quoting | {彼|かれ}が{来|く}るなんて！ | |
| 〜なんか | casual など: modest, dismissive | {私|わたし}なんか | rude about someone else's things |

references.title: The N3 kanji
references.body:
The 370 kanji this course adds, in the order of the lessons that teach them. With the 102 kanji
of Japanese N5 and the 177 of Japanese N4 (each listed in that course's kanji reference, "The
course kanji" and "The N4 kanji") they make 649. Any lesson in this course may use a kanji from
any of the three lists, and a word is written with kanji when all its kanji are on them.

On'yomi (readings that came from Chinese) are in katakana; kun'yomi (native Japanese readings) are
in hiragana, with the okurigana in brackets: あぶ(ない) means the kanji is read あぶ in {危|あぶ}ない.
Only the readings you meet at N3 are given, and many kanji have others. A reading in brackets
after another, like ガイ after カイ, is a sound change in compounds ({三階|さんがい}). Stroke counts
are those of the tracing pads. Lesson 30 adds no kanji.

| Kanji | Meaning | On'yomi | Kun'yomi | Strokes | Words | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| {部屋|へや} | へや | room | 11 |

| {景色|けしき} | けしき | view, scenery | 14 |
| {白髪|しらが} | しらが | white hair | 16 |

Reminders from earlier courses: {今日|きょう}, {今年|ことし}, {今朝|けさ}, {明日|あした}, {上手|じょうず},
{下手|へた}, {大人|おとな}, {一人|ひとり}, {二人|ふたり}, {時計|とけい}.

## Kanji with more than one reading at N3

The word decides the reading. These are favourite JLPT kanji-reading questions.

| Kanji | Readings | Examples |

| 無 | ム, ブ | {無理|むり}, {無料|むりょう} / {無事|ぶじ} |
| 等 | トウ, ひと(しい), など | {平等|びょうどう}, 〜{等|とう} / {等|ひと}しい / {等|など} |

| 階 | カイ (ガイ) | {二階|にかい} / {三階|さんがい} |
| 決 | ケツ (ケッ) | {決断|けつだん} / {決心|けっしん}, {決|けっ}して |

references.title: Keigo (honorific, humble and polite language)
references.body:
The keigo of N4 (lessons 27–28) and N3 (lesson 24) in one place. The key question is always: who
does the action? Raise the other person's actions (honorific), lower your own (humble), and be
polite to the listener whatever happens (polite).

## The kinds

| Kind | Who it's about | What it does | Examples |
|---|---|---|---|
| Polite (ていねいご) | anyone | polite to the listener | です, ます, ございます, でございます |
| Honorific (そんけいご) | the other person or their side | raises the person who acts | いらっしゃる, お{待|ま}ちになる, お{待|ま}ちです, {来|こ}られる |
| Humble (けんじょうご) | you or your side | lowers you when your action involves them | まいる, お{持|も}ちする, お{送|おく}りいたします, {説明|せつめい}させていただく |
| Courteous (humble verbs used for politeness) | your side, or things | courteous to the listener; nobody needs raising | {電車|でんしゃ}がまいります, {父|ちち}は{銀行|ぎんこう}で{働|はたら}いております |
| Beautifying お/ご | words | makes a word refined; fine for your own things | お{茶|ちゃ}, ご{飯|はん}, お{手洗|てあら}い |

## Special verbs

| Ordinary | Honorific (others) | Humble (yourself) |
|---|---|---|
| いる | いらっしゃる | おる |
| {行|い}く | いらっしゃる, お{越|こ}しになる | まいる; うかがう (to visit someone) |
| {来|く}る | いらっしゃる, お{越|こ}しになる, お{見|み}えになる | まいる |
| {言|い}う | おっしゃる | {申|もう}す, {申|もう}し{上|あ}げる |
| する | なさる | いたす |
| {食|た}べる, {飲|の}む | めしあがる | いただく |
| {見|み}る | ごらんになる | はいけんする |
| {聞|き}く (ask, hear) | お{聞|き}きになる | うかがう, うけたまわる |
| {知|し}っている | ご{存|ぞん}じだ | {存|ぞん}じている, {存|ぞん}じております |
| {思|おも}う | お{思|おも}いになる | {存|ぞん}じる |
| {会|あ}う | お{会|あ}いになる | お{目|め}にかかる |
| {受|う}ける (accept an order) | お{受|う}けになる | うけたまわる |
| {分|わ}かる (accept a request) | | しょうちする, かしこまる |
| くれる | くださる | — |
| あげる | — | {差|さ}し{上|あ}げる |
| もらう | — | いただく |
| {寝|ね}る | お{休|やす}みになる | — |
| です | でいらっしゃる (people) | でございます (polite) |
| ある | — | ございます (polite) |

The ます forms of いらっしゃる, おっしゃる, なさる and くださる end in います: いらっしゃいます,
おっしゃいます, なさいます, くださいます.

## Patterns

| Pattern | Kind | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| お + stem + になる | honorific | お{帰|かえ}りになる | (they) go home |
| ご + noun + になる | honorific | ご{利用|りよう}になる | (they) use |
| お + stem + です | honorific (short) | お{待|ま}ちです, お{持|も}ちですか | (they) are waiting; do you have…? |
| ご + noun + です | honorific (short) | ご{予約|よやく}ですか | do you have a booking? |
| 〜でいらっしゃる | honorific です (people) | {田中様|たなかさま}でいらっしゃいますか | are you Mr Tanaka? |
| 〜られる (passive form) | light honorific | {社長|しゃちょう}が{戻|もど}られました | the president is back |
| お + stem + ください | honorific request | お{待|ま}ちください | please wait |
| お + stem + いただけますか | very polite request | ご{確認|かくにん}いただけますか | could you check? |
| 〜ていただけないでしょうか | very polite request | {変|か}えていただけないでしょうか | could you possibly change it? |
| お + stem + {願|ねが}います | notices, announcements | お{待|ま}ち{願|ねが}います | please wait (firm) |
| お + stem + する | humble | お{持|も}ちします | I'll carry it |
| お + stem + いたす | humbler | お{送|おく}りいたします | I'll send it |
| ご + noun + する / いたす | humble | ご{説明|せつめい}いたします | let me explain |
| 〜させていただく | humble (with your permission) | {説明|せつめい}させていただきます | allow me to explain |
| 〜ております | courteous 〜ている | {受|う}け{付|つ}けております | we accept |
| 〜てまいります | courteous 〜ていく / てくる | {寒|さむ}くなってまいりました | it's getting colder |

Rules of thumb:

- Verbs with a special form don't take the patterns: ×お{見|み}になる (→ ごらんになる), ×お{行|い}きに
  なる (→ いらっしゃる), ×お{見|み}する (→ はいけんする).
- Don't double up: ×おっしゃられる, ×お{帰|かえ}りになられる. One honorific is enough.
- 〜させていただく on group 1 verbs takes only せ: {行|い}かせていただく, not ×{行|い}かさせていただく.
- お goes with native words, ご with Sino-Japanese words; exceptions include お{電話|でんわ},
  お{時間|じかん}, お{食事|しょくじ}.

## Polite words

| Ordinary | Polite | | Ordinary | Polite |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| {人|ひと} | {方|かた} | | {今|いま} | ただいま |
| だれ | どなた | | {今日|きょう} | {本日|ほんじつ} |
| どこ | どちら | | {明日|あした} | {明日|みょうにち}, {明日|あす} |
| こっち, ここ | こちら | | {昨日|きのう} | {昨日|さくじつ} |
| どう | いかが | | {去年|きょねん} | {昨年|さくねん} |
| いい | よろしい | | {次|つぎ} (time) | {次回|じかい} |
| ちょっと | {少々|しょうしょう} | | 〜ぐらい | {約|やく}〜 |
| 〜さん | 〜{様|さま} | | {皆|みな}さん | {皆様|みなさま} |
| {私|わたし} | {私|わたくし} | | {家|いえ} (theirs) | お{宅|たく} |
| {会社|かいしゃ} (yours / ours) | おんしゃ / へいしゃ, {当社|とうしゃ} | | {店|みせ} (ours) | {当店|とうてん} |
| {客|きゃく} | お{客様|きゃくさま} | | すみません | {恐|おそ}れ{入|い}ります |

## Inside and outside (uchi and soto)

| Talking to an outsider about… | Use | Example |
|---|---|---|
| the outsider, their company, their family | honorific, 〜{様|さま} | {西田様|にしださま}はいらっしゃいますか。 |
| your own colleague or boss | humble, surname only | {西田|にしだ}はただいま{外出中|がいしゅつちゅう}でございます。 |
| your own family | humble, {父|ちち} / {母|はは} | {母|はは}がよろしくと{申|もう}しておりました。 |
| yourself | humble | わたくしがうけたまわります。 |

Inside your own company, the same boss gets honorific forms: {西田|にしだ}{部長|ぶちょう}はいらっしゃいますか。

## Business set phrases

| Phrase | When |
|---|---|
| お{電話|でんわ}ありがとうございます。〜でございます。 | answering the phone at work |
| いつもお{世話|せわ}になっております。 | opening a call or email to another company |
| {恐|おそ}れ{入|い}りますが、… | before a request or question |
| お{手数|てすう}ですが、… / お{手数|てすう}をおかけしますが、… | asking someone to go to some trouble |
| {少々|しょうしょう}お{待|ま}ちください。 | asking someone to wait |
| お{待|ま}たせいたしました。 | after keeping someone waiting |
| しょうちいたしました。 / かしこまりました。 | accepting a request: "certainly" |
| うけたまわりました。 | "noted" (an order, a booking, a message) |
| もうしわけございません。 | a formal apology |
| {折|お}り{返|かえ}しお{電話|でんわ}いたします。 | "we'll call you back" |
| ご{用件|ようけん}をうかがってもよろしいでしょうか。 | asking what a call is about |
| 〜の{際|さい}は | "when (you)…" in notices and emails |
| 〜ていただければ{幸|さいわ}いです。 | "I'd be grateful if you could…" in emails |
| {今後|こんご}ともよろしくお{願|ねが}いいたします。 | closing a business email |
| {失礼|しつれい}いたします。 | entering, leaving, ending a call |

## A business email frame

1. {件名|けんめい} (subject): short and specific: {打|う}ち{合|あ}わせ{日時|にちじ}のご{確認|かくにん}.
2. The company, the department and the person, with {様|さま}: みどり{商事|しょうじ} えいぎょう{部|ぶ} {山本様|やまもとさま}.
3. Greeting and your name: いつもお{世話|せわ}になっております。さくら{電機|でんき}の{西田|にしだ}でございます。
4. Thanks for last time, if there was one: {先日|せんじつ}はありがとうございました。
5. The business, introduced with さて: さて、{次回|じかい}の{打|う}ち{合|あ}わせについて…
6. What you'd like them to do, softly: 〜いただけますでしょうか, 〜いただければ{幸|さいわ}いです.
7. Closing: どうぞよろしくお{願|ねが}いいたします。
8. Your signature: company, department, name.

## Keigo verbs in the drills

Your conjugation drills include the keigo verbs that the app can conjugate, but only in forms
people really use. They leave out double or odd forms: no potential, volitional, passive or
causative for {存|ぞん}じる, まいる, {申|もう}す and いたす; no volitional, passive or
causative for {申|もう}し{上|あ}げる, うけたまわる, うかがう and しょうちする. いらっしゃる, おっしゃる, なさる and くださる
aren't drilled.

references.title: Reasons, conclusions and judgements
references.body:
Module 2's patterns (lessons 6–10): causes, conclusions with わけ, "no need" and "not
necessarily", should and ought, and the ず form. "N" is a noun, "V" a verb.

## Causes (lesson 6)

| Pattern | Joins to | Feeling | Style | Can a request or plan follow? | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 〜から | plain or polite form | none | everyday | yes | {雨|あめ}だから、{行|い}かない |
| 〜ので | plain form (な-adj. / N + な) | none | softer, polite | yes, polite ones | {雨|あめ}なので、{家|いえ}にいてください |
| 〜て | て form | none | casual link | no | {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}って、{困|こま}った |
| 〜ため(に) | N の, な-adj. な, plain form | none | formal, written, announcements | only polite requests in notices | {大雪|おおゆき}のため、{休校|きゅうこう}です |
| 〜おかげで | N の, な-adj. な, plain form | good (grateful); ironic for bad | all | no | {先生|せんせい}のおかげで{合格|ごうかく}した |
| 〜せいで | N の, な-adj. な, plain form | bad (blame) | all | no | {雨|あめ}のせいで{中止|ちゅうし}になった |
| 〜せいか | as せいで | "maybe because" | all | no | {寒|さむ}さのせいか、{体調|たいちょう}が{悪|わる}い |
| 〜ことから | plain form; な-adj. な / である; N である | reasoning from a fact; how a name arose | explanations, writing | no | {石|いし}が{白|しろ}いことから、この{名前|なまえ}がついた |
| 〜{結果|けっか} | V-た, N の | outcome of an action or process | all, a little formal | no | {調|しら}べた{結果|けっか}、{原因|げんいん}が{分|わ}かった |
| 〜によって | N | neutral cause | written | no | {台風|たいふう}によって{木|き}が{倒|たお}れた (lesson 13) |

Purpose ため and cause ため: purpose takes the dictionary form of an action someone chooses
({合格|ごうかく}するために{勉強|べんきょう}する); cause takes past forms, states and things nobody
chooses ({勉強|べんきょう}しなかったために{落|お}ちた).

## わけ (lesson 7)

わけ joins like a noun: plain form, な-adjective + な, noun + な or という.

| Pattern | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| 〜わけだ | so that's why (explaining a fact); which means (a conclusion) | それで{高|たか}いわけだ |
| 〜というわけだ | so that's how it is (summing up) | それで{遅|おく}れたというわけです |
| 〜わけではない / わけでもない | it's not that…; with {全部|ぜんぶ}, いつも, みんな: partial negation | {全部|ぜんぶ}{分|わ}かるわけではない |
| 〜わけがない (casual わけない) | there's no way that… | そんなことができるわけがない |
| V-dict. + わけにはいかない | can't (for social or moral reasons) | {休|やす}むわけにはいかない |
| V-ない + わけにはいかない | have to (can't not) | {行|い}かないわけにはいかない |
| どういうわけか | for some reason | どういうわけか、{今月|こんげつ}はお{金|かね}が{余|あま}った |

### わけ and はず

| | わけ | はず (N4) |
|---|---|---|
| Positive | わけだ: so that's why / which means (you know the fact or work it out) | はずだ: it should be so (an expectation, not yet confirmed); also "no wonder" ({寒|さむ}いはずだ) |
| Negative | わけがない: no way (emotional, spoken; works for your own refusal: {二度|にど}と{行|い}くわけがない) | はずがない: can't be (reasoned from what you know) |
| Overlap | {彼|かれ}が{忘|わす}れるわけがない ≈ {彼|かれ}が{忘|わす}れるはずがない | |

## No need, not necessarily (lesson 8)

| Pattern | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| V-dict. + ことはない | there's no need to (reassuring) | {心配|しんぱい}することはない |
| V + {必要|ひつよう}はない | not required (formal, notices) | {写真|しゃしん}を{用意|ようい}する{必要|ひつよう}はありません |
| 〜なくてもいい (N4) | you don't have to | {出|だ}さなくてもいいです |
| 〜ないことはない / ないこともない | it's possible, I suppose (hesitant yes) | {行|い}けないことはない |
| 〜とは{限|かぎ}らない | not necessarily | {高|たか}いものがいいとは{限|かぎ}らない |
| {必|かなら}ずしも〜ない | not necessarily (needs a negative) | {必|かなら}ずしも{正|ただ}しいわけではない |
| {別|べつ}に〜ない (N4) | not particularly | {別|べつ}に{問題|もんだい}はない |
| 〜て{済|す}む | it only took… | {電話|でんわ}で{済|す}んだ |
| 〜ないで{済|す}む / 〜ずに{済|す}む | didn't have to after all | {待|ま}たないで{済|す}んだ |
| A ことは A が / けど | I do A, but… | {行|い}くことは{行|い}くけど… |

Don't confuse V-dict. + ことはない (no need) with V-た + ことはない (have never: N5).

## Should and the way things are (lesson 9)

| Pattern | Voice | Notes | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| V-dict. + べきだ | my judgement: it's right | する → するべき / すべき; negative べきではない (not ×〜ないべき); past べきだった; strong, avoid to superiors | ルールは{守|まも}るべきだ |
| 〜ものだ | that's how things are; what one is expected to do | general truths and social norms; ものではない: one shouldn't; casual もんだ | {夜|よる}は{静|しず}かにするものだ |
| V-た + ものだ | used to (nostalgic) | repeated past actions, not one event | よくここで{遊|あそ}んだものだ |
| V-dict. / V-ない + ことだ | the thing to do is… (advice) | from seniors, in advice columns | {毎日|まいにち}{話|はな}すことだ |
| 〜たほうがいい (N4) | friendly advice | to friends and colleagues | {早|はや}く{寝|ね}たほうがいい |
| 〜なければならない (N4) | a requirement | rules, laws, duties | きっぷを{買|か}わなければならない |
| 〜ことになっている | it's the rule | rules set by others | {八時|はちじ}までに{出|だ}すことになっている |
| 〜ことにしている | my own rule | a personal habit | {電話|でんわ}に{出|で}ないことにしている |
| {決|けっ}して〜ない | never | promises, warnings, writing | {決|けっ}して{忘|わす}れない |

## The ず form and "no choice" (lesson 10)

| Dictionary form | ない form | ず form |
|---|---|---|
| {食|た}べる | {食|た}べない | {食|た}べず |
| {行|い}く | {行|い}かない | {行|い}かず |
| {言|い}う | {言|い}わない | {言|い}わず |
| する | しない | せず |
| {来|く}る | {来|こ}ない | {来|こ}ず |

| Use | 〜ずに / 〜ず | 〜ないで | 〜なくて |
|---|---|---|---|
| without doing | ✓ (a bit formal) | ✓ | ✗ |
| instead of | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ |
| cause | ✓ in writing | rarely | ✓ (everyday) |
| request (〜ください) | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |

| Pattern | Joins to | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| 〜しかない | V-dict. | no choice but to | {歩|ある}いて{帰|かえ}るしかない |
| 〜てしょうがない / てしかたがない | て form (feelings, sensations) | unbearably (your own feelings) | {眠|ねむ}くてしょうがない |
| 〜ずにはいられない | ず form | can't help doing | {笑|わら}わずにはいられない |
| 〜ようがない | ます stem | there's no way to | {直|なお}しようがない |
| 〜てもしかたがない | て form | it's no use | {今|いま}さら{心配|しんぱい}してもしかたがない |
| 〜ている{場合|ばあい}じゃない | ている form | this is no time for | {寝|ね}ている{場合|ばあい}じゃない |

Set phrases with ず: {思|おも}わず (involuntarily), {相変|あいか}わらず (as ever), とりあえず (for now),
{必|かなら}ず (without fail).

references.title: Time and change (module 1)
references.body:
Module 1's patterns for timing and change, with their forms and the limits that trip learners
up. "Dict." is the dictionary form; N is a noun.

## While and during (lesson 1)

| Pattern | Meaning | Form | Example | Limits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 〜うちに | while (a state) lasts: do it now | い-adj. / な-adj. + な / N + の / 〜ている / ある, いる + うちに | {若|わか}いうちに{旅行|りょこう}したい | the state is one that will end |
| 〜ないうちに | before (something unwanted) happens | ない form + うちに | {暗|くら}くならないうちに{帰|かえ}ろう | not for planned events in time order: {来|く}る{前|まえ}に |
| 〜ているうちに | while doing A, B came about | 〜ている + うちに | {聞|き}いているうちに{眠|ねむ}くなった | B is a change you didn't plan |
| 〜{間|あいだ} | all through (a period) | dict. / 〜ている / N + の + {間|あいだ} | {夏休|なつやす}みの{間|あいだ}、ずっと{家|いえ}にいた | N4 |
| 〜{間|あいだ}に | at some point within (a period) | as above + に | {留守|るす}の{間|あいだ}に{友|とも}だちが{来|き}た | a period seen from outside |
| 〜{最中|さいちゅう}に | right in the middle of (an interruption follows) | N + の / 〜ている + {最中|さいちゅう}に | {会議|かいぎ}の{最中|さいちゅう}に{電話|でんわ}が{鳴|な}った | actions and events with a peak, not stages of life |
| 〜{最中|さいちゅう}だ | in progress right now | as above + だ | {今|いま}、{試験|しけん}の{最中|さいちゅう}です | |
| 〜{途中|とちゅう}で | on the way; halfway through (an event) | dict. / N + の + {途中|とちゅう}で | {帰|かえ}る{途中|とちゅう}で{雨|あめ}に{降|ふ}られた | で for events |
| 〜{途中|とちゅう}に | on the way (where something is) | as above + に | {駅|えき}へ{行|い}く{途中|とちゅう}に{本屋|ほんや}がある | に with ある, いる |
| 〜{中|ちゅう} | in progress | N + {中|ちゅう} | {会議中|かいぎちゅう}, {電話中|でんわちゅう}, {午前中|ごぜんちゅう} | |
| 〜{中|じゅう} | all through, all over | time or place + {中|じゅう} | {一日中|いちにちじゅう}, {世界中|せかいじゅう}, {今日中|きょうじゅう} | {今週中|こんしゅうちゅう} takes ちゅう |

## Every time, the moment, only after (lesson 2)

| Pattern | Meaning | Form | Example | Limits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 〜たびに | every time | dict. / N + の + たびに | {会|あ}うたびに{大|おお}きくなっている | A must happen again and again |
| 〜ごとに | every (unit), at each | number + counter / N + ごとに | {十分|じゅっぷん}ごとに, {駅|えき}ごとに | {一日|いちにち}おきに = every other day |
| 〜たとたん(に) | the moment A, B (unexpected) | た form + とたん | {乗|の}ったとたん、ドアが{閉|し}まった | B is past and not the speaker's plan; no requests |
| 〜てはじめて | only after A did B (a realization) | て form + はじめて | {住|す}んではじめて{分|わ}かった | |
| 〜てからでないと | not until A (can B) | て form + からでないと / からでなければ | {買|か}ってからでないと{入|はい}れない | second half negative or difficult |
| 〜ついでに | while doing A anyway, also B | dict. / た form / N + の + ついでに | {駅|えき}に{行|い}くついでに{寄|よ}る | A is the main errand |
| 〜ぶりに | for the first time in (a gap) | length of time + ぶりに | {三年|さんねん}ぶりに{帰|かえ}った | ぶりの + N |
| めったに〜ない | hardly ever | めったに + negative | めったに{乗|の}らない | always negative; positive: たまに |

## Stages of an action (lesson 3)

| Pattern | Meaning | Form | Example | Limits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 〜ところだ | about to / in the middle of / just did | dict. / 〜ている / た form + ところだ | {今|いま}{作|つく}ったところです | N4 |
| 〜ところに / ところへ | just as (someone or something arrived) | the three ところ forms + に | {出|で}かけようとしているところに{電話|でんわ}が{来|き}た | B is an arrival or event |
| 〜ところを | the scene someone saw, caught, helped | the ところ forms + を + {見|み}る, {見|み}られる, {助|たす}ける… | {寝|ね}ているところを{見|み}られた | お{忙|いそが}しいところ(を): set phrase |
| 〜たところ | when I did A, I found B | た form + ところ + past result | {電話|でんわ}したところ、{閉|し}まっていた | B is a discovery, not your next action |
| 〜かける / 〜かけの | half done; on the point of | ます stem + かける / かけの + N | {食|た}べかけのパン, {忘|わす}れかけていた | |
| 〜たて | freshly done | ます stem + たて(の) | {焼|や}きたてのパン, できたて | only a few verbs: ×{食|た}べたて |
| 〜きり | only | number / N + きり (っきり) | {二人|ふたり}きり, {一度|いちど}きり | |
| 〜たきり | did A and never… since | た form + きり + negative | {出|で}かけたきり{帰|かえ}らない | second half negative |
| 〜たばかり | just did (it feels recent) | た form + ばかり | {買|か}ったばかりの{靴|くつ} | N4 |

## As things change (lesson 4)

| Pattern | Meaning | Form | Example | Limits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 〜につれて | as A changes, B changes | dict. / N + につれて | {年|とし}を{取|と}るにつれて{弱|よわ}くなる | gradual change in A; B a change, not a plan or request |
| 〜にしたがって | following (instructions); as | dict. / N + にしたがって | {説明|せつめい}にしたがって{書|か}く | したがう in kana |
| 〜とともに | together with; as; at the same time as | N / dict. + とともに | {年|とし}とともに{変|か}わる | formal, written |
| 〜{一方|いっぽう}だ | keeps on …ing (usually for the worse) | dict. + {一方|いっぽう}だ | {人口|じんこう}は{減|へ}る{一方|いっぽう}だ | needs an ongoing change |
| 〜ば〜ほど | the more …, the more … | ば form + dict. + ほど; 〜ければ〜いほど; 〜なら〜なほど | {練習|れんしゅう}すればするほど{上手|じょうず}になる | ほど alone also works |
| 〜ようになる / 〜なくなる | come to / stop | dict. / potential + ようになる; ない form → なくなる | {話|はな}せるようになった | N4 |
| 〜{化|か} | becoming…, -isation | N + {化|か}(する) | {少子化|しょうしか}, {都市化|としか} | |

Numbers in change: 〜{割|わり} = tenths ({三割|さんわり} = 30%), 〜パーセント, 〜{分|ぶん}の〜 (bottom number
first: {三分|さんぶん}の{一|いち}), 〜ばい (times), {半分|はんぶん}. A proportion ({割合|わりあい}) is
{高|たか}い / {低|ひく}い; an amount is {多|おお}い / {少|すく}ない.

## Intending and pretending (lesson 5)

| Pattern | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| 〜ようとする | try to; be about to (N4) | {起|お}きようとした |
| 〜ようとしたとき / ところに | just as I was about to | {寝|ね}ようとしたとき、{電話|でんわ}が{鳴|な}った |
| 〜ようとしない | (someone) won't | {父|ちち}は{医者|いしゃ}に{行|い}こうとしない |
| 〜つもりで | with the intention of, as if | {運動|うんどう}するつもりで{歩|ある}く |
| 〜たつもり | thought I had (but hadn't) | かぎをかけたつもりだった |
| 〜つもりだった | meant to (but didn't) | {早|はや}く{寝|ね}るつもりだった |
| 〜ふりをする | pretend (plain form; な-adj. + な; N + の) | {寝|ね}ているふり, {病気|びょうき}のふり |
| 〜たことにする | treat it as having happened | {行|い}ったことにする |
| 〜なかったことにする | treat it as not having happened | {聞|き}かなかったことにする |
| 〜ことにする / ことにしている | decide to / make it a rule (N4) | {毎朝|まいあさ}{歩|ある}くことにしている |

references.title: Written style: です/ます, だ and である
references.body:
Japanese has three styles: polite (です / ます), plain (casual speech, and the だ style of diaries,
blogs, novels and news articles) and the written である style of reports, essays, textbooks and
editorials (lesson 26). Choose one style for a whole text: だ and である can share a text, but
です / ます shouldn't join them.

## Sentence endings

| | Polite | Plain (だ style) | Written (である style) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Noun | {原因|げんいん}です | {原因|げんいん}だ | {原因|げんいん}である |
| Noun, negative | {原因|げんいん}ではありません | {原因|げんいん}ではない (じゃない in speech) | {原因|げんいん}ではない |
| Noun, past | {原因|げんいん}でした | {原因|げんいん}だった | {原因|げんいん}であった |
| Noun, past negative | {原因|げんいん}ではありませんでした | {原因|げんいん}ではなかった | {原因|げんいん}ではなかった |
| な-adjective | {深刻|しんこく}です | {深刻|しんこく}だ | {深刻|しんこく}である |
| い-adjective | {高|たか}いです | {高|たか}い | {高|たか}い (×{高|たか}いである) |
| い-adjective, past | {高|たか}かったです | {高|たか}かった | {高|たか}かった |
| Verb | {増|ふ}えます | {増|ふ}える | {増|ふ}える |
| Verb, ている | {増|ふ}えています | {増|ふ}えている | {増|ふ}えている |
| Guess | {増|ふ}えるでしょう | {増|ふ}えるだろう | {増|ふ}えるだろう / であろう |
| Explaining | {増|ふ}えるんです | {増|ふ}えるんだ / のだ | {増|ふ}えるのである |
| Modest opinion | 〜のではないでしょうか | 〜んじゃないかな (speech) | 〜のではないだろうか |
| Should | 〜べきです | 〜べきだ | 〜べきである |
| It is thought | 〜と{思|おも}います | 〜と{思|おも}う | 〜と{考|かんが}えられる / 〜と{思|おも}われる |

## Joining clauses

| Word | Speech (て form) | Writing (stem + 、) |
|---|---|---|
| Group 1 verb | {降|ふ}って、 | {降|ふ}り、 |
| Group 2 verb | {調|しら}べて、 | {調|しら}べ、 |
| する | {研究|けんきゅう}して、 | {研究|けんきゅう}し、 |
| ある | あって、 | あり、 |
| 〜ている | 〜ていて、 | 〜ており、 |
| い-adjective | {高|たか}くて、 | {高|たか}く、 |
| Noun, な-adjective | {問題|もんだい}で、 | {問題|もんだい}であり、 |
| Negative verb | {降|ふ}らないで / {降|ふ}らなくて、 | {降|ふ}らず、 (する → せず, {来|く}る → {来|こ}ず) |
| Negative い-adjective | {高|たか}くなくて、 | {高|たか}くなく、 |
| Negative noun | {原因|げんいん}ではなくて、 | {原因|げんいん}ではなく、 |

## Words

| Speech | Writing | | Speech | Writing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| でも, だけど | しかし, 〜が | | すごく, とても | {非常|ひじょう}に, かなり |
| だから | そのため, したがって | | ちょっと | {少|すこ}し, やや |
| それに | また, {更|さら}に, その{上|うえ} | | {色々|いろいろ}な | {様々|さまざま}な |
| AとB (nouns) | AおよびB | | やっぱり | やはり |
| 〜みたいだ | 〜ようだ | | 〜って | 〜という, 〜とは |
| ぐらい | {約|やく} | | 〜など | 〜{等|とう}, 〜など |
| {私|わたし}たち | {私|わたし}たち, われわれ | | これから | {今後|こんご} |
| どうして | なぜ | | {一番|いちばん} | {最|もっと}も |

## Numbers

| | Example | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Horizontal text | 2026{年|ねん}, {約|やく}30%, 1,500{万人|まんにん} | Arabic numerals |
| Vertical text | {二〇二六年|にせんにじゅうろくねん}, {三〇|さんじゅう}パーセント | kanji numerals, often digit by digit with 〇 |
| Units | {万|まん} (10⁴), おく (10⁸), ちょう (10¹²) | おく and ちょう have kanji outside N3 |
| … or more / or less | 〜{以上|いじょう} / 〜{以下|いか} | include the number |
| under | 〜{未満|みまん} | excludes the number: {十八歳|じゅうはっさい}{未満|みまん} = 17 and under |
| about | {約|やく}〜 | written for 〜ぐらい |

vocab.example: わたしは がくせいです。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm a student.
vocab.note: Often left out when it's clear you're talking about yourself.

vocab.example: ゆきさんは がくせいです。
vocab.exampleEn: Yuki is a student.

vocab.example: せんせいは にほんへ いきます。
vocab.exampleEn: The teacher is going to Japan.
vocab.note: Also a title after a name (たなかせんせい), for teachers, doctors and other respected professionals. Not used for yourself.

vocab.example: がっこうへ いきます。
vocab.exampleEn: I go to school.

vocab.example: にほんへ いきますか。
vocab.exampleEn: Are you going to Japan?

vocab.example: うちへ かえります。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm going home.

vocab.example: みずを のみます。
vocab.exampleEn: I drink water.
vocab.note: Means cold or room-temperature water; hot water is おゆ.

vocab.example: ごはんを たべます。
vocab.exampleEn: I eat a meal.

vocab.example: ほんを よみます。
vocab.exampleEn: I read a book.

vocab.example: がっこうへ いきます。
vocab.exampleEn: I go to school.
vocab.note: Polite form: いきます.

vocab.example: うちへ かえります。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm going home.
vocab.note: Polite form: かえります. かえる is also the word for frog (a noun).

vocab.example: みずを のみます。
vocab.exampleEn: I drink water.
vocab.note: Polite form: のみます.

vocab.example: ごはんを たべます。
vocab.exampleEn: I eat a meal.
vocab.note: Polite form: たべます.

vocab.example: ほんを よみます。
vocab.exampleEn: I read a book.
vocab.note: Polite form: よみます.

vocab.example: きょうは あめです。
vocab.exampleEn: It's raining today.

vocab.example: あした、がっこうへ いきます。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm going to school tomorrow.

vocab.example: きょうは あめですね。
vocab.exampleEn: It's raining today, isn't it?
vocab.note: あめ is also a different word, candy; the context tells you which.

vocab.example: ともだちは 「いっしょに いきましょう」と いいました。
vocab.exampleEn: My friend said, "Let's go together."

vocab.example: てがみを かきます。
vocab.exampleEn: I write a letter.

vocab.example: なまえは ジョン・スミスです。
vocab.exampleEn: My name is John Smith.
vocab.note: Someone else's name is politely おなまえ.

vocab.example: コーヒーを のみます。
vocab.exampleEn: I drink coffee.

vocab.example: いっしょに いきましょう。
vocab.exampleEn: Let's go together.

vocab.example: せんせいは 「おはようございます」と いいました。
vocab.exampleEn: The teacher said, "Good morning."
vocab.note: Polite form: いいます; いいました = said. Spoken "yū".

vocab.example: なまえを かきます。
vocab.exampleEn: I write my name.
vocab.note: Polite form: かきます.

vocab.example: たなかさん、おはようございます。
vocab.exampleEn: Good morning, Mr Tanaka.

vocab.example: おはよう、ゆきさん。
vocab.exampleEn: Morning, Yuki.
vocab.note: For family and friends; use おはようございます with teachers, colleagues and strangers.

vocab.example: こんにちは、たなかさん。
vocab.exampleEn: Hello, Mr Tanaka.
vocab.note: Written with the particle は, read "wa". Not used with your own family.

vocab.example: こんばんは。さむいですね。
vocab.exampleEn: Good evening. It's cold, isn't it?
vocab.note: Written with the particle は, read "wa".

vocab.example: おかあさん、おやすみなさい。
vocab.exampleEn: Good night, Mum.

vocab.example: おやすみ、また あした。
vocab.exampleEn: Night, see you tomorrow.

vocab.example: せんせい、さようなら。
vocab.exampleEn: Goodbye! (a pupil to the teacher at the end of the day)
vocab.note: Sounds rather final or formal; friends say じゃあね or またね.

vocab.example: じゃあね、また あした。
vocab.exampleEn: Bye, see you tomorrow.

vocab.example: またね！
vocab.exampleEn: See you!

vocab.example: じゃあ、また あした。
vocab.exampleEn: Well, see you tomorrow.

vocab.term: ありがとうございます
vocab.example: どうぞ。 — ありがとうございます。
vocab.exampleEn: Here you are. — Thank you.
vocab.note: For something already finished, ありがとうございました.

vocab.example: ありがとう、ゆきさん。
vocab.exampleEn: Thanks, Yuki.

vocab.term: どうもありがとうございます
vocab.example: てがみ、どうも ありがとう ございます。
vocab.exampleEn: Thank you very much for the letter.

vocab.example: ありがとう。 — どういたしまして。
vocab.exampleEn: Thanks. — You're welcome.
vocab.note: Can sound a little formal; many people just say いいえ.

vocab.example: すみません、コーヒー おねがいします。
vocab.exampleEn: Excuse me, a coffee, please.
vocab.note: Gets attention, apologises lightly, and thanks someone who went to trouble for you. Often pronounced すいません.

vocab.example: ごめんなさい、おそく なりました。
vocab.exampleEn: I'm sorry I'm late.
vocab.note: To family and friends; casual ごめん. To a teacher or at work, すみません.

vocab.example: はい、がくせいです。
vocab.exampleEn: Yes, I'm a student.

vocab.example: いいえ、せんせいです。
vocab.exampleEn: No, I'm a teacher.
vocab.note: Also brushes off thanks or an apology, "not at all".

vocab.example: はじめまして、スミスです。
vocab.exampleEn: How do you do? I'm Smith.
vocab.note: Only at a first meeting.

vocab.term: よろしくおねがいします
meanings: please treat me well (after introducing yourself)
I look forward to working with you
vocab.example: スミスです。よろしく おねがいします。
